text:
Ryū ga Gotoku Kenzan!: final chapter walkthrough

MAJOR STORY AND BOSS SPOILERS: This covers Chapter 12 of the original Japanese PS3 game, including both departure points, Kojiro, the Five Demons and Tenkai. It stops at the end of the playable route rather than retelling the ending scenes.

BEFORE LEAVING GION

Begin by speaking to the employee at Tsuruya's main entrance and entering the farewell gathering. After the scenes, Kojiro tells Kiryu where Haruka has been taken. Ito then offers his sword, which you collect from the blacksmith in Rakugai.

Do not rush from the blacksmith straight into the departure conversation if you are pursuing completion. This is the last opportunity to finish anything that needs Gion: its dojo, shops, local jobs and other district-specific activities.

There is also a final training event to arrange. If you have completed all Gion Martial Arts Dojo and Zanki Dojo training, speak to Komaki at the Gion dojo. Then visit Zanki Dojo, speak to the students outside and go to Sanjusangendo to witness the meeting between the masters. This unlocks Gion Martial Arts: Sword Reversal.

To record that Heat Action later, use unarmed combat against a regular enemy wielding a real sword while below 20% health, with enough Heat to activate it when the sword attack comes. Learning it alone only completes the ability entry. Do the dangerous low-health setup somewhere controlled, then heal; do not arrive at the final island badly injured just because you were ticking off a move.

Return home and speak to Ito when everything in Gion is finished. Choosing to depart permanently removes access to Gion for the remainder of this story run. Keep a separate save before saying you are ready.

THE FINAL PREPARATION WINDOW

Visit Koetsu at his mansion after leaving Gion. He directs you to the boatman at Riverside Tea House and allows you to change the time by resting at the mansion. This helps with remaining time-sensitive work outside Gion. It does not let you re-enter the district.

Before boarding the boat, visit En no Ozuma on River Road and complete Asura special training. The reward is Mysteries of the Sword: Swallow Drop. It becomes available in this final preparation window and can only be performed against the upcoming Kojiro boss.

Check the actual learned ability, not just whether you spoke to the trainer. You need two swords for the action. Have a usable single sword and greatsword or club available as well, because the island contains ranged enemies, armour, barriers and different boss behaviours.

Refill health and recovery supplies, complete any desired equipment upgrades and save again. The boat is the second point of no return: boarding ends the remaining free-roam preparation. Kojiro is only the first major encounter on the island, so plan your inventory for a long sequence afterward.

SASAKI KOJIRO AND SWALLOW DROP

Kojiro's long sword reaches farther than Marume's, and he moves faster. Try to draw out an attack, evade it and close the distance during his recovery. Rolling can help you cross the gap, but repeatedly rolling into him without reading the attack is not a substitute for timing.

When Kojiro enters Heat mode, your attacks still hurt him but no longer reliably interrupt him. Keep your defence ready even when you land the first hit of a combination. Trading several attacks just because your own sword connected can drain supplies you need for the army battle afterward.

To perform Swallow Drop, have two swords drawn while Kojiro is in Heat mode and remain close enough for his True Swallow Counter sequence to trigger. Complete the prompts, then activate the offered Heat Action.

The sequence has six QTE inputs. KHHsubs notes that the final successful input is the crucial one for enabling Swallow Drop, but missing earlier prompts still costs health. Aim to complete the entire sequence rather than deliberately taking damage.

Do not finish Kojiro before the action registers if you want full Heat Action completion. A powerful greatsword strategy can win the duel while bypassing the very trigger you came prepared to use. Reload the mainland save if necessary; later island bosses cannot substitute for him.

THE BEACH ARMY

After Kojiro, Tenkai sends in a long series of troops. Spearmen form the boundary of the arena. Touching those perimeter spears briefly staggers Kiryu, so circle within the space rather than hugging the edge to escape a crowd.

Gunmen arrive in two ambush waves, with QTEs after the 28th and 48th defeated enemies. When they appear, prioritise them. A distant shot can interrupt you and leave the surrounding melee enemies free to pile on damage.

The later waves include armoured enemies with long-reaching weapons. Clear the more mobile ordinary troops, isolate an armoured target and use the greatsword to break its protection. Heat Actions can also damage through armour.

The supplies shown around the beach become collectible after the battle. Do not build your survival plan around reaching one in the middle of a wave. When the fight ends, sweep the shore and heal before entering the fortress.

At the entrance, the Five Demons launch a combined QTE sequence. It continues even if you miss an input, so keep responding to the following prompts. One mistake is not a reason to stop trying and accept the rest of the damage.

YELLOW DEMON: TELEPORTS AND THE FIRST KEY

When the bridge is destroyed, drop into the lower area. The fall is part of the route. The Yellow Demon attacks near the pillars on the left.

His size is misleading: he moves like a ninja and can teleport behind you. Smoke is your warning. Be ready to roll and turn instead of continuing to guard in the direction he occupied a moment ago.

He also throws shuriken at range. Guard them with a sword, but stay ready for the repositioning that follows. Fighting toward the right-hand side of the area reduces his opportunities to use the pillar attack.

After winning, interact with his body and take the key. Then use it on the gate to the right. The Demon keys are not merely decorative boss rewards; failing to collect one leaves the corresponding route locked.

FIRST MINE AND WHITE DEMON

In the first mine section, examine the blocked stone wall before collecting explosives from the eastern side. Carry an explosive back, deploy it beside the wall and move away. Archers on the opposite side of the gap cannot be reached here, so keep moving to avoid their flaming arrows rather than searching for a route to kill them.

Beyond the wall, the White Demon begins with an ambush QTE. He swings a greatsword quickly, and his white aura reduces damage until it is worn down. Keep attacking during safe openings rather than expecting one powerful strike to end the fight.

The surrounding archers are an important part of this encounter. Fight near the central barrier, which provides cover from their arrows. Otherwise an arrow can stagger you just as the Demon attacks. Avoid being knocked down: his grounded finishing attack has no escape QTE.

Collect his key from the body and unlock the next door.

SECOND MINE AND BLACK DEMON

The next section again needs an explosive to remove a wall, but this time you can collect one without first examining the barrier. Kill the accessible enemies before carrying it. Flaming arrows can detonate the explosive in your hands, and surviving archers can continue bothering you in the following boss area.

There are additional completion opportunities here if needed: the Tengu Staff supports Thrust Mastery, and the stairs support Stair Mastery. Complete them only if you can do so without entering the next fight short on health or supplies.

The Black Demon fights like a wrestler. He can block sword attacks with his arms and punish close contact with an unblockable throw. Bait a committed attack, dodge around him and strike the recovery from the side or back.

Keep away from the cliff edge, especially when both fighters are hurt. His Cliff Drop can trigger while Kiryu is running near the edge below half health and the Demon is below one-quarter health. Failing that QTE causes an immediate game over. Remaining nearer the middle and healing before reaching that situation is safer than trusting a last-second prompt.

Take his key and open the next door.

THE WHARF AND BLUE DEMON

At the wharf, prioritise the archers and gunmen before focusing on the ninja. Once again, perimeter spears can interrupt movement. Trying to chase a ninja while ranged attackers repeatedly stagger you wastes health and time.

After clearing the troops, approach the boats to meet the Blue Demon. He uses a spear, with attacks resembling Inshun's, and adds shuriken at range. Face him for the spear attacks and do not assume you can safely absorb a thrust during his Heat mode: a connecting thrust can lead into a damaging sequence with no escape prompt.

He can vault to the opposite dock. Kiryu must go around on foot. Guard the shuriken while approaching rather than attempting to jump across after him.

Once he falls, collect the key and unlock the door. The surrounding enemies do not have to be eliminated before you leave this section, and they do not follow through the door. Break the chain beyond it with the greatsword to continue. There is also a Spirit Sword pickup along this stretch if you want it.

RED DEMON: FIRE AND REINFORCEMENTS

The Red Demon waits in the large tea room. He has ninja movement, shuriken, caltrops and an unblockable fire-breath attack. Prioritise evasion over standing directly in front of him with your guard held. Rolling away also helps when the fire animation is difficult to read in a crowded fight.

He begins with two supporting ninja and can summon two more reinforcement waves. During those waves he disappears and cannot be damaged. Defeat the visible ninja to bring him back, while avoiding the caltrops he continues throwing from concealment.

The room also has suitable surfaces for Tatami Flip and Shadow Stab if you still need those actions. Your immediate objective, however, is to survive the waves and finish the Demon.

Take his key, break the chain to lower the bridge, cross and unlock the door. Check all three steps if you seem stuck after the boss.

FINAL SUPPLIES AND TENKAI

The final troop section combines ninja with gunmen. Remove the shooters first. These enemies drop recovery items, giving you a chance to rebuild your inventory before the last boss. Collect what you need before moving into the rocky area.

Tenkai uses a rapid-firing pistol. The greatsword can block bullets, but its movement speed makes chasing him awkward. Use the large boulders as cover, let him expend a burst and attack while he reloads. Then reposition behind cover rather than trying to maintain a long, uninterrupted exchange.

His mist attack briefly stuns Kiryu. Recover and reset your position rather than immediately swinging while another volley is coming.

At 1,000 remaining health, Tenkai begins healing himself. Close in and attack during that animation. Waiting behind a rock through the healing phase lets him undo your progress; this is the moment to press the opening.

Defeat him to complete the playable story. Let the ending and credits finish, and retain your story saves alongside the resulting clear data. If you recorded Dry Leaf Smash, Escape Strike and Swallow Drop at their unique encounters, the most restrictive story-specific Heat Action opportunities are now behind you.

text:
The Democratic Party is using ‘Palestine’ as a disguise. https://t.co/98EZdzLPgZ
The Democratic Party is using ‘Palestine’ as a disguise.
Their slogans are about “Palestine” — but their real agenda has absolutely nothing to do with Palestinians.
JOSHUA HOFFMAN

As Democrats celebrated their sweeping victories across America this week, one word kept appearing in the speeches, statements, and celebrations of some of the party’s most energized candidates and supporters.

That word is Palestine — some make-believe place thousands of miles away, whose conflict with Israel (i.e., the Jews) has somehow become one of the defining political causes of America’s emerging Left.

In Michigan, chants of “Free Palestine” erupted as Abdul El-Sayed celebrated becoming the first Muslim elected to the United States Senate. He denounced American support for Israel, attacked AIPAC, and declared that Michigan’s tax dollars should be spent on domestic priorities rather than what he called “apartheid or genocide or war.”

In New York, Brad Lander, the Jewish Democrat elected to represent the state’s 10th Congressional District, promised to become “the Jewish member of Congress who is boldest in support of Palestinian freedom.”

Another New York winner, Darializa Avila Chevalier, demanded a complete arms embargo against Israel and the Palestinian “right of return.” During her June primary victory celebration, supporters had erupted into chants of “Free Palestine.” She was a Columbia University protest organizer before becoming a congressional candidate, and opposition to Israel is central to her political identity.

And these were hardly isolated figures.

Claire Valdez, another newly elected New York congresswoman, declared after winning her Democratic primary in June that she would continue calling for Palestinian liberation. She connected that commitment directly to domestic spending, arguing that Americans should use their money to improve lives at home rather than destroy them abroad.

In Colorado, Melat Kiros, another victorious democratic socialist, had similarly promised during her primary victory speech to stop what she called the “genocide in Palestine.” Following her November victory, she again called for accountability over what she described as American complicity in the conflict.

The same political movement helped propel Chris Rabb in Pennsylvania and Donavan McKinney in Michigan to congressional victories. Palestinian-American organizer Aber Kawas also won a New York State Senate seat after explicitly making Palestinian advocacy part of her challenge to the Democratic Party establishment.

These victories represent a meaningful political development, even if they do not mean that every Democrat, or even most of their voters, shares the same views. But here is what Americans need to understand: “Palestine” is not really about Palestinians. It has become a political symbol, an organizing principle, and an exceptionally useful instrument for a much broader anti-American ideological project.

That project is about who holds power in American society, who controls its wealth, which institutions deserve legitimacy, how history should be understood, and whether the political and economic order that made the modern West possible should be preserved or fundamentally transformed.

In fact, “Palestine” has become something of a password within this movement. Say it loudly enough, and you immediately communicate where you stand on a whole range of issues that have absolutely nothing to do with Palestinians.

You are against billionaires, corporations, capitalism, Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), American imperialism, and just about every established institution that supposedly perpetuates inequality and oppression. You support redistributing wealth, fundamentally restructuring American society, and replacing existing power structures with something entirely different.

And you can communicate all of that with just two words: Free Palestine. It is not simply a foreign-policy position, but an all-encompassing political identity.

The easiest way to understand this phenomenon is to examine what the Democratic Socialists of America, the organization behind several of these politicians, actually believes. Alongside demands to “Free Palestine,” they advocate aggressive wealth taxes, public ownership of major corporations and essential industries, abolishing ICE, and dramatically restructuring American political institutions.

They are not interested in reasonable reforms and continuous improvements, but in burning many of the existing systems down to the ground. Their ambitions extend well beyond ordinary changes. They propose abolishing the United States Senate, replacing the president and Supreme Court with institutions subordinate to Congress, and creating an entirely different political and economic system.

What does any of this have to do with the Israeli-Palestinian conflict? What does nationalizing major industries have to do with Palestinian self-determination? What does restructuring the American judiciary have to do with Gaza?

Nothing inherently, yet they have been packaged together as parts of one unified moral and political struggle. To support one increasingly means being expected to support the others. “Palestine” has become the gateway through which a much broader ideological revolution is being sold to American voters.

Protesters hold a "free palestine" banner with flags

photo: Leonardo Basso/Unsplash
And there is another dimension to this phenomenon that deserves considerably more attention: the Left’s remarkable ability to reinvent itself around whichever cause happens to dominate the cultural conversation.

A few years ago, Black Lives Matter was omnipresent. Politicians took knees, corporations issued statements, celebrities posted black squares on Instagram, and Americans were encouraged to demonstrate their moral virtue by publicly embracing the movement.

Before and alongside that, climate change became the defining moral emergency for an entire generation of activists. Greta Thunberg became an international celebrity. Politicians warned that civilization was running out of time. Young people marched in the streets and demanded that governments fundamentally restructure the global economy.

Climate change did not disappear. Racial issues did not disappear. What changed was the intensity of the cultural attention. The political spotlight moved on to October 7, 2023, Israel’s subsequent war against Hamas in Gaza, and the flood of images, videos, protests, and online campaigns that followed. Suddenly, “Palestine” became the defining moral cause of the moment. The slogans changed. The flags changed. The hashtags changed. But the underlying political psychology remained remarkably familiar.

Here was another opportunity to identify an “oppressed” population, accuse established institutions of perpetuating “injustice,” and demand that society reorganize itself around a moral emergency.

For activists who had previously built their public identities around other causes, “Palestine” offered a fresh opportunity to demonstrate their righteousness. It was the latest cause around which to rally, the latest opportunity to feel morally superior, and the latest way to distinguish the enlightened from the supposedly ignorant, indifferent, or evil.

This is the politics of feeling good about being good. And it is much easier than the politics of actually governing.

The great advantage of declaring yourself an ally to an “oppressed” people is that you do not necessarily have to explain how you intend to solve their problems. You can simply announce that you stand with them, identify their supposed “oppressors,” and demand that everyone else do the same. The political applause is immediate. The political responsibility can be postponed indefinitely.

And a politician who declares that they stand “against genocide” can instantly claim a kind of moral authority that politicians discussing healthcare financing, housing construction, or infrastructure spending cannot. Who wants to argue about the details of an insurance reimbursement system when someone else is claiming to “fight genocide”?

Show me the emerging American Left’s detailed policy proposals. I cannot recall one. Having a list of sweeping demands is not the same thing as having serious, workable governing strategies. “Free Palestine” is not governance. The same applies to many of the movement’s domestic ambitions like “abolish ICE,” “tax the rich,” “Medicare for All,” and “end capitalism.”

Announcing an outcome does not resolve the difficult questions of cost, implementation, incentives, public support, or unintended consequences.

It is easy to promise affordable housing. It is considerably harder to explain how to construct enough homes, reform zoning, lower building costs, and overcome local opposition.

It is easy to promise that billionaires will pay for everything. It is considerably harder to demonstrate precisely how much revenue a proposed tax will generate, how businesses and investors will respond, and whether the resulting system can sustainably finance the promises being made.

It is easy to condemn war. It is considerably harder to explain how a democracy should respond when a terrorist organization massacres its citizens, takes hostages, and promises to repeat the attack.

That is the difference between political performance and political competence.

It is also why the movement increasingly resembles what political theorists call Third Worldism: a worldview that interprets global affairs principally through the struggle between an exploitative Western world and supposedly “oppressed” peoples fighting for “liberation.”

Just look at the “rising stars” of the Democratic Party. Ilhan Omar was born in Somalia. El-Sayed’s parents are Egyptian. Mamdani was born in Uganda. Rashida Tlaib’s parents are from the West Bank. These politicians and others have literally imported Third Worldism into the Democratic Party.

Under this worldview, national conflicts are rarely examined on their own historical terms. Instead, they are inserted into a larger story about colonialism, capitalism, racial hierarchy, and Western domination. Israel is reduced to an outpost of Western imperialism, and “Palestine” becomes the symbolic representative of everyone supposedly “oppressed” by the system.

And once one accepts this framework abroad, it becomes remarkably easy to apply it at home.

If Israel represents settler colonialism, America can be condemned through the same lens. If Israeli soldiers represent occupation, American police and immigration agents can be portrayed as instruments of an analogous system. If wealth is understood principally as the product of exploitation, redistribution becomes a moral obligation rather than an economic proposition to be evaluated on its merits. And if established institutions are inherently “oppressive,” replacing the people who control them becomes an act of “liberation.”

This is how an argument ostensibly about “Palestine” can become an argument about who should control America’s wealth, institutions, and government. It is also how “Palestine” becomes a weapon in the Democratic Party’s internal struggle for power. Defeating a “pro-Israel” (really, a pro-Western) Democratic incumbent can therefore be presented as simultaneously defeating the donor class, confronting American imperialism, and advancing social justice. One electoral victory becomes a triumph over multiple supposed systems of “oppression.”

There is no need to persuade voters that a longstanding incumbent has failed on housing, healthcare, or education if that incumbent can instead be portrayed as “supporting Israel genocide.” It is a shortcut to moral disqualification. Nobody has explained the underlying strategy more clearly than Aber Kawas, the newly elected Palestinian-American state senator from New York.

After winning her Democratic primary in June, Kawas openly discussed how “Palestine” was being used to redefine progressive regressive politics. She argued that politicians who champion affordability or oppose immigration enforcement must also speak out about “Palestine” to demonstrate ideological consistency. A politician can support universal healthcare, higher taxes on wealthy Americans, workers’ rights, affordable housing, and virtually every other major liberal policy.

But if that politician supports Israel’s existence as a Jewish state and rejects the movement’s characterization of Israel as inherently “oppressive,” their liberal credentials can suddenly become suspect. That is not ordinary foreign-policy debate. It is an attempt to redefine the ideological boundaries of an American political movement. And once those boundaries are established, enforcing them becomes a powerful instrument of political control.

This is how relatively small but highly organized ideological factions can transform much larger political parties. They need not immediately convince every voter. They need only establish the rules by which politicians, donors, activists, and institutions are judged.

This is why Americans should be careful not to confuse the popularity of a political cause with the seriousness of the movement advocating it. For all their grandstanding about Palestinian “liberation,” what are these politicians actually doing to improve Palestinians’ lives?

Sanctioning Israel, demanding arms embargoes, berating AIPAC, threatening to arrest Benjamin Netanyahu, and calling for an end to American military aid might generate applause at campaign rallies, but none of it constitutes a serious plan for Palestinian prosperity, security, or self-government.

You know what would actually make a difference? Removing Hamas from power in Gaza, holding Mahmoud Abbas and his inner circle accountable for corruption and self-enrichment, building functioning Palestinian institutions, and creating an economy that offers Palestinians something more promising than perpetual conflict.

And even then, why has this particular issue become such an obsession within the Democratic Party? The U.S. faces enormous challenges involving the strength of the dollar, global supply chains, access to critical minerals and rare earths, economic competitiveness, and the rise of China. Those issues have far greater implications for America’s long-term prosperity and global influence than the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

Yet you would never know it from listening to the “Free Palestine” crowd, whose political priorities seem to revolve around condemning America’s allies, attacking its institutions, and championing causes thousands of miles from home. For all their talk about “liberation,” one question remains conspicuously unanswered: What, exactly, is their vision for making America better?

A serious movement should welcome those questions. A movement built around political performance prefers to condemn the people asking them.

Tom Emmer once helped launch a Somalia Caucus in Congress. More than a decade later, he was telling Somalis to “go the hell back to where they came from.”

In June 2015, Emmer joined Keith Ellison, then a Democratic congressman from Minnesota, to launch the bipartisan Congressional Somalia Caucus. The goal was to support peace, stability and democratic governance in Somalia.

But Emmer's rhetoric toward Somalis has since taken a different turn.

As President Donald Trump intensified his attacks on Somali Americans, Emmer echoed his rhetoric. In June 2026, the Republican congressman claimed Somalis “don't assimilate” into American society and said those who refuse to do so should “go the hell back to where they came from.”

Congresswoman Ilhan Omar responded: “I assimilated all the way to Congress and this idiot still tells me to go back where I came from.”

The November 3 election offered a striking contrast.

Minnesotans reelected both lawmakers in separate congressional districts, but Ilhan received nearly 60,000 more votes in her district than Emmer did in his.

♛ RKOS RADIO 006: FOLLOW THE MONEY

NEW INVESTIGATIVE FILES

NOVEMBER 8, 2026

THE MACHINERY BEHIND THE CURTAIN

Corporate political spending, concealed vendors, influencer payments, AI propaganda, and criminal corruption cases.

I found several new stories that go beyond our previous investigations. One involves major AI companies and their executives financing rival political advertising networks. Another concerns a former congressman convicted of secretly representing a foreign government.

1. AI money funding both sides of American politics

Documented funding • No criminal finding

BELLINGCAT INVESTIGATION • NOVEMBER 2, 2026

Funding reported from Greg and Anna Brockman, Andreessen Horowitz, and its founders$125M
Leading the Future network

Funding from Anthropic for a competing AI-policy agenda$40M
Public First Action

Bellingcat examined more than 300 online political video advertisements and identified something striking.

The Leading the Future network, backed by donors including OpenAI president Greg Brockman and venture capital investors, financed advertisements supporting candidates from both major parties. The opposing Public First Action network, supported by Anthropic, also backed candidates across party lines.

Most examined ads did not mention artificial intelligence, even though AI policy was a central concern of the sponsoring networks.

OpenAI said it does not direct Leading the Future's activities and that the relevant participation was personal, not on the company's behalf. Bellingcat found no evidence of unlawful coordination with candidate campaigns.

bellingcat

RKOS question: When advertisements emphasize immigration, affordability, or party loyalty, how easily can voters identify the industry's policy interests behind the money?

2. More than $36 million routed through little-known vendors

Unresolved regulatory allegations

Bellingcat also identified more than $36.4 million in payments by the Leading the Future network to four recently established companies with minimal identifiable public business presence.

The reported payments included more than $20 million to Lantern Production Consultants and $13 million to Summit Ridge Media.

The Campaign Legal Center filed a complaint alleging that certain payments concealed the ultimate purposes of political spending. The FEC had not ruled on the complaint when the investigation was published.

The companies' structure and payments warrant scrutiny, but those facts alone do not prove they were illegitimate businesses or that a crime occurred.

bellingcat

3. One political operator linked to hundreds of committees

THE GUARDIAN • NOVEMBER 1, 2026

A Guardian investigation examined the activities of political treasurer Thomas Datwyler.

According to its analysis of federal filings:

He served as treasurer for more than 350 federal political committees, including around 100 super PACs.

Super PACs he managed spent more than $2 million across the 2024 and 2026 cycles helping candidates who were also his clients or opposing their rivals.

In one Florida congressional race, a campaign and a legally independent supporting super PAC shared 14 vendors.

Some funding moved through nonprofits that were not required to reveal their donors.

Datwyler said his businesses maintain internal safeguards and comply with applicable laws. Shared personnel and vendors do not themselves prove prohibited coordination.

The Guardian

The question: How can voters independently establish whether organizations operating through overlapping service providers are genuinely independent?
4. Journalists tested whether influencers would hide political payments
NEWSGUARD • OCTOBER 30, 2026
Initially expressed interest in undisclosed paid political posts.21 / 60
35% of influencers contacted

NewsGuard created a fictitious political consulting firm and offered up to $2,000 for TikTok videos promoting political messages without revealing payment.

Twenty-one influencers initially expressed interest without objecting to the secrecy condition. The responses included 12 of 30 left-leaning creators and 9 of 30 right-leaning creators.

This was a controlled journalistic test, not proof those creators actually published deceptive advertisements.

NewsGuard

5. A former congressman secretly worked for Venezuela

U.S. DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE • OCTOBER 2, 2026

This one went through a criminal trial.

Former Republican congressman David Rivera was sentenced to 10 years in federal prison after a jury convicted him of offenses involving acting as an unregistered agent of Venezuela and laundering money.

Prosecutors presented evidence concerning a $50 million contract with a subsidiary of Venezuela's state-owned oil company, undisclosed lobbying, and approximately $1.5 million in proceeds deposited into a Florida state campaign account.

Unlike the disputed political funding cases above, this resulted in a conviction and sentence.

United States Department of Justice

6. Bribery money buried in a backyard

U.S. DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE • AUGUST 24, 2026

Former Baldwin Park councilman Ricardo Pacheco admitted accepting bribes connected to government decisions, including a police union contract.

The Justice Department reported that Pacheco had buried $62,900 in cash in two locations in his backyard.

Former Compton councilman Isaac Galvan also admitted participating in a bribery arrangement connected to cannabis business permits. Both received 18-month federal prison sentences.

United States Department of Justice

7. Nearly seven out of ten tracked AI political ads lacked disclosures

ASSOCIATED PRESS • SEPTEMBER 2026

Researchers at the Wesleyan Media Project identified at least 164 political advertisements made or enhanced with AI during the election cycle.

Share of identified AI ads without AI-use disclosures69%

The sample also showed that 80% of identified ads came from Republican candidates or aligned organizations. Some AI ads were plainly satirical, while others posed greater risks of misleading viewers. Disclosure laws vary by state, and not every unlabeled ad violates the law.

AP News

♛ RKOS investigative verdict

The strongest leads here are the AI-industry political spending networks and the overlapping political financial structures. They offer concrete opportunities to examine public records, donors, contractors, and accountability.

The strongest established criminal cases are Rivera's conviction and the California bribery cases.

For our next RKOS RADIO investigation, I'd go after one central question:

Who ultimately receives the millions flowing through political advertising vendors, and what services did that money actually purchase?

That's a specific, testable question. We can follow public filings instead of guessing at hidden masterminds.

♛ RKOS RADIO: THE PAPER TRAIL DOESN'T CARE WHICH PARTY YOU SUPPORT.

text:
🔭 Fireballs, a Mars–Jupiter pairing, and Voyager 1 approaching one light-day from Earth

November 2026 is shaping up as a remarkably generous month for anyone willing to look up, with three meteor showers, a striking predawn meeting between Mars and Jupiter, a dazzling supermoon to close out the month — and, far beyond the planets, a historic milestone for NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft.

The first shooting stars come from the Southern and Northern Taurids, two related showers that reach their highest activity about a week apart: the Southern around November 5, the Northern around November 12. Both are named for the constellation Taurus, the point in the sky from which their meteors appear to originate. Neither is prolific — even under excellent conditions, each typically produces only about five meteors per hour. What the Taurids lack in numbers they make up for in quality, occasionally throwing off fireballs, exceptionally bright meteors that can make even a quiet night of skywatching memorable.

Later in the month, the Leonids offer another chance, with the best viewing expected in the early morning hours of November 17 and 18, once the Moon has dropped below the horizon. Under ideal conditions observers could see roughly 15 meteors per hour, though actual counts will generally be lower. The practical advice is simple: get away from bright city lights, give your eyes about 30 minutes to adjust to the darkness, and watch a broad section of sky rather than concentrating on one small area.

Meteors are not the only reason to set an early alarm. Before sunrise on November 15 and 16, Mars and Jupiter will form an eye-catching pairing in the southeastern sky, separated by only about 1.2 degrees — slightly more than the apparent width of two full Moons placed side by side. Jupiter will be the brighter of the two, while Mars stands out by its characteristic reddish hue, and no telescope or binoculars will be needed. Their closeness, though, is an illusion of perspective: viewed along our line of sight the planets appear side by side, but they remain separated by enormous distances in space. Watched over several consecutive mornings, they will first creep closer together before their positions shift and they begin drifting apart again.

Meanwhile, far beyond anything visible from a backyard, Voyager 1 is approaching a distance of one light-day from Earth — the first human-made object ever to travel that far. A light-day is the distance light covers in 24 hours, and because radio signals move at the speed of light, a message sent from Earth will now take a full day to reach the spacecraft. An immediate reply takes another 24 hours to arrive, so even the fastest possible round-trip conversation spans roughly 48 hours. The milestone is a stark measure of how far the probe has traveled since leaving Earth — and of how challenging communication across that distance has become.

text:
📈 4/5. AI vs. Dot-Coms, Real Estate, and Financial Bubbles.

People compare the AI boom to previous speculative bubbles. But these comparisons often overlook the underlying economic mechanisms.

Consider the dot-com bubble.

The internet was a genuine technological revolution. It transformed communication, commerce, information distribution, logistics, banking, and entire industries.

It also contributed substantially to productivity growth.

Yet countless internet companies were valued on expectations that proved unrealistic. When the bubble burst in 2000, enormous amounts of speculative capital disappeared.

The internet survived. The revolution continued.

AI could follow a similar pattern — but potentially with a more direct impact on the production of knowledge and services.

The internet primarily made information, communication, and transactions dramatically more accessible and efficient.

AI can also perform parts of the intellectual work itself.

It can write code, analyze documents, prepare reports, coordinate processes, and complete tasks that previously required direct human effort.

The difference is not that the internet failed to improve productivity. It clearly did.

The difference is that AI may extend automation into a much broader range of cognitive tasks performed at individual workplaces.

Now consider the US housing bubble before 2008.

Rising property prices, mortgage expansion, securitization, and financial leverage created enormous paper wealth and speculative activity.

But doubling the market price of an existing house does not double its useful output or make its occupants twice as productive.

In fact, research has shown that property booms can divert capital toward less productive activities.

Similarly, speculative financial bubbles involving derivatives, leveraged securities, or asset-price expectations can expand market valuations without producing proportional improvements in society’s productive capacity.

Financial markets and instruments can provide essential services, of course. Their speculative excesses are the issue.

Cryptocurrency speculation offers another comparison: price appreciation does not automatically demonstrate equivalent real-world economic value.

AI is different in one fundamental respect.

Its commercial value can be directly connected to work performed, time saved, costs reduced, and entirely new capabilities created.

That does not eliminate speculation or guarantee profitability.

But it gives the underlying technological revolution an unusually direct connection to everyday economic productivity.

text:
KENZAN! SHOGI RANKING: THE COMPLETE LADDER

Play at Narikane Shogi in Rakugai from 5-6. Entry is listed as 50 Mon. Beat an opponent above your current grade to advance. The grades climb from Rank 10 toward Rank 1, then from 1st Dan through 10th Dan, followed by Shogi King.

Below is the full opponent roster and the prize for that level. Where two names share a rank, both belong to that rank; this is not a claim that the game requires two wins before every promotion. Choose the stronger unlocked opponent when trying to move upward.

RANKS 10–1

Rank 10: Nukesaku and Mataro. Reward: Manju.
Rank 9: Ofuu and Torachiyo. Reward: Kujo Onion.
Rank 8: Tarosuke and Iwahiko. Reward: Tri-Colour Dango.
Rank 7: Yannosuke and Heikichi. Reward: Rice Ball.
Rank 6: Shinemon and Tatsugoro. Reward: Pepper.
Rank 5: Keizo and Kyuhei. Reward: Ginger.
Rank 4: Gonzaemon and Kyubei. Reward: Snail.
Rank 3: Ekichi and Daian. Reward: Unrefined Sake.
Rank 2: Genshiro and Eizaemon. Reward: Sludge Worm (Medium).
Rank 1: Ihei and Jinbei. Reward: Nada Refined Sake.

All these opponents allow replays. Use them to revisit a dropped-piece threat or an undefended capture rather than repeating the same move without understanding why it failed.

Early opponent descriptions offer a useful choice. Nukesaku is weak overall; Mataro attempts a defensive game. Ofuu attacks, while Torachiyo favors defense and gives up relatively readily. Tarosuke attacks less predictably, Iwahiko builds a firmer defense, and Yannosuke/Heikichi continue the attacking/defensive split. Their style does not guarantee a particular reply.

DAN OPPONENTS

1st Dan: Kennosuke. Scallop. Replays allowed.
2nd Dan: Yujiro. Vitality Pill. Replays allowed.
3rd Dan: Fujihiko. Frenzy Pill - High Grade. Replays allowed.
4th Dan: Danji. Vitality Pill - High Grade. Replays allowed.
5th Dan: Oyuki. Horse Meat. Replays allowed.
6th Dan: Zenzaburo. Sarashi. Replays allowed.
7th Dan: Kotetsu. All-Purpose Pill - High Grade. Replays allowed.
8th Dan: Mankichi. Konpeito. No replays.
9th Dan: Eisuke. Castella. No replays.
10th Dan: Ho-oh. Gambler's Tobacco. No replays.
Shogi King: Seio. Gold Comb. No replays.

A PRACTICAL PLAN FOR STANDARD POSITIONS

Develop one attacking side instead of pushing unrelated pawns across the whole board. Opening your bishop's diagonal and advancing the pawn in front of the rook are useful themes, but check the opponent's reply before continuing either plan.

Move the king away from your main rook battle and keep golds close enough to cover it. Do not walk the king into a bishop diagonal while trying to build a castle. A solid position that survives a rook drop is worth more than a pawn won by exposing your back rank.

Against attacking opponents, defend the threatened point with enough pieces and look for a capture that turns their advanced piece into a useful drop. Against defensive opponents, improve your own pieces and create a second weakness instead of sacrificing into a defended castle.

Before a major exchange, inspect both players' hands. The board can look quieter after a trade while the newly available drops make it much more dangerous. Save your replays for the first mistaken assessment, before the position deteriorates further.

At 8th Dan and above, calculate the opponent's strongest check, capture and fork before confirming. There is no takeback safety net. A proposed attacking move should answer two questions: what does it threaten, and what happens if the opponent checks your king instead?

Defeating Seio clears the ranking requirement, not all shogi completion by itself. Finish the ten numbered trials and Final Trial in Gion as well.

text:
$COHR KEY READ-THROUGHS FROM COHERENT’S FISCAL Q1 2027 EARNINGS CALL

Coherent’s results indicate that AI networking investment is expanding across several distinct layers: conventional transceivers, connections between data centers, integrated optics, and the manufacturing infrastructure supporting those products. The strongest positive implications concern optical transport, compound-semiconductor production equipment, substrates, and qualified optical connectivity suppliers. The important negative implications are more selective: copper connectivity faces a longer-duration substitution risk, merchant laser demand cannot be extrapolated directly from transceiver growth as customers increase internal production, and strong optical revenue growth is requiring substantial cash investment. The approximately $20 billion PhotonLink agreement validates the scale of integrated-optics demand, but does not establish orders for competing suppliers or identify the unnamed customer. Several peers had already reported strong results before November 4, making this call corroborating evidence and an extension of demand visibility rather than a prediction of those completed quarters. Country labels below identify primary listing markets; material manufacturing geography is distinguished separately.

OPTICAL TRANSPORT AND NETWORKING SYSTEMS

DISTRIBUTED AI CREATES A SECOND NETWORKING INVESTMENT CYCLE OUTSIDE THE DATA CENTER (READ-THROUGH 1)

Affected companies: Ciena Corporation (CIEN: United States); Nokia Corporation (NOKIA: Finland).

Directional impact and magnitude: Strongly positive for optical transport demand. High consolidated relevance for Ciena; high relevance to Nokia’s Optical Networks business but a more moderate consolidated effect because Nokia retains substantial exposure to other markets.

Call evidence: Coherent’s scale-across revenue exceeded $200 million, increased 53% sequentially, and nearly quadrupled year over year. Management expects quarterly revenue to approximately double from that level by the end of calendar 2027. Anderson attributed the expansion to “large AI workloads that are spanning multiple data centers” and identified demand for ZR/ZR+ modules, line cards, amplifiers, ROADMs, and complete solutions. Multi-rail revenue is expected to begin ramping in March 2027.

Transmission mechanism: Distributed AI workloads require greater transport capacity between facilities, not just more connections within individual clusters. That translates into demand for coherent optical engines, line systems, amplification, optical switching, and associated network-management capabilities. Ciena and Nokia participate directly in these product categories. The investment implication is that optical transport can benefit from AI deployment even where customers increase utilization of existing facilities rather than build entirely new campuses. More effective use of installed fiber still requires upgraded transmission equipment.

The exposure is particularly material for Ciena. Its September 3 release showed Optical Networking revenue of approximately $1.19 billion, representing 71.3% of consolidated revenue. Nokia’s October 22 report showed 18% constant-currency growth in Optical Networks and projected 25% to 30% growth for its combined Optical and IP Networks businesses in 2027. Coherent’s subsequent acceleration supports the underlying demand assumptions behind those outlooks.

Near-term catalysts: Subsequent order and shipment updates, capacity availability, and the March 2027 multi-rail introduction. Coherent’s product ramp is evidence of the end-market opportunity, not a disclosed order for either peer.

Longer-duration implication: AI investment broadens the optical transport customer base beyond traditional telecommunications operators. However, Coherent’s increasingly complete solutions and direct hyperscaler sales also introduce competition for portions of system-level spending. The high-conviction conclusion is positive market demand, not automatic market-share gains or proportional growth across every transport vendor. This signal should not be transferred indiscriminately to wireless infrastructure or telecommunications service-provider earnings.

OPTICAL COMPONENTS AND INTEGRATED PHOTONICS

HIGH-POWER LASERS GAIN STRATEGIC VALUE, WHILE MERCHANT EML GROWTH FACES AN INSOURCING LIMIT (READ-THROUGH 2)

Affected companies: Lumentum Holdings (LITE: United States); Marvell Technology (MRVL: United States), through its proposed acquisition of Lumentum and existing optical connectivity portfolio.

Directional impact and magnitude: Strongly positive for qualified high-power CW lasers and integrated optical assemblies. Negative for assumptions that merchant EML purchases must grow proportionally with transceiver production. The positive opportunity is potentially material to Lumentum; the negative effect is product-specific and does not establish a consolidated revenue decline.

Call evidence: Coherent’s approximately $20 billion PhotonLink agreement is anchored by its 400-milliwatt CW laser and includes a higher-level solution beyond the laser. PhotonLink revenue is expected to exceed $100 million in March 2027 and $250 million per quarter before the end of calendar 2027. Separately, Anderson disclosed that the internal-versus-external indium phosphide sourcing mix “hasn’t changed much in a year,” but expects it to shift toward internal production as capacity expands.

Transmission mechanism: CPO and related architectures create demand for qualified external light sources, laser modules, and associated optical assemblies. Lumentum has a documented ultra-high-power laser and external-laser-source portfolio addressing this requirement. Its November 2 results independently disclosed another major NPO/CPO win with purchase commitments exceeding $5 billion. The combined evidence supports a market moving beyond demonstrations toward substantial commercial commitments.

The negative implication concerns the composition of future laser demand. Coherent’s internal production has so far expanded broadly alongside its transceiver requirements, allowing external suppliers to participate in growth. If internal production subsequently grows faster than internal consumption, purchased EML content per transceiver declines. Merchant suppliers can therefore experience slower growth in their addressable purchases even while the overall transceiver market expands rapidly. Coherent did not identify its external suppliers or purchasing allocations, so a specific Lumentum customer-revenue loss cannot be quantified or asserted.

Near-term catalysts: Coherent’s December-quarter CW laser shipments, the March PhotonLink milestone, and subsequent disclosures of Lumentum’s own integrated-optics shipments. Lumentum’s November 2 results already contained strong demand evidence; Coherent’s call reinforces that evidence rather than creating the entire thesis.

Longer-duration implication: Value increasingly depends on qualification, optical power, reliability, packaging, and integrated content rather than generic laser-unit exposure. Marvell’s proposed combination could strengthen electrical-optical co-design, while Coherent’s independence remains attractive to customers seeking a supplier without competing semiconductor interests. Neither positioning establishes a guaranteed winner. Lumentum’s announced fixed exchange ratio of 4.5 Marvell shares also means its trading response cannot be separated from Marvell’s share price and transaction-completion risk.

OPTICAL MANUFACTURING AND ASSEMBLY

PLUGGABLES AND INTEGRATED OPTICS CAN COEXIST, BUT MANUFACTURING GROWTH IS NOT CASH-FLOW-LIGHT (READ-THROUGH 3)

Affected company: Fabrinet (FN: United States), with major manufacturing operations in Thailand.

Directional impact and magnitude: Positive and highly material for operating demand; negative for near-term cash conversion and for treating outsourced optical manufacturing as requiring little incremental capital.

Call evidence: Coherent expects both 800G and 1.6T transceiver revenue to grow, with 800G growth continuing through calendar 2027. Anderson stated, “We expect pluggable transceivers to remain the dominant form factor for scale-out networks over the coming years.” Simultaneously, Coherent spent approximately $776 million on quarterly capital expenditure and expects another sequential increase.

Transmission mechanism: Overlapping 800G and 1.6T cycles support assembly, alignment, packaging, and testing demand without requiring an immediate replacement of the installed manufacturing model. New NPO/CPO programs can add manufacturing work rather than simply eliminate conventional transceiver production. Fabrinet’s November 2 call independently described growth in hyperscaler-direct and merchant transceivers, capacity installation for OCS and multi-rail, and expected NPO/CPO contributions toward the end of fiscal 2027.

This is a material company-level exposure. Fabrinet reported approximately $777 million of data center revenue, or 53% of total revenue, up 78% year over year. Its own disclosures therefore support the demand transmission without requiring an assumption that Coherent has awarded it a particular program.

The negative read-through is equally concrete. Fabrinet reported approximately $21 million of operating cash flow against approximately $159 million of capital expenditure, producing roughly $137 million of negative free cash flow. Capital expenditure included approximately $77 million for a Santa Clara campus. Even excluding that purchase as a limited analytical adjustment, cash after the remaining capital expenditure would still have been negative by approximately $60 million. Coherent’s expansion burden corroborates that cash investment is occurring across the manufacturing chain, not only at vertically integrated laser producers.

Near-term catalysts: December-quarter program ramps and the planned January 2027 expansion in Fabrinet’s manufacturing capacity. These are primarily revenue-conversion and utilization catalysts, not evidence that installed capacity immediately becomes revenue.

Longer-duration implication: The simplistic claim that CPO eliminates Fabrinet’s opportunity is contradicted by both companies’ customer discussions. The more relevant risk is whether additional manufacturing content earns sufficient returns after capacity, working capital, qualification, and ramp costs. Coherent’s prospective 45% gross margin must not be transferred to Fabrinet’s assembly economics; Fabrinet’s latest adjusted gross margin was approximately 12.1%.

COPPER INTERCONNECT AND CONNECTIVITY SEMICONDUCTORS

OPTICAL SCALE-UP CHALLENGES COPPER ATTACH RATES, NOT CREDO’S ENTIRE CONNECTIVITY BUSINESS (READ-THROUGH 4)

Affected company: Credo Technology Group (CRDO: United States).

Directional impact and magnitude: Negative for long-duration assumptions about copper AEC penetration in links that migrate to optics. Limited immediate earnings impact from this call alone. Potentially material to the exposed copper product opportunity, but not a high-conviction negative conclusion for Credo’s consolidated business because it also sells optical products.

Call evidence: Coherent expects initial integrated-optics deployments in scale-out, followed by scale-up CPO and NPO in late calendar 2027 or early 2028. Chip-to-chip optical connectivity was placed further out, in 2029 to 2030. Management described the central opportunity as “converting copper links to optical links over time.”

Transmission mechanism: Where an optical connection replaces a copper connection, the associated AEC content is no longer purchased for that link. Optical reach and bandwidth can also permit larger scale-up domains, changing the mix of connections rather than simply increasing demand for the existing copper implementation. This creates a real terminal-growth constraint for models that assume copper retains its current role across progressively larger systems.

The boundary is important. The call does not identify a Credo design loss, establish that all short-reach copper connections disappear, or demonstrate an immediate reduction in AEC shipments. Coherent’s initial CPO ramp addresses scale-out applications that may replace existing optical implementations rather than copper. The more relevant copper substitution window begins with scale-up adoption, not the first December-quarter PhotonLink shipment.

Credo’s September 1 disclosures identify a portfolio spanning AECs, optical transceivers, silicon-photonics PICs, optical DSPs, and Ethernet and PCIe retimers. Optical adoption can therefore remove copper content while creating opportunities elsewhere in Credo’s portfolio. Likewise, a lower discrete DSP attach rate in a particular integrated design does not imply elimination of all optical DSP or retimer demand.

Near-term catalysts: Customer architecture announcements and Credo’s product-level design-win disclosures. The call’s late-2027/early-2028 scale-up timetable does not support an immediate, across-the-board reduction in near-term AEC estimates.

Longer-duration implication: Credo’s valuation depends increasingly on its ability to capture the migration across copper and optical products, rather than on an indefinitely expanding copper-only opportunity. The high-conviction negative is architectural substitution within specific links; the company-wide outcome depends on retained and replacement content.

COMPOUND-SEMICONDUCTOR MATERIALS

SUBSTRATES BENEFIT FROM VERTICAL INTEGRATION, BUT SUPPLY ASSURANCE DOES NOT ELIMINATE CHINA EXPOSURE (READ-THROUGH 5)

Affected company: AXT (AXTI: United States), whose disclosed substrate manufacturing facilities are in China.

Directional impact and magnitude: Strongly positive for the indium phosphide substrate opportunity and material to AXT’s operating outlook. No specific Coherent supplier allocation is established.

Call evidence: Coherent doubled internal indium phosphide output capacity year over year and plans to more than double it again by the end of calendar 2027. Management stated that it has secured necessary substrates and uses more than 5 substrate suppliers. Expansion is concentrated on 6-inch production, with further capacity planned beyond 2027.

Transmission mechanism: Producing lasers internally removes demand for some externally manufactured finished devices, but does not remove the need for substrate inputs. This creates an important distinction between upstream substrate exposure and merchant laser exposure. A qualified substrate producer can participate in the industry’s capacity expansion regardless of whether the finished laser is consumed internally or sold to another transceiver manufacturer.

AXT’s October 29 release independently showed the materiality of this demand channel. Revenue increased 54% sequentially to $73.4 million, driven by exceptionally strong indium phosphide demand, while adjusted gross margin reached 56.1%. Management also cited productivity gains and expansion in high-value, large-diameter products. Coherent’s subsequent manufacturing roadmap supports the duration of that demand environment, but is not a newly disclosed AXT purchase order.

The geographic qualification is critical. Coherent’s Texas, Sweden, and Switzerland manufacturing footprint does not establish a substrate supply chain independent of China. AXT’s own disclosures identify Chinese production facilities and export permits as a material risk. Coherent’s statement that supply has been secured improves customer-level confidence, but does not prove that export-license timing, shipment execution, or alternative-source qualification has ceased to matter.

Near-term catalysts: AXT’s shipment conversion, export-permit execution, large-diameter product qualification, and customer capacity ramps. Its October results were already public; the incremental signal is greater confidence in sustained demand into 2027.

Longer-duration implication: Substrates offer exposure to a broader set of optical manufacturing outcomes than a particular finished-device architecture. However, doubled device-output capacity does not imply doubled substrate units or revenue. Larger wafers, better yields, device mix, and customer sourcing shares affect the conversion. Coherent’s supplier diversification also limits the case for assuming permanent scarcity pricing.

PHOTONICS PRODUCTION EQUIPMENT

THE OPTICAL BUILDOUT IS ALREADY LARGE ENOUGH TO CHANGE AIXTRON’S COMPANY-LEVEL EARNINGS MIX (READ-THROUGH 6)

Affected company: AIXTRON (AIXA: Germany).

Directional impact and magnitude: Strongly positive, with high company-level materiality. This is a targeted compound-semiconductor equipment implication, not a blanket positive conclusion for every wafer-fabrication equipment supplier.

Call evidence: Coherent’s quarterly capital expenditure reached approximately $776 million, with another sequential increase expected. Its 6-inch indium phosphide expansion spans Texas and Sweden, with Zurich production expected during the first half of calendar 2027. Management is planning further capacity beyond 2027.

Transmission mechanism: Expanding qualified InP laser and photonic-device production requires epitaxial growth capability alongside downstream processing, assembly, and test. AIXTRON’s G10-AsP platform directly addresses InP manufacturing, including 6-inch production. Its disclosed Nokia deployment establishes a verified production-equipment role, while its October 29 results showed optoelectronics representing approximately 68% of equipment orders and InP-related demand comprising the majority of backlog.

This is already a substantial earnings driver rather than a small optional exposure. AIXTRON reported quarterly orders of €274.9 million, up 122% year over year, and equipment backlog of €549.4 million. Coherent’s call reinforces the customer investment cycle underlying that backlog. It does not establish that Coherent purchases every relevant tool from AIXTRON, nor does it justify allocating a fixed percentage of Coherent’s total capital budget to the company.

The cash-flow transmission is also differentiated. Coherent is consuming cash to build manufacturing capacity, while AIXTRON reported €138.4 million of quarterly operating cash flow, substantially supported by customer advances. Funding can therefore move upstream before final optical products generate cash. AIXTRON’s cash position benefits during the ordering phase, but advance receipts are not recurring earnings and can reduce cash collected when equipment is subsequently delivered.

Near-term catalysts: Conversion of existing equipment backlog into shipments and customer acceptance through 2027. The already-completed Coherent capacity doubling partly reflects equipment previously ordered and installed, so it should not be counted again as an entirely new equipment-order catalyst.

Longer-duration implication: Continued expansion beyond 2027 provides a more durable demand signal than a single wafer-size conversion. The main risks are customer capacity overshoot, equipment productivity reducing required tool counts, and orders being pulled forward rather than permanently increasing. Coherent’s roadmap supports the cycle’s duration, not an unlimited extension of current order growth.

OPTICAL FIBER AND CONNECTIVITY

FIBER CONTENT BENEFITS FROM COPPER REPLACEMENT, BUT BANDWIDTH GROWTH IS NOT A FIBER-KILOMETER FORECAST (READ-THROUGH 7)

Affected company: Corning Incorporated (GLW: United States).

Directional impact and magnitude: Positive and highly relevant to Optical Communications, with meaningful consolidated earnings implications.

Call evidence: PhotonLink includes complex fiber assemblies and connectors across CPO, NPO, and chip-to-chip applications. Coherent identifies copper-to-optical conversion as a major incremental market. At the same time, management emphasized that its scale-across solutions help customers make better use of existing fiber.

Transmission mechanism: Replacing electrical connections with optical links creates demand for fiber pathways, connectors, cable assemblies, and higher-density connectivity inside and around data centers. Corning has independently verified exposure through its May 6 NVIDIA partnership, which includes expansion of U.S. optical connectivity capacity by 10 times and U.S. fiber production capacity by more than 50%. The connection is therefore supported by a disclosed commercial relationship, not merely thematic association.

The opportunity is material to the group. Corning’s October 27 release reported Optical Communications sales of $2.38 billion, up 44%, representing approximately 47% of group core sales. Enterprise Networks sales increased 84%, and generative-AI product sales more than doubled. Coherent’s call reinforces demand longevity and an expanding set of optical endpoints.

The less obvious distinction is between connectivity content and raw fiber distance. Higher bandwidth can be carried over existing installed fiber through improved transmission equipment. Consequently, Coherent’s nearly quadrupled scale-across revenue is not evidence that outside-plant fiber demand grew at the same rate. The cleaner read-through is to high-density data center connectivity and assemblies, rather than a proportional increase in newly laid long-distance fiber.

Near-term catalysts: Conversion of Corning’s existing customer agreements into shipments and continued enterprise-connectivity growth. These agreements predate Coherent’s call; the new evidence supports the demand environment rather than establishing another Corning award.

Longer-duration implication: Optical penetration can increase fiber and connector content per deployed compute system. However, Coherent manufactures specialty fiber and assemblies itself. The $15,000 maximum PhotonLink content estimate cannot be assigned to Corning, and Corning should not be assumed to supply every component in that architecture.

AI COMPUTE AND NETWORKING PLATFORMS

QUALIFIED OPTICAL CAPACITY REDUCES NVIDIA’S DEPLOYMENT RISK, WHILE ADVANCE FUNDING BECOMES PART OF PLATFORM COMPETITION (READ-THROUGH 8)

Affected company: NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA: United States).

Directional impact and magnitude: Positive for networking execution and system-deployment reliability. Potentially important strategically, but the direct consolidated revenue or EPS benefit cannot be quantified from this call.

Call evidence: Coherent’s 400-milliwatt CW laser covered by the NVIDIA partnership is expected to begin generating revenue in the December quarter. Internal indium phosphide capacity doubled ahead of the original schedule. Management also said that LTAs typically include upfront customer payments to help finance the capacity required for those customers.

Transmission mechanism: Qualified laser and optical-assembly availability reduces the risk that networking components delay deployment of larger accelerated-computing systems. This is a stronger inference than treating every dollar of supplier optical revenue as incremental NVIDIA sales. An optical component can gate a much larger system deployment, but the call does not disclose a previously constrained NVIDIA shipment quantity or a recovered revenue amount.

The relationship is verified. The March 2 partnership announcement included a nonexclusive multibillion-dollar purchase commitment, future access and capacity rights, and a separate $2 billion NVIDIA investment in Coherent. The November call provides operating evidence that the manufacturing program is progressing toward commercial shipments. The investment amount should not be relabeled as a quarterly customer prepayment, and investment funding, purchase commitments, and capacity rights should not be added together as if they were separate revenue awards.

The negative counterpoint is that supply assurance increasingly requires capital commitment and longer purchasing horizons. Large platforms can use their balance sheets to secure capacity, potentially raising the cost of competing at scale. However, the agreement is nonexclusive, and Coherent’s additional anchor customer demonstrates that access is not reserved solely for NVIDIA. The unnamed $20 billion customer cannot be identified from the call.

Near-term catalysts: December-quarter production shipments and subsequent networking-platform qualification and deployment disclosures. These are execution catalysts rather than proof of additional accelerator demand.

Longer-duration implication: Competitive advantage increasingly includes control over qualified optical supply, packaging, and manufacturing readiness alongside compute silicon and software. Coherent’s progress strengthens NVIDIA’s supply-assurance position, but does not demonstrate customer returns on AI spending, eliminate facility-power constraints, or establish that supplier capacity

text:
I'd like to elaborate on why Republican voters are far more likely to move when prices surge. This demographic largely consists of the middle class and a significant number of small business owners—people who are deeply sensitive to return on investment (ROI) and government policy whenever there are major economic fluctuations. Crucially, they also possess the financial capacity to actually pack up and relocate. 

On the other hand, while many Democratic voters may also be vocal with their grievances, a large portion relies on government welfare programs. For instance, if they are accustomed to California's robust welfare benefits, moving to Texas or other states offers very little economic advantage, as many of those safety nets simply do not exist there. 

That 'welfare lock-in' effect is precisely why we are seeing the current demographic and political shift.

🏀🏀 SATURDAY #FantasyBasketball RECAP STORM 🏀🏀

SOME OF YOU FORGET TO DO SO, so I remind you as always: please follow. And actually while you're at it, subscribe to my show, which is far better than any simple tweet. https://t.co/L2WFdgM5kK

Nuggets @ Pacers
🏀 I'm not 100% sold on this but I think it's possible all 5 Nuggets starters can be top-100 fantasy producers. It's also possible that it's just two. I'll add this: I'm not sure any of Braun, Cam or Gordon are IMPACT level guys, and maybe that's all that really matters.
🏀 Zubac had some fouls and is ramping up. Remain patient.
🏀 Andrew Nembhard had the type of game that H2H players tend to forgive quickly, but it just takes a couple of these hollow ones to pull his 9-cat rank back under the start line. It's why I never full bought into the roto side. He's still a solid Hali fill-in for H2H spots, though

Nets @ Hawks
🏀 Nolan Traore had another good one but he seems quite ripe to taper off given he's shooting 54% on the year so far. Probably worth a play when Mikel Brown gets a rest day (coming right up), though
🏀 Day'Ron Sharpe has put a few decent ones together in some non-blowout, non foul trouble games and his season rank is up to 153. As I've said a bunch of times on the pod, I was low on him but not THIS low and I expected him to push back up the board a bit. I didn't see much of a way to buy low since folks that had given up would probably have dropped him. Folks on the wire don't have the chance to succeed he does, so he always had that narrow "at least he's a starting center" thing. Anyway hold is the point
🏀 Danny Wolf started and played 31 mins and we can toss him on a watch list for now
🏀 Kingston Flemings once again started for the Hawks but once again didn't really do much. I'm still not sold that he's going to be anywhere near top-100

🏀 Aaron Wiggins has already had a hot, cold and new hot streak in just 2.5 weeks and seems like he's going to settle somewhere right along the border. Probably startable all year without a ton of upside but that'll play in H2H and roto too if you're maybe down 1 or 2 injuries.
🏀 Dyson Daniels is up to #37

Wizards @ Thunder
🏀 No AD again, but this time they played a good team and RUH ROH. Anyway, Sarr and Kyshawn survived it so count your blessings on those 2. Sarr is probably not a buy low any more after this short AD absence.
🏀 Aday Mara popped back into the starting 5 and that's when we know we've got a little success on the horizon. He remains a definite must-roster guy while Chet is out but there'll be some nasty ones, some really good ones, and it'll probably all level off in the 85-to-115 range
🏀 Alex Caruso can be safely left on waivers
🏀 Jared McCain is on one of his little couple game heaters even with lower mins. I don't have the stones to try to ride the wave. Maybe you do. Just not my way of playing fantasy hoops.

Here's the thing: I know it seems like the sky is falling but he's not going to shoot 36% all year, and confidence will beget more success. It'll be okay. I can almost promise.

text:
On the issue of how the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway affects beaches, I have a friend who runs a beach house in Okun Ajah. 

He said the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway has brought them more customers from the mainland because the drive to the beach is now smooth. The trip from Surulere (Stadium) to Okun Ajah Beach takes about 30 minutes, compared with the usual three to four hours due to traffic on the Lekki-Ajah highway veering off from Abraham Adesanya.

I didn’t believe him, so I left my house in Surulere and got to the beach in exactly 46 minutes. It took exactly 32 minutes to travel from my house through V/I and onto the coastal road, before turning off at Okun Ajah. From the turnoff to Okun Ajah and the Beach itself, which is further inland, it took exactly 14 minutes. If the beach were one of the closer ones, the final drive would take approximately four to five minutes after turning off the coastal road.

This was my personal experience. I told my friends and loved ones, but they couldn't believe me.

Now, almost every other weekend, I drive my family to different beach houses to experience what they have to offer. We don't go in the afternoon; we usually leave Surulere at around 7pm and are already settled at the beach by 8pm. 

We enjoy the atmosphere for about three hours, then drive home. Most weekend evenings, we’re home and in bed before 11pm

My boys are loving the experience. The plan is to visit all the beaches and give an honest opinion. So far, we’ve covered almost 40%, or thereabouts.

These are my personal experiences with my family and a few friends.

text:
Heineken won a Grand Prix at Cannes Lions 2026 with voice notes. Uber Eats, Columbia and Clash Royale each took one too. The rules behind all four are free to copy.

I've judged award entries, and I've written our own. Here's what wins:
1. Start with a habit everybody has. Heineken in Brazil built a WhatsApp bot that turned a long voice note into a free beer.
2. One idea, one sentence. Uber Eats let fans build their own Super Bowl ad inside the app.
3. Give people something to do, not just something to watch. Columbia's CEO offered the company to anyone who finds the edge of the Earth. Nobody can win it. Anybody can argue about it.
4. Show the score, not the effort. Judges skip "we worked really hard." If you can't show a number, show behaviour: queues, shares, replies.
5. Steal the rule, not the ad. Clash Royale invited the copycat games' players over and paid them in gold and cards.

So, for your shop, this week:
1. Find the habit your customers already have.
2. Write your idea in one sentence. If it needs two, cut.
3. Give people something to do, not just something to read.
4. Count what changed.

Juries don't reward money. They reward a truth you can feel in one second. You've got those for free.

· · ·

Heineken thắng một giải Grand Prix tại Cannes Lions 2026 nhờ tin nhắn thoại. Uber Eats, Columbia và Clash Royale cũng mỗi thương hiệu giành một giải. Những quy tắc đằng sau cả 4 chiến dịch đều chép lại được, miễn phí.

Mình đã chấm bài dự thi giải thưởng, và cũng đã viết hồ sơ dự thi của chính tụi mình. Đây là những điều giúp thắng giải:
1. Bắt đầu từ một thói quen ai cũng có. Heineken ở Brazil làm một con bot WhatsApp, biến một tin nhắn thoại dài thành bia miễn phí.
2. Một ý tưởng, gói trong một câu. Uber Eats cho người hâm mộ tự làm quảng cáo Super Bowl của riêng họ ngay trong app.
3. Cho người ta việc để làm, chứ không chỉ thứ để xem. CEO của Columbia hứa trao công ty cho bất kỳ ai tìm ra mép Trái Đất. Không ai thắng được. Ai cũng cãi nhau về chuyện đó được.
4. Cho thấy kết quả, đừng kể công. Ban giám khảo bỏ qua câu "chúng tôi đã rất cố gắng". Nếu không có con số, hãy cho thấy hành vi: hàng người xếp chờ, lượt chia sẻ, lượt phản hồi.
5. Học lỏm quy tắc, đừng chép quảng cáo. Clash Royale mời người chơi bản nhái chuyển qua, rồi trả cho họ bằng vàng và thẻ bài trong game.

Vậy nên, với tiệm của bạn, trong tuần này:
1. Tìm thói quen mà khách của bạn đã có sẵn.
2. Viết ý tưởng của bạn trong một câu. Cần tới hai câu thì cắt bớt.
3. Cho người ta việc để làm, chứ không chỉ thứ để đọc.
4. Đếm xem điều gì đã thay đổi.

Ban giám khảo không trao giải cho tiền bạc. Họ trao giải cho một sự thật bạn cảm được trong một giây. Những sự thật đó thì bạn có sẵn, miễn phí.

text:
Deepinder Goyal’s (@deepigoyal) ₹85,000 Temple wearable attracted so much traffic that its website crashed shortly after pre-orders opened. I have a weird hypothesis about why that happened.

I think it happened partly because AI is making us intellectually insecure and physically obsessive.

For a long time, knowledge and intelligence were important sources of competence, status and self-worth. You studied more, knew more, thought faster and developed expertise that gave you an advantage over others.

Now AI can do most of your work. It's undoubtedly making us more productive, but I wonder if it's also making us a little insecure about our own abilities. When a machine can do so much of what we previously took pride in doing ourselves, it's natural to question what makes us valuable.

Perhaps some of that need for achievement and control will increasingly find its way into our bodies.

Look at the growing fascination with supplements, sleep scores, biomarkers, longevity protocols, glucose monitors, VO2 max and recovery tracking. Of course, there's a genuine desire to be healthier. But I suspect there's something else at work too.

Our bodies offer a sense of ownership over our achievements that AI is making harder to find in intellectual work. AI can design a workout or recommend a diet, but it can't lift weights, endure a run or resist a sugar craving on our behalf. We still have to put in the effort, and we can take personal satisfaction in the results.

As more of our intellectual work becomes easier to outsource, I suspect the body will become an increasingly important source of personal pride, status and control.

Perhaps Temple is the next evolution of wearable trackers. But I wouldn't be surprised if its appeal also reflects a much larger shift in how we seek to feel capable and valuable in an age of AI.
