text:
“The old system under the law of Moses was only a shadow, a dim preview of the good things to come, not the good things themselves. The sacrifices under that system were repeated again and again, year after year, but they were never able to provide perfect cleansing for those who came to worship. If they could have provided perfect cleansing, the sacrifices would have stopped, for the worshipers would have been purified once for all time, and their feelings of guilt would have disappeared. But instead, those sacrifices actually reminded them of their sins year after year. For it is not possible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins. That is why, when Christ came into the world, he said to God, “You did not want animal sacrifices or sin offerings. But you have given me a body to offer. You were not pleased with burnt offerings or other offerings for sin. Then I said, ‘Look, I have come to do your will, O God— as is written about me in the Scriptures.’” First, Christ said, “You did not want animal sacrifices or sin offerings or burnt offerings or other offerings for sin, nor were you pleased with them” (though they are required by the law of Moses). Then he said, “Look, I have come to do your will.” He cancels the first covenant in order to put the second into effect. For God’s will was for us to be made holy by the sacrifice of the body of Jesus Christ, once for all time. Under the old covenant, the priest stands and ministers before the altar day after day, offering the same sacrifices again and again, which can never take away sins. But our High Priest offered himself to God as a single sacrifice for sins, good for all time. Then he sat down in the place of honor at God’s right hand. There he waits until his enemies are humbled and made a footstool under his feet. For by that one offering he forever made perfect those who are being made holy. And the Holy Spirit also testifies that this is so. For he says, “This is the new covenant I will make with my people on that day, says the Lord: I will put my laws in their hearts, and I will write them on their minds.” Then he says, “I will never again remember their sins and lawless deeds.” And when sins have been forgiven, there is no need to offer any more sacrifices. And so, dear brothers and sisters, we can boldly enter heaven’s Most Holy Place because of the blood of Jesus. By his death, Jesus opened a new and life-giving way through the curtain into the Most Holy Place. And since we have a great High Priest who rules over God’s house, let us go right into the presence of God with sincere hearts fully trusting him. For our guilty consciences have been sprinkled with Christ’s blood to make us clean, and our bodies have been washed with pure water. Let us hold tightly without wavering to the hope we affirm, for God can be trusted to keep his promise. Let us think of ways to motivate one another to acts of love and good works. And let us not neglect our meeting together, as some people do, but encourage one another, especially now that the day of his return is drawing near. Dear friends, if we deliberately continue sinning after we have received knowledge of the truth, there is no longer any sacrifice that will cover these sins. There is only the terrible expectation of God’s judgment and the raging fire that will consume his enemies. For anyone who refused to obey the law of Moses was put to death without mercy on the testimony of two or three witnesses. Just think how much worse the punishment will be for those who have trampled on the Son of God, and have treated the blood of the covenant, which made us holy, as if it were common and unholy, and have insulted and disdained the Holy Spirit who brings God’s mercy to us. For we know the one who said, “I will take revenge. I will pay them back.” He also said, “The Lord will judge his own people.” It is a terrible thing to fall into the hands of the living God. Think back on those early days when you first learned about Christ. Remember how you remained faithful even though it meant terrible suffering. Sometimes you were exposed to public ridicule and were beaten, and sometimes you helped others who were suffering the same things. You suffered along with those who were thrown into jail, and when all you owned was taken from you, you accepted it with joy. You knew there were better things waiting for you that will last forever. So do not throw away this confident trust in the Lord. Remember the great reward it brings you! Patient endurance is what you need now, so that you will continue to do God’s will. Then you will receive all that he has promised. “For in just a little while, the Coming One will come and not delay. And my righteous ones will live by faith. But I will take no pleasure in anyone who turns away.” But we are not like those who turn away from God to their own destruction. We are the faithful ones, whose souls will be saved.”
Hebrews 10:1-39 🤗🕊💖

text:
On 4 November, it was my great honour to host the Royal House of Georgia's inaugural Hong Kong Investiture & Gala Dinner at the Hong Kong Golf & Tennis Academy, with 110 distinguished guests joining us for a memorable black-tie evening of recognition, fellowship and shared purpose.
 
Presided over by HRH Crown Prince Davit Bagration of Mukhrani and Georgia, the ceremony conferred 39 royal honours through the Order of the Eagle of Georgia and the Order of Saint Queen Tamar. I warmly congratulate our new Knights and Dames, whose contributions across business, healthcare, philanthropy and public service remind us that true nobility is measured not by title, but by service to others.
 
We were privileged to hear from our Guests of Honour: Dr. Ronald Lam Man-kin, JP, Director of Health of the Hong Kong SAR Government, Mr. Dave Yau Shu-fung, KStJ, Commissioner of the Hong Kong St. John Ambulance Brigade, and Father Stephan Rothlin, SJ, Director of the Macau Ricci Institute, who also offered Grace. Their reflections, together with HRH's royal address, brought the evening's values vividly to life.
 
I was deeply honoured to be appointed Rector General for Greater China, alongside Professor Johnnie Chi Kau Chan as Rector for Hong Kong SAR and Dr. Sir Billy Chan as Rector for Macau SAR.
 
This is only the beginning. We envisage an annual investiture in a different province of the Chinese Mainland, bringing together existing members and new recipients. Nominations are already coming forward, including from CPPCC circles and individuals who have contributed to the Belt and Road Initiative. Each will be carefully assessed: recognition must reflect genuine merit and a commitment to giving back.
 
Above all, the evening affirmed that the real prestige of an honour lies in what we can achieve together for others. I look forward to building on the friendships and common purpose forged that night.
 
2026年11月4日晚，格魯吉亞王室首屆「香港授勳典禮暨慶典晚宴」在西貢香港高爾夫球及網球學院圓滿舉行，逾百位政商及社會各界嘉賓應邀出席，共證歷史時刻。典禮由格魯吉亞王室首領大衛·巴格拉季昂王儲殿下（HRH Crown Prince Davit Bagration of Mukhrani and Georgia）偕同其子喬治王子殿下（HRH Prince Giorgi）親臨主禮，並頒授「格魯吉亞之鷹勳章」及「聖塔瑪女王勳章」兩項歷史悠久的王室殊榮，合共頒發39項榮譽予38位在商界、醫療、社會公益、公共服務及共建「一帶一路」等領域作出卓越貢獻的傑出領袖，當中包括多位香港黑龍江社團總會及香港黑龍江經濟合作促進會的同仁。每一位獲此殊榮者均經過嚴謹審慎的評核，實至名歸；作為主辦方，我謹向各位新晉爵士與女爵士（Knights and Dames）致以最誠摯的祝賀！  
 
當晚，香港特區政府衛生署署長林文健醫生, JP 及香港聖約翰救傷隊總監游樹峯先生, KStJ 親臨擔任主禮嘉賓並發表致辭，澳門利氏學社社長羅世範神父（Father Stephan Rothlin, SJ）亦致辭並於晚宴前領禱，為盛會注入深厚的人文與倫理意涵；而大衛王儲殿下的王室致辭，更為整個夜晚定下了莊重而溫暖的基調。我深感榮幸於典禮上正式獲委任為格魯吉亞皇家騎士團大中華區總團長（Rector General for Greater China），聯同香港特別行政區團長陳志球教授, SBS, BBS, JP（Prof. Johnnie Chan）及澳門特別行政區團長陳比利爵士（Sir Billy Chan），共同肩負拓展騎士團大中華區會務與慈善使命的重任。

I kissed her shoulder. "I'm serious. Why are you looking at me like I just asked you to run a marathon?"

"Baby, do you know what you're asking?"

"You're my wife. Who else am I supposed to ask?"

"I thought marriage was supposed to give me some peace."

I smiled. "This is peace. You'll leave the house happier and I'll have a good day."

"What happens when I'm tired?"

"Then I'll be very convincing until you change your mind."

We negotiated. I wanted five mornings a week. She offered two. We landed on four, with weekends off so she could "recover."

The first few days I was thrilled. I'd wake up, remind her of our deal. By the middle of the week she was dragging. One morning she stayed in the shower forever. Another morning she said her back hurt. When I asked if she still wanted me, she looked panicked and said of course she did, she was just exhausted.

text:
November 7 Saint Hieron of Mytilene (Gerone, Ierone) Nicander, Hesychius, and Companions, the 33 Martyrs of Mytilene.
Died c. 300.
.
Hieron was born in Tyana in Cappadocia of a good and devout mother, Stratonika, who was blind. Hieron was a very zealous Christian and served his blind mother with great filial love. 
.
The co-ruling emperors Diocletian (284-305) and Maximian (284-305) sent a large military detachment headed by Lysias to Cappadocia to eradicate Christianity there, and also to conscript healthy and strong men into the imperial army. Among those pressed into service, Lysias also ordered his men to draft Hieron, who was distinguished by his great physical strength and dexterity.
.
For two reasons he did not wish to join the army, and he resisted and drove off those who had been sent to take him. Hieron was loath to leave his helpless mother, and it was grievous for him even to consider that, as a soldier, he would be compelled to offer sacrifices to idols. When they attempted to seize him by force and bring him to Lysias, he took a stick and started beating the soldiers who had been sent to bring him. The soldiers scattered, ashamed of being defeated by a single man.
.
Hieron then hid himself in a cave with eighteen other Christians who would not offer sacrifice to the pagan gods. Lysias would not risk losing his soldiers by storming the cave. Upon the advice of Cyriacus, one of Hieron’s friends, Lysias lifted the siege of the cave and withdrew his detachment. Then Cyriacus persuaded Hieron not to offer resistance to the authorities. Hieron was arrested along with other Christians, and they were all taken before the eparch of the town of Melitene.
.
Soon Hieron had a vision in his sleep, in which his impending martyrdom was foretold. A man clad in a brilliant white garment appeared to Hieron one night and said: ``Behold, Hieron, I proclaim salvation to you: you shall not wage war for an earthly king, but for the Heavenly King you will complete your struggle, and you shall soon come to Him to receive honor and glory.'' At this, Hieron's heart was filled with inexpressible joy.
.
In Melitene they were all thrown into prison and Hieron, with great zeal, strengthened all the prisoners in the Faith, urging that not even one of them fall away, but that all willingly offer their bodies to torture and death for Christ. All but one confessed their faith in the Lord Jesus Christ. The exception was Hieron's kinsman Victor, who fell away from the Faith. 
.
The tormentors beat the martyrs. They cut off one of Hieron's hands and arms to the elbow, then flogged and tortured him in various ways until they beheaded him and the others. Going to the place of execution, these thirty-three martyrs chanted the Psalm: Blessed are the undefiled in the way, who walk in the law of the Lord (Psalms 118:1)
.
A certain rich and illustrious Christian by the name of Chrysanthus ransomed Hieron’s head from Lysias. When the persecutions finally ceased, he built a church on the place where they executed the holy martyrs, and he placed the venerable head in it. The bodies of all the executed saints were secretly buried by Christians. In reign of the emperor Justinian, during the construction of the church of Hagia Eirene (Holy Peace), the venerable relics were uncovered and found incorrupt.
.
The other martyrs are: Hesychius, Nicander, Athanasius, Mamas, Barachius, Callinicus, Theogenes, Nikon, Longinus, Theodore, Valerius, Xanthius, Theodoulus, Callimachus, Eugene, Theodochus, Ostrychius, Epiphanius, Maximian, Ducitius, Claudian, Theophilus, Gigantius, Dorotheus, Theodotus, Castrichius, Anicletus, Themelius, Eutychius, Hilarion, Diodotus and Amonitus.
.
Eternal Father, I wish to honor Saints Hieron, Nicander, Hesychius, and the Martyrs of Mytilene, and I give Thee thanks for all the  graces Thou hast bestowed upon them. I ask Thee to please increase grace in  my soul through the merits of this saint, and I commit the end of my life to them by this special prayer, so that by virtue of Thy goodness and promise, Saints  Hieron, Nicander, Hesychius, and the Martyrs of Mytilene might be my advocate and provide whatever is needed at that hour. Amen.

text:
The Evolution of Randall Amplifiers, 1970-2026

Randall Amplifiers was founded in 1970 by Don Randall, a former Fender executive instrumental in developing Fender's sales organization and marketing. Based in California, Randall became known for powerful solid-state amplifiers before expanding into modular tube, hybrid and all-tube designs.

1970s - Early solid-state era

Randall's early amplifiers employed transistor technology, including field-effect transistor (FET) preamplifier designs. These circuits offered high input impedance, substantial clean headroom and consistent operation without vacuum-tube maintenance. Engineer Gary Sunda played an important role in developing Randall's early amplifiers.

1980s - The RG series

The RG series established Randall's reputation for high-gain solid-state amplification. The RG100ES became particularly influential, combining transistor preamplification, aggressive distortion, responsive equalization and a powerful solid-state output section.

These designs relied heavily on preamp gain shaping to establish their characteristic response, rather than the power-stage distortion associated with heavily driven tube amplifiers.

Early 1990s - Century 200

The Century 200 advanced Randall's high-power solid-state approach. Rated at 200 watts, it became associated with Dimebag Darrell of Pantera, whose recordings helped establish Randall as an important manufacturer in heavy metal.

Dimebag's sound also depended on external equalization, effects, pickups, speaker cabinets and recording techniques.

Late 1990s - Warhead

Randall developed the Warhead signature amplifier around Dimebag Darrell's performance requirements. Its solid-state architecture incorporated high-gain circuitry and additional sound-shaping and effects features intended to consolidate elements of his stage equipment.

The Warhead reinforced Randall's commitment to solid-state amplification when many competing high-gain manufacturers emphasized vacuum tubes.

2002 - MTS modular tube system

Developed with Bruce Egnater, Randall's Modular Tube System introduced interchangeable analog tube preamplifier modules.

The 100-watt RM100 accommodated three modules, allowing different preamp circuits and control settings within one amplifier. The system used actual vacuum tubes rather than digital amplifier simulations.

MTS offered musicians considerable flexibility without requiring multiple complete amplifiers.

2005-2006 - Valve-Dynamic hybrid

Randall introduced the V2 and T2, combining tube circuitry with high-power MOSFET output stages.

The Valve-Dynamic power section employed a 12AT7 tube driver feeding transistor circuitry, rated at 400 watts RMS into 4 ohms and 280 watts into 8 ohms.

The V2 combined tube and solid-state preamp paths, demonstrating Randall's continuing experimentation with different amplification technologies.

2013 - Thrasher and modern all-tube amplification

Working with designer Mike Fortin, Randall introduced the Thrasher 120, a 120-watt all-tube amplifier using six 12AX7 preamp tubes and four 6L6 output tubes.

Its distinctive low-frequency and high-frequency gain controls allowed musicians to adjust how different frequency ranges entered the distortion stages.

The Thrasher, Satan and RD Diavlo families marked Randall's expanded commitment to modern high-gain tube amplification.

2020s - Continuing evolution

Randall continues offering solid-state RG amplifiers alongside tube-powered RD and Thrasher models.

Its history illustrates how transistor, tube, modular and hybrid circuits can coexist, each providing different approaches to gain generation, frequency shaping and power amplification.

The accompanying amplifier illustrations are representative depictions, not authenticated production photographs.

Another week of heavy selling in tech. The Nasdaq lost 5.5%, the S&P 500 3.07% and the VIX jumped almost 35%, with CNN Fear & Greed back in extreme fear. 

The equal weight index and the Russell held up clearly better, with the equal weight index beating the cap weighted S&P by about 2%.

─────────────────

DOTCOM FRACTAL STATUS

There was a detailed update on Friday and the reading has not changed. The structures remain intact. With more structure added, especially in the Nasdaq, it looks as if the Nasdaq follows the 2007 structure in its final act, and the correction that began in the summer fits that structure on both the large and the small time frame. 

The chances are good that the correction is either already behind us or close to its end, which many do not expect. If the recovery that began on Friday continues early in the week, analysts will probably answer reflexively that it is only a dead cat bounce, as they did in April 2025 and again in April this year, which led to many misjudgments. One should still not be surprised if it goes lower once more.

https://t.co/I2eJtRMmld

The S&P also seems to follow the 2007 structure and has not gone as deep so far. The difference to 2007 is that the breadth only corrected then once the S&P began to sell off, while in this phase breadth started to correct much earlier without the index showing it. A large part of the correction has therefore already run hidden, and the index is now catching up.

https://t.co/2fLBrkQEke

The Russell gave back the whole recovery it had started and formed a lower low on Friday. 

The reading is unchanged. A bounce lies ahead, and the area between roughly 2,900 and 3,000 could be tested once more. A stronger move toward new all time highs is not ruled out, but technically much would have to happen first. For now the Russell has its top in, and after the bounce the correction should continue lower.

Energy lost 10.47% as oil fell almost 12%. For the last leg up to come, breadth probably has to return, because the momentum is out of semiconductors. A hard comeback there is possible, but the reading of the SOX makes it difficult, and a comeback in breadth is more likely.

Yields fell for the fourth week in a row, the 2 year most.  Oil dropped almost 12% on hopes for a peace deal after the midterms, while gold gained 4.84% and silver 5.61%, so among the commodities the precious metals are stronger than almost everything else this week.

CRYPTO

Ethereum: 2,238 | Weekly: −1.56%

Bitcoin has fallen for five weeks in a row and has bounced twice off the 50 week moving average that many watch. A weekly close below it would mean the bear market is not over and new lows are coming. 

At the same time the biggest names in the scene are speaking up again. They read the start of the correction in traditional markets as the beginning of the broad correction, as it often is around the midterms, expect crypto to be dragged down and see traditional markets finding their low only at the end of the year or early next year. Even so, crypto held up well against traditional markets, and Bitcoin against the S&P was almost unchanged on the week.

The core of the debate is the new cycle. One camp says the bottom is in and the new cycle has begun, the other says the bottom is not in yet and the new cycle starts afterwards. Why many indicators work less reliably than people are used to may simply come from the width of the cycle in traditional markets, in which crypto no longer experiences the cycle many expect. 

My reading is that this is only a bullish phase inside a bear market that has not ended, in which Bitcoin makes another corrective rally, as in the second half of 2021 or in 2025, while the altcoins complete the structures they could not finish at the end of 2025. 

That is why I look less at structures that build from scratch after a classic cycle bottom and more at those that follow a completed bull cycle, as after April 2021. A lot of the misunderstanding comes from thinking only in black and white.

─────────────────

RETAIL AND NARRATIVE MONITOR

Both monitors cover the week of October 25 to 31, so they do not yet reflect last week's selloff in equities or the further drop in Bitcoin. Interest among newcomers stays at the bottom. The crypto search score held at 1 for a second week, and with Bitcoin falling below 80,000 neither bargain hunters nor panic arrived. Bitcoin searches stand only 28% and Coinbase searches 20% above their five year lows, the equity score rose to 32 from 29, and Coinbase's third quarter shows monthly users at 7.4 million, 20% fewer than a year ago, with consumer spot volume down 59%.

https://t.co/MVaaBoZF5i

In the Narrative Monitor the bull share rose to 52% from 47%, above 50% for the first time since mid September, while searches for the four year cycle and for a bottom stay above 90% of all weeks since 2021. Most of that week's searches came before the drop below 80,000, so this week's data will show whether the crowd turned more cautious. A small, mostly unconvinced core and an absent public is still the picture, and the warning would come with a bull share above 60% and rising supercycle searches while retail stays away.

https://t.co/uDRC0wyj2V

─────────────────

CREDIT MONITOR

The broad junk bond market started to move. The high yield spread widened to 348 basis points, up 45 in a month and only 12 below the stressed trigger near 360, while BB bonds rose to 2.13% from a low of 1.50% in late August and CCC spreads held at 13.20%. The signal changed from DIVERGING to CONFIRMING, which is no relief, because with the S&P now 5.9% below its high, stocks have started to confirm what credit has signaled since late September. 

https://t.co/ZMAcIxPeEr

Stress concentration fell to 5.2, but only because BB is rising and not because CCC is falling, which is how stress began to spread in 2000 [Link]. A high yield spread above 360 basis points with BB holding above its recent range would turn the signal to STRESSED.

─────────────────

MIDTERMS

The midterms were one of the topics of the week. Democrats won the House by a wide margin and flipped the Senate, with seven Republican seats changing hands, and they did so in traditionally Republican states as well. In Texas, Democrats won both the Senate seat and the governorship, and voters cited high prices and the war in Iran. Stocks rallied on Wednesday, with the Dow having its best post-midterm day since 1982. 

On Thursday the Nasdaq fell 5.5% as fears grew that a Democratic Congress and states like Texas could tighten rules or even pause the buildout of AI data centers. I would not over-interpret this. It is not a fundamental reason, the market is looking for an explanation, and the sell off of the heavyweights was visible in the structure beforehand.

─────────────────

MACRO AND EARNINGS REVIEW

On Friday the October jobs report beat expectations clearly, with 165,000 jobs, unemployment at 4.1% and September revised higher. Expectations for a December hike rose, but the 10 year yield fell about 1.8% on the week and closed Friday only slightly higher, by roughly 0.5%, which I would not overweight. 

The reading fits, because yields would have reacted much more strongly if the market saw the jobs data as the core of the inflation problem, and Warsh has pointed out that the labor market is not the reason for inflation, so the reflex that strong data means a hike does not hit the core of it. As I laid out in my post on payrolls around the top, payrolls are no longer the best indicator of strength at the end of a cycle, and the level the market celebrates is low compared with earlier cycles.

https://t.co/rzZmczQSMF

Earnings continued with Apple, Palantir, AMD, Super Micro, Arista and Qualcomm. 

Apple earned 2.10 dollars per share on revenue of 114.5 billion, up 12%, and Palantir grew revenue 96% to 2.31 billion and raised its outlook, yet both fell after the reports before Apple reached a record high on Wednesday. AMD grew data center revenue 97% but free cash flow fell 64%, and the stock fell 17% on Thursday. Super Micro beat revenue by a wide margin and Arista rose 12% on guidance, while Qualcomm lost 9.5% on a weak outlook and Arm 13% despite 27% revenue growth. AppLovin jumped 31%. Expectations were mostly met or beaten, but the market now reacts to outlooks, margins and cash flow more than to the quarter just reported.

─────────────────

GEOPOLITICS

On Iran, markets are pricing in peace, with Brent down about 16% on the week, its biggest drop since 2020, as the midterm result raised hopes of de-escalation. Qatar submitted a 48 hour plan in which Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz and commit to nuclear talks. Neither side has formally accepted it, and Iran is reviewing it. Trump says the talks continue and a deal is still possible, yet the US struck an Iranian air defense system on Qeshm Island on Saturday for the second time in five days, and attacks on tankers continue. One energy analyst sees an 80% probability that fighting resumes.

In Russia and Ukraine, negotiators from both sides and the US meet on Tuesday in Abu Dhabi for a fourth round of talks. Ahead of it, Russia hit Kyiv and other regions with missiles and drones on Saturday, damaging networks that carry power from nuclear plants to Kyiv, while Ukraine struck industrial sites in Oryol. Zelensky says Moscow is stepping up the pressure before the talks.

─────────────────

THE WEEK AHEAD

October CPI follows on Tuesday, with consensus at 0.3% on the month after 0.6% in September, core at 0.2%, and a Cleveland Fed estimate of about 3.7% year over year. 

Producer prices follow on Friday, expected at 0.3% to 0.4% after 1.3% in September. CPI is the last inflation report before the Fed's December 9 meeting. 

It can come out hotter than expected, as the ISM prices component and energy prices suggested, but with yields lower the weight of the data should be a different one. 

CoreWeave reports on Tuesday and Cisco on Thursday.

─────────────────

BOTTOM LINE

The picture is interesting. Until early summer we saw very strong advances in the indices and in single stocks, and since the summer a correction has been running that is still not over. At the same time the rotation was in full swing. The indices looked strong while many sectors bled and were already in bear market territory weeks ago, and now the indices are catching up with what the weak breadth had shown. 

Tech gave up the most last week, while the equal weight index and the Russell held up comparatively well, and Bitcoin and Ethereum did too, despite the Binance hack more than a week ago and despite the selloff in tech. That shows the rotation is still under way.

Next to technical data, Fibonacci levels and support zones, the psychological side is often ignored. Many in traditional markets now call for a further correction, and big names have started to look at a fourth quarter bottom again, which is actually good for the market. In crypto the crowd will not be right. It looked at a fourth quarter bottom, watched the rally from the sidelines and now hopes it goes lower. The more big names say it will go much deeper because the indices are correcting, the more people take that narrative back up, and those on the sidelines will not start building positions now but wait, as so often, for the best possible entry, which is neither here nor at 72,000 but much lower.

Many compare today's structure with 2023, but psychologically there is a clear difference. The Retail Monitor and the Narrative Monitor both show interest at an extreme low. If this were the 2023 structure and the bottom were already in, it would meet a base that is far more uncertain than it was then, because at the same point in 2023 sentiment had already flipped clearly toward a bullish bias. The flip came quickly, the majority already assumed the bottom was in, and the structure held without forming a new low. 

Today many compare the structure but expect another leg down, while the flip has not happened yet. On the psychological timeline we are still behind the 2023 structure, and since that structure held with a better psychological base, it is hard to imagine that with less interest and no flip yet, much lower lows should follow now.

Whichever narrative is used, whether the election, the better jobs data or inflation, all of them point lower, which is exactly the kind of setting in which markets tend to turn. The market expects another hike in December and with it more pressure on risk assets, yet Treasuries have fallen since the end of September, and they may well have seen their top. In this phase the market does not move as rationally as many would like. The index surface has already corrected far more than the indices show, and Nasdaq and S&P seem to follow the 2007 structure in their final act, whose base in the years before was the same Dot-com fractal from 1996 to 2000. History does not repeat but rhymes, so the end phases can still run somewhat differently.

The current reading therefore strongly allows that we are already at the end of the correction or close to it, in traditional markets and in crypto. Psychologically the sentiment is perfect for a further rise. The rally in crypto was driven more by uncertainty and worry than by conviction, so declines fall on a base that never assumed it could go higher, and the altcoins, which are still bleeding and have given back most of the August move, offer the base from which further gains can start.

I stay with the picture of all the sequences we see, which recall 2000 and a combination with 2007, with several indices already having followed their Dot-com patterns and now in correction mode. We are in the last phase, and crypto will probably not experience a complete new spring in it, but a last rally before the final bell.

text:
PAYROLLS AROUND THE TOP | November 7, 2026
─────────────────

Friday's payroll report beat expectations, with 165,000 new jobs in October, and jobless claims came in better than expected too. The verdict was quick: the economy is strong. It is worth asking what strong used to look like.

In the year before the 2000 top, the US added 250,000 jobs a month. Before the 2007 top, 106,000. Over the last twelve months, 74,000. And the economy is bigger now. 

Applied to today's 159 million payroll jobs, the pace of 2000 would mean about 307,000 jobs a month, the pace of 2007 about 123,000. Today's job growth is a quarter of 2000 and a little over half of 2007.

─────────────────

The recent months did pick up, to 137,000 a month since August. That is no all clear. In March 2000, right at the top, the report showed 484,000 new jobs, partly census hiring, and the slide into recession began within a year.

The numbers themselves keep moving. August was first reported at 162,000 and now stands at 186,000. The benchmark revision in August erased 706,000 jobs, about 78% of the gains first reported for the year to March 2026. 

Near turning points, monthly payrolls are the least reliable data we have. 

A beat is measured against expectations that have been lowered for years.

Crypto × AI convergence is a long-term thesis—not protection against a selloff.

text:
India’s Future Tech Builders – Week 4
India has been writing software for the world for thirty years. But almost no Indian company has ever owned the silicon that software runs on. One Hyderabad firm is changing that — and it just built a chip for ISRO.

Let me tell you about MosChip Technologies (NSE: MOSCHIP).

This is not an assembly plant. This is not a packaging unit. This is the design layer — the place where a blank sheet of paper becomes a working chip. Fabless semiconductor design, ASIC and SoC engineering, turnkey silicon from netlist to packaged part.

Very few listed Indian companies do this. Almost none do it at scale.

Here is the breakdown.

What they are doing right
MosChip is a pure-play design house. Their work sits inside satellites, telecom networks, defence electronics, and AI systems. The track record is not a pitch deck — it is silicon in the field.

- ISRO’s navigation programme. In January 2026, MosChip delivered a custom 28nm SoC to ISRO’s Space Applications Centre. They handled everything — DFT architecture, physical design, package design, tester board design, post-silicon bring-up. Packaged silicon was validated and delivered. That is end-to-end accountability from design intent to working part.
- C-DAC’s 5nm HPC processor. MosChip is building India’s indigenous high-performance computing chip in 5nm technology, in collaboration with Socionext. It is progressing well and taping out soon. This is not a peripheral project. This is strategic national infrastructure.
- About 100 tape-outs in FY26. Legacy nodes, advanced nodes, across different fabs. Test chips, respins, derivative chips. That volume of tape-out activity is the clearest signal that the design engine is real.
- Two Fortune 500 wins. Project wins for the Product Engineering business from two companies in the top 50. And 12 new customers added across Australia, Europe, Japan, and South Korea.

The numbers for FY26 reflect that momentum. Revenue grew 25.3% to ₹585 crore. PBT rose to ₹41.6 crore. Revenue CAGR since FY22 is 41%.
Then Q1 FY27 happened. Revenue fell 14% year-on-year to ₹116 crore. PAT collapsed 78% to ₹2.45 crore. EBITDA margin narrowed to 10.15%.

Management’s explanation is specific, not vague. Certain turnkey ASIC engagements reached the tape-out stage during the quarter, where revenue recognition shifts to later milestones. And the Product Engineering Services business saw a longer order conversion cycle.

That is the nature of this business. Turnkey silicon is milestone-linked. Revenue is lumpy by design. One quarter’s miss does not invalidate a three-year tape-out record. But it does demand scrutiny.

What is going in their favour
The structural wind is not a cycle. It is a reordering of the global chip supply chain.

India’s semiconductor mission needs design, not just fabs. The India Semiconductor Mission has committed billions to fabrication and packaging. But chips do not begin in a fab. They begin in a design centre. MosChip is one of the very few listed Indian companies that sits at that layer. When the government wants indigenous silicon — for defence, space, or strategic computing — MosChip is a natural partner.

The DLI scheme is a direct pipeline. MosChip’s VIDYUT smart energy meter IC was developed under the Design Linked Incentive scheme, taped out, and is back in the lab with promising bring-up results.This is not a subsidy story. It is a product story. A chip designed in India, for Indian infrastructure, with government support to cross the valley of death.

Global design work is shifting to India. The company added customers in Australia, Europe, Japan, and South Korea in a single year. With 10 of the world’s top 20 semiconductor firms already as clients, MosChip is a direct play on design reshoring — not just cost arbitrage, but capability arbitrage.
The balance sheet supports the ambition. Net worth is around ₹409 crore. Reliance on external debt is low. The fabless model is asset-light, so capex requirements are limited. CRISIL has the rating on watch positive.

How they can prove they are the company of the future
A tape-out record is a credential. A product business is a company.

They need to prove that VIDYUT becomes a commercial chip, not just a lab success. The smart meter market in India is enormous. If MosChip can supply the IC that sits inside those meters, that is a repeatable product revenue line — something the company has not had at scale.

They need to prove that the C-DAC 5nm HPC programme converts into milestone payments and follow-on work. It is the most visible strategic project in their portfolio. Delivering it cements their position as India’s go-to partner for advanced-node design.

They need to prove that the Vayavya Labs acquisition closes and integrates. Vayavya brings embedded systems capability, marquee customers, and a higher-margin business model. CRISIL explicitly flags the acquisition as a rating sensitivity. If it closes, MosChip’s addressable market expands. If it stalls, the growth narrative loses a leg.
If they pull these off, they are not just a design services vendor. They become India’s first vertically capable fabless semiconductor company — owning IP, designing silicon, and delivering packaged parts to strategic customers.

Where they need to be careful
Here is where I get uncomfortable.

The Q1 FY27 collapse is not a one-off data point. The December 2025 quarter also saw profit fall sharply. One weak quarter is timing. Two is a pattern. Management needs to show that the PES order conversion cycle has actually shortened, not just that it will.

Margins are compressing. Operating profitability moderated to 10.2% in FY26 from 12% in FY25. In Q1 FY27 it fell to 8.2%. The reasons are legitimate — workforce expansion, training, AI capability building, lower utilisation. But investment without revenue cover erodes the buffer.

Turnkey revenue is inherently lumpy. The same milestone structure that delayed Q1 revenue will delay revenue again. Investors need to underwrite a business where a single large project’s timing can swing a quarter. That is not a flaw in MosChip. It is the nature of the model. But it requires a different lens than a steady-state product company.
The Vayavya acquisition carries legal uncertainty. The Supreme Court status quo order delayed the transaction. Additional security of ₹200 crore was directed. MosChip says it has no financial impact, and due diligence is expected to conclude in the coming months. But until it closes, the synergy story is a promise, not a number.

Who they are actually competing with
This is not a crowded listed universe. That is part of the appeal. But the competition is real, and it comes in different shapes.

eInfochips (Arrow Electronics) is the largest Indian heritage design services player, now backed by a global distributor. They operate at a scale MosChip is still building towards, with deep customer relationships across embedded and silicon engineering.

Wipro and Cyient run large engineering R&D practices that include semiconductor design. They have balance sheets and global delivery networks that a mid-cap cannot match. But design is one service line among many for them. For MosChip, it is the entire company.

Tata Elxsi is the premium engineering services brand, with strong automotive and media exposure. They are not a pure silicon play, but they compete for the same engineering talent and the same large-account relationships.

Global design houses and captive centres are the structural competitor. Every major semiconductor company has an India centre. MosChip’s edge is not cost. It is single-owner accountability — netlist to packaged silicon, one team responsible for the outcome. That is a specific value proposition that captive centres and staff-augmentation firms do not offer.

Kaynes Technology and CG Power appear in the same “Indian semiconductor” basket, but they operate at different layers. Kaynes is OSAT and EMS. CG Power is moving into packaging. They are ecosystem partners, not direct competitors in design.

How they can leave the competition behind
MosChip cannot outspend Wipro. It cannot outscale eInfochips overnight. So it has to win on a different axis.

Own the “netlist to silicon” promise completely. The ISRO delivery proves they can take a design from intent to validated packaged part. Very few Indian companies can credibly make that claim. Every marketing rupee, every business development conversation, every hire should reinforce that positioning. Do not drift into staff augmentation. Compete on outcome, not headcount.

Win the strategic silicon programmes before anyone else builds the muscle. ISRO, C-DAC, defence PSUs. These are long-cycle, high-barrier engagements. Once you are the design partner on a 5nm HPC processor or a navigation SoC, you are inside the tent. The next programme follows. This is how you build a moat that a larger services firm cannot easily replicate.

Use Vayavya to move up the stack. Embedded systems capability plus silicon design capability equals a fuller solution. If the acquisition closes, integrate it fast and cross-sell. Do not run it as a separate island.

Turn VIDYUT into a product beachhead. A chip designed for Indian smart meters, backed by the DLI scheme, is not just a project. It is a template. If it works commercially, the next product can be designed for a different Indian infrastructure vertical — power, rail, telecom. Product revenue is the difference between a services multiple and a semiconductor multiple.

The path I hope they take: Prove the product, then scale the platform
I would not say stop investing in capability. I would say sequence the proof.
Make VIDYUT commercially real. Make the C-DAC milestones visible. Close Vayavya and show the embedded synergy in numbers. Then use that credibility to win more strategic silicon programmes.

The design services business funds the product ambition. The product ambition is what changes the valuation. Do not let the ambition outrun the proof.

Final thought
MosChip is at an inflection point. They proved an Indian fabless company can deliver a custom SoC to ISRO and tape out a 5nm processor for C-DAC. They proved they can add customers across four new geographies in a year. Now they need to prove they can convert that engineering credibility into durable, less lumpy earnings.

If VIDYUT sells and Vayavya integrates, this becomes a serious semiconductor product story. If Q1 becomes a trend, the market will stop paying for the promise.

I am watching the VIDYUT commercial rollout and the Vayavya closure very closely. You should too.

Follow @WallStreet2Web3  for more honest case studies on Indian companies.

Do your own due diligence before investing. Pure-play semiconductor design in India is still a small-cap niche, and design-services businesses can be cyclical.

text:
Discover What the Open Source X Code Just Changed👇
X just quietly shifted the open source ranking code on Nov 5 and early likes plus real reading time now carry more weight than they did a week ago. I check the repo so you do not have to.

The ranking model does not simply reward “engagement.” 
Instead, it estimates the probability that a specific viewer will perform specific actions. The ranking logic is essentially: Score = sum of (weight × probability of each predicted action).

In plain English: you do not optimize for generic engagement. You optimize for specific positive actions while avoiding the negative ones, because negative actions reduce your score.

Here is exactly what moved in home-mixer/params/param.rs:

- Likes climbed from 0.66 to 0.708, the highest public value yet
- Continuous time spent on a post rose from 0.006 to 0.0075
- A plain tap into the post fell from 0.3 to 0.274
- Staying 10+ seconds after that tap eased from 0.4 to 0.385
- Opening a video dropped from 0.02 all the way to 0
- Regular share ticked up from 2 to 2.118
- “Not interested” grew harsher from -52.27 to -53.07

These signals kept the exact same weights they already had:

- Copy-link shares (still the single biggest positive signal at 20)
- Replies (still 5, or higher when it is a mutual follow)
- Quotes (still 5)
- DM shares (still 5)
- Follows from a post (still 4)

X offered no explanation for any of the changes. The numbers are simply what the live defaults now say.

A month ago a like was only 0.5. Time spent sat at 0.004. Every successive change has pointed the same direction: the system pays more for people who stay and engage than for those who merely glance.

If you are small this is the lever you can still pull. You will not out-volume large accounts, but the people who already see your post can now move the needle harder when they like it and finish reading. Those early likes still decide which new posts receive the extra push in the first two hours and first 200 views.

Video open itself is now worthless. The system appears to care more about whether viewers keep watching after they open. Make the first seconds count. Your profile is also being scored for how long people remain after they tap it, so treat the pinned post and bio as part of the ranking surface.

One more detail from the code that most people miss:

The open-source code runs an AI check on replies under accounts with roughly 250k+ followers. One of the flags it can apply is literally named “llm slop.” If your reply gets that label, it can be blocked from the original poster’s notifications unless they already follow you. The label can last 14 to 30 days. Grey-badge and high-credibility accounts are exempt. Small accounts are not. In short: do not paste Grok, ChatGPT, or Claude-style replies under large accounts if you want them to reach the person.

The system also detects near-identical replies. When it marks a reply as a duplicate or copypasta, that reply is suppressed from notifications. This covers both obvious copy-paste spam and lightly edited AI replies that still look the same. Writing each reply in your own words avoids the flag.

Both rules exist in the public code to cut low-effort and AI-generated reply spam under high-visibility posts.

What still holds:
- New posts still receive their initial boost in the first two hours and first 200 views
- The single largest positive number remains 20 for someone copying your link
- Mutual back-and-forth is still heavily rewarded
- Originals from accounts under 50k can still surface higher when early viewers like them

What keeps costing you:
- Pasting AI replies under big accounts
- Copy-paste replies that trigger the duplicate label
- Chasing the tap instead of the stay and the like
- Off-topic posts that draw “not interested”
- Publishing when your people are asleep and wasting the two-hour window
- Adult media in three of your last five posts, low-quality or misinfo labels, engagement bait, hashtag stuffing, or stacking replies under one large post
- Not Interested: a user explicitly selecting “Not Interested” on your post
- Block Author: a user blocking your account
- Mute Author: a user muting your account
- Report: a user reporting your post or account
- Not Dwelled: a user scrolling past your post without stopping

I have watched these weights climb for likes and dwell while pure clicks keep sliding. The code is telling us the same thing every week: stop optimizing for the glance. Write posts people finish and like. Reply in your own voice. Protect the first two hours.

Receipts live in the public repo. The rest is just reading what the numbers already say.

text:
Rocky 50th Anniversary Fact of the Day: Carrie Snodgress

According to Sly's Official Rocky Scrapbook (1977) and other source material, actress Carrie Snodgress (1945-2004) was the original choice to play Adrian in Rocky. She was formally offered the part.

Stallone was even in the process of rewriting Adrian from Jewish descent to Irish-American.  However,  Snodgress' agent told her to hold out for more money. 

The producers held firm -- the $1M nax budget was not flexible. The search for Adrian went on, until Talia Shire aced her audition. 

The Official Rocky Scrapbook goes into some details about the process.  Stallone wrote that Talia was the physical opposite of how he initially pictured Adrian.  But her audition changed his mind immediately. 

In "The Steps", Carrie Snodgress isn't mentioned at all. Perhaps it's because her name and career aren't widely remembered anymore. 

Sly now writes that Talia was his exact mental picture of Adrian  -- a 100% contradiction of his first book about the film.

At any rate, the process from early drafts to the Carrie Snodgress offer to hiring Talia is how Adrian Klein evolved into Adrian Penino and from Jewish to Irish to Italian.

text:
Researchers in Japan have taken an encouraging step towards plastics that leave a shorter legacy in the ocean: building enzymes into compostable polyester films to help them break down even on the deep-sea floor.

The team embedded cutinase, an enzyme that uses water to split chemical bonds in polyester chains. Working from within the material, it helps release smaller, water-soluble molecules that microorganisms may then metabolize—a different strategy from treating plastic already in the ocean.

In a five-month field experiment off Japan, 757 metres below the surface, thin films of three compostable polyesters—PBS, PBSA and PCL—with 3% embedded cutinase lost nearly all their measured mass. Matching enzyme-free films showed little mass loss.

That measures the loss of material from the films, not complete conversion into harmless end products on the seabed. A separate laboratory test using coastal seawater supported a further biological step: enzyme-containing PBS reached about 51% of its theoretical oxygen demand in a month, consistent with partial microbial mineralization.

This work offers a promising design direction for less persistent materials: give selected plastics a built-in route to breakdown, rather than relying entirely on the environment to do the work.

text:
🌺 Remembrance Sunday morning weather update for Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly. 🌺

Good morning, everyone,

First, on this Remembrance Sunday, we take a moment to remember all those who gave their lives for our freedom, those who served, and those who never returned home.

We will remember the Lest We Forget. 

Now, onto our Sunday weather, and the good news is that it's not looking too bad at all!

Sunday morning 🌤️

It's another fairly chilly start for parts of Cornwall, with temperatures ranging from around 3°C to 12°C. Some sheltered inland locations could have a touch of frost, along with a few mist and fog patches.

But there's some lovely autumnal sunshine on offer, with blue skies and varying amounts of cloud. Of course, knowing Cornwall, one village will be enjoying the sunshine while the next is wondering where somebody has hidden it!

Winds will turn from southwesterly to southeasterly, generally around 0–25 mph.

Sunday afternoon 

Much of Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly should enjoy a mainly dry afternoon, with sunny spells and some cloud hanging around.

Temperatures will reach around 9°C to 14°C, so not too bad for November! A reasonable afternoon for a coastal walk, although do take care around exposed coastal areas.

Sunday evening and overnight 🌙

From around 5–6pm, cloud will gradually increase from the southwest, and by around 9pm, much of Cornwall could be underneath a blanket of cloud.

Evening temperatures will range from around 5°C to 12°C, with the increasing cloud helping to prevent temperatures from falling too sharply overnight.

And what about next week? 

Well, our relatively quiet November weather could be coming to an end!

High pressure is gradually losing its grip, allowing Atlantic low pressure to influence our weather.

Monday should start mainly dry with some brighter spells, but showers could arrive later in the day. Temperatures will be around 11–14°C.

Tuesday and Wednesday could bring spells of rain, possibly heavy at times, along with some stronger winds.

Towards Thursday and Friday, there's also a possibility of colder northerly winds developing as high pressure builds to the northwest of Britain.
There's still some uncertainty, so we'll be watching the weather models closely. No need to panic-buy the snow shovels just yet! 

🐾 Smudge and Gus weather verdict

Smudge says Sunday gets four paws for some lovely window sunshine!

Gus has heard about the colder winds later next week and has already booked himself a permanent place beside the radiator. Preferably with room service! 

Wherever you are across Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly today, especially if you're attending a Remembrance Sunday service or parade, wrap up warm and take care.

Have a peaceful Remembrance Sunday, everyone.

🌺 Lest We Forget.

Kind regards,
KWT Dave

One should never use only a single wick for a lamp. A lamp with a single wick is lit only in the presence of a deceased person; it symbolizes the soul merging into the Supreme Divine (Paramatma). Steel lamps (diyas) should never be used for *deeparadhana* (ritual lighting of lamps). A single-wick lamp is often lit before a deceased person, signifying that the soul has merged with the Supreme Being. One should not use a matchstick to light a lamp; instead, use an incense stick (*agarbatti*). If the lamp happens to go out, one should chant "Om Namah Shivaya" 108 times before relighting it; doing so prevents any untoward consequences.

After the *deeparadhana*, it is auspicious to apply *kumkum* (vermilion) in three places and offer *akshitas* (sacred unbroken rice grains). In a home where a lamp is kept lit from sunset until sunrise, poverty cannot reside. When preparing for *deeparadhana*, always pour the oil first, and then place the wicks.

FIRST SUNDAY IN CAMP ☀️😇💃

Happy Sunday, Corps Members! 😁

One beautiful thing about Sundays in camp is that you get to enjoy a little break from the usual military routine. You won't hear the morning bugle until later in the evening, usually around 4 PM. 💃

From morning until about 2 PM, you are generally free to wear casual clothes, attend church ⛪ or mosque 🕌, or relax in your hostel. However, some camps may still require everyone to wear their white-on-white outfit throughout the day. So, follow your camp's rules. 😂

After 2 PM or 3 PM, it's time to return to your familiar white-on-white uniform.

NOW, LET'S TALK ABOUT TODAY'S LUNCH! 🍗🍚

Today's menu in many camps is Jollof rice and chicken! Yes, you read that correctly. Jollof rice and chicken! 😁

Even if you have been avoiding camp food since arrival, today might be worth making an exception. 😂

Here's a little tip: Some of your platoon members, roommates or bunkmates may decide to eat at Mami Market instead of collecting their camp meals. If they willingly offer you their unused meal tickets, you can help them collect their meals.

Just make sure you have permission, follow the camp's meal collection rules and don't take anyone's ticket without consent.

You can also keep some food for dinner if you have more than enough. And please, remember to save some drinking water for later. 😂

Enjoy your first Sunday in camp. Relax, eat well and make beautiful memories!

Stay cool and enjoy camp life! ❤️

text:
Part2 Taipei Stage Greeting report
#追蹤者遊戲W水魚交融 
#チェイサーゲームW水魚の交わり 
#中村ゆりか #台湾
Paraphrased translation, so there might be some errors. (Yurika gave a lot of insightful answers about her approach to portraying Fuyu, the scene, as well as her process of incorporating music into the story)

----------------------
MC:
Matsuyama-sensei, as the original creator, what do you think is the most important thing when it comes to maintaining a long-lasting relationship?
Matsuyama:
Including the cast, staff, director, producers, and everyone involved in filming, there are so many people fulfilling different roles. But I think what's important is for everyone to understand one another.
(Then he suddenly changed the topic to talk about Yurika's love for manga!??)
Matsuyama:
I heard something surprising earlier. Apparently, you really like manga! This happened in Tokyo, right? Earlier, when I heard you were going to a manga café, I thought, "Nakamura Yurika goes to manga cafés?!" And you actually went there and read manga, right?
🌙:
That's right! I really like manga, and I often read it at home, too. But I never want to throw it away. I keep collecting it, and my home gets completely packed! Libraries and manga cafés are wonderful. Being able to read so much there reminded me what great places they are.
Matsuyama:
I can understand a library, but there are ordinary customers in manga cafés! You just walked in? In Tokyo?
🌙:
Yes, in Tokyo.
Matsuyama:
In Tokyo?! That's just wow!
By the way, do you have manga cafés like that in Taiwan? (The audience said yes.) She was right there in the open area of the manga café! Pretty unbelievable, right?
🌙:
When I was little, I used to play computer games there. Do you know Bomberman? I was really into it as a child. Going there brought back those memories. As an adult, I want to revisit places that feel nostalgic.
Matsuyama:
So it comes with a computer, and normally you get a private booth, right?
🌙:
But I was in the café lounge.
Matsuyama:
Why?! That's risky! Everyone could see you! In Japan, the computer rooms are completely private. You can even lock the door from the inside. I was surprised you sat in an open area. You chose the open lounge instead of a private, lockable booth!

----------------------
MC:
Matsuyama-sensei, what different emotions does the live-action film offer compared with the manga?
Matsuyama:
Manga often simplifies what it shows. Live action can convey a much greater amount of information. Take the argument near the end. You can really feel the intensity. Even watching it makes your heart race. That's unique to live action. What was filming that argument like?
🌙:
Until just before filming, there was no part where we went up the stairs from the living room. Maybe we were so overwhelmed that our bodies naturally wanted to act or move around. I remember it being the director's request. Adding that movement made the scene easier to perform. Their emotions were focused on one thing: pushing their own wishes and desires onto each other, without room to consider the other person. You could see how overwhelmed they both were.

-----------------
MC:
You also performed the song "Aishiteru" yourself. How do you feel this song captures the emotional journey between Fuyu and Itsuki in the film?
🌙:
"Aishiteru" is not just about liking someone. It is about love deepening as you spend more time together. The longer you are together, the more accustomed you become to each other. The precious things beneath that familiarity can fade from view. But the song is about gently embracing even those parts and moving forward together. It portrays what lies beyond the love the two already share. I hope that as people watch the film and hear the song, they find something that resonates with their own experiences.
Matsuyama:
I'm curious about the timing of the song's production. There was the songwriting, composing, and then recording the vocals. By the time all of that happened, had you already received the script and finished filming?
🌙:
The movie was filmed during the summer, right? It was during the summer, but I felt like the song was coming together while we were still filming.
Matsuyama:
So initially, you only had the script to work with, and you were developing the lyrics and the overall image of the song based on that?
🌙:
Yes, at one point, we also involved the director on set and discussed things like, "Is this the right way to convey the message? Does the order of the lyrics work?" with the producer…

--------------------
MC:
Which scene in the whole work moved you the most, or which was your favorite?
Matsuyama:
As I mentioned earlier, the scene with water being poured over the (Fuyu's) head was one of my favorites. When Fuyu was at the DD office, Nakamura-san was mostly filming alone, right? Was it all done in a day? We reserved two weeks, but only filmed for nine days.
🌙:
It was pretty hectic, especially with all the dialogue. It reminded me how difficult filming a drama is.
Matsuyama:
So many people coordinate schedules and prepare everything. Honestly, you spend more time waiting than shooting. Filming itself can be over quickly, but the hours on set are long. That's a little behind-the-scenes story. A scene may look brief on screen, but it can take an enormous amount of time to shoot.
🌙:
It's almost like a factory! The staff worked so hard, too. Even while rubbing their sleepy eyes, they kept going, holding their cameras and doing their best. Through the camera lens, they were able to capture the characters' emotional shifts and even the most delicate, subtle expressions. I think that's something only this team could have done. We've worked together for so long that we've become comfortable with one another. We could open up to each other, and there was a strong sense of trust between us. Watching the finished film made me realize once again that this was a work made possible because of that trust. You really can't fake those things, can you?

----------------
Question from an audience member: (Asked in Mandarin)What have you eaten since coming to Taiwan?
Matsuyama-shachou asked for recommendations for food that provides a balanced diet.
Fans: Medicinal hotpot, stinky tofu...
Yurika said she ate a bit of this and a bit of that backstage during yesterday's live, including soup, braised pork rice, hotpot, and xiaolongbao. The hotpot was divided into two halves, one spicy and one regular.

text:
Arteta may have found another solution to Arsenal's midfield problem: Bruno Guimarães.

His second-half performance against Hull City was outstanding. Once Declan Rice came off, Bruno took control of the midfield. He carried the ball, broke opposition lines with his passing and started dictating the tempo.

What caught my attention was the difference between his first-half influence and his performance after the break. He looked like a completely different midfielder.

I want Arteta to consider giving Bruno more responsibility as Rice's deputy. We have Zubimendi, Merino and Myles Lewis-Skelly, but Bruno offers the aggression, technical quality and forward passing needed to unlock stubborn low blocks.

I also believe he benefits from playing alongside Rice because he doesn't have to shoulder the entire midfield responsibility himself.

Let's be honest, most of Arsenal's players were frustrating in the first half, with Noni Madueke being a notable exception. But the team raised its level after the 65th minute, and Bruno was central to that improvement.

This is the Bruno Guimarães Arsenal need. Low blocks, beware!

text:
🎥 ECPS Interview / VIDEO

🇷🇸 Prof. Nebojša Vladisavljević: Serbia’s Student Movement Represents Democratic Renewal, Not Another Wave of Populism

✍️ Interview by Selcuk Gultasli

⁉️ Can a grassroots democratic movement dismantle competitive authoritarianism without reproducing the exclusionary politics and concentration of power it seeks to overcome?

📺 Watch the ECPS video interview with Professor Nebojša Vladisavljević of the University of Belgrade, who examines Serbia’s historic student-led electoral breakthrough and its broader implications for populism, authoritarian resilience, and democratic transformation.

⚡ Following nearly two years of nationwide protests, the October 25, 2026, electoral defeat of Aleksandar Vučić’s ruling coalition opened a new chapter in Serbia’s political history. But does the fall of an entrenched authoritarian government necessarily signal the beginning of democratic consolidation?

🔎 Key themes explored in the video interview:

✊ Democratic Renewal Beyond Populism: Professor Vladisavljević challenges interpretations of the Students’ List as another expression of anti-establishment populism, highlighting its commitment to political pluralism, inclusive citizenship, and constitutional accountability.

🏛️ The Paradox of Competitive Authoritarianism: How electoral manipulation, institutional abuse, and restrictions on political freedoms can generate grievances that ultimately strengthen popular resistance against authoritarian incumbents.

🗳️ From Street Protests to Parliamentary Victory: How student organizations, civil society networks, independent journalism, and citizen-led election monitoring helped convert sustained democratic mobilization into electoral success.

🤝 Overcoming Ethnonational Divisions: Why cooperation between Serbian and Bosniak students offers important lessons about minority inclusion, civic solidarity, and bottom-up democratic integration.

⚖️ The Difficult Road to Democratic Consolidation: Why electoral victory alone cannot dismantle entrenched clientelism, restore judicial independence, reform security institutions, or guarantee accountable government.

🌍 Comparative Lessons for Democratic Resistance: What Serbia’s experience reveals about the possibilities and limitations of challenging competitive authoritarianism in Turkey, Georgia, Hungary, and beyond.

💬 “I wouldn’t describe this as an anti-establishment mobilization. The target was Vučić’s authoritarian, personalist rule.”

🚨 Professor Vladisavljević also cautions against equating regime change with democratic consolidation:

💬 “Short-term efforts obviously won’t be sufficient.”

🎬 Watch the video interview for a scholarly examination of one of the most consequential questions confronting contemporary democracies: 🔗 https://t.co/JVypJfuwAJ

5 AM Top-of-the-Hour News

Republican Congresswoman Lauren Boebert's race with Democrat Eileen Laubacher is still undecided in Colorado. NewsNation's Miyoshi Price reports Boebert's camp is getting ready for a recount (OC: ): “In a statement, her attorney says in part, we are investigating some very unusual voting patterns and expect this election to head to a recount one way or another. In Colorado, the state automatically does a recount when the difference is less than 0.5%. Otherwise it costs the candidate who wants to recount big bucks. Bobert supporters are already getting emails asking for donations to fund a potential recount. ”
A recount could cost a candidate up to 100-thousand dollars.

UFC CEO Dana White says he's heading to Washington, D.C., to meet with President Trump on Monday after the president offered him the White House press secretary job,
Trump made the announcement on social media, praising White as "a violent Fighter and Warrior."
Speaking to reporters after a boxing event in London, White responded to the offer:: “I'm flying to Washington DC right now. I'm going to meet with him. We have a meeting on Monday, so I'm sure I'll have more to talk about after that. ”
White has not confirmed whether he plans to accept the offer, leaving questions about his next move.

A North Carolina man said his wife used ChatGPT to carry out an attempted murder plot against him, according to a lawsuit filed Thursday against San Francisco-based OpenAI.: “I found a handwritten note that my wife had made clear all convos clear all conversations log out of chat GPT, and then below that was basically a detailed plan of how to poison, incapacitate, lethally inject, um, and then do physical destruction. ”
James Gates survived his wife’s alleged murder attempt last year "after ChatGPT fueled her delusions about him and crafted a personalized plan to help her poison him," attorneys representing Gates wrote.: “From the onset, I knew, I knew Chad GBT was had something to do with it, but I didn't know at the time. You know to what extent there were Thousands of conversations over months. ”
Gate's wife was charged with attempted murder in 2025, but prosecutors later dropped the case.

Four people are dead, including two children, as authorities in Wisconsin investigate a grisly scene.
Police responding to a 9-1-1 call, found four deceased individuals: an adult female, a male child, a female child, and an adult male.
A second female child who was also inside the residence, was transported to a local hospital for medical treatment. Her current condition is unknown.
Officers also reported finding a deceased dog inside the home.
A firearm believed to have been involved in the incident was recovered at the scene.
The investigation is ongoing.

No. 11 Notre Dame withstood a late charge from Miami to knock off the undefeated No. 1 team in the country and cement its College Football Playoff resume.
Miami wide receiver Elijah Lofton nearly had an unbelievable play to tie the game, but he ultimately was unable to hold onto the ball in the corner of the end zone with 3:36 remaining.: “First, Notre Dame. Down there. Football knocked out there and it is in fact incomplete. ”
The win is the first over a top 16 team over the past two years; the Fighting Irish were previous 0-3 against such opponents.

The Heritage Foundation last week ousted one of their top longtime scholars, Robert Rector.
The intellectual architect of welfare reform, Rector had challenged Heritage President Kevin Roberts last year for his defense of Tucker Carlson.
Rector had been with Heritage since 1984. He is most famous in conservative intellectual circles for playing a major role in crafting the 1996 welfare reform law signed by former President Bill Clinton.

A new study says two "forever chemicals" have been tied to a more deadly form of breast cancer.
Researchers reported in the Journal of Clinical Oncology that women with higher blood levels of the two common forever chemical substances are more likely to develop a harder to treat type of breast cancer.
Researchers found they had a 67 to 93 percent increased risk of ER-negative breast cancer.

In my journey through life I have discovered that tactical honesty serves as a gentle guide when facing difficult conversations with family or friends allowing me to speak truth without causing harm by selecting the right moment and words carefully so that understanding grows instead of resentment this practice has become second nature to me as I reflect on past moments where rushing into blunt statements led to unnecessary pain yet pausing to consider the impact always brought better results fostering deeper connections that last through challenges and joys alike over time this method feels like a quiet strength I carry daily helping me navigate uncertainties with calm assurance.

Honesty always remains at the core of my interactions because without it trust erodes slowly like sand beneath waves leaving only doubt in its place I recall times when I withheld small truths thinking they were harmless but they accumulated into barriers that took effort to dismantle now I choose openness consistently knowing it builds a foundation for everything else in my relationships and personal growth this constant commitment brings a sense of peace as I wake each morning ready to engage authentically with the world around me.

It always needs a thoughtful approach to balance directness with kindness so that the message lands softly yet clearly in the hearts of those I care about I have seen how this balance prevents misunderstandings and encourages mutual respect in my daily exchanges from work discussions to heartfelt talks at home the need for such care becomes evident when emotions run high and a single misstep could widen gaps instead of closing them.

Karma to form positive cycles in return because the energy I put out through honest exchanges comes back multiplied in unexpected ways that enrich my existence I notice this in the support I receive during tough periods which mirrors the support I offered earlier creating a loop of goodwill that sustains me emotionally and spiritually as years pass this awareness deepens my appreciation for how actions ripple outward.

To form bonds that withstand time and trials I focus on consistency in my words and deeds allowing love to emerge naturally without force or expectation this process feels organic like a seed growing into a sturdy tree providing shade for all involved in my circle of loved ones the act of forming these ties brings fulfillment as I witness them evolve into sources of comfort and inspiration.

Unconditional love arises when honesty meets patience and understanding turning ordinary moments into profound connections that do not demand perfection but celebrate presence I cherish how this love manifests in quiet gestures and shared silences that speak volumes more than words ever could in my experience it requires no conditions or proofs simply an open heart ready to accept and give freely regardless of circumstances.

Love becomes the ultimate reward for embracing these principles in my life filling each day with gratitude for the paths chosen and the lessons learned along the way as I look back I feel thankful for every instance where tactical honesty paved the way to stronger unconditional bonds that continue to shape my world in gentle meaningful ways this reflection leaves me content and hopeful for the future ahead.

2/ Scheduled Departure

Dan used to wake up, walk out to a freezing car, sit on a frozen seat, and wait for the windshield to clear.

Scheduled Departure fixes all of it.

You tell the car what time you leave. It works backward from there. It finishes charging just in time, which also lets you take advantage of cheaper off-peak electricity rates if your utility offers them. Then it warms or cools the cabin right before you walk out, so you step into a perfect temperature.

Same car. Same house. Completely different mornings.

You can set it per location, so home and work can have different rules. Most people set it once and forget it exists, which is exactly the point.

text:
My second crisis hit along with many other rational people in February 2022.

You wake up one morning and realize the country where you were born, raised, built a family, and ran a business has become a rogue state. On a moral level, you have nothing in common with that same 80 to 90% of the population. It is technically your homeland, but it has turned into complete alien territory.

There is a line in a famous Russian rock song: "She might not be pretty, but we love her anyway." For me, it became the exact opposite: she looks fine on the surface, but underneath, she is rotten. I realized I could not and would not pay taxes to a system that burns that money on artillery shells and bombs to kill people in Ukraine, with whom we share deep personal and cultural ties.

For nearly two years, I could barely work. I felt sick to my stomach. What made it worse was that many clients saw nothing wrong at all. They celebrated the exit of Western brands, cheered for a window of opportunity, and convinced themselves that economic isolation would bring a domestic boom.

The years 2022 and 2023 forced a brutal audit of everything: the market, my clients, and myself. I had to face the fact that I had been naive, ignoring clear red flags that had been waving since 2014, 2016, and 2019. It turned into a raw, fundamental dilemma: what side of history are you standing on, and can you live with your own conscience? I cut ties with numerous clients purely on moral grounds. The best-case outlook for Russia looked like a northern version of Iran: forced dogma, cultural stagnation, a cordoned-off intranet, and monopoly rule.

I was ready to leave marketing for good. Modern technology pulled me back.

For a few projects, I started diving into neural networks, brushing up on math and statistics, writing scripts, and picking up no-code development. I looked at the Western market: what CRM platforms they rely on, how they structure pipeline architecture, and what automation stacks they run. It clicked. I saw an active, scalable, constructive market. Sure, it comes with cultural, linguistic, and regulatory barriers, but it offers room for real systems engineering instead of endless smoke and mirrors.

The second wave of clarity hit toward late 2024, when the storm became undeniable even to die-hard optimists back home. Old clients started reaching out again cautiously. It became obvious that three days had failed, three years had failed too, and a deep crisis was closing in.

By 2025, former clients came knocking in waves, but there was nowhere left to return. The domestic internet had turned into a suffocating, state-run walled garden choked with bots and state-funded vanity budgets. I told business owners straight up: "Forget the domestic market. There are zero fundamentals for growth here for the next ten years, even if the conflict stops tomorrow. Look broader: Central Asia, Kazakhstan, Mongolia. Look at Chinese manufacturers: they supply the CIS, India, and Africa out of a single plant. Why can't you?"

I began translating Western B2B playbooks, such as systematic cold email outreach, multi-agent AI workflows, and complex automation sequences, to heavy industrial companies. The contrast was staggering.

Businesses that were fundamentally sound and had capital immediately jumped at the chance to tap international channels. They signed off on solid budgets and paid proper fees without hesitation. Meanwhile, cash-strapped businesses kept nickel-and-diming over pennies and demanding miracles.

That was when my biggest historical mistake hit me: for years, I had been working with bottom-feeders. I poured hard-earned skills into clients who simply were not worth the investment. If a founder runs on wishful thinking and bad management, no head of marketing will ever save that ship.
