text:
My first severe burnout hit me back in 2018. It was not just routine fatigue, but a fundamental disillusionment with the market.

It started with conversations with peers, owners of marketing agencies in my home million-plus city. I looked inside their operations and was appalled. About 80 to 90% of it was outright theater: inflated rankings, fake traffic, painted reports. Nobody was even trying to deliver actual business results. People were just cynically monetizing the client's lack of competence.

It got under my skin so much that I decided to run an experiment and test this model myself. I took on a client and basically fed him lines for a year, manufacturing the illusion of progress. I stacked every dollar he paid me into a separate pile. I was convinced that after a couple of months he would snap out of it and say: "Man, this is pure garbage," and I would silently hand back every single cent.

A year passed. He never snapped out of it.

When I got tired of playing along with the circus, I told him I was terminating the contract. In response, he called repeatedly, practically begging me to keep going. The man was asking me to keep taking his money for doing absolutely nothing.

That broke me completely. I realized an ugly truth: this unethical imitation model works flawlessly. In regional small business, it covers 90% of the market. The client does not want to dig into the mechanics; he wants to buy a comfortable price point. The agency sells him that price along with a cheap illusion of control. Everyone is happy, and margins are great.

Your problems start the exact moment you genuinely want to deliver growth for the client's business.

To drive real growth, you have to dig into operations, overhaul processes, build end-to-end analytics, and pour in hundreds of hours that a small business simply cannot afford. I tested every model: pay-per-lead, revenue share, retainers tied to KPIs. In nine out of ten cases, you crash head-on into the core bottleneck of small business: the owner himself. Sales reps drop leads, the product lags behind, but the marketer who brought the wrong crowd always gets the blame.

When you decide to do the job properly, your addressable market shrinks to a razor-thin layer of mature companies. Meanwhile, the remaining 90% of the market has a massive, persistent appetite for fake marketing, with zero appetite for real change.

In 2018 and 2019, that realization knocked me out of the game for nearly a year. Total apathy and a complete dead end.

There is only one way out of this trap: stop selling cheap parlor tricks and bargain-bin leads to people who just need a sedative. Either you agree to be a low-budget clown, or you step into a completely different league. Move where people track unit economics instead of clicks, and where marketing is baked into the business model rather than slapped on like a patch on a leaky bucket.

text:
Tweet 9
The lock your carrier must give you free:

7 lines. A number you rent rather than own. 320 complaints in three years, then 1,611 in one. A regulator writing down that your address and your last bill don’t prove who you are. A 1980s protocol with no authentication running 800 networks. German bank accounts emptied in January 2017. And a free lock that is off by default.

Now the honest part.

The overwhelming majority of SIM changes are legitimate, and the FCC says so in the order itself. Carriers process these constantly for people who genuinely lost a phone. Any authentication strong enough to stop every attacker also strands real customers at the worst moment of their week — and that tradeoff is why the old process was weak, not pure negligence.

SS7 attacks are also not cheap or common. They require access to a telecom network, which means either buying it from a complicit small operator or being a state. The Register’s 2017 reporting noted carriers’ position that exploitation demands significant technical and financial resources. For most people, SIM swapping is the realistic threat and SS7 is not.

And the FBI’s figures are complaints, not measurements. Rising numbers partly reflect rising awareness and reporting. The 15-fold jump I calculated in Line 2 is real arithmetic on real published figures — and some of it is people finally knowing what to call this.

“You can change a password. You cannot change who your carrier gives your number to.”

“SMS is not your second factor. It’s your only one.”

Next time a service offers you two-factor by text, don’t accept the default. Ask whether the same channel is also the account recovery route — because if it is, the second factor is decorative.

And the two minutes worth spending right now. Open your carrier’s app and find the setting called Number Lock, SIM Protection, Port Freeze or similar. Switch it on. The FCC required your carrier to offer it free in 2023, and it is almost certainly off.

Why keep this one. Not the lock. The FCC’s list of what doesn’t count as identity. Your birthday, your address, your last payment, your recent calls — a regulator formally ruled all of it insufficient. Every organisation still asking you those questions to verify you is using a method their own government has written off.

A person may attain wealth, status, power, or titles, yet the true essence of reality—the genuine standard of character, along with the sweetness and purity of truth—remains beyond their reach. Such individuals—dishonest, corrupt, and tainted—are shameless, reckless, and of the basest nature. They represent the worst of their kind; even if they happen to speak the truth, they may still be dishonest, corrupt, thieving, violent, or even murderous—a shameless group that enriches itself at the expense of the rights of the poor. To profane the sacred essence of creation—the fragrance of the heart—and to reduce women to mere objects for public display is an act of the utmost atrocity and contempt; it is a supreme insult to all of humanity. Wealth, status, or one’s occupation are not the root of our problems. An honest person can never be truly poor, for worldly wealth, power, titles, or fame do not define the state of the soul. In fact, these are often dangerous traps—a strategy designed to cultivate a class of dishonest people. The soul is neither inherently rich nor poor; and work is, at its core, a path illuminated by the light of the soul. Therefore, let us seek our true identity and wisdom at the source of truth. O soul, look back toward the distant past and contemplate the light of the future—toward a world that existed long before the 8.3 billion people who now inhabit this universe; yet, today, we all live in the presence of that very light.  Therefore, remain steadfast on the path of truth and build upon that foundation as much as you possibly can. For you are a living soul, and as such, you deserve our deepest respect. O soul, you are truly wonderful. You have come with the destiny of becoming the pure, fragrant heart of all creation—emerging as a brilliant, blue-green light, the very essence of life. Never abandon the truth, for you were born upon the path of truth; to forsake the truth is to sever your connection to the source of all existence in this universe. Thank you. By the will of God Almighty and the blessings of the Most Holy Virgin Mary, Princess Leonor de Todos los Santos de Borbón y Ortiz has emerged—a soul illuminated by a profound, blue-green cosmic aura, standing in the presence of the eternal and indestructible sun. I offer her my unwavering support and respect, for she is a sovereign reflection of that sacred Being who permeates all of creation. O soul, you are truly beautiful; you shall return, manifesting once more as this vibrant, blue-green light of life. You are ever in my thoughts, held with the deepest respect. The Supreme Being resides within her. Amen. This act of respect strengthens the foundation of truth. Thank you. To exploit women by depicting them in a state of nudity is an atrocious crime—a deep stain in the eyes of the entire universe. Therefore, as men, protect women and show them the utmost respect. To deprive women of their dignity is to plunge humanity into a darkness riddled with hatred, jealousy, aggression, violence, religious exploitation, and a craving for wealth and status—a truly humiliating existence. Life itself is neither a problem nor merely a human construct. Remain ever steadfast on the path of truth, for therein resides the Supreme Being. Amen.

🇱🇺 🇧🇪 Grand Duke Henri attended the inauguration of Drottning Astrids Församling of the Church of Sweden in Brussels. 

The ceremony was part of the celebrations marking the Centenary of the Marriage of Queen Astrid (née Princess of Sweden) & the future King Leopold III, as well as the 400th Anniversary of the Church of Sweden abroad.

As Grandson of Queen Astrid, Grand Duke Henri took part in the tribute alongside his first cousin, Princess Astrid of the Belgians. 

On the occasion, Their Royal Highnesses unveiled a new portrait of Queen Astrid & a commemorative brass plaque.

text:
🦆 The geese saved Rome in 390 BC. But a flock of wild ducks saved my grandfather in the 1950s

Throughout history, survival often comes down to bizarre, unpredictable variables.

In the 1950s, mandatory military service in Bulgaria lasted a grueling three years. If you were unlucky, you got assigned to the most remote, harsh borderlands, places like the cold hills of Ivaylovgrad. Poor infrastructure, severe weather, and the constant threat of border incidents made it a brutal posting for a young conscript, completely cut off from home.

That was precisely where my grandfather was sent.

🥚 The Unconventional Flock

Back at his family's small farm near Plovdiv, his parents were desperate for a way to get him transferred closer to home.

Years prior, they had done something completely impractical for regular farmers: they rescued an injured wild duck and a clutch of abandoned eggs from the nearby river reeds. They placed the eggs under a domestic hen, who raised the hatchlings as her own.

While most villagers raised standard livestock for meat and eggs, my great-grandparents kept this peculiar flock of healthy, beautiful, remarkably docile wild ducks simply out of care. It made zero economic sense at the time, until fate showed up on a motorcycle.

🏍️ The Trade of a Lifetime

A high-ranking military commander rode into the village searching for authentic decoy ducks for hunting. Word spread, and he was directed to the farm.

The moment he saw the birds, he was struck by their striking plumage and calm demeanor. He immediately offered to buy them on the spot.

My great-grandparents didn't ask for money. They asked for a favor: "Move our son to a safer posting closer to home."

The commander made a single phone call.

🎯 From Border Patrol to Officer's Quarters

Overnight, my grandfather was transferred from the harsh, high-risk border duty in Ivaylovgrad to a small, quiet officer barracks right in the heart of Plovdiv.

His new "hardship duty"? Maintaining the grounds, playing cards, and spending his days at the range practicing marksmanship with double-barreled shotguns and sniper rifles. He earned the official military specialty of "Shooter" while getting regular weekend leaves to visit the farm.

A generation later, my father didn't have the luxury of a duck trade, so his service wasn't nearly as easy. But by then, times had softened slightly, and he was fortunate enough to serve at an airfield near the city.

By the time my generation came around, mandatory conscription was abolished entirely in favor of a professional army. I never had to rely on a flock of ducks to alter a military posting, but to this day, "lucky duck" moments show up in my life as bizarre, statistical coincidences. 🦆

Random acts of care have a strange way of compounding over time. You never know which unconventional decision today will end up saving your family tomorrow.

text:
🚨 Bullish Wiener Capital: Downgrading $WMT to UNDERWEIGHT, PT $80 (−36%)

At 45x trailing earnings, Walmart now trades above its own 1999 dot-com multiple (~39x). We believe the market is ignoring several structural risks.

1) Circular financing
Walmart's own fintech, OnePay, offers its customers buy-now-pay-later loans (via Klarna) so they can buy... Walmart's products. With consumer credit at record highs and rates rising, we worry what happens to revenue when the customer can no longer borrow.

2) Capex with no clear payoff
For every product Walmart sells, it must first buy inventory. This is a capital-intensive, zero-sum model, and we favour capex-light businesses in this environment. Depreciation risk is severe: much of that inventory is perishable, and a banana's useful life is closer to 5 days than the 6 years bulls seem to assume. Stores also need constant refurbishment with technology that will likely be obsolete within a few years.

3) No moat
Switching costs are zero. A shopper can walk across the road to Target, Aldi or Costco, or order from Amazon or Temu without even getting in the car. Aldi is effectively an open-weight Walmart.

4) Political and ESG risk
Walmart captures ~25% of all SNAP dollars, and critics argue taxpayers also subsidise its wage bill. With federal debt at record levels and SNAP in the political crosshairs, we view this dependence as unsustainable. Thousands of stores run freezers and lights around the clock, and we expect growing local opposition to new supercenters on power and water grounds.

5) Insiders are selling
The Walton family sells stock almost every quarter, most recently ~$220M in a single February filing. The people who know Walmart best clearly think the stock is running hot.

6) Valuation
$WMT: 45x trailing / 39x forward, 6% revenue growth, 3% net margin
$NVDA: 24x trailing / 12x forward, 106% revenue growth, 64% net margin
The last time Walmart traded near these multiples, the stock went nowhere for most of the next decade while earnings rose ~2.6x. It has even moved its listing to the Nasdaq. Classic late-cycle behaviour.

Our $80 PT sits just below the Street low of $81. We prefer capex-light, high-margin businesses with real pricing power. Unfortunately, the market tells us those are the dangerous ones.

Satire. Not advice.

text:
*The Significance of Lighting a Lamp (Deeparadhana)*
The lamp is a symbol of knowledge—a divine light that dispels the darkness of ignorance. It is a Hindu tradition to light a lamp before the deity in one’s home, typically during the morning and evening hours. In some households, a lamp is kept burning continuously; this is known as an 'Akhanda Deepam' (uninterrupted lamp). We follow the tradition of lighting a lamp at the commencement of all auspicious occasions. Just as the light of a lamp banishes darkness, knowledge eradicates ignorance and negligence. Therefore, to attain the supreme wealth of knowledge—which encompasses all forms of prosperity—we light a lamp during sacred moments, serving as a witness to our thoughts and actions. A traditional oil lamp holds profound spiritual significance. The ghee or oil poured into the lamp, along with the wick, symbolizes our inner desires and the egoistic tendencies within us.* *One should understand that as a lamp is lit before the Divine, the desires within us gradually evaporate, and the ego begins to burn away.*

*In the Stone Age, people fashioned lamps out of stone. Such lamps were used for worship in temples. Later, earthen lamps (pramidas) came into use. Those who were affluent used lamps made of gold or those studded with precious gems (navaratnas) for their worship.*
 special results.*
The daily lighting of a lamp at home is known as 'vyashti' (individual/household) deeparadhana; it brings light to the home and bestows prosperity upon the entire family. Similarly, lighting lamps in temples invokes the grace of the deities and yields profound benefits. A lamp lit near the sacred Tulsi plant is called 'Vrindavana' deeparadhana.*

*Lamps offered specifically to the Deity during worship are known as 'archana' lamps. Small lamps used during daily rituals are called 'niranjana' lamps. A lamp lit within the sanctum sanctorum (garbhagudi) is termed a 'nanda' deepam, while a lamp lit in the sanctum of Goddess Lakshmi is called a 'Lakshmi deepam'.*

*A lamp lit upon the 'bali peetham' (altar/platform) within the temple premises is known as a 'bali deepam'; it serves to ward off the 'evil eye' (drishti) from the temple.* A lamp lit atop a tall pillar nearby is known as an 'Akasha Deepam' (lamp of the sky).

In 'Panchayatana' temples—dedicated to the five primary deities: Shiva, Vishnu, Ambika (Devi), Ganapati, and Aditya (the Sun)—the lamps lit for worship take on various forms. In Shaivite traditions, one may find lamps shaped like Nandi (the sacred bull) or a Naga (serpent).

In the worship of Vishnu, lamps are often crafted in the forms of His attributes: the Shankha (conch), Chakra (discus), Gada (mace), and Padma (lotus).

A lamp with a single wick is considered moderate; two wicks signify family unity; three wicks bring the blessing of virtuous progeny; four wicks represent the accumulation of livestock and wealth; and five wicks signify the growth of prosperity and abundance.

It is considered auspicious to use lamps (pramidas) made of clay, silver, or 'panchaloha' (an alloy of five metals). Silver lamps are the most preferred, followed by those made of panchaloha. When lighting a lamp, it is best to place a small plate underneath it. If using a clay lamp, it should be placed upon another clay lamp (or a clay base).

Lighting a lamp at home, especially during the twilight hours (sandhya), is highly recommended. It brings daily auspiciousness, dispels negative forces, and ensures the well-being of everyone in the household.

text:
5. The Moment Contact Becomes Compromise

There comes a point, however, when ordinary association crosses into deliberate cooperation with wrongdoing. Second Corinthians 6:14 commands, “Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers: for what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness? and what communion hath light with darkness?” The surrounding passage concerns righteousness, unrighteousness, light, darkness, Christ, Belial, and the temple of God in contrast with idols. The issue is not that a saved person must refuse every conversation, commercial transaction, or ordinary encounter with someone outside Christ. The issue is a binding union that brings the believer into fellowship with influences contrary to his allegiance to the Lord. A yoke joins those beneath it in a common undertaking. That distinction demands careful application because not every association possesses the same character. An honest employment contract is not automatically the same thing as joining an idolatrous religious enterprise. A conversation with an unbeliever is not equivalent to assisting him in spreading false doctrine. The believer must examine what the partnership requires him to do, affirm, promote, or tolerate—not merely whether somebody involved happens to be lost. Biblical separation addresses real compromise rather than imaginary contamination.

Suppose a Christian is invited to participate in a business arrangement that requires falsifying accounts, misleading customers, or deliberately concealing known misconduct. His obligation is clear because Scripture commands truthfulness. Suppose a religious organization offers him influence or financial advantage in exchange for promoting teaching that contradicts the gospel of Jesus Christ. He cannot excuse his participation by announcing that his private convictions remain sound. Suppose a friend asks him to provide a false explanation intended to conceal fraud or another serious offense. Friendship does not cancel responsibility. Romans 12:9 commands, “Abhor that which is evil; cleave to that which is good.” The Christian may value the person making the request while refusing to perform the wrong. He may speak respectfully, explain his conviction, and accept the personal cost of obedience. The line between witness and accomplice is crossed when you begin doing, defending, or enabling what God’s word commands you to reject. A private disagreement with wickedness offers little defense when your public conduct is helping it succeed.

The danger becomes subtler when compromise develops gradually through the desire to remain accepted. First Corinthians 15:33 warns, “Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners.” The believer must therefore examine influences rather than assume that his convictions are incapable of being weakened. A man may begin by tolerating conversations that mock holiness, then participate in the mockery, and eventually defend the behavior because he no longer wishes to appear different. Another may enter a questionable arrangement intending to provide a Christian influence, only to discover that continued participation requires silence whenever wrongdoing becomes profitable. None of this means every unbelieving acquaintance is corrupting or that Christians must approach society with permanent suspicion. It means prolonged cooperation carries responsibilities, especially where moral boundaries are repeatedly tested. First Corinthians 10:31 declares, “Whether therefore ye eat, or drink, or whatsoever ye do, do all to the glory of God.” That is a useful question to bring into any proposed partnership. If maintaining the arrangement requires you to disobey Scripture, the arrangement has become too expensive, no matter how profitable it looks on paper. A Christian should never sell his testimony for privileges that will disappear long before his final account before Christ.

text:
Finding the Balance Between Jesus and God’s Promise to Israel 

Can we talk about the deepest layer of prophecy in the Bible? Because right now, looking at the world, a lot of people are wrestling with a massive question: How do we balance what the Bible says about Israel’s enduring place in God’s plan with the clear prophecies pointing to Jesus? 

Take a look at Isaiah 53. If you’ve spent time in church, you know it as the ultimate preview of the cross—written 700 years before Jesus was born. It speaks of a specific man, a "man of sorrows," who was pierced for our transgressions and crushed for our iniquities. As Christians, we read that and see Jesus perfectly. 

But if you talk to a Jewish scholar, they will tell you that the "Suffering Servant" in Isaiah isn't a single person—it’s a personification of the nation of Israel. They see a description of a people who have been historically despised, rejected by men, and passed through the fires of unfair global persecution for thousands of years. 

Here’s the radical truth: Both layers can be true at the exact same time. They don't cancel each other out. 

Think about it this way. God made an irrevocable, unconditional promise to the ethnic nation of Israel. He chose them for a job—to be a light to the world and the lineage that brought the Messiah into human history. Because God bound His reputation to them, Israel has been the target of intense spiritual warfare for 4,000 years. The systemic hatred and persecution they have faced—historically and right now—is the tragic consequence of that chosen identity. 

But when Jesus came, He didn't come to "replace" Israel. He came as the ultimate representative of Israel. 

Jesus took the entire identity, the calling, and the centuries of unfair suffering of the Jewish people and concentrated it onto His own shoulders on the cross. He lived the perfect life the nation couldn't live, and bore the weight of the sins of the whole world. 

So when you look at Isaiah 53, you are seeing a beautiful, dual-layered prophecy:

1. The living pattern of a nation that has quietly endured the world’s cruelty for centuries.

2. The ultimate individual—Jesus Christ—who stepped into that pattern of suffering to bring about eternal salvation. 

God hasn't broken His promises to the Jewish people, and He hasn't changed the path of salvation through Christ. The history of Israel's suffering is a living testament to God's faithfulness, pointing us directly to the one who ultimately bore it all. 

The Multi-Front War and the Raw Reality of Spiritual Opposition 

To take this a step deeper, we have to look at the raw reality of the spiritual warfare surrounding this prophetic puzzle. History shows us that this isn't just a political struggle; it’s a spiritual one. And the Bible explicitly warns that both Jews and Christians—the "People of the Book"—will face intense global opposition as history moves toward its climax. 

If we are being completely honest about the ideological landscape, scripture and foundational religious texts reveal a fundamental incompatibility that cannot be ignored. For example, when you examine the core theological framework of Islam, there is a clear, written mandate regarding the relationship with Jews and Christians—explicitly stating in Quran 5:51 that believers of that faith are not to take Jews and Christians as allies or friends in a spiritual or political covenant. 

Beyond that, the text contains highly direct commands concerning those who do not believe. In passages like Quran 9:5 and Quran 47:4, the text explicitly instructs followers to fight and slay the non-believers. This opposition extends from this world into the afterlife. In the authoritative Islamic texts of Sahih Muslim (2767a and 2767b), it is explicitly recorded that on the Day of Resurrection, a Jew or a Christian will be delivered to every Muslim to be sent to Hell-fire in their place as their rescue. 

This isn't about individuals; it's about the reality of an ideology. The foundational texts themselves establish a worldview where the covenant of Abraham, the security of the Jewish people, and the divinity of Christ are fundamentally rejected. From a scriptural standpoint, it is an ideology designed to stand in direct opposition to both Judaism and Christianity. 

But the pressure doesn't just come from one direction. We are living in an era where the assault on biblical truth is a multi-front war. On one side, you have aggressive religious ideologies; on the other, you have a rapidly growing secular world of non-believers, skepticism, and cultural hostility that wants to erase biblical values entirely. 

Why is this happening? Because the spiritual enemy of our souls wants to destroy the two groups of people who carry God's truth on earth: the Jewish people, through whom the promises and covenants were given, and the Christian Church, who carries the gospel of Jesus Christ to the ends of the earth. 

When you see the rising tide of global hostility targeting both Jews and Christians right now, it shouldn't surprise us. It is the exact spiritual landscape the Bible predicted. The world may try to isolate us and force us to compromise, but it only proves that the spiritual warfare is real—and that the final chapters of God's plan are unfolding exactly as written. 

The Ultimate Deception and the Coming Prophetic Collision 

To tie this entire prophetic puzzle together, we have to look at how these competing worldviews are headed toward a massive, climactic collision. In Islamic eschatology, there is a central figure expected to appear in the end times known as the Mahdi (the "Guided One"). When you study what their texts say the Mahdi will do, a striking and sobering realization emerges for Christians: the Islamic description of their ultimate savior reads like a mirror image of the biblical Antichrist. 

From a Christian theological perspective, the parallels between the Mahdi and the Antichrist described in the Book of Revelation are too precise to be a coincidence: 

First, both figures rise to power during a time of global chaos, presenting themselves as peacemakers. The Bible warns in Revelation 6 and 13 that the Antichrist will establish a global kingdom and forge a 7-year peace treaty. Similarly, Islamic tradition teaches that the Mahdi will rule the world for 7 years, establishing a global caliphate and bringing peace through a unified system. 

Second, their religious mandates are identical in their opposition to biblical truth. The Bible states that the Antichrist demands total worship, outlaws Christianity, and beheads those who refuse to follow him (Revelation 20:4). Islamic texts explicitly state that when the Mahdi arrives, he will offer a choice: conversion to Islam or death, effectively seeking to eliminate Christianity and Judaism from the earth. 

Third, look at the fate of Jerusalem. The Bible prophesies that the Antichrist will conquer Jerusalem, desecrate the temple, and establish his seat of power there. Islamic tradition teaches the exact same geographic climax—that the Mahdi will make Jerusalem the capital of his global Islamic caliphate. 

What one faith views as its ultimate holy savior, the Bible explicitly warns is the ultimate deception. It shows us that the spiritual warfare we see playing out in the headlines right now is mapping perfectly to a future scriptural blueprint. 

When you look at the whole picture—from the historical persecution of the Jewish people, to the explicit mandates of the texts we see today, to the matching end-times prophecies—it becomes clear that history is not spinning out of control. It is spinning directly into place. As believers, our job isn't to live in fear of these coming deceptions, but to recognize the times, stand firm in biblical truth, and keep our eyes fixed on Jesus Christ, the true King who will ultimately conquer it all.

text:
Where Should the Philippines Build Its Nukes?

We’re going to build some nuclear power plants in the Philippine. Where do we put them?

The PH DoE thinks 4 big reactors by 2050 would be enough but more ambitious and serious observers think a dozen might not be enough. Whatever the future holds we can think about where we want and need them and where we do NOT want nor need them.

A dozen reactors are not likely to mean a dozen sites either. Just having a pair of reactors on a single site compared to two sites with a single reactor each, by rule of thumb, will save you 15 percent or more on the cost of the output. Save with one office building, one access road, a common output transmission corridor. The trend lately has to build 4 or even 8 at one site although I suspect the latter is a bit of an overconcentration of assets for Luzon.

The critical need is power for the Luzon power grid, the largest of the three in the archipelago – the others serve the Visayas and Mindanao. It is over 50 percent of the population and electrical load. It is the most prosperous and is growing the quickest of the three regions. Plus, the commercial products available on the market, all tested in operation and conservatively designed, are large reactors. These plants generally range from 1,000 MW to 1,400 MW and are available from the US, South Korea, and France. Russia and China also offer these but are generally excluded from consideration due to geopolitical considerations. The Canadians offer a unique product called CANDUs that are rated at 700 MW per reactor but they like to sell them as pairs for 1,400 MW.

What do we look for in a good nuclear site and where do we avoid?  Let’s start with the fact that power plant needs cooling water.  The PH has lots and lots of coast line and not so much fresh water so seawater cooling is generally the only option worth considering. Best if you can draw deep ocean water since the cooler the seawater the higher the plant efficiency. You have to discharge the heated seawater within the strict environmental temperature limits so a good sweeping ocean current is a plus. If you can design a clever arrangement to take advantage of both deepwater suction and swirling current discharge you’d look like the Sual coal plant on Lingayen Bay in Pangasinan. Too bad it’s taken.

Electrically, you have to get your output to market and have a separate backup power source for startup and safety. For a pair of large reactors you would likely tap into the 500,000 Volt (500kV) transmission substations of NGCP. Shorter is better, obviously, but a substation is seldom too far away. NGCP generally likes easy-to-build and maintain routes over flat land but short hops over rugged terrain can have fewer issues for acquisition of easement. One also needs a separate corridor for a startup power line. To start a cold plant you need about 50 MW to get all the huge pumps spinning before you can make real power inside the core. If the plant and the output lines tripped, 10 to 20 MW via this startup line keeps the safety and shutdown gear running without depending on the pair of emergency diesel generators and their week’s worth of stored fuel. These loads are low enough that 115 kV or 220 kV voltages could be adequate.

Since you’re on the coast, having a small port nearby is very handy. There are several large and heavy components that have to be delivered. Transport by sea with a short road is far preferred to a distant port and a long road trip. Import delivery to Port of Manila and transfer to a local delivery barge means the local port can be modest. Plus, you’ll need huge quantities of rebar, structural steel, and cement. You’d want local quarries for crushed rock and sand even if you have to build your own.

You’d think avoiding typhoons would be high on the list but nuclear power plants are rather indifferent to high winds and intense local rainfall drainage can be designed for. That’s good because you can’t avoid typhoons on any Luzon coast. The transmission lines are the primary vulnerability from typhoons but that's NGCP's job.

Another thing you can’t avoid in Luzon is earthquakes. There are two specific issues. One is the physical shaking that we define as “peak ground acceleration.”  Surprisingly, building directly over a deep fault is not that big a deal. A number of plants globally have done so to the full approval of their national regulator. The geologists look at the depth, age, rocks, length, etc of the fault. From that a frequency spectrum, from very slow, subsonic waves to faster shakes in the audible range, is prepared with a peak ground acceleration in terms of percent of normal gravity with normal gravity a 1.0 g (yes, gravity is an acceleration.) For Bataan, the geologists suggested about 0.3+ g but the designers chose to be conservative and bumped it up 0.4 g. Most reactor offerings can meet that as a standard product and some offer a regular upgrade option of 0.5 g. Specific reactors in California have been later custom uprated to 0.75 g and some in Japan to 1.0 g. For reference, the US Geological Survey puts 0.4 g at the top of the “Very Strong” Intensity VII category or near the bottom of the “Severe” Intensity VIII.

If designing for severe shaking is possible, what you CAN’T have is ground displacement. The foundation has to stay in one place and one piece – you can’t overcome the north end of a reactor going north while the south end moves south. But the possibility of that is not hard to detect because standard practice is drilling lots of bore holes and digging long and deep trenches looking for signs of movement in the geological record.

A couple of other hazards should be considered – volcanoes and tsunamis. The direct effects of volcanos are easy to avoid. PhilVolcs has detailed maps for all the 26 active or probably dormant volcanoes in the country with lava flows, lahar paths, etc mapped out – easy to avoid since they are not on a coastline anyway. What designers do have to consider is the ash fall. It is another roof load to consider and the HVAC air intakes might need extra robust dust filtration.

Tsunamis are always a threat and again, PhilVolcs has hazard maps for most of the coast line. The PhilAtom Act that established an independent regulator codifies that certain vital equipment has to be at a minimum 8.2 meters of inundation over sea level.

Finally, another thing to avoid – a city. You always give a nuke some distance from civilians. There’s an “exclusion area” around the plant fence of up to a kilometer. A major population center needs to be 10 to 50 miles away.

The DoE does reoccurring surveys of potential sites and I’ve looked at half a dozen sites on my own in a “plausibility” survey where local acceptance might be high. Any final decision will need some serious money spent of detailed geotechnical surveys and transmission planning before a site is selected and an application to PhilAtom made.

The host community of a selected site would benefit tremendously and flourish. A two-unit plant can operate for 80 years and have a staff of a thousand engineers and craftsmen, all well paid, solid citizens with money to spend in the local economy.

Don’t let special interests or hostile elites get in the way of a broader prosperity for the people from a nuclear power plant.

Joseph Somsel
BSNE, MBA

How hosting regional matches in the US can revolutionize CONCACAF’s business model? 

As political and logistical circumstances force  Haiti to play home games abroad in Miami, where it can fill MLS Stadiums like the NU Stadium, it exposes an unexploited commercial goldmine. 

CONCACAF federations often play to empty stadiums at home, missing out on massive financial potential. By implementing a hybrid scheduling model—where nations play half their home games locally and half in US cities via bilateral agreements with MLS teams—CONCACAF can directly tap into affluent diaspora populations living in the US.

This strategy offers a mutual win: it provides teams like Haiti, Jamaica, Cuba, and the Dominican Republic with packed US stadium revenues (such as Miami's DRV PNK or Hard Rock Stadium) with potential for heavy merchandise sales, thereby simultaneously driving local economic impact for US cities, boosting MLS fan engagement by hosting these teams in their Stadiums where these local population will be stimulated to engage the local MLS team. This model could generate millions in retail and ticketing revenue. 

Gamaliel E. Frederick

text:
I mean, if even SpaceX is struggling to get new projects built in Texas, how on earth is Anthropic supposed to secure all the compute it needs?

It's almost as though they've got exactly the govt regulation they asked for, except perhaps they didn't anticipate quite this much pushback on construction, permitting and infrastructure, especially so quickly after the midterms.

The irony is that commercially, doesn't this just strengthen the hyperscalers? (As oppose to other model makers). They're the ones sitting on existing data centre capacity, power allocations and infrastructure, which they can increasingly lease out at a premium. Anthropic can't just build its way out of the problem, so it becomes even more dependent on Microsoft and the others, presumably converting whatever existing CPU capacity they can to GPU workloads.

Nvidia might still benefit for a while as that existing capacity gets upgraded, but there's a limit to how much hardware you can squeeze into infrastructure that wasn't designed for it. 

Eventually that buffer runs out, and without new builds, where does the next wave of demand actually go?

So the biggest winners are arguably the compute landlords, at Anthropic's expense. Meta also benefits from having secured its own capacity, which it declined to offer Anthropic, while OpenAI has the additional advantage of being further along with its own chip development.

Unless Anthropic is betting on a flight to quality, where most of the smaller LLM players simply don't survive and capacity eventually frees up, I struggle to see the commercial logic here. The open source will continue today to mine of them. 

But maybe this is exactly what they anticipated that ask the maker takes liability for their products. Nobody would really release anything new outside of close door B2B settings. Which will be no great. 

The timing seems particularly bad. If you've already got a $200 billion war chest, why chase another $100 billion when the real bottleneck isn't money anymore, but the ability to actually deploy it? At some point, more capital doesn't solve a physical infrastructure constraint. It just makes the existing infrastructure owners more powerful.

text:
Nothing is impossible with Musk: The following is a summary from Grok with respect to the chip fab. - politicians are playing a dangerous game which could disadvantage the electorate and the country. 
Yes, he could in principle, but it would be expensive, delay the project significantly, and forfeit most of the Texas-specific advantages already secured.
Terafab is a real, confirmed joint Tesla/SpaceX (with Intel involvement) semiconductor megafactory planned for Grimes County, Texas, on/near the former Gibbons Creek power plant site by the reservoir. It was formally announced in March 2026, the Grimes County site was confirmed in August 2026, and it is described as aiming for the largest chip manufacturing facility on the planet (plans for >100 million sq ft of manufacturing space, vertical integration of logic/memory/packaging/test, targeting massive AI compute output for Optimus, Cybercabs, and SpaceX space-based systems). First-phase investment has been stated at ~$16.8 billion, with filings and county documents referencing potential totals up to ~$119 billion across phases.
As of early November 2026:
•A research/pilot fab precursor is underway on the Giga Texas North Campus in Austin.
•At the Grimes County production site, groundbreaking and site preparation (clearing, earthworks/grading) have occurred; foundations and further civil work are planned to ramp in late 2026, with limited operations targeted later (around late 2027 or beyond depending on phase).
Practical and legal constraints on moving it “today”
•Incentives and agreements: Grimes County granted a 100% property tax abatement on improvements/new property for a 10-year period (roughly 2027–2036) in exchange for an upfront payment plus annual fixed payments (around $20 million/year) and investment/job commitments. School districts approved related JETI program tax limitations, and the state provided a Texas Enterprise Fund grant. Reports on the executed agreements indicate SpaceX has termination rights (e.g., 30 days’ notice in some provisions), with limited clawbacks (such as repayment of abated taxes for a capped number of years, net of payments made). Moving would largely forfeit these benefits and require renegotiating (or starting over on) incentives elsewhere.
•Sunk costs and site work: Land has been acquired or controlled in the area (thousands of acres scale referenced), permits and site surveys advanced, and physical site preparation is underway. Engineering, design, supplier outreach, and related work have progressed. These are not zero-cost to abandon.
•Timeline and complexity: Leading-edge semiconductor fabs are among the most capital-intensive, infrastructure-heavy, and timeline-sensitive projects (cleanrooms, specialized utilities, water/power, workforce, equipment lead times). Restarting site selection, land acquisition, permitting, incentive negotiations, and construction in another state would add years of delay. Texas already hosts major Tesla/SpaceX operations, has the research fab nearby, and offers a relatively business-friendly environment that Musk has favored.
•Control: As controlling stakeholder/CEO of Tesla and SpaceX, Musk has substantial authority over the decision. Earlier in the process, other locations were still under consideration. There is no indication of an irreversible government mandate forcing the project to stay in Grimes County once planned. Private capital projects can generally be abandoned or relocated, subject to contracts, incentive terms, and any land/lease obligations.
In short: Legally and as a matter of corporate control, Musk could direct the companies to halt or relocate the Grimes County production site and pursue another state. Practically, doing so today would waste significant sunk investment and time, lose the negotiated Texas incentives, and set the overall program back substantially. It is far from a simple or cost-free move at this stage of planning and early construction.

text:
If you are still waiting for some massive CEX collapse to trigger a Perp DEX season, you are missing the point. The shift is already happening right now

Smaller exchanges are quietly dying out because they can't afford compliance anymore

BitMEX stopped trading, BitMart is winding down, and CoinEx is closing operations because legal costs are too high. Centralized platforms below the top tier are cooked. For perp traders, this means mid-tier CEX liquidity is gone for good and moving to DEXs where you don't need US rails.

The recent massive hacks show a huge flaw in centralized custody

The $6.3B Binance hit and the $387M Bitget hack weren't about stolen private keys. They were inside jobs: an engineer's hacked laptop on Binance and a zero-day exploit on Bitget that allowed fake withdrawal requests through the backend. Even if top exchanges cover the losses, freezing withdrawals completely ruins trading strategies

When your funds get locked during a hack, you immediately start looking for decentralized venues.

The idea of trading stocks on centralized exchanges is hitting a wall

Tech companies are using SEC rules to fight back: Tesla, SpaceX, Nvidia, and Microsoft have filed over 56 official objections against tokenized stocks on platforms like OKX. Big tech is blocking this to protect their shareholder registers

If you want real exposure to stocks without corporate gatekeepers, centralized wrappers won't work anymore

Let's be real - Perp DEXs are not perfectly safe. We saw the $285M Drift exploit, plus there is always a risk of oracle lag arbitrage, admin key hacks, and MEV bots frontrunning you

The point of a Perp DEX is not absolute safety, it’s self-custody and clear rules. On a DEX, you get liquidated based on open code, not because some hidden risk committee panicked and froze your account

Perp DEX market share is growing simply because CEXs are falling apart under compliance pressure and bad tech

Hyperliquid is absorbing the capital post-Binance hack because it offers deep open interest and zero fees without centralized counterparty risk

Stop listening to moonboys

text:
The record establishes that the cryptocurrency sector has operated, and continues to operate, as a meritless casino whose purported value propositions have been systematically exposed as illusory. Technical analysis, chart patterns, and schematic frameworks long advanced as predictive instruments have failed in sequence, leaving no residual analytical limb upon which market participants may rely. Concurrently, the demographic cohort now entering productive adulthood has directed its speculative and entrepreneurial energies toward streaming platforms, regulated gambling, and AI-assisted business scaling; activities that, whatever their defects, at least generate measurable external utility or entertainment value. The industry’s inability to capture this generation in sufficient volume, prior to the exhaustion of its earlier cohorts, constitutes a structural failure of onboarding that the evidence shows cannot be remedied by further price appreciation alone.

The institutional-adoption narrative, once treated as a terminal bull case, has likewise collapsed under examination. The original thesis, articulated by as early as 2011 by sophisticated technical actors, ie my close friend from GA tech and others, was that governments and large institutions would be induced to accumulate, after which early holders would distribute into that demand. When that accumulation in fact occurred, the anticipated distribution phase did not produce the permanent re-rating that was forecast; instead, the same entities that entered have demonstrated the capacity to exit without regard to retail holders. The subsequent discovery that pattern recognition, wave counts, and on-chain schematics offer no reliable edge merely confirms what the distributional mechanics already revealed: the asset class possesses no independent claim to value capable of surviving the departure of its original promotional constituency.

In light of the foregoing, I submit that the road has terminated short of the critical mass required to sustain the structure as anything other than a residual zero-sum game among a diminishing set of participants. Absent a demonstrable utility that the new generation elects to adopt, and absent any predictive apparatus that has not already been falsified, the trajectory toward zero is the residual outcome consistent with the record.

TL; DR 

WE ARE FUCKING FUCKED.

Macro Observatory Week 45 Sunday Omnibus

In today's Omnibus - our weekly deep-dive where we unpack one aspect or other of current capital markets behaviour in order to illuminate one feature or other of how our force-balance matrix telemetry works, we look at the physics of a 'Bearish Trap'. What happens mechanically when retail and algorithmic short-covering pushes fast-twitch price action into an institutional vacuum.  

The Anatomy of a Bearish Trap: Reading horizon asymmetry in the S&P 500, Nasdaq 100, and the tech hardware equities🛰️

If you spent Friday afternoon watching standard financial media or glancing at simple daily candlestick charts, the tape appeared to stage a spirited, late-session defense. Headlines spoke of dip buyers defending key technical floors, indices paring weekly losses, and risk appetite tentatively finding its feet.

Looking behind the scenes at the mechanical matrix, however, tells a radically different story.

Single-horizon price charts flatten market reality into two dimensions: price and time. They show where a transaction crossed, but they remain completely blind to the structural weight behind it.

Our force-balance telemetry reads the tape across three distinct mechanical gears: Daily kinetic velocity (intraday order-flow impulse), Weekly institutional flow (multi-day capital accumulation or distribution), and Monthly structural depth (the foundational collateral reservoir).

When these three gears turn in opposite directions, the matrix exposes the most lethal setup in modern algorithmic trading: The Bearish Trap.

               The Mechanics of the Horizon Disconnect
       ┌──────────────┴──────────────┐
Illusion                                                         Structural vacuum
(daily impulse)                                                      (weekly flow)
Fast-twitch short                          Institutional order books 
covering & retail chasing                                      evaporated
                                                     ▼
                          Result: Mechanical Bearish Trap
                 Forward vector pointing to direct rollover

# The physics of a Bearish Trap: Kinetic impulse vs. structural depth
What is a Bearish Trap in quantitative terms?

It is not a subjective candlestick pattern or a moving-average crossover. It is a distinct, unsustainable mathematical divergence between fast-twitch intraday price velocity and intermediate capital commitment.

At Friday’s close, four systemic instruments triggered explicit Bearish Trap classifications across our grid:

Ticker                Role                   Phase             Gauge (D/W/M)
                     in ecosystem
$NAS100         Tech             🟢  | 🔴  | 🔴       0.6878/  
                       benchmark                                    0.0612/0.3395 
$RTY           Small-caps      🟢  | 🔴  | 🔴       0.6863/

$TSLA         High-beta        🟢  | 🔴  | 🔴        0.6518/

                        canary                                            0.0538/0.3662         
$SPX500    Market-cap    ⚪  | 🔴  | 🔴        0.5889/
                        anchor                                            0.0296/0.2646

Examine the gauge reading of Weekly institutional flow.

In the Nasdaq 100, fast-twitch daily velocity surged to 0.6878, yet the weekly gauge closed at 0.0612. In the S&P 500, daily velocity reached 0.5889, while weekly volume flatlined at 0.0296.

This is textbook volume asymmetry:

Intraday air pocket: When algorithmic systematic programs and market makers cover short positions heading into a weekend, they pull their ask offers higher. A tiny trickle of retail market-on-close buying can easily push the daily gauge into the green simply because there is no immediate selling liquidity standing in the way.
Institutional absence: Because real money - sovereign wealth funds, corporate treasuries, pension rebalancers - remains entirely on the sidelines, the weekly gauge captures zero accumulation.

Driving price up on a weekly reading of 0.0296 is like pushing an empty box up an escalator. The moment the covering impulse halts, there is no bid beneath the floor. The machine registers this immediately: the S&P 500 sits in Bearish Consolidation with its forward probability vector locked onto Emerging Bear Breakdown.

## The silicon engine at absolute max compression velocity ( $TSM & $NVDA)
If you want to know whether an equity index bounce is authentic, don't look at the headline index itself; instead, look upstream at the physical foundries and chip designers that power modern corporate cash flows.

Throughout the week, while software names and platform giants gyrated wildly, the physical silicon complex suffered a decisive structural breakdown:

                                                                             Gauge reading
Ticker         Current phase                  Daily  Weekly  Monthly
$TSM         ⚪  | 🔴  | 🔴            0.4023/0.0000/0.0918
$NVDA      🔴  | 🔴  | 🔴            0.3290/0.0000/0.0863
$AVGO      🔴  | 🔴  | 🔴                0.1370/0.0009/0.1270

Look at the intermediate weekly volume for Taiwan Semiconductor ( $TSM) and Nvidia ( $NVDA): literal zero (0.0000).
To see two of the most liquid, widely held, systemic companies on Earth print a complete evaporation of weekly institutional accumulation - accompanied by monthly structural foundations below 10% - is an extraordinary quantitative anomaly.
Foundry heartbeat: Taiwan Semi manufactures the silicon wafers for Apple, Nvidia, AMD, and Qualcomm. When $TSM carries an intermediate volume gauge of 0.0000 and maps its forward vector straight into Emerging Bear Breakdown, it signals that institutional allocators have turned the tap completely off.
Transmission lag: Passive index funds ( $SPX500USD, $NAS100) are capitalization-weighted. They can temporarily levitate on the defensive cash reserves of Apple ( $AAPL at 0.4945 M) or Microsoft ( $MSFT at 0.5580 M). But an economy cannot build a sustained info-technology expansion when the foundries and GPU architects carry zero capital support.

Friday’s tech rally was a body moving after its heart had already stopped beating.

### The real-economy confirmation: Energy and Copper capitulate
A genuine, organic risk-on inflection requires confirmation from the physical economy. If global enterprises are truly re-accelerating their capital expenditure, demand for raw energy and industrial wiring must expand.
Instead, the matrix captured an outright collapse in physical demand bellwethers:

Brent Crude ( $BCOUSD): Closed Friday trapped in Macro Bleed ( 🔴  | 🔴  | 🔴) (Daily 0.3394, Weekly 0.0000, Monthly 0.0602). Structural energy demand has effectively flatlined, logging zero weekly accumulation and targeting active Macro Rejection.
Doctor Copper ( $XCUUSD): Closed in Bearish Consolidation (⚪  | 🔴  | 🔴) (Daily 0.5809 vs. Weekly 0.0365 and Monthly 0.2982), targeting Emerging Bear Breakdown.
Much like the equity benchmarks, Copper experienced a fast-twitch daily pop (0.5809), but its weekly institutional support was crushed to 0.0365.

When crude oil registers a multi-month depth of 0.0602 and copper carries a weekly reading of 0.0365, the real economy is not pricing a soft landing or an industrial rebound; it is pricing an acute phase of Regime IV (deflationary demand drag & capital attrition).

#### Where capital actually went: The monetary preserve
If intermediate capital evacuated the S&P 500, drained out of semiconductors, and abandoned physical energy, where did it go?
The matrix shows that institutional balance sheets did not buy equities on Friday; they warehoused capital inside monetary scarcity and rate-defensive cash:

Platinum ( $PLATINUM): Locked in Macro Moon (🟢  | 🟢  | 🟢) (Weekly 0.9863, Monthly 0.7357). An historic flight into hard, un-printable physical assets.
Monetary Gold ( $GOLD) & Silver ( $XAGUSD): Defended pristine high-altitude Bullish Consolidation (⚪  | 🟢  | 🟢) (Gold Weekly 0.9333 / Monthly 0.6514; Silver Weekly 0.9629 / Monthly 0.6857).
Front-end cash ( $SHY): Anchored comfortably above baseline parity at (⚪  | ⚪  | ⚪) 0.5391 Weekly / 0.5090 Monthly.
Sovereign duration ( $TLT): Defended its levee at (⚪  | ⚪  | ⚪) 0.5226 Weekly / 0.5036 Monthly.

Capital is operating with total clarity. It is bypassing industrial risk, stepping over beaten-down consumer cyclicals, and ignoring unbacked tech pops. It is seeking refuge in sovereign duration, short-term cash yielding 5%, and scarce monetary metals.

Bottom line
The core value of viewing the global market through a multi-horizon force-balance matrix is that it insulates the operator from the emotional pull of the daily tape.
When you look under the bonnet at this week's close, the lessons are clear:
Never confuse daily velocity with institutional accumulation: A daily gauge of 0.6800 in $NAS100 or $RTY means nothing when weekly flow sits below 0.1500. It is a mechanical trapdoor.
Watch the silicon canary: Until Taiwan Semi ( $TSM) and Nvidia ( $NVDA) begin repairing their weekly volume from 0.0000, any rally in broad equity benchmarks is an unhedged counter-trend short squeeze.
The S&P 500 forward vector has spoken: With $SPX500USD in Bearish Consolidation on 0.0296 weekly volume, the matrix points directly toward Emerging Bear Breakdown.

The machine does not predict what central bankers or politicians will do or say next week. It simply registers the physical forces already moving through the global financial plumbing. Heading into Monday, those forces are wound tightly in a classic bearish coil - and the structural floor remains completely hollow.

🚨 A woman posing as a cosmetic surgeon was arrested in Florida after allegedly injecting women with dangerous household substances to give them fuller figures. One of her patients later d!ed.

In November 2011, authorities arrested Oneal Ron Morris, who had no medical licence or legitimate qualifications to perform cosmetic procedures.

Morris offered inexpensive b*ttock and body enhancement injections, sometimes visiting clients at their homes or motels and wearing medical scrubs to appear professional.

Investigators alleged that she injected clients with dangerous substances, including cement, mineral oil and bathroom caulking, and used cotton balls and superglue to seal the injection sites. Some victims suffered severe infections, painful swelling and other complications. 😨

One woman reportedly paid $700 for a procedure in 2010. Instead of receiving a legitimate cosmetic treatment, she was left with serious health problems and required medical attention.

The case took an even more tragic turn in March 2012, when 31-year-old Shatarka Nuby d!ed after undergoing repeated injections from Morris. A medical examiner attributed her death to massive systemic silicone migration throughout her body. 💔

Nuby had reportedly undergone around 10 treatments between 2007 and 2011. Before her death, she had written to Florida health authorities describing how her skin had become dark, hardened and discoloured.

In February 2017, Morris pleaded no contest to manslaughter and practising medicine without a licence. She was sentenced to 10 years in prison followed by five years of probation.

The case became a chilling example of the dangers of unlicensed cosmetic procedures and the devastating consequences of putting appearance before medical safety.

A lower price is never worth risking your life.

text:
Lane Kiffin’s long-running interest in Demond Williams Jr. makes any future portal pursuit feel like more than ordinary recruiting.

Kiffin and Ole Miss originally recruited Williams out of Basha High in Arizona and landed his commitment in late 2022. Arizona’s Jedd Fisch flipped him, and Williams later followed Fisch to Washington. Earlier this year, after Williams signed a deal to return to the Huskies, he briefly entered the portal and was linked to LSU before ultimately staying in Seattle. Now that he’s expected to enter the portal after the 2026 season, the same circle is forming again.

That history matters because of what has happened at LSU. Sam Leavitt has been productive at times under Kiffin, but the turnover issues have been consistent. He led the SEC in interceptions early, has thrown picks in most games, and has drawn public criticism from fans and former players after uneven performances (including against Ole Miss and Alabama). He’s a big, physical dual-threat with a strong arm who can create with his legs, but the decision-making and accuracy problems have limited the ceiling so far.

Williams offers a different style. He’s smaller and more explosive as a runner, with the lateral quickness and breakaway speed to stress defenses in the open field. Last season he was a dynamic rushing threat alongside his passing production. The two are both modern dual-threats, just different versions: Leavitt is the more prototypical pocket passer who can also run power, while Williams is the higher-twitch creator who forces defenses to account for him on every play.

Whether Williams becomes the starter in Baton Rouge in 2027 depends on several things. Leavitt still has eligibility and has shown he can put up numbers when he’s taking care of the ball. Williams will have other options, and the NIL market for a proven dual-threat starter will be competitive. But if Leavitt’s turnover issues persist through the rest of this season, and if Kiffin decides he wants a different dynamic under center, the prior recruiting relationship gives LSU a built-in connection most programs don’t have.

It’s not guaranteed. The portal is messy and money talks. Still, the combination of Leavitt’s early inconsistencies and Kiffin’s long-running interest in Williams makes the possibility more realistic than it would be for a random quarterback.
