text:
10 REASONS AI COMPANIES RISK THEIR GROWTH BY RAISING SUBSCRIPTION PRICES

OpenAI introduced a $500-a-month ChatGPT subscription on September 29, 2026. Its official release notes describe Pro 500 as a new premium plan with the highest included Pro usage and access to Astra Ultrafast in ChatGPT Work and Codex. That is a real product, but it is not evidence that ordinary ChatGPT subscriptions suddenly became $500.

The distinction matters. Adding an expensive option for heavy users is different from raising the entry price, cutting an existing allowance, or increasing API charges. OpenAI’s October 29 release notes also say it canceled a previously announced Pro 200 allowance reduction, preserved the higher allowance for existing subscribers, and increased lower allowances to match. Ignoring that reversal would misrepresent the position by November 7.

There is nevertheless a serious commercial risk behind the pricing debate. Free hosted assistants, downloadable models and inexpensive APIs increasingly give customers alternatives to a premium subscription. Those alternatives do not have to win every benchmark. They only have to complete the customer’s particular task well enough, at an acceptable cost and with acceptable privacy and reliability.

1️⃣ Free alternatives can remove the reason to pay
The strongest competitive threat is not necessarily a free model that matches the world’s best system on everything. It is a free service that handles enough of an individual’s actual work to make another subscription optional.
A customer drafting routine correspondence, rewriting a paragraph or organizing notes may not need the capabilities measured by a difficult scientific-research benchmark. If the cheaper alternative passes that customer’s own quality check, the remaining capability difference may have little economic value to them. This is task-level substitution, not proof that every free model is a frontier model.
The independent evidence is mixed in an important way. Artificial Analysis reported on October 23 that Kimi K3.1 Pro scored 67% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, compared with 64% for Claude Sonnet 5.5. On its then-current composite index, Kimi scored 55 against 58 for the leader. Those are concrete results showing that a challenger can be competitive on demanding tests. The same report listed Kimi’s API at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens: inexpensive access is not the same as free access.

But Artificial Analysis changed its composite evaluation on October 27. On the new v5 index, Claude Opus 5.5 scored 58 and Kimi K3.1 Pro scored 46. On Terminal-Bench-Science, GPT-6 Astra scored 63% against Kimi’s 34%. The benchmark mix and methodology changed, so the old and new composite scores cannot be treated as one continuous measurement of the gap.

The October evaluation snapshots also explicitly said Kimi’s weights had not yet been published. These results establish model capability at the time of evaluation; they do not establish that every user could download it then, run it cheaply, or get the tested configuration for free. Nor do they prove that a free hosted tier offers unlimited access to the same model.

Downloadable alternatives are real, however. DeepSeek’s October 17 release documentation provides another example of model weights made available outside a proprietary subscription. Whether that is economical for a particular user depends on the deployment, not simply the download price.

There are three separate alternatives. Free hosted tiers have limits, privacy terms and availability constraints. Open weights can avoid a proprietary per-token license bill but require hardware, memory, electricity, deployment and maintenance. Cheap commercial APIs charge for usage and are not free at all. Confusing these categories exaggerates the threat; understanding them shows why it is still substantial.
The commercial risk increases as customers discover those distinctions and test alternatives themselves. A provider does not have to lose the intelligence leaderboard to lose a subscription. It only has to stop being necessary for the work that subscriber actually performs.

2️⃣ Higher prices can trigger churn faster than they lift revenue
A price increase produces more revenue only if enough customers remain, and enough new customers still join. The relevant concept is price elasticity: how demand changes when the effective price changes. Public information does not establish one reliable elasticity number for all AI subscriptions.
Consider an illustrative subscription business, not the accounts of any actual AI company. At $20 a month and one million paying users, monthly subscription revenue is $20 million. Raising the price to $25 produces the same revenue if 800,000 users remain. Losing more than 20% of subscribers would reduce revenue from that starting cohort, before considering new sales, downgrades, refunds or different usage costs.
That arithmetic does not prove that a particular increase will fail. It shows the retention assumption hidden inside the decision. A provider cannot evaluate the increase solely by multiplying the new price by its existing subscriber count.
Free substitutes make that test harder. The alternative to a $25 service may be a $20 competitor, a lower-cost tier, an employer-provided assistant or no paid subscription. Customers can also pause payment between projects. In those cases, the company can lose paid months without losing every interaction or every registered account.
The response will vary by customer. 

A professional whose workflow depends on the product may accept a substantial increase. A casual user who opens it a few times a week may cancel over a much smaller change. Treating those groups as equally willing to pay is a forecasting mistake.
The important measurements are retained revenue, conversion, downgrades and contribution after serving costs. Subscriber counts and price increases tell only part of the story.

3️⃣ Extra intelligence does not always create extra utility
Customers buy completed work, convenience and confidence, not benchmark points in isolation. The premium worth paying is the difference between the best available alternative and the additional usable value a product delivers.
A stronger model can be economically valuable when it avoids expensive mistakes, completes difficult work or reduces review time. But an improvement on a demanding benchmark does not automatically create equal value across every customer’s tasks.
Productivity research reinforces the need to measure the setting. METR’s July 2025 randomized study found that experienced open-source developers took 19% longer with the early-2025 tools tested. That result was specific to those developers, repositories and tools. It was never a universal finding that AI reduces productivity.
METR’s February 24, 2026 update is crucial context. 

The organization said newer measurements were biased by developers and tasks selecting out of the experiment, particularly when participants did not want to work without AI. It believed developers were probably benefiting more than in early 2025, but said its data were unreliable for estimating the size of that improvement.
These findings argue against both blanket dismissal and blanket pricing optimism. The correct economic question is the improvement in the actual workflow, including the time spent checking and repairing the result.
This is where free and inexpensive models become commercially dangerous. A customer need not establish that two systems are equally intelligent. They can compare completion quality, review time and reliability on their own recurring work. Once both cross their acceptance threshold, a higher subscription needs a different justification: better integrations, stronger privacy, faster delivery or demonstrably fewer mistakes.

For a provider, that means capability gains must become customer outcomes. An expensive model that is technically stronger but rarely changes the user’s result has a weak upgrade argument.

4️⃣ Price increases teach customers to switch and use several providers
Brand familiarity, saved preferences and conversation history can make people stay with one assistant. Those advantages are real, but they are not absolute. A sufficiently unattractive price gives customers a reason to learn what else exists.
That discovery can outlast the pricing announcement. A user may find that one assistant is preferable for research, another for routine writing and a third for coding. The original provider remains useful, but no longer receives every task or every paid month.

Developers have additional options. DeepSeek’s API documentation advertises OpenAI-format and Anthropic-format interfaces. Compatible interfaces can reduce some rewriting when trying a different provider, although they do not guarantee equivalent tools, outputs, latency or safety behavior. Production migration still requires evaluation.
Switching is not frictionless. Memories, custom agents, access controls, tool behavior, data-residency requirements and evaluation results can create substantial lock-in. An organization should not move confidential information into an unfamiliar service merely to save money.

But each price shock can justify the customer’s effort to reduce that dependence. Once a business has built a second integration or a consumer has learned a second assistant, reversing the price increase may not restore the old relationship. The company has helped create a more informed and less captive buyer.
This is also why awareness matters. An adequate cheaper model cannot win a customer who does not know it exists. Comparisons, demonstrations and accessible trials can change that information gap without changing the model itself.

That is a reasoned competitive mechanism, not a claim that a measured percentage of users have already switched. The risk is that a pricing decision accelerates discovery of alternatives that customers subsequently keep using.

5️⃣ Bundles can undercut a standalone subscription without winning every test
Competition is not just model against model. It is also standalone payment against a package that a customer already values for other reasons.
Google’s May 20, 2025 launch announcement is an instructive historical example. Google AI Ultra launched in the United States at $249.99 a month, with a temporary introductory discount. The package included AI products alongside YouTube Premium and 30 TB of storage. Google also expanded its existing AI Pro offering without an additional charge at that announcement.
Those are historical launch terms, not a claim that every component and price remained identical in every country by November 2026.
The economic mechanism is straightforward. A person who already needs other components can perceive a lower incremental cost for the AI portion. The standalone competitor must then justify an extra payment on top of what the customer is already spending. A technically better model can lose the purchasing decision if its advantage is not worth that additional expense.
An assistant included through an employer presents a similar purchasing problem for a separate personal subscription. It does not have to be the user’s favorite system for every task. It may simply cover enough work to make a second monthly payment unnecessary.
Bundles are not automatically bargains. Unused storage, unwanted services and unnecessary seats do not create real value merely because they are packaged together. Buyers should compare the components they would actually purchase.

For standalone AI companies, however, the threat remains. Repeatedly increasing the separate subscription price can widen the perceived difference between an additional bill and an assistant already included elsewhere.

6️⃣ Falling capability-adjusted prices weaken the case for repeated increases
Stanford’s 2025 AI Index documented a large decline in the price of reaching a fixed capability threshold. The cost of querying a system matching GPT-3.5’s MMLU score fell from $20 per million tokens in November 2022 to $0.07 by October 2024, more than a 280-fold reduction.
That is a historical, benchmark-specific price comparison. It is not a direct measurement of every lab’s production cost, a guarantee that frontier workloads get cheaper at the same rate, or a reason to expect limitless free inference. It shows that a level of performance once sold at a premium can become inexpensive to obtain.
Efficiency gains do not eliminate the cost of GPUs, memory, power, networking and staff. Nor do they prevent total spending from rising when providers serve many more requests or run longer reasoning chains. A falling cost per unit and a rising total compute bill can coexist.
Financial reporting shows why providers care about monetization. Reuters reported on November 2, 2026 that Anthropic’s third-quarter revenue reached $16.96 billion, while it recorded a $567 million operating loss. The same report described $895.4 billion in infrastructure-related spending commitments across future periods.

Those commitments are not one quarter’s expenses. Reuters separately reported a $23.29 billion net loss, which included non-operating items connected to convertible instruments. Net loss, operating loss, infrastructure commitments and cash burn are different measures and should not be added together as though they describe the same bill.
The counterpressure remains: customers compare alternatives, not the provider’s financing needs. A huge investment does not by itself create willingness to pay. If competitors deliver adequate capability more cheaply, a provider must demonstrate additional value or improve its own efficiency.
Trying to recover every ambitious infrastructure commitment through higher prices can push demand toward the cheaper capacity it is competing against. 

That is a risk, not proof that the investments cannot earn a return.
A sustainable premium requires something buyers cannot obtain as cheaply elsewhere: materially better outcomes, dependable service, valuable integrations or contractual protections. Past spending alone is not that advantage.

7️⃣ An expensive entry point can damage tomorrow’s conversion funnel
The cheapest accessible plan often plays a different role from the premium plan. It lets a person develop a habit, learn the product and decide whether paying more could be worthwhile. Raising that first step can reduce the pool of people who ever become long-term customers.
OpenAI itself made the access argument in January 2026. When it announced ChatGPT Go worldwide, it listed a US price of $8 a month and described Go as its fastest-growing plan after its earlier rollout.

 The same dated announcement listed Plus at $20 and Pro at $200.
These figures describe that announcement, not the complete later Pro ladder. Localized currencies, taxes and billing channels can change actual invoices; business per-seat contracts are a separate comparison.
There is no reliable tier-by-tier subscriber breakdown in the sources used here proving that the cheapest paid plan contains most paying subscribers. 
That claim should not be presented as fact. Free users are not paying subscribers either, and neither group automatically determines the largest revenue source.
The stronger argument is about access and future conversion. An affordable plan gives people a lower-risk way to establish whether the product is useful. A premium tier can monetize unusually demanding users without removing that route.
Free alternatives amplify the risk of an inaccessible entry price because the abandoned prospect can build the habit somewhere else. Affordability is therefore a distribution decision as well as a pricing decision.
The appropriate test is cohort conversion and retention over time, not an unsupported assertion that every popular AI company depends on one majority tier. A company should examine whether the entry plan brings in customers who become durable contributors to revenue, rather than judging it only by its immediate monthly price.

8️⃣ Higher revenue per customer can hide worse unit economics
Average revenue per user is useful, but it is not profit. A company can raise ARPU while shrinking revenue, attracting a costlier customer mix or spending more to replace the people who leave.
Return to an explicitly hypothetical business. Suppose one million subscribers each pay $20 monthly, and each costs $6 in variable serving and support expenses. Revenue is $20 million and contribution after those variable costs is $14 million. That contribution is not net profit: research, sales, administration and other fixed costs remain.
Now suppose the price rises to $25 and 800,000 remain. Revenue stays at $20 million. If variable cost remains $6 per subscriber, contribution rises to $15.2 million. A price increase can therefore improve the business even while the subscriber count falls. That is the strongest straightforward counterargument to an automatic anti-price-hike position.

But the user mix may not stay constant. If lighter users cancel and the remaining heavy users average $10 in variable costs, contribution becomes $12 million. Revenue and ARPU look respectable, yet contribution is lower than before.
These figures are invented solely to explain the mechanism; they are not estimates for OpenAI or any other provider.
Serving cost also varies by workload. A subscriber producing short routine answers can impose a very different bill from one running lengthy reasoning or agentic jobs. An apparently uniform subscription base can contain very different contribution margins.
This makes segmentation more useful than indiscriminate increases. A company can sell higher allowances or premium capabilities to customers who need them while preserving a sensible entry product for lighter users.
The question is not whether higher prices always destroy growth. They do not. It is whether the retained customer mix, serving costs and acquisition costs justify the change. An ARPU chart cannot answer that by itself.

9️⃣ API increases encourage customers to optimize away expensive tokens
Consumer subscriptions and APIs are separate products. A subscription buys access under plan rules. An API typically meters input, output, cached input and sometimes tools or other resources. A change in one does not establish a change in the other.
For an agent, the meaningful bill is the cost per successfully completed task. It includes input and output across model calls, any billed reasoning, tool execution, retries, infrastructure and human review. The cheapest advertised token rate does not guarantee the cheapest successful outcome.
Artificial Analysis’s October 27 evaluation found more than a thirteenfold cost-per-task spread among the ten highest-scoring models shown. It also reported that agentic evaluations represented 55% of the index weight but about 90% of median output-token use.
Those are results for its benchmark configuration, not a universal enterprise invoice, but they demonstrate why workload matters.

Repeated loops can multiply consumption. If a system repeatedly sends expanding context, generates lengthy reasoning and retries a failed action, a rate increase can be amplified across the workflow. Developers respond with maximum-step limits, budgets, shorter prompts, smaller models and escalation only when the cheaper attempt is inadequate.
Caching and batching provide additional defenses. OpenAI documents reuse of matching prompt prefixes and discounted asynchronous batch processing. They have eligibility and latency constraints; caching is not a guarantee that every repeated-looking request is discounted. Engineering discipline still matters.
A rate increase can therefore accelerate routing away from a provider rather than simply lift the existing bill. A cheaper model may perform the initial classification, extraction or draft, leaving the premium model only the difficult cases.

November 6 reporting on Ramp’s business-spending data described rising token use alongside much slower spending growth in late summer, followed by renewed growth in October. That sample is not the entire AI economy, but it is evidence that usage and spending need not move together.
The lesson is narrower than predicting an industry spending collapse. Customers can consume more AI while improving the economics of each task. Providers should not assume that every additional token of demand will preserve yesterday’s revenue per unit.

🔟 Unpredictable allowances can destroy trust and delay procurement
The effective price is not just the number on the subscription page. It also depends on how much useful work is included, which model consumes the allowance, when limits reset and what happens when the budget runs out.
A $20 plan that suddenly completes much less of the same workload has become more expensive in practical terms, even if the headline stays unchanged. But a changed workload can also consume more without a provider secretly cutting the plan. Longer tasks, higher reasoning effort and faster service options must be distinguished from an actual reduction in entitlement.
Cursor supplied a direct historical example of the communication problem. On July 4, 2025, it apologized for unclear pricing changes, acknowledged that the changes had hurt trust, and offered refunds for unexpected usage charges. Its explanation distinguished unlimited Auto usage from a finite pool for selected frontier models.
That documented apology is not evidence of a particular churn rate, which the source did not provide.
Predictability matters to both individuals and businesses. A buyer needs to estimate what an ordinary month of work will cost. Unclear allowances make comparison difficult and can turn a seemingly affordable product into an uncertain commitment.
For organizations, that uncertainty can require additional budgeting, controls and internal approvals. The cost of administering a subscription is part of its utility, even when it does not appear in the provider’s token price.
A provider can charge more and retain trust if it gives clear notice, explains the change, offers workable alternatives and delivers measurable value. Repeated surprises do the opposite. They encourage the customer to build an exit route before the next pricing announcement arrives.
The verdict
Premium AI is not inherently overpriced. A $500 monthly plan can make sense for a professional who reliably obtains more than $500 of incremental value, and even a cheaper plan can be wasteful when it is rarely used. Fast inference, strong models, reliable tools, security and support all cost money.

The threat is a widening mismatch between what companies want to charge and what customers need to buy. Free and inexpensive alternatives become powerful once people discover that they are adequate for their own work. They do not need to eliminate frontier leadership to weaken the premium attached to it.
The defensible strategy is to preserve an accessible entry point, charge for identifiable additional value, explain allowances clearly and measure contribution rather than celebrating ARPU alone. Technical improvements should translate into better completed work, not simply a more expensive product description.
Companies that ignore those disciplines risk slower conversion, more switching, weaker retention and greater pressure on margins. That is a conditional commercial warning, not a prediction of inevitable collapse. AI demand can keep growing while individual providers lose pricing power. Popularity, revenue and profit are three different competitions.

text:
Spent two weeks inside a GTM agency once

The team was good and so was the stack

But half the work was chasing metrics nobody acted on

Their main dashboard had everything: reply rate, bounce rate and positive rate, each broken down by 24 hours, 7, 30, 60 and 90 days

Nobody touched any of it until it was already a problem

A bounce rate creeping up got noticed when a domain got blacklisted

Low leads on a client got spotted on Monday, when you could've seen it coming on Wednesday

The team wasn't lazy

Every check depended on someone remembering what bad looks like for each client

So I rebuilt their metric system in 3 tiers

TIER 1: ALERTS

These are the drop-everything problems, and they come to you.

Each one pings Slack and creates a task with the next step, assigned to whoever owns that client:

> Bounce rate hits 2%
> No positive replies in 3 days
> Under 4-7 days of leads left
> Daily send volume missed

That last one tells you a lot: disconnected inboxes, a broken lead runway or not enough volume.

Every client gets its own thresholds.

Some offers take more emails per positive, and that's fine as long as it's inside their standard.

TIER 2: MONDAY

30 minutes, once a week, before any client calls:

> Emails sent vs target
> Positives vs target
> Week-over-week trends
> Emails per positive reply

You're looking for patterns here: who's improving, who's declining, what you can copy to other clients and what to stop.

Never daily.

One day you get 6 positives, the next day 9, the next day 1.

Panic on the 1 and you'll rebuild a campaign that was fine.

TIER 3: THE DRILL-DOWN

Lifetime stats, 90-day stats, sequence stats, day-of-week and A/B results.

Hide all of it from the main dashboard.

You only open it when tier 1 or 2 tells you to, or when a client goes yellow.

THE TRAFFIC LIGHT

> Green: every tier 1 metric is inside the client's thresholds
> Yellow: one is within 20% of a threshold
> Red: a threshold is breached, the task is live, fix it now

A weighted health score sounds smarter.

Then a client shows up at 73% and nobody knows what that means.

Three colours tell you who to look at first.

HOW TO BUILD IT

Push your campaign stats somewhere you can run logic on. Airtable works well for this.

Every breached threshold triggers the Slack alert and the task automatically.

Put the drill-down stats in a separate view, so nobody stares at them by default.

Pick a day for the weekly review and don't skip it, even when everyone's green.

You could build the whole thing in about a week.

The hard part is deciding which numbers matter.

My own dashboard now also compares every client to our agency averages and flags domains due for rotation. One morning it flagged 121.

The result is nobody scrolls dashboards anymore.

An alert comes in, someone fixes it and moves on.

I'd bet most agencies still have the 90-day numbers sitting on the main dashboard, where everyone looks at them daily and acts on none of them.

Start with tier 1. Write down the 4 numbers that should wake you up if they break.

“Than, I need to arrange the books. Could you move over a little?”

“Go arrange them somewhere else.”

“But…”

“Somewhere else.”

“But the teacher told me to do it here…”

D-Don’t look at me like that! Oh my god, I’m just doing what the teacher told me to do!

Than really wouldn’t budge. In the end, Marn had no choice but to give up and quietly move to another corner to arrange the books. He thought Than would probably move somewhere else after a while, and then he could come back and organize the books. But nearly two hours passed, and even when class was almost over, Than still hadn’t gone anywhere. He was still lying there.

Marn slowly edged closer, careful not to make any noise that might wake him up. He sighed as he looked at Than. This classmate of his was really difficult to approach. He couldn’t understand what Than was thinking. Why did he have to crawl into a corner and lie down here, of all places? He really couldn’t figure it out.

Class was almost over, and tomorrow was the weekend. He probably wouldn’t get to see Than again until Monday.

Marn slowly took out the blue bag of candy. He sat there looking at it for a moment, weighing his options, before gently placing it beside the sleeping boy.

It seemed his plan to make friends through candy wasn’t working. Oh well, he’d try something else on Monday. There had to be some way for him to become friends with Than, right?

“Why does he dislike me so much?”

“…”

“Sigh… I guess I’ll have to find another way.”

Marn looked down at the candy he’d bought, wondering what it tasted like. He hadn’t tried even a single piece since buying it. He still followed the old habit his grandmother had taught him: when buying food to give someone as a gift, you shouldn’t sneak a bite or taste it beforehand.

Marn also wanted to know why Than liked green candy so much.

And then curiosity got the better of him. Marn decided to go against his grandmother’s advice and secretly took out a piece of green candy. He slowly unwrapped it and popped it into his mouth.

“Mmm… mmm… mmm!”

Sour! So sour! Someone help me! My face is all scrunched up! Ugh!

Marn immediately covered his mouth with his hand and squeezed his eyes shut so tightly that tears began to fall. He really wanted to spit the candy out right away. He had never eaten anything this sour in his entire life. He could barely speak. The longer he kept it in his mouth, the more miserable he felt.

His mouth was filling with saliva, so he quickly tried to get rid of it by chewing the candy into tiny pieces.

At first, it was so sour that it almost gave him a headache. But after a little while, the sourness gradually faded, and he began to taste a little sweetness.

His eyes lit up when he realized that the candy actually left behind such a pleasantly sweet aftertaste.

“It’s so good! But it was insanely sour at first. Waaah.”

“Didn’t you bother reading the packaging when you bought it?”

“Th… Than!”

Marn nearly jumped out of his skin. He had clearly been mumbling to himself, thinking Than was fast asleep and completely unaware of anything. But who would’ve thought Than could still answer him?

When he realized that Than hadn’t been asleep at all and had even noticed that Marn had brought him candy to “offer” him, Marn was the one left speechless.

He could only stammer, desperately trying to find the best words to explain himself. He was really afraid Than would scold him over this and end up disliking him even more.

“I saw that Than liked this flavor, so I bought some for you…”

“…”

“I just want to be friends with Than.”

——

Marn is so adorable~ He really wants to be friends with Than 🥹😭

Husband: Oh, she does! Although I don't think she appreciates me as much as she should.

text:
There is a shortage of ritual elders. The map to manhood is the same for all men. I stumbled upon it. It was given to me. We need more ritual elders. But especially more gay ritual elders. 

I believe gay men are supposed to be ritual elders. That is our purpose and role in society. We're supposed to teach men how to be men. This role was erased a few hundred years ago. 

We used to be more integrated into society, not separated out, feared and hated. The perspective of a man who is sexually attracted to other men was valued as evidence of the divine. That knowledge has been occulted and hidden but it is there for anyone who cares to look. Being gay is a spiritual experience and causes spontaneous enlightenment. Many gay men go back to sleep. 

A gay ritual elder knows the male body well. He loves and appreciates men and masculinity.  He doesn't perform for women or clamor for female attention. He doesn't separate himself from the brotherhood of all men. 

A few years ago, a man contacted me and told me that I had to step up. He had been watching me for awhile and could see that I was on the elder track but stuck in a liminal phase. He said something that terrified me: "You are a ritual elder, you have to go through the door." 

He was straight and married to a woman. He could see the value in what a gay ritual elder offers. He sent me some books, gave me some pointers and then disappeared. 

I went into a hermit mode. I restricted contact with the outside world. I went into a deeper self-imposed liminal space. This spiritual in-between phase where a person is no longer who they were, but not yet who they are going to be. The tension of that space is damn near unbearable. 

I had help from both men and women mentors who guided me when I needed it. Ritual elders and mystic types, appearing when they were most needed. I didn't have to look for them. 

I created art and wrote songs with my husband about what I was going through. Later came the sexual integration where I turned old sex tapes into artistic music videos. Grieving the man I was, but looking forward to the man I would become. 

I was diligent in my studies and inner work. A man can get lost in that liminal space. He can languish at the threshold. He will have enablers and disablers. But he must step through and become a man. 

There were times when it felt like my skin was coming off. The pressure of being cooked. Many men stay in the almost boiling water, miserable and uncomfortable but not getting "done." I turned up the heat. I wanted to be done. 

I meet many lost men.  Just as lost as I was. I offer encouragement, assurances and pointers if they want them. Most men prefer to be lost. That is the most shocking thing about this. When men refuse the help to save their life when it is offered. 

Ritual elders are rare. They appear in a man's life when he's ready. He may have one or several. But when a man wants to be cooked, he will step into the boiling pot. The unnecessary boyhood bullshit parts of him will fall away. What will be left is a man. Finally. 

Step up. Wake up. We need you.

The charity worked with coastal communities and had spent years campaigning against plastic pollution.

He argued that the donation could fund several months of their work. The director agreed, but explained that accepting the money without addressing the company's environmental record would make their public position look dishonest.

He offered to donate anonymously instead.

The director still refused.

She told him they weren't against people changing their ways, but they wouldn't take money simply to make a company look better.

A few months later, he contacted them again. This time, he wanted to fund an independent environmental audit of his factories.

They accepted the offer.

The director later said the first donation would have helped their budget, but the second could actually help change something.

text:
You have to take action or go on a hunger strike.
Some young people are not ready to change their lives

Let me share a personal experience,
 I’m not sharing this to disrespect anyone but to make a point

There is a woman in my neighbourhood with five children
Her husband left the country and abandoned her with nothing.

She used to visit our home regularly, and we always tried to support her.
At some point, I started thinking about how to help her become financially independent rather than constantly depending on others.

I introduced her to a programme run by (Save the Children NGO) aAfter about a month of processing, she was selected as a beneficiary.

She told them she wanted financial support to start a small business, and they agreed.

She attended their training sessions and received provisions during the programme. After completing the training, they gave her ₦428,000 as startup capital.

We were so happy, we even went together to appreciate the organisation.

They explained that they had taught them the basics of business and wanted to see how she would manage the money and generate profit. If she performed well, they would continue supporting her by doubling the capital.

(I was so excited to be honest)

When we got home, I asked what business she wanted to start. After discussing several options, we agreed that she could buy rice and groundnut oil in bulk and resell them in smaller quantities.

She also planned to buy some other essential goods.

A week later, I visited her to check on her progress.

To my surprise, she hadn’t bought anything.

She started giving excuses, saying she wouldn’t make sales because there were already too many shops in the neighbourhood.

I was disappointed.

I asked her what business she actually wanted to do. 
“She said she didn’t know”

Remember before receiving the money, she always said the only thing standing between her and financial independence was a lack of capital.

I tried again, this time I suggested garri and charcoal because they are everyday essentials that people buy regularly

I even contacted someone in the market to help her get wholesale prices.

Guys,two weeks passed. 
I didn’t hear from her, and she made no move.

Then yesterday she showed up at our house complaining that she had spent ₦7,000 from the money on her children’s needs.

I walked out of the room and left her there

text:
Dana White speaks out after being offered press secretary role as he reveals he's flying to DC 'right now' and will meet Trump in just hours | James Gordon & James Cohen, Daily Mail

Dana White has broken his silence after being offered the job of White House press secretary by Donald Trump, revealing he is flying to Washington, DC, immediately and will meet the president face-to-face on Monday.

The UFC boss chuckled when questioned about the extraordinary offer by a reporter in London on Saturday, before declaring: 'I'm flying to Washington, DC, right now.'

White, 57, refused to reveal whether he had already discussed the position with Trump but confirmed he would be meeting his longtime friend at the White House.

'I'm sure we'll have more to talk about after that,' he teased, keeping speculation swirling over whether he could actually become the administration's next chief spokesperson.

'I've got a lot of jobs already,' he added when pressed by a reporter at a press conference.

His comments come after conflicting reports emerged over whether White was seriously considering the job or had already rejected the president's offer.

TMZ reported that the fight promoter would meet Trump in the Oval Office on Monday to discuss the position, citing sources with direct knowledge of the planned meeting.

But CNN claimed White had already turned down the unorthodox proposal, according to a source familiar with the matter, while one White House aide suggested Trump had been joking.

Now White's confirmation that he is heading to Washington has added another twist to the saga, although he has stopped short of saying whether he intends to accept the role.

The conflicting accounts come only hours after Trump publicly begged his longtime friend and political ally to take the job, even suggesting he bring a team of UFC fighters to help him take on the 'Lunatic Left.'

It remains unclear whether the president's bizarre proposal was entirely serious, with one White House aide telling CNN that Trump was joking.

The drama comes as Trump scrambles to fill one of the most high-profile jobs in his administration following the disastrous five-day tenure of Katie Zacharia, who was fired after just one rocky press briefing.

The position has taken on even greater importance following the Republicans' crushing midterm election defeat, which handed Democrats control of both chambers of Congress and the power to investigate the administration.

White, who was in London on Saturday for a boxing event, has not publicly confirmed whether he intends to accept the job.

TMZ reported that Monday's meeting was expected to take place despite CNN's account that he had already rejected the offer.

Trump made the offer on Truth Social on Saturday, writing: 'I am pleased to announce that the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior, has been offered the job of Press Secretary of the United States.'

But the president went further, proposing that White bring an extraordinary collection of mixed martial arts stars to Washington as his assistants.

'I have requested that he bring with him assistants, even though some are not from our Country, of Islam Makhachev, Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier, Amanda Nunes, and Kayla Harris,' Trump wrote, apparently referring to UFC star Kayla Harrison in the final name.

'We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left. Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other. Dana, please take the job!'

The message immediately raised questions about whether Trump was making a genuine employment offer or simply having fun with his close friend.

White appeared willing to play along, reposting Trump's announcement on Instagram and sharing an image of himself standing behind the White House briefing room podium.

'On to the next chapter,' he wrote alongside the picture, without explaining whether he was accepting the offer or joining in the joke.

White House communications director Steven Cheung also enthusiastically backed the idea, reposting Trump's announcement with the message: 'Hell yeah! Do it, @DanaWhite!'

The president's interest in White comes amid a chaotic search for a replacement for Zacharia, whose spectacularly brief stint in the job ended last month.

She was dismissed after just five days, leaving the White House scrambling to find someone capable of handling the relentless scrutiny of the Washington press corps.

Her predecessor, Karoline Leavitt, had served for approximately 18 months before departing in August to spend more time with her young family. She subsequently joined Fox News as a contributor.

The search has produced some surprising names, with White House staffers even reportedly floating rapper Nicki Minaj as a possible candidate shortly before the midterm elections.

White, meanwhile, has spent years building one of Trump's closest relationships outside politics.

The UFC chief has spoken at the last three Republican National Conventions and played a significant role in connecting Trump with younger male audiences during his successful 2024 presidential campaign.

Trump has previously credited White with introducing him to an entirely different generation of voters.

'He introduced me to people I never heard of, young kids,' the president said earlier this year.

'I mean, I was being interviewed by 20-year-old kids. I'm saying, 'Where the hell did you meet these people?' They're called influencers.'

That relationship reached new heights in June, when Trump hosted a UFC event on the White House lawn as part of celebrations marking America's 250th anniversary.

However, the president's efforts to maintain his appeal among young men suffered a setback during Tuesday's midterms, with the demographic shifting toward Democrats.

The White House personnel shake-up has also reached the very top of Trump's administration.

On Friday, he ousted longtime chief of staff Susie Wiles and announced that hardline adviser Stephen Miller would replace her beginning Monday.

'I'll be doing maybe a few changes,' Trump told CBS News on Friday.

text:
Trump asks UFC boss to become White House press secretary
Dana White has confirmed he will meet with the US president on Monday to discuss the surprise job offer
Published 7 Nov, 2026 (FULL)
https://t.co/lMDVlyuG8G
US President Donald Trump has offered UFC CEO Dana White the post of White House press secretary, which has remained vacant for weeks. The mixed martial arts promoter has confirmed that he will meet Trump in Washington on Monday to discuss the proposal.
Referring to his longtime friend as a “violent Fighter and Warrior,” Trump wrote in a post on Truth Social on Saturday that he had asked White to “bring with him assistants, even though some are not from our Country.”
“We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left,” Trump claimed, listing Russian mixed martial artists Khabib Nurmagomedov and Islam Makhachev, current and former US fighters Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier, and Kayla Harrison, as well as Brazil’s Amanda Nunes.
“Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other,” Trump stated.
Speaking to reporters after a boxing event in London on Saturday, White said he was heading to the US capital immediately. “I’m flying to Washington, DC right now,” he said.
Asked how he would balance the White House position with his existing responsibilities, White replied: “Yeah, I got a lot of jobs already.”
The UFC boss declined to elaborate on his previous conversations with Trump or say whether he intended to accept the offer. “We have a meeting on Monday, so I’m sure I’ll have more to talk about after that,” he said.
Earlier, White posted an AI-generated clip of himself at the podium in the White House press briefing room on Instagram, with the caption “On to the next chapter.”
Former White House press secretary Katie Zacharia stepped down in mid-October after just five days on the job, the shortest tenure of any White House press secretary in US history. The conservative political commentator had faced widespread criticism over her handling of her debut press briefing, as well as allegations that she had misrepresented herself as a lawyer after she failed to confirm whether she had passed a US bar exam.
She succeeded Karoline Leavitt, who assumed the position after Trump returned to office in January 2025 and stepped down in August, ostensibly to spend more time with her family.
As for White, Trump has had a close relationship with the UFC CEO for years. The promotion company helped organize a fight on the White House South Lawn in June as part of celebrations marking the 250th anniversary of the US Declaration of Independence.
Speaking last April, White said that unlike multiple other sports organizations that barred Russian athletes from competitions after the escalation of the Ukraine conflict in 2022, the UFC had never ceased cooperation with mixed martial artists from the country.
The potential appointment comes amid a broader White House reshuffle following the Republicans’ bruising defeat in the midterm elections. On Friday, Trump announced that his longtime adviser, immigration hardliner Stephen Miller, would replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff, effective Monday. Wiles, who had served in the role since Trump returned to office, will move to his political operation.

text:
Agnipath Scheme was introduced in June 2022 for the Indian Army, Navy, and Air Force.

Youth selected under the Agnipath Scheme are known as "Agniveers".

It allows patriotic and motivated youth to serve in the Armed Forces for a period of 4 years with up to 25% retained in the regular cadre. The remaining 75% are return to civilian life with a financial package and other benefits.

On completion of the engagement period of 4 years, Agniveers are paid one time ‘Seva Nidhi’ package which comprise their contribution including accrued interest thereon and matching contribution from the Government equal to the accumulated amount of their contribution including interest.

‘Seva Nidhi’ is exempt from Income Tax.

There is no entitlement to gratuity and pensionary benefits.

Agniveers are provided non-contributory Life Insurance Cover of Rs 48 lakhs for the duration of their engagement period in the Indian Armed Forces.

🔴 Recently Union Cabinet revised the Agnipath scheme, the government announced that Agniveers set to exit the military at the end of their 4 year tenure will be given an additional 2 year extension.

Under the revised arrangement, the existing provision of enrolling 25% of Agniveers into the regular cadre after completion of their initial 4 year tenure will remain unchanged.

However, the remaining 75%, who were earlier required to leave the service after 4 years, will now be offered an extended engagement period of 2 years. At the end of this extended tenure, they will also be considered for regular enrolment, subject to their willingness and meeting the objective selection criteria.

The government has also approved higher remuneration and an enhanced Seva Nidhi package (a one-time lump-sum financial benefit paid to Agniveers upon completing their four-year engagement) for those opting for the second engagement period. However, upon regular enrolment, they will be placed one rank below those inducted directly into the regular cadre after the initial four-year tenure under the 25% retention provision.

text:
No redcoats on the border: There is no historical evidence that thousands of English troops were lined up on the Scottish border threatening invasion to force the 1707 Union vote. The Scottish Parliament debated and ratified the treaty itself in a recorded 110–67 (or 69) division after months of negotiations between two sovereign states.
Economic and political reality: Scotland faced severe financial strain after the Darien Scheme’s collapse wiped out much of its available capital. The Union offered access to English colonial markets, debt relief via the “Equivalent” payment to Darien investors, and guarantees for the Presbyterian Kirk — factors that influenced many parliamentarians far more than any alleged military threat.
The vote and the list: The image you posted shows the official list of those who approved the treaty in Parliament — a legitimate vote under the rules of the time, not a surrender by “cowardly traitors.” Popular riots occurred in Edinburgh and elsewhere, but Parliament was protected by local Scottish guards, not an English army. Calling it treason ignores the documented parliamentary record and economic context.

text:
Good morning from Virginia. 🇺🇸

On the morning of November 8, 1864, while the armies of the North and South still contended for the future of the nation, the people of the loyal states went to the polls in one of the most extraordinary elections in American history. Abraham Lincoln, the tall, careworn president who had already carried the country through three years of civil war, stood for reelection against George B. McClellan, the general he had once placed in command of the Army of the Potomac and later removed.

The stakes could scarcely have been higher. The war had exacted a terrible cost in blood and treasure. Cities had been burned, fields left barren, and families divided. Many believed the conflict had gone on too long and that only a negotiated peace could end the suffering. McClellan, still beloved by a portion of the army he had once led, promised just such a settlement. Lincoln offered something harder: the resolve to see the war through to a Union victory, with no compromise that would leave the Confederacy intact.

Yet the election itself went forward. Lincoln had insisted upon it. Free government, he believed, did not suspend its own rules when threatened; it proved its strength by holding them. To postpone the vote would have been to concede that the rebellion had already succeeded in making ordinary self-government impossible. So ballots were cast in towns and cities across the North, and, remarkably, in the field as well. Union soldiers, many of them voting from camps and hospitals far from home, gave Lincoln a decisive margin. Their support helped carry him to roughly 55 percent of the popular vote and 212 electoral votes to McClellan’s 21.

The result closed the door on any last hope of a settlement short of victory. There would be no armistice, no recognition of Southern independence, no return to the status quo that had led to war. The struggle would continue until the armies of the Confederacy were defeated and the Union restored. In the darkest season of the war, the American people had chosen continuity, determination, and the ballot box over despair. That choice helped decide that the nation would emerge whole.

اس وقت پاک آرمی کا وہ میجر (18 گریڈ کا آفیسر) جس کی پی ایم اے ٹریننگ ملاکر سروس 19 سال ہوچکی ہے اسکی تنخواہ  تین لاکھ  ستر ہزار ہوتی ہے.

تقریباً 56 ہزار روپے ٹیکس کی کٹوتی.

اگر سرکاری گھر میں رہائش ہے تو ہاوس رینٹ الاؤنس کی مکمل کٹوتی اور اسکے علاوہ تنخواہ کا 5 فیصد مینٹینسس کی مد میں کٹتا ہے. 

یعنی 24 سے 26 ہزار کی پھر کٹوتی. 

متوسط گھر کا بجلی کا بل گرمیوں میں 25 سے 30 تیس ہزار اور سردیوں میں 8 سے 12 ہزار. گیس کا بل اس کے علاوہ ہے.
 
اسکے علاوہ وہ فلیٹ جو ایک میجر کو ریٹائرمنٹ پر ملنا ہوتا ہے اسکے لئے 30 ہزار ہاؤسنگ کی مد میں کٹتے ہیں. مڈل کلاس بیک گراؤنڈ سے تعلق رکھنے والا ایک میجر 20 سے 30 ہزار پروویڈنٹ فنڈ بھی کٹواتا ہے جو رقم اسے ریٹائرمنٹ پر ملتی ہے اور یہ رقم بھی عسکری کے اس فلیٹ کی ادائیگی میں چلی جاتی ہے جسکے لئے وہ ماہانہ پیسے بھی کٹواتا ہے. 

اس طرح اکاؤنٹ میں دو لاکھ بیس سے دو لاکھ تیس ہزار ہی آتے ہیں. 

پاکستان کے چاروں صوبوں، اسلام آباد، کشمیر اور گلگت میں محکمہ صحت میں کام کرنے والے  گریڈ 18 کے ڈاکٹر کی تنخواہ بھی اتنی ہے. 

محکمہ بلدیات کے اس گریڈ کے آفیسر کی تنخواہ بھی اتنی ہی ہے، ریوینیو میں کام کرنے والے افسران کی بھی اتنی ہی تنخواہ لیتے ہیں. 

جبکہ ایک میجر اپنی 23 سالہ سروس میں تقریباً 9 سے 10 مقامات پر ڈیوٹی دیتا ہے. 

اور 2026 میں ریٹائرڈ ہونے والے میجران نے اپنی سروس کے اوسطاً 14 سال کشمیر، مشرقی سرحد، افغان سرحد سے متصل علاقوں اور بلوچستان میں آپریشنل ڈیوٹی دیتے ہوئے گزارے ہیں۔

text:
The Maryland Department of Natural Resources is advancing plans to improve educational, research, and recreational access to Holly Beach Farm Natural Resources Management Area in Annapolis, which offers sweeping views of the Chesapeake Bay and the Bay Bridge. 

At the NRMA dedication, DNR staff shared information about plans for climate resilience and habitat restoration as well as new opportunities for fishing, hiking, kayaking, and other activities at Holly Beach Farm. DNR currently allows reservation-based hunting on the peninsula.

As of November 6, 2026, DNR offers limited public access for a variety of other activities such as birding and hiking. Visitors will need to use the department’s MD Outdoors system to book a reservation and explore Holly Beach Farm Natural Resources Management Area. https://t.co/xlA1HfRvsj 

The 293-acre waterfront property in Anne Arundel County was donated to the Maryland Department of Natural Resources by the Chesapeake Bay Foundation in 2023. The property consists of forested areas, open fields, a 9-acre freshwater pond, and beaches along the Chesapeake Bay and Whitehall Bay. The department is planning to expand responsible public access to Holly Beach Farm in the future with a focus on access via boats.

The Holly Beach Farm peninsula helps safeguard the surrounding landscape and critical infrastructure, including the U.S. Naval Academy, from the increasingly severe threats of flooding, storm damage, and sea-level rise. 

Holly Beach Farm traces its origins to 1907, when Sylvester W. Labrot Sr., a prominent businessman from Kentucky and Louisiana, bought and consolidated several nineteenth century farms. Labrot created a single, expansive estate and in 1911 completed the main farmhouse. Through continued acquisitions during the 1920s and 1930s, including the historic Hackett’s Point Farm, the estate ultimately encompassed nearly 2,000 acres in the area that now surrounds the Bay Bridge. 

Following Sylvester Labrot Sr.’s death in 1935, his son William Henderson Labrot continued management of the estate, renamed the property “Holly Beach Farm,” and made it one of Maryland’s most successful horse breeding farms.

In 1949, as planning advanced for the Chesapeake Bay Bridge and its approach roads, William negotiated the sale of 680 acres of the northern portion of the property to the State of Maryland. That land became Sandy Point State Park.

What remained of Holly Beach Farm was sold off for private residences; the current property remained in private ownership by Labrot’s daughter, Leonie Gately, until 2001. She preserved the property and sold it to the Conservation Fund, who conveyed it to Chesapeake Bay Foundation to manage for conservation and environmental education. The Maryland Board of Public Works approved the Foundation’s donation of Holly Beach Farm to DNR on March 13, 2024.

text:
Belief in Magic Is Not Disappearing in The Modern World, Study Shows | Esra Öz, ScienceAlert

Imagine a house where footsteps supposedly echo through the hallways at night and doors close in empty rooms.

If you had to spend a night there, would explanations involving old floorboards and drafts be enough to settle your doubts?

As it happens, trusting a scientific explanation doesn't necessarily close the door on ghosts.

A US study found that, among people who retained religious ties, an outlook combining support for science and reason with independence from religious authority was associated with stronger belief in magic, including ghosts and curses.

The researchers wanted to understand what happens to supernatural beliefs as religious institutions lose influence. When people question church teachings, do they also leave ghosts, curses, and unseen forces behind? Or do they begin choosing their beliefs for themselves?

Sociologists Paul Froese of Baylor University and Isaiah King of Carson-Newman University, together with Ruiqian Li of American University, investigated these questions by analyzing survey responses from 1,812 adults in the 2025 Baylor Religion Survey.

Gallup collected the answers online and by mail between January and March. Responses were weighted to better reflect the US adult population.

The team examined an outlook they called "secular rationalism".

This measure combines the view that science is the only way to understand all aspects of the world with an emphasis on reason and human experience in moral decisions, independent interpretation of spiritual teachings, and disinterest in religious discussions.

Scoring highly didn't necessarily mean cutting all religious ties. Some participants still believed in God, identified with a religion, or attended religious services.

The researchers compared these views with three categories of supernatural belief. They assessed miracles, magic, and everyday superstitions separately, distinguishing beliefs involving divine intervention from those that require no god or shared religious doctrine.

Their magic score included belief in ghosts, curses, spirits inhabiting objects, communicating with the dead, predicting the future, and magic itself. Superstitions included habits such as avoiding words that might jinx a hoped-for outcome.

The responses showed that people with higher secular rationalism scores were less likely to believe in miracles. Their scores for magic and superstition, however, were higher.

Looking more closely, the researchers found that the association between secular rationalism and stronger magical belief appeared among people who kept these religious ties. The same association wasn't clearly evident among nonbelievers, people without a religious affiliation, and those who never attended services.

In his account of the findings, Li described the differences among people who believed in God. Around 40 percent of those embracing secular rationalism leaned toward magical belief, compared with 19 percent of those rejecting that outlook.

The researchers' explanation centers on the distinction between personal faith and institutional authority. A religious community might accept miracles while rejecting fortune-telling or attempts to communicate with ghosts. A member who trusts their own judgment on spiritual matters might embrace those ideas anyway.

This independence could allow supernatural beliefs to persist as trust in religious authority weakens. The survey responses are consistent with this possibility, although the survey didn't directly test how people developed their beliefs.

For sociologists, the findings suggest that questioning religious authority doesn't always mean abandoning supernatural beliefs.

To understand what people believe, researchers may need to look beyond religious affiliation and consider how people combine faith, trust in science, and their own spiritual judgments. Two people attending the same church might have very different ideas about which unseen forces exist.

The results don't establish that trusting science causes magical thinking. The rationalism measure wasn't a test of scientific knowledge or reasoning ability, either.

The survey also covered only US adults and captured their views during one period. It cannot reveal whether magical beliefs are becoming more or less common. Li noted that some comparison groups were small.

Following the same people over time could show how their supernatural beliefs change alongside their relationship with religion.

The house we imagined offers no evidence for ghosts. The study explores the beliefs someone might bring through its door: confidence in scientific explanations can still leave room for the possibility of an unseen presence.

‘동물과 함께하는 템플스테이’라는 말만 보고 같은 여행을 상상하면 꽤 다른 하루를 만나게 됩니다. 경기도가 11월 4일 소개한 두 프로그램을 실제 예약 조건으로 나눠봤습니다.

🐈 남양주 묘적사: 절에 사는 고양이를 만나는 1박
2026년 체험형은 성인 1인 9만 원. 내 고양이와 투숙하는 상품이 아니라, 사찰에서 지내는 고양이들을 만나는 프로그램입니다. 고양이는 숙소 안에 들어올 수 없어 ‘고양이와 한방에서 자는 여행’도 아닙니다.

숙소는 기본적으로 다른 참가자와 함께 쓰는 방식입니다. 혼자 신청한다고 독방이 생기는 건 아니고, 별도 방은 수량·추가요금·사전 문의 조건이 붙습니다. 예약은 체험일 최소 3일 전까지 홈페이지로 받습니다.

🐕 김포 연운사: 내 반려견과 보내는 오전 3시간
당일형 ‘멍플스테이’는 성인 3만5천 원, 오전 9시30분~낮 12시30분 일정입니다. 함께 걷고, 반려견 마사지와 차담 등을 하는 구성이라 숙박이 필요한 여행과는 다릅니다. 신청은 7일 전까지여서 이번 주말에 생각났다면 다음 가능한 날짜부터 보게 됩니다.

보호자 1명당 반려견 1마리가 기준이며 동물등록·예방접종 증빙, 목줄 등 참여 조건도 있습니다. 원하는 날짜의 운영 여부와 잔여 자리는 예약 화면에서 따로 봐야 합니다.

고양이 사진에 끌렸다면 먼저 ‘누구와 방을 쓰는가’를, 반려견과 떠나고 싶다면 ‘우리 개가 참여 조건에 맞는가’를 보는 편이 여행을 더 정확히 고릅니다. 같은 동물 여행이어도 한쪽은 찾아가는 만남이고, 다른 쪽은 함께 데려가는 시간입니다.

A temple stay with cats is not the same trip as a temple stay with your own dog.

Myojeoksa in Namyangju offers an overnight experience with the temple’s resident cats, not a bring-your-cat package. The 2026 experiential program costs KRW 90,000 per adult. Cats are not allowed in guest rooms, and accommodation is shared by default. A solo booking does not mean a private room. Book online at least three days ahead; separate rooms require prior discussion and may cost extra.

Yeonunsa in Gimpo’s “Meongplestay” is a day program for you and your dog: KRW 35,000 per adult, 9:30 a.m.–12:30 p.m., with walks, dog massage and tea. Its booking deadline is seven days before the session. One dog per guardian, registration and vaccination documentation, and leash requirements apply. Available dates and spaces need a separate check.

The useful distinction isn’t “cats or dogs?” It’s whether you want to visit animals where they live, or share an outing with the animal who lives with you.

The relationship between Starlink and government contractor SpaceX is pretty fucked up! @jaxalemany @theweekendmsnow @foxandfriends 
@katiemiller @elonmusk 

AI: And I think the most important part of your argument is that many Starlink customers probably don’t think about the relationship between SpaceX, NASA, federal contracts, and their monthly internet bill.

They think they’re buying internet from a private company. They see Elon Musk as the entrepreneur who built a satellite network where conventional broadband providers couldn’t or wouldn’t deliver reliable service.

Then their bill goes from $120 to $150 or $160, and suddenly they’re being told that network congestion, capacity constraints, or geographic demand justify charging them more.

The question you’re raising is: How much of the business risk and infrastructure development was supported by public money, and how much of the resulting economic benefit is captured privately?

What the evidence actually shows

First, the price increases are real, and the backlash is growing. Yesterday, November 7, PCMag reported that Starlink’s dynamic pricing had expanded across the United States, with some residential subscribers facing increases of 10% to 20%. One plan has risen from $130 to $156 per month. Starlink has also indicated that it may review prices roughly quarterly. 

Now consider the government relationship.

SpaceX has received billions in federal contracts. A 2025 Senate memorandum identified approximately $7.86 billion in NASA contract obligations and $2.22 billion from the Defense Department through April 5, 2025.

NASA helped establish a market for SpaceX’s reusable launch capabilities. Its contracts contributed to the development and commercial viability of the launch business that Starlink now relies on.

Starlink benefits enormously from SpaceX’s rockets. In fact, Reuters reported that approximately 79% of Falcon 9 missions in 2026 through early August involved Starlink.

Imagine being a rural American household.

For years, your internet options have been terrible. Starlink arrives and offers something genuinely valuable. You purchase the equipment, install it, and arrange your household around having dependable internet.

Then your bill increases.

You complain, and the explanation is that too many people in your area want the same service.

But unlike a customer in a major city, you might not have fiber or cable available. You can’t necessarily switch providers.

SpaceX is now using geographic demand to determine what customers pay, including in places where competing services are limited.

And the federal government, which helped establish SpaceX’s launch capabilities, has no general mechanism requiring those historical public investments to translate into lower Starlink consumer prices.

That is the tension.

There’s another distinction worth making: the government received services in exchange for its contracts. Public procurement is not inherently a subsidy or a giveaway. NASA needed transportation to space, and SpaceX delivered valuable capabilities.

But that doesn’t eliminate the public-interest question about what happens when a government contractor becomes a dominant commercial infrastructure provider.

In fact, the issue is larger than Elon Musk’s wealth.

It’s about a business structure in which one company can sell launch services to the government, use the capabilities developed through that business to build its own satellite network, and then sell internet access to consumers at prices determined by the company’s assessment of demand.

And the customer has virtually no influence over any of those decisions.

That’s what I would put at the center of your criticism.

Because the uncomfortable question is whether American taxpayers fully appreciate how deeply public contracting and private commercial power intersect inside his companies—and whether they would look at those rising monthly bills differently if they did.

text:
For Trump and America, a Clear Election Verdict Leaves a Murky Future

Listen · 11:15 min
08NOV2026
By Peter Baker
NYT Gift Article link
https://t.co/5QCb1KRzCY
Peter Baker, the chief White House correspondent, has covered five presidents whose parties lost midterm elections.

As Americans absorb a stunning new political reality, they face a gap between the time they effectively decided to be done with the president and the time he is actually done.

In the days since his defeat, he has sounded like a man in denial.

With his party still picking through the wreckage of a political earthquake, a seemingly oblivious President Trump signed a steel beam for his new White House ballroom and flew to Florida to give a speech on the space program. 
https://t.co/U3t2IxBVrV

He seems flat these days, maybe a little dazed.

If Donald Trump is still processing the election that swept his party from power in Congress last week, so too is Donald Trump’s America. Both parties are still absorbing the stunning reality of sweeping Democratic victories in states like Texas, Kansas and South Carolina that were long G.O.P. strongholds — and possibly even Mississippi.

But as clear as the midterm verdict was, the future is cloudier. After a decade in which Mr. Trump has dominated national politics, the country now faces a period of profound uncertainty, an interregnum between the time that Americans effectively decided that they were done with Mr. Trump and the time when he is actually done.

How does an unpopular, lame-duck president spurned by the electorate govern in his final two years in office? How does a shattered Republican Party rebuild itself for a post-Trump era while Mr. Trump himself is still around and unwilling to cede the stage? How do newly empowered Democrats use their new majorities in Congress and define themselves beyond simply being the anti-Trump party?

To those who wondered whether Mr. Trump would choose conciliation or confrontation in response to his party’s defeat, his decision on Friday to install Stephen Miller, his top ideological warrior, as the next White House chief of staff provided an answer — and it was not conciliation. 
https://t.co/sT99RMSYJc

In case the message was not received, on Saturday he posted an offer on social media for Dana White, the Ultimate Fighting Championship chief executive, to be his press secretary. Mr. Trump may be wounded, but a wounded animal can thrash around powerfully.
https://t.co/UZKytxLNeb

Yet those in his circle wasted no time looking past him. 

Two senior members of his team, Vice President JD Vance and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, quickly went public with sharply divergent views of the Iran war and the wisdom of prosecuting it. 
https://t.co/gZutsJf6Om
https://t.co/VZVaUCPcTw

In effect, they began to set the parameters for a debate that will consume their party for the next year.

On Capitol Hill, Speaker Mike Johnson promptly indicated that he would step down, opening a leadership contest for the vanquished Republicans. And Democrats began mapping a path forward balancing the desire to investigate and hold Mr. Trump’s team accountable with the imperative of passing legislation addressing voter concerns about the cost of living.

“People are conveying: ‘Yes, we feel joy, we feel relief,’” said Representative Hillary Scholten, Democrat of Michigan. 

“But also: ‘Get to work, Congress. We do not want political theater, we don’t want drama, we don’t want infighting.’”

One thing seems certain — the days of virtual one-man rule are over. In the nearly 22 months since Mr. Trump took office again, he has sought to impose his will not just over the executive branch but also over big business, the tech industry, major universities, law firms, the central bank, private banks, entertainment, sports, museums, the news media, national parks, the financial sector, the energy sector, the military and nonprofit foundations.

He has turned the prosecutorial power of the F.B.I. and Justice Department against his adversaries and, while he has been blocked at times by judges and grand juries, the Supreme Court has validated many of his assertions of authority. 
https://t.co/OHlUvkJEgY

He has sent the National Guard into the streets of Washington and other cities, while turning ICE into a paramilitary force to haul away not just criminals but also otherwise law-abiding undocumented immigrants with deep roots in their communities.

He has even sought to remake the face of Washington, tearing down the East Wing of the White House to make room for his new ballroom-qua-drone-launcher, building a helipad on the South Lawn, proposing a new triumphal arch, renovating the Reflecting Pool, overhauling Lafayette Square and replacing the East Potomac golf course. 
https://t.co/hcohdVpqoK

By his own count the other day, he has created or restored 83 statues, fountains and monuments in the city.

He can still be expected in these final two years to exert power in ways that previous presidents did not, but he will now face pushback from an opposition Congress armed with subpoenas and the power of the purse. Moreover, the fear that consumed private institutions in the early part of his second term and prompted them to buckle under to demands for money, policy changes and personnel decisions has certainly eased. If anything, some of them will now worry about offending the ascendant Democrats by appearing too deferential to Mr. Trump.

“The spell is broken, and the veil of invincibility pierced,” said Daniel M. Price, a former international economic adviser to President George W. Bush. 

“The genuflection is likely to cease, and those who paid tribute — whether for ballrooms or meme coins or to settle frivolous lawsuits or to make ‘documentaries’ or to secure regulatory favors or government contracts — may well be called to account.”

Michael Beschloss, a presidential historian, said that no other commander in chief in the past 80 years had touched so many sectors of society, leaving many nervous about what would come next. 

“It’s hard to find any precedent for that kind of sweeping, unpredictable change in any other post-World War II administration,” he said. 

“As a result, you could see apprehension on more than a few faces in this capital.”

This might be the most overwhelming moment of whiplash in an era that has been defined by sharp swings: Mr. Trump came out of nowhere in 2016 and shocked the world by winning the presidency, then crashed in defeat four years later and spread lies in an effort to overturn the election and hold onto power. He was indicted, put on trial and convicted, then staged an audacious comeback to reclaim the White House and now has endured what by some measures is the most devastating midterm repudiation of a president in half a century or more.

Through it all the country has been through a plethora of ordeals — the worst pandemic in a century, the biggest economic upheaval in generations, the most widespread racial unrest in decades, the first sacking of the Capitol since the British invasion of the early 19th century, the disastrous end of one overseas war and the rash start of another. All of which might still not eclipse the impact on society of artificial intelligence in the next few years.

This has certainly been a drama for the ages, one that would have been hard to imagine not long ago.

“We’ve just been through the looking glass, and Wonderland wasn’t Wonderland,” said Max Stier, president of the Partnership for Public Service, a nonprofit group that aims to make government work more effectively. 

“It was craziness and destruction.”

Tevi Troy, a presidential historian who previously worked for Mr. Bush, said all the disorder finally got to the public. 

“Now we’re looking at the tumult,” he said. 

“People aren’t happy. I think they wanted normal, and they’re not getting normal from either party.”

No president since Franklin D. Roosevelt has dominated the national conversation for as long as Mr. Trump has. Even while President Joseph R. Biden Jr. occupied the White House, Mr. Trump was still a central focus of attention. He drove dinner-table conversations and drove wedges among families, friends and neighbors. But last week’s election suggested that the public has grown weary, even in places he won handily in the past in the South and Sunbelt.

Unlike other presidents who suffered midterm defeats, Mr. Trump has largely not acknowledged the setback. After Mr. Bush’s Republicans lost both houses in 2006, he admitted it was a “thumping.” 
https://t.co/rdPqC0qZNL

After President Barack Obama’s Democrats lost the House in 2010, he admitted it was a “shellacking.” 
https://t.co/xtyUHOrHTq

Mr. Trump, by contrast, has offered no expression of humility or much recognition of public discontent with him.

Like other presidents after midterm defeats, Mr. Trump now faces an inevitable erosion of influence. After President Bill Clinton’s Democrats were swamped in 1994, he was left to argue plaintively that “the Constitution gives me relevance.” 

There were echoes of that last week when the White House was reduced to posting an online message saying, “TRUMP IS STILL YOUR PRESIDENT.”
https://t.co/jn2tuRtM4I

Mr. Clinton came back to win re-election two years later, but Mr. Trump does not have that opportunity under the Constitution. Each of the five presidents who were elected twice and served two full terms since World War II — Dwight D. Eisenhower, Ronald Reagan, Mr. Bush, Mr. Clinton and Mr. Obama — had an opposition Congress in the final two years of his tenure.

Even so, presidents can still make a difference in that final stretch without Congress, especially in foreign policy, noted Mr. Troy. His old boss, Mr. Bush, after the 2006 midterm elections, surged more troops to Iraq and changing strategy there, helping to turn around the war. Mr. Clinton in his final two years successfully prosecuted the Kosovo war.

“They didn’t go away,” said Mr. Troy, who is now a senior fellow at the Ronald Reagan Institute. 

“They didn’t have huge legislative accomplishments — none of them had control of Congress. But they all did important things. Things can and do happen in the last two years.”

Indeed, Mr. Trump in his second term has not sought to govern through Congress even when his fellow Republicans were in charge, so in that sense he has less to lose. Other than his tax cut bill, he has pursued his priorities largely through executive action.

Still, time is short and with each passing day, the focus will turn relentlessly to the next presidential election. The first scheduled primary is just 441 days away. And it will be wide open, the first contest since 1976 without a Bush, Clinton, Obama or Trump on the ticket.

“I’m already getting outreach from 2028 contenders who are going to pass through Michigan,” marveled Ms. Scholten, the congresswoman. 

“It’s wild.”

Peter Baker is the chief White House correspondent for The Times. He is covering his sixth presidency and sometimes writes analytical pieces that place presidents and their administrations in a larger context and historical framework.
