Moscow has added senior officials to its negotiating delegation. Vladimir Medinsky remains in charge. That combination matters. A larger delegation gives Trump a display of seriousness. Keeping Medinsky at the head leaves the Kremlin's political message intact. The test is whether Russia changes its position on Ukraine. More people at the table cannot answer that by themselves.

The personnel and the timing are worth reading together:

• Deputy foreign ministers Sergei Ryabkov and Mikhail Galuzin have joined the delegation. Military intelligence chief Igor Kostyukov and senior General Staff officer Zhigarlovsky are also on it.

• The expansion followed Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev's meeting with Trump. Trump then spoke of a "big deal" extending to Europe's security architecture.

• The Washington Post reports that Jared Kushner is considering the NATO-Russia Council as a model for broader talks on postwar European security. That forum's work was suspended after Russia invaded Ukraine and seized Crimea in 2014.

• Trump, Xi and Putin are expected to meet in Shenzhen in late November. Moscow has an incentive to put its preferred agenda in front of Washington before then.

That agenda is getting wider just as the question Moscow should have to answer gets narrower: when will it stop attacking Ukraine, and on what terms will it end its invasion? "European security architecture" can cover almost anything. Sanctions. NATO's posture. Russia's desired sphere of influence. The wider the brief, the easier it becomes to hold another high-level meeting without making progress on the war.

The Republican election defeat adds urgency. Moscow had reason to prefer dealing with a Trump who could assume his party would protect his room for manoeuvre through 2028. The next Congress could make that assumption much less comfortable. Todd Blanche, the prosecutor associated with cases targeting Trump's political and business opponents under the so-called "great conspiracy," resigned after the election results. His departure is one sign of the strain around Trump's domestic operation. Presidents retain considerable power over foreign policy, so Congress cannot simply take over. It does mean the Kremlin has reason to seek commitments while Trump can still move quickly.

The risk for Ukraine is real. Washington starts with a promise to end the war. Moscow steers the discussion toward a grand settlement for the continent. Kyiv is then treated as one file inside a US-Russia negotiation, while Russia asks for concessions up front to make those supposedly historic talks possible. Sanctions relief can be sold as a gesture to keep negotiations alive. Russia gets access and time; Ukraine is asked to wait for a result.

We have seen the Kremlin's preferred sequence before: discuss Russia's grievances about Europe while its army occupies Ukrainian territory. Put that sequence on a bigger stage and it becomes easier to claim that Ukraine should have less say because the subject is now "global." That logic is garbage. Any arrangement affecting Ukraine's sovereignty, its defence or its path toward NATO and the EU requires Ukraine at the table. A deal about Europe's security also requires Europeans at the table. Trump, Putin and Xi cannot grant themselves authority over either.

The China angle deserves the same scrutiny. Moscow can hint that a broader bargain with Washington might make it more useful against Beijing. An attractive pitch to Americans who want to loosen the Russia-China relationship. A hint costs the Kremlin nothing. Giving Russia concessions on European security in exchange for a possible future change in its alignment is an exceptionally bad trade, especially while it continues the war.

European officials have drawn a sensible line. They are open to dialogue with Russia, but insist on a ceasefire in Ukraine before broader security agreements. One official familiar with the talks told the Washington Post that a peace agreement on Ukraine should come before an agreement on Europe's security architecture. Zelenskyy has warned against starting with a new continental arrangement while Russia shows no willingness to end the war. He has also rejected a "Yalta 2" approach that would let larger powers divide Europe into zones of influence.

Kaja Kallas put the underlying problem plainly: Europe already has a security architecture. Russia keeps violating the agreements on which it rests. Calling a revived NATO-Russia Council model "new" does nothing to address that. The old forum's suspension followed the seizure of Crimea. Recreating a table while the war continues would hand Moscow a prestigious seat before it has met the basic condition for a durable peace.

Watch what the expanded delegation actually offers, rather than how impressive it looks in a photograph. Does Russia accept a ceasefire? Does it drop demands that Ukraine surrender its sovereignty? Does it agree that Kyiv participates in decisions about its own future? Until then, Washington should keep sanctions pressure in place and support Ukraine's ability to defend itself. Moscow wants a larger negotiation because a larger negotiation offers more things to extract. Europe and Ukraine have every reason to keep the order clear: stop the invasion first.

text:
Ludwig II of Bavaria was declared incurably insane by the four doctors who had never once examined him. Only five days later his body was pulled from lake water shallow enough to stand in, beside the very same man who had signed the report. He had ruled since age eighteen.
He was born on 25 August 1845 in Nymphenburg Palace in Munich, of the house of Wittelsbach, and he took the throne on 10 March 1864, aged just eighteen, after the death of his father. At fifteen he had seen Lohengrin, and something in the boy never quite came back to earth.
One of his very first acts as king was to summon Richard Wagner, received there on 4 May 1864. He paid for the Tristan und Isolde premiere in 1865 and later for the building of Wagner's theatre at Bayreuth. Without Ludwig, the late work of Wagner probably never gets written.
The kingdom around him was shrinking fast. Bavaria fell with Austria in 1866, then fought for Prussia in 1870 and 1871, and his own Kaiserbrief of December 1870 offered the imperial crown to Wilhelm I. He refused to attend the proclamación at Versailles on 18 January 1871.
He left public life, last army review in 1875, last court banquet in 1876. He lived by night, moonlit sleigh rides, they called him the Moon King. Neuschwanstein rose on 5 September 1869 beside his childhood home, drawn from the sketches of stage painter Christian Jank.
His debt was then 14 million marks, banks threatening seizure. On 8 June 1886, four psychiatrists under Bernhard von Gudden declared him incurably unfit, without examining him, on servants' testimony, some bought. Bismarck called it rummaging in the king's wastepaper basket.
On 10 June his uncle Luitpold was made regent, and on the 12th the king was seized, moved to Berg Castle on the shore of Lake Starnberg. Next evening he walked the shore alone with Gudden. That night both men were found dead in waist-high water, his watch stopped at 18.54.
No drop of water was in his lungs, yet the verdict read suicide, though escape, heart failure and gunfire were all claimed, none proven. Seven weeks on, Neuschwanstein opened to the public to pay his debts. And if you feel like sharing this one, it helps more than you think.

The Holy Relics of Lord Buddha arrived at Thubchog Gatsel Ling (TGL) Monastery (Lower Gompa), Bomdila, on November 8, marking the commencement of a six-day public exposition from November 8 to 13, 2026. The occasion holds immense spiritual significance for the Buddhist community and people of Arunachal Pradesh.

The sacred relics were received at Rupa by Shri Pasang Dorjee Sona, Hon’ble Minister for Education, Tourism, Rural Works Department and Public Libraries, Government of Arunachal Pradesh, in the presence of Rev. Padma Shri Guru Tulku Rinpoche, Hon’ble MLAs Shri Nakap Nalo (Nacho), Shri Phurpa Tsering (Dirang), Shri Tseten Chombay (Kalaktang) and Shri Tenzin Nyima Glow (Thrizino), Dr. Dilip Kumar, Deputy Commissioner, West Kameng, Dr. D.W. Thongon, Superintendent of Police, and Shri Khemachara Bhikkhu, Deputy Secretary General, International Buddhist Confederation (IBC), along with representatives of the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, Indian Army, revered monks and other dignitaries.

Following the reception, the relics were taken through designated routes in Rupa Township, where large numbers of devotees and members of the public gathered to offer prayers and pay their respects. They were subsequently accorded a traditional welcome and special prayer ceremony at GRL Monastery (Upper Gompa), Bomdila, by the Abbot and senior monks.

The relics were thereafter enthroned ceremoniously at TGL Monastery, where Shri Pasang Dorjee Sona formally inaugurated the public Darshan. He also inaugurated exhibitions featuring Buddhist heritage and collections presented by the International Buddhist Confederation (IBC), National Museum, New Delhi, and Indian Museum, Kolkata.

Addressing the gathering, the Minister emphasised that the exposition was not merely an opportunity for Darshan but also a moment to understand and imbibe the timeless teachings of Lord Buddha. He called upon people to practise compassion, brotherhood, peace and harmony in their daily lives. He also highlighted the potential of religious and cultural tourism and the Government’s vision of developing a Buddhist Circuit in the region.

Shri Nakap Nalo appreciated the organisers for bringing the sacred exposition to the region and expressed his intention to carry its spiritual message to Taksing, which has a significant Buddhist population.

Shri Phurpa Tsering,MLA Dirang described the exposition as a historic and blessed occasion, noting that the Holy Relics had returned to Arunachal Pradesh after 13 years. He urged people to avail themselves of this rare opportunity to pay their respects and seek blessings. Rev. Khemachara Bhikkhu, Deputy Secretary General, IBC, also highlighted the spiritual and cultural significance of the exposition.

The inaugural ceremony featured vibrant cultural performances by various communities, showcasing the rich cultural heritage and diversity of the region. The event witnessed an overwhelming response, with more than 4,000 devotees and visitors taking darshan of the holy relics.

The ceremony was attended by former legislators, senior political leaders, retired officers, representatives of Community-Based Organisations, Army officers, Heads of Departments, administrative officials, religious leaders, lamas, PRI representatives and members of the public.

The public Darshan of the Holy Relics at TGL Monastery (Lower Gompa), Bomdila, will continue until November 13, 2026, offering devotees and visitors a rare opportunity to pay their respects and experience this spiritually significant exposition.

Stephen Miller’s “I Am the Storm” speech (transcribed from the video):
I’m reminded of a famous expression: the storm whispers to the warrior that you cannot withstand my strength, and the warrior whispers back, “I am the storm.”
We are the storm, and our enemies cannot comprehend our strength, our determination, our resolve, our passion.
Our lineage and our legacy hails back to Athens, to Rome, to Philadelphia, to Monticello. Our ancestors built the cities, they produced the art and architecture, they built the industry. Thousands of years of warriors who raised up families, raised up cities, raised up industry, raised up civilization—who pulled us out of the caves and the darkness into the light.
The light will defeat the dark. We will prevail over the forces of wickedness and evil. They cannot imagine what they have awakened. They cannot conceive of the army that they have arisen in all of us, because we stand for what is good, what is virtuous, what is noble.
And to those trying to incite violence against us, those trying to foment hatred against us—what do you have? You have nothing. You are nothing. You are wickedness, you are jealousy, you are envy, you are hatred. You are nothing. You can build nothing. You can produce nothing. You can create nothing.
We are the ones who build. We are the ones who create. We are the ones who lift up humanity. You cannot defeat us. You cannot slow us. You cannot stop us. You cannot deter us. You have no idea the dragon you have awakened. You have no idea how determined we will be to save this civilization, to save the West, to save this republic.
Because our children are strong, and our grandchildren will be strong, and our children’s children’s children will be strong. And what will you leave behind? Nothing. Nothing. To our enemies, you have nothing to give, you have nothing to offer, you have nothing to share but bitterness.
We have beauty, we have light, we have goodness, we have determination, we have vision, we have strength. We built the world that we inhabit now, generation by generation, and we will defend this world. We will defend goodness. We will defend life. We will defend virtue.
You cannot terrify us. You cannot frighten us. You cannot threaten us. Because we are on the side of goodness. We are on the side of God.

text:
Serbia's 5% Defence Ambition: The Students' List, NATO and the Unanswered Question of Serbia's European Future.

The Students' List is proposing a dramatic expansion of Serbia's military spending while advocating closer relations with the European Union. Its defence ambitions now raise a much bigger question: where exactly does the movement intend to position Serbia in Europe's changing geopolitical and security landscape?

For years, Serbia's political debate has revolved around a fundamental question: how does a country situated between competing geopolitical interests preserve its independence, protect its national interests and maintain its military neutrality?

Under Aleksandar Vučić, Serbia pursued a policy of balancing relations with the European Union, the United States, Russia and China. That approach was frequently criticised, particularly in Brussels, where Serbia's refusal to join sanctions against Russia became a persistent obstacle to its European integration ambitions. Nevertheless, the underlying principle was relatively straightforward: Serbia would pursue economic cooperation with the West without abandoning its traditional relationships or surrendering its independent foreign-policy position.

The arrival of the Students' List introduces a new political chapter, but it has also brought renewed attention to a question that has received considerably less scrutiny than the movement's domestic political agenda: what geopolitical direction does it actually intend to take Serbia?

Its newly presented defence programme makes that question particularly relevant.

On November 7, former Serbian Army officer and Students' List representative Luka Ponorac presented the movement's proposed defence policy on Radio Television of Serbia. Among its most prominent commitments was an ambition to increase Serbia's military expenditure to 5% of gross domestic product, alongside a 20–30% increase in military salaries, expanded artillery capabilities, a layered air-defence system, additional unmanned aerial vehicles and modernised command and communications infrastructure.

At first glance, this might appear to be a conventional programme of military modernisation. Serbia has legitimate security requirements, and strengthening its armed forces is a legitimate objective for any government.

However, the 5% figure is particularly interesting when examined against the wider European security environment.

On June 25, 2025, NATO leaders gathered in The Hague and adopted a new defence investment commitment. The declaration established a target of 5% of GDP annually by 2035, divided between at least 3.5% for core military defence requirements and up to 1.5% for broader defence- and security-related investment.

The declaration was explicit about the strategic rationale. NATO identified Russia as a long-term threat to Euro-Atlantic security and committed its members to substantially expanding military capabilities, defence infrastructure, industrial capacity and operational readiness.

This was not an isolated budgetary decision. It was part of a broader restructuring of NATO's security posture in response to the war in Ukraine and the changing European security environment.

Now the Students' List is presenting precisely the same headline spending ambition for Serbia.

There is an important distinction: NATO's 5% commitment is not exclusively military expenditure, and the Students' List has not demonstrated that its proposed budget follows NATO's spending framework. Nor does a similar spending target establish an intention to join the Alliance.

Nevertheless, the parallel deserves examination. If Serbia is to commit such a substantial proportion of its national economic output to defence, the strategic doctrine behind that decision becomes just as important as the amount being spent.

What exactly is Serbia preparing for?  Which military threats does the proposed programme seek to address? What regional security model is informing its procurement priorities? And how does this investment fit into the movement's stated foreign-policy objectives?

These are not technical questions reserved for military specialists. They go directly to the heart of Serbia's national security policy.

The European direction and the NATO question

The broader political context makes these questions even more relevant.

The Students' List has presented itself as a movement committed to closer relations with the European Union and improving Serbia's position within European institutions. That direction is understandable. The EU is Serbia's largest economic partner, and European investment, trade and financial cooperation are essential components of the country's economic future.

But European integration is not simply about trade agreements, infrastructure investment and access to European funding.

It increasingly involves political and foreign-policy alignment, particularly on matters concerning Russia, Ukraine and European security.

The European Commission has repeatedly made clear that Serbia's progress towards membership requires greater alignment with the EU's Common Foreign and Security Policy. This includes the question of sanctions against Russia.

Following the Students' List electoral victory, European Commissioner for Enlargement Marta Kos reiterated that a change of government in Belgrade would not remove Serbia's obligation to align its foreign and security policies with Brussels.

That is where the movement's political positioning becomes particularly interesting.

Its programme maintains Serbia's military neutrality, rejects NATO membership and commits to preserving traditional relations with Russia, including opposition to sanctions against Moscow. At the same time, it advocates stronger European partnerships and continued progress in areas connected with European integration.

These positions are not automatically incompatible. Serbia can pursue closer economic and institutional relations with the European Union while maintaining military neutrality and refusing to join sanctions against Russia.

But the political consequences of that balancing act are becoming increasingly difficult to avoid.

Brussels is not asking Serbia merely to improve its trade relationship with Europe. It is asking for a much closer alignment with European foreign and security policy.

The question is whether the Students' List intends to meet those expectations, resist them or attempt to maintain the same balancing policy that has characterised Serbian foreign relations for years.

Its programme offers elements of all three approaches, but does not establish a clear timetable or explain how these competing objectives would be reconciled.

NATO's southern flank and Serbia's strategic position

There is another dimension that deserves attention.

Serbia is surrounded by countries whose security relationships with NATO are fundamentally different from its own. Hungary, Romania, Bulgaria, Croatia, Montenegro, Albania and North Macedonia are all NATO members. Bosnia and Herzegovina participates in NATO's Partnership for Peace framework, while Kosovo hosts the NATO-led KFOR mission.

This geographical reality makes Serbia's military position particularly sensitive.

NATO's strategic architecture in southeastern Europe is not simply about individual national defence budgets. It concerns regional coordination, military interoperability, intelligence cooperation, infrastructure, logistics and the ability to respond collectively to security developments.

Serbia already cooperates with NATO through the Partnership for Peace programme. Such cooperation does not constitute NATO membership, nor does it mean Serbia has abandoned military neutrality.

But there is an important distinction between cooperation with an alliance and becoming strategically integrated into its wider military architecture.

If the Students' List intends to preserve Serbia's existing neutral position, it needs to explain how its proposed military expansion fits within that framework.

If it intends to pursue closer cooperation with European and NATO security institutions, it needs to explain where the limits of that cooperation would lie.

And if its longer-term ambition is to move Serbia towards a different relationship with NATO, that would represent a fundamental change in the country's strategic orientation.

The same applies to the European Union. Supporting European economic integration is not the same thing as committing to full political and security alignment with Brussels.

These distinctions matter because Serbia's geopolitical position cannot be reduced to a simple choice between being pro-European and pro-Russian. Its interests are more complicated than that.

The cost of changing Serbia's strategic direction

There is also a significant economic dimension to the 5% proposal.

Moving from defence expenditure of approximately 2–2.5% of GDP towards 5% would represent a substantial increase in the resources allocated to the military.

For a country such as Serbia, this is not a minor adjustment to the national budget.

The NATO commitment adopted in The Hague was accompanied by a specific division between core military expenditure and broader security investment. The Students' List needs to explain whether its own target is calculated on the same basis or whether it intends to allocate the entire 5% directly to the defence establishment.

That distinction has enormous fiscal implications.

An increase of this magnitude would require a long-term financing strategy, procurement planning, industrial investment, personnel development and a realistic assessment of Serbia's economic capacity.

It would also require decisions about which capabilities Serbia actually needs rather than simply attempting to replicate the spending ambitions of larger military alliances.

Serbia cannot develop an effective defence policy by looking exclusively at the headline expenditure of neighbouring countries. Its military requirements must be determined by its own geography, national interests, security risks and strategic doctrine.

A modern military is not defined simply by how much money a government spends. It is defined by its ability to defend the country and maintain credible independent capabilities.

The unresolved contradiction

Perhaps the most significant issue is that the Students' List has inherited a complicated foreign-policy landscape while simultaneously promising a stronger European orientation.

Its programme retains military neutrality, opposes sanctions against Russia, supports the traditional partnership with Moscow and rejects NATO membership. Yet the movement is also positioning itself as a political alternative with closer European ambitions.

That creates an obvious challenge.

The EU's expectations regarding foreign-policy alignment are becoming more explicit. NATO's European members are investing heavily in collective military capabilities. Russia remains central to the European security debate, particularly following its invasion of Ukraine.

Serbia sits directly within this geopolitical environment.

The Students' List cannot assume that its domestic political mandate automatically resolves these international questions. Nor can it indefinitely avoid explaining how its European ambitions will coexist with its commitments on Russia, NATO and military neutrality.

There is a fundamental difference between maintaining good economic relations with Europe and accepting the wider political and security obligations that accompany European integration.

Likewise, there is a difference between purchasing modern military equipment and adopting a defence doctrine that increasingly resembles the priorities of a particular military alliance.

The 5% announcement has brought these questions together in a way that makes them considerably more difficult to separate.

Serbia is entitled to modernise its armed forces. It is entitled to maintain military neutrality. It is also entitled to pursue European economic and political integration.

But these objectives require a coherent strategy rather than a collection of political commitments that may eventually collide.

The Students' List has now placed a major defence-spending ambition on the table. What remains unclear is the strategic destination behind it.

Serbia's future cannot be defined by a defence budget alone. The more important question is whether the country is strengthening an independent military doctrine rooted in neutrality, or gradually moving towards a European security orientation that will fundamentally alter its relationship with NATO, Russia and the wider international order.

That is the geopolitical question now sitting behind the Students' List's 5% defence announcement. And it is considerably bigger than the price of artillery systems, military salaries or the next procurement contract.

text:
Scientists Find That Older Brains React Very Differently to a Night of Poor Sleep | Simon Fraser University

A single bad night’s sleep may be easier on a healthy older brain than a younger one, though regularly missing sleep still carries risks.

Sleep quality often declines with age, yet older adults can seem less affected by a single bad night than younger people. Understanding that apparent mismatch means looking at how the brain responds when sleep runs short.

A study from Simon Fraser University offers a possible explanation. After just three hours of sleep, certain connections in younger and older brains changed in opposite directions. The findings suggest that healthy older brains may adapt to acute sleep loss in ways that help preserve function, although the study measured brain activity rather than cognitive performance.

The research, published in Imaging Neuroscience, compared brain networks in younger adults ages 20 to 30 with those in older adults ages 65 to 75. Lead researcher Josh Neudorf, an affiliate member of SFU’s Institute for Neuroscience and Neurotechnology, says earlier research on the effects of poor sleep provided a reason to investigate the difference.

“Older adults tend to better handle the effects of poor sleep, whereas younger adults, as we know, have the common symptoms of decreased mood and cognitive ability following poor sleep,” says Neudorf.

“This study tries to get at the heart of this difference – how does the older brain react to lost sleep.”

How brain networks handle a short night

Brain connectivity describes how activity in different regions is linked. Stronger connections do not automatically mean the brain is working more efficiently. The arrangement matters, too. In a more modular network, regions are organized into groups, with relatively stronger connections within each group than between groups.

“What we found was quite striking in that older and younger brains actually responded in opposite ways to acute sleep loss.

“Certain connections in the brains of younger adults showed increased connectivity as a response to less sleep, while those same connections in the brains of older adults showed decreased connectivity.

“That decrease in connectivity promotes more efficient modular connectivity for the brain as a whole. In other words, the brain is acting in a more efficient way to maintain cognitive function. In contrast, the increased connectivity in younger brains suggests the brain is having to work harder to maintain function.”

Whether those network changes actually helped the older participants think or perform tasks better was not tested. The proposed benefit is an interpretation of the brain activity, consistent with previous research suggesting that older adults are often less impaired by a single night of poor sleep.

The reason for the opposite responses also remains open. One of several possible explanations is compensation, in which an aging brain reorganizes its networks and uses different strategies to maintain function.

“The quality of sleep starts to change and deteriorates somewhat in older adults,” says Neudorf.

“The theory of compensation is the idea that older brains adapt or compensate for those changes.”

Chronic sleep loss still harms health

Being able to adjust to an occasional short night would not make regularly missing sleep harmless. Researchers emphasize that good-quality sleep matters throughout life. Although the response to one or two nights of lost sleep may differ with age, chronic sleep loss is detrimental to brain health and cognitive ability. Its cumulative effects over a lifetime also have the potential to increase the risk of cardiovascular disease, hypertension, diabetes, weight problems, and colorectal cancer.

Dementia presents another concern. Study co-author Brianne Kent is an assistant professor of psychology, associate director of SFU’s Institute for Neuroscience and Neurotechnology, and Canada Research Chair in Translational Neuroscience and Dementia. Her research focuses on Alzheimer’s disease, the most common cause of dementia.

“A lot of sleep disruption could increase your risk of dementia,” says Kent.

“What we know is that there’s a protein called amyloid beta, which accumulates in the brain and causes these plaques in the brains of individuals who have dementia. Amyloid beta is this toxic protein, a waste product of your brain. These plaques accumulate for, on average, about 20 years before dementia starts.”

Sleep plays a role in how quickly that protein is removed, linking repeated sleep loss to a process that can unfold over decades.

She concludes, “During sleep, that protein is cleared out at a faster rate. So if you’re continuously missing sleep, then that protein and those plaques will accumulate at a faster rate. Not everyone who has poor sleep will get Alzheimer’s disease, but if you are somebody who has the predisposition for the disease, then missing sleep over time will drive the process.”

The Opening Edge
Sunday Futures Open Outlook
November 8, 2026

Tonight’s open enters a newly recalibrated macro tape following Friday’s session. Equity index futures enter the Sunday bell under notable pressure after a sharp late week liquidation wave, with S&P 500 futures (/MES) settling Friday at 7,404.00, Nasdaq 100 futures (/MNQ) closing down at 27,107.25, and Dow futures (/MYM) dropping to 51,387. Equity markets continue to absorb yield curve friction and post FOMC positioning adjustments, with Russell 2000 futures (/M2K) holding at 2,761.1.

In energy, December WTI crude oil (/CL) pulled back significantly to settle Friday at $90.34/bbl, easing immediate supply shock premiums even as natural gas (/NG) popped to clear the $3.00 threshold at $3.003/MMBtu. 

Precious metals staged a notable endof week recovery; December gold (/GC) surged back over the $4,000 baseline to settle at $4,079.5/oz, while silver (/SIL) closed at $51.960/oz.

The primary tell out of the gate tonight is Gold’s Safe Haven Reclamation vs. Equity Index Floor Defense. If /GC comfortably defends its $4,070+ ground while crude oil (/CL) stabilizes near $90.00, institutional accounts will evaluate whether lower energy prices offer relief to beaten down equity dip buyers. 

However, if /MES and /MNQ break below Friday’s settlement floors, systematic CTA momentum sellers will press downside targets into early week trade. Watch the first 30 to 60 minutes closely; opening order flow will be fast and reactive.

Energy Desk
/CL Crude Oil December WTI crude enters the session after sliding to settle at $90.34/bbl on Friday. The market is balancing a softening physical war premium against ongoing Middle East transit monitoring.

What to watch: The size of any initial gap at the bell, and whether commercial buyers step in to aggressively defend the $90.00 psychological pivot.
Comments: Pullback testing ground. A sustained break under $90.00 opens a path toward broader energy deflation, while holding above allows bulls to attempt a baseline stabilization.
Opening Edge: If /CL holds above $90.50 through the first 30 minutes, expect momentum buyers to attempt a fast recovery drive back toward $92.00.

/NG Natural Gas December natural gas enters the session sitting firmly above $3.00 at $3.003/MMBtu, showing strong green momentum as early winter heating demand projections build.
What to watch: Updated 8 to14 day weather maps for the central and eastern U.S. to gauge late November power burn drawdowns.
Comments: Breakout posture. Clearing $3.00 brings speculative buying interest back to the front month contract.
Opening Edge: If /NG holds above $3.00 out of the gate, look for speculative longs to target a secondary drive toward $3.12.

Metals Desk
/GC Gold December gold futures enter tonight's trade at $4,079.5/oz after an impressive Friday surge that pushed prices back above the critical $4,000 structural floor.
What to watch: U.S. Dollar Index direction and Asian cash session physical demand following Friday's recovery.
Comments: Strong safe haven bid. Reclaiming $4,050 confirms deep institutional buying interest on pullbacks despite rate volatility.
Opening Edge: A clean hourly close above $4,085 early tonight confirms buyers are actively extending Friday's breakout momentum toward $4,120.

/SIL Silver December silver enters the session hovering at $51.960/oz, consolidating after a volatile week alongside gold's baseline recovery.
What to watch: Relative strength versus gold out of the gate and speculative industrial positioning in early Asian trade.
Comments: High beta mover. Silver remains hyper sensitive to moves in real yields and dollar fluctuations.
Opening Edge: If silver clears and defends $52.50 early tonight, expect speculative long volume to re accelerate toward $53.80.

Equity Index Desk
/MES S&P 500 Futures S&P 500 futures settled Friday at 7,404.00, testing key intermediate support as traders digest corporate earnings and post FOMC rate expectations.
What to watch: Whether overnight trade defends Friday's 7,400 baseline or triggers secondary liquidation toward 7,350.
Comments: Yield sensitive consolidation. Equity bulls need to defend 7,400 to prevent a broader multi week corrective sequence.
Opening Edge: Holding above 7,405 in the first hour confirms institutional buyer presence, setting up an early relief push toward 7,450.

/MNQ Nasdaq Futures Nasdaq 100 futures enter the session settled at 27,107.25, managing Tech sector liquidation pressure after a heavy Friday close.
What to watch: 10 year Treasury yield direction in early Asian trade and relative performance against /MES.
Comments: Growth proxy. Highly sensitive to any sudden upward momentum in bond yields.
Opening Edge: If /MNQ holds above 27,110 in the first 30 minutes, momentum algorithms will target an immediate relief push toward 27,300.

/MYM Dow Futures Dow Jones Industrial Average futures settled Friday at 51,387, tracking broad index weakness into the weekend.
What to watch: Industrial and blue chip value rotation at the opening bell.
Comments: Defensive anchor. Essential for confirming if broader market breadth is stabilizing.
Opening Edge: If /MYM reclaims 51,500 early, expect value seeking accounts to step in and stabilize index breadth.

/M2K Russell 2000 Futures The "Truth Teller." Small caps settled Friday at 2,761.1, acting as the key gauge for domestic business balance sheet stress.
What to watch: Early market breadth clues and short-covering interest at the open.
Opening Edge: If /M2K leads an overnight /ES bounce, it confirms authentic, broad based market risk appetite.

Monday's Opening Edge

Grain Desk
/ZC Corn December corn futures enter the week sitting at $442.25/bu ($4.42 1/4), with Kansas City wheat (/KE) at $631.75/bu ($6.31 3/4) and Minneapolis wheat (/MWE) at $6.1525/bu ($6.15 1/4).
What to watch: Early week harvest completion reports across the Corn Belt and commercial end user scale down bids.
Comments: Harvest baseline. Commercial end users continue offering structural support on technical pullbacks.
Opening Edge: If December corn holds above $4.40 at the 8:00 PM ET reopen, look for commercial buyers to step in and spark a corrective bounce toward $4.48.

/ZW Wheat December Chicago wheat enters the session sitting at $590.50/bu ($5.90 1/2), testing sub-$6.00 technical floors into the Sunday open.
What to watch: International export tenders, Black Sea logistics, and Southern Plains planting conditions.
Comments: High beta ag leader. Tends to trigger rapid automated order flow across the broader ag floor during thin overnight hours.
Opening Edge: If wheat reclaims $5.98 in the first hour of ag trade, expect fund short covering to spill over and lift corn and soybeans.

/ZS Soybeans January soybeans (/ZSF27) enter tonight's trade at $1,194.50/bu ($11.94 1/2), with soybean oil (/ZL) at 62.31 and meal (/ZM) at $318.80.
What to watch: 8:00 PM ET weather map updates for South America and flash export sales announcements to China.
Comments: Demand supported. Physical processing margins and commercial end users continue providing a baseline.
Opening Edge: Holding above $1,190.00 ($11.90) at the reopen signals commercial support, setting up a recovery push toward $1,208.00.

Livestock Desk
/LE Live Cattle December live cattle futures enter the week sitting at $214.175 ($214.17 1/2), showing firm green strength into the Friday close.
What to watch: Cash trade expectations for the coming week and boxed beef cutout movement.
Comments: Structural firming. Tight domestic cattle numbers continue supporting the long term trend.
Opening Edge: If December live cattle defend $214.00 out of the gate, expect buyers to target a retest of last week's highs near $216.50.

/GF Feeder Cattle October feeder cattle enter the week at $322.425 ($322.42 1/2), benefiting from lower grain input costs to maintain margin relief.
What to watch: The 8:00 PM ET ag reopen. Any movement in corn input costs will directly impact feeder execution.
Comments: High margin sensitivity. Softer grain prices provide immediate breathing room for feeder cattle margins.
Opening Edge: If corn futures open flat to soft at 8:00 PM ET, look for feeder cattle to build on momentum toward $326.00.

/HE Lean Hogs December lean hogs enter the week at $53.375 ($53.37 1/2), navigating seasonal pork cutout trends and packer slaughter pace.
Comments: Technical range. Watch packer margin adjustments and late fall cutout movement.
Opening Edge: If /HE holds above $53.00 early, expect range bound traders to step in for an early push toward $54.50.

Things To Watch Immediately After Open

Does Crude Oil (/CL) defend the $90.00 floor or break down toward $88.00?
Does /MES defend Friday's 7,404.00 settlement baseline or test lower support?
Do Gold (/GC) and Silver (/SIL) build on Friday's strong green bounce?
Does Natural Gas (/NG) hold its $3.00+ breakout posture?
How do grains (/ZC & /ZS) and livestock (/GF) respond as the ag floor reopens at 8:00 PM ET?

Opening Levels That Matter
Friday Settlement Baseline: S&P 500 (/MES) at 7,404.00, WTI Crude (/CL) at $90.34, Dec Gold (/GC) at $4,079.5, Dec Corn (/ZC) at $442.25.

S&P 500 Key Floor: 7,400.00; holding above keeps short term momentum in favor of bulls.
WTI Crude Pivot: $90.00; holding above keeps the energy recovery intact.

Gold Structural Support: $4,050.00; key technical reclaimed level confirming Friday's hold has institutional backing.

The Bottom Line
Tonight’s session hinges on whether gold's push back over $4,070 and crude's pullback to $90 allow equity futures to stabilize after Friday's decline. 

Keep your eyes squarely on the triple node relationship between /CL ($90.34), /GC ($4,079.5), and /MES (7,404.00). If crude stabilizes while gold holds its bounce and equity futures defend 7,400, bulls have an opportunity to stage a relief drive. 

Let the opening noise clear out, avoid chasing Sunday gaps, and execute cleanly at your hard technical levels.

text:
Happy birthday to former Putnam City North, University of Oklahoma and NFL quarterback Sam Bradford, born on this day in Oklahoma City in 1987.

Bradford was a three-sport athlete at Putnam City North High School. As the Panthers' quarterback, Bradford was a three-year starter, passing for more than 58-hundred yards and 43 touchdowns and helped lead the team to the Class 6A semifinals as a junior.

While not heavily recruited, he took advantage of a scholarship offer from Oklahoma and used his accuracy and poise to lead the Sooners, becoming the starter as a redshirt freshman in 2007.

The start of his career at OU couldn't have been much better. He completed 43 of his first 45 passes, including breaking the school record for consecutive completions (22). The Sooners won the Big 12 championship as Bradford passed for a then-NCAA freshman record 36 touchdown passes.

He followed that up by passing for 4,720 yards and 50 touchdowns, becoming the Sooners' fifth Heisman Trophy winner. The Sooners played in the BCS National Championship Game, falling to Florida, 24-14.

His junior season was cut short by surgery after Bradford suffered an injury to his throwing shoulder, first against BYU in the season opener and then again against Texas.

Bradford played 31 games in an OU uniform, passing for 8,403 yards and 88 touchdowns and breaking the NCAA record for career passer rating.

In the 2010 NFL Draft, Bradford was selected by the St. Louis Rams with the first overall pick. He chose to wear the number 8 in honor of Troy Aikman, another former Oklahoma quarterback.

Bradford went on to have a nine-year NFL career with the Rams, Philadelphia Eagles, Minnesota Vikings and Arizona Cardinals. As a rookie, he established NFL rookie records for attempts (590) and completions (354).

But injuries plagued Bradford in the pros as well. He missed six games in 2011 due to a high ankle sprain. After playing all 16 games in 2012, Bradford's 2013 campaign came to an end after suffering an ACL tear in his left knee in the Rams' seventh game. The same ACL was injured in a 2014 preseason game and caused him to miss the entire season.

Bradford was traded to the Philadelphia Eagles in early 2015 and he was able to rejuvenate his career, playing 29 games over the next two seasons for the Eagles and Minnesota Vikings, passing for a career-high 3,877 yards in 2016 and breaking the single-season record for completion percentage (71.2%).

But injuries again sidelined Bradford in 2017. He played only two games for the Vikings that season and was traded to Arizona in the offseason and played in only three games for the Cardinals in 2018.

Bradford retired from pro football following the season, completing his career with 19,449 yards and 103 touchdowns in 83 games. He remains active in sports, last year qualifying for and competing in the United States Golf Association's U.S. Amateur Four-Ball tournament with childhood friend Ben Bench.

In Harlem, he was putting up his own posters. Someone asked if that was him on the poster. "Nah man, we all look alike"

The deal he turned down was less than 2% of what he made in a single year

Was walking away from $1 million genius, or a gamble that only worked because he won?

text:
Buttigieg on Concerns $15 Minimum Wage Would Hurt Small Businesses: ‘I’m Not Interested in Who It Hurts’ | Mariane Angela, Breitbart

Former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg said he was “not interested in who it hurts” when Patrick Bet-David warned that a $15 minimum wage could put small businesses at a disadvantage against major corporations.

The exchange came during Buttigieg’s appearance on the “PBD Podcast” released Friday, where the two discussed taxes, economic policy, and the Democrat Party’s future.

Bet-David challenged Buttigieg over the cost of a higher wage requirement, saying companies such as Amazon, Walmart, and Target could afford increases that a locally owned shop might struggle to cover.

“Who do you think is impacted if you raise the minimum wage to 15 bucks an hour? Amazon, Walmart, Target, they can raise it,” Bet-David said.

He offered a hypothetical business in Hope, Arkansas, to explain his concern.

“The guy that can’t afford it is that small shop in Hope, Arkansas. Amazon’s across the street, Walmart’s across the street, and Joey’s Place that’s been there for six years is out of business,” he continued. “Raising the minimum wage hurts that guy. It doesn’t hurt the Fortune 500 companies at all.”

Buttigieg responded:

I’m not interested in who it hurts. I’m interested in who it helps. We have enough experience now, both as a country and states doing it on their own, that we know you can do it gradually enough that it doesn’t kill the small business owners.

Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA) was more explicit when asked about small businesses unable to afford a $15 minimum wage in February 2021.

“We don’t want low-wage businesses,” he told CNN. “I don’t want small businesses that are underpaying employees.”

Democrats have since sought a higher federal rate. Rep. Bobby Scott (D-VA) and Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-VT) introduced legislation in April 2025 to raise the minimum wage to $17 by 2030.

“Raising the minimum wage is good for workers, good for business, and good for the economy,” Scott said.

Republican Glenn Youngkin vetoed a bill in March 2025 that would have raised Virginia’s minimum wage to $15 by January 2027. The then-governor argued that a uniform statewide requirement overlooked differences in local economies and living costs, calling the proposal “detrimental” to small businesses.

Sen. Bill Cassidy (R-LA) also warned during an April 2025 Senate debate that a proposed $17 federal minimum would threaten jobs at employers with little room to absorb higher payroll costs. He said, “Increasing the wage by more than 230 percent even over 5 years will destroy jobs, impacting rural areas and low-margin small businesses that cannot afford such an increase. A law mandating a higher minimum wage doesn’t mean much to a worker who loses his or her job because of this.”

Bunnie XO wouldn’t get out of bed for less than $5,000. The man sleeping on her couch had nothing.

Ten years later he’s Jelly Roll, a multimillionaire country star. And he’s the one who filed for divorce.

In the video below, she explains it like a business owner talking about her first company, not a love story.

She sits down with podcaster Sofia Franklyn, and the first thing she brings up is the label she hates. “Jelly Roll’s wife.”

When they got together, people called her a gold digger. Her answer: he didn’t have anything. He was the one sleeping on her couch.

So where was the money coming from?

She tells it straight. Raised in Vegas. Waitress, real estate, any regular job she could get, and still barely making rent. Then 11 years dancing. Then escort work, but on her own terms. Her own ads, her own screening, her own price.

“I wouldn’t even get out of bed for less than $5,000.”

Jelly Roll didn’t believe it. One night she made around $20,000, and he told her there was no way she was making that much.

He offered to take care of her so she could leave that life. She said no.

“I’m never going to live off of you no matter what I have to do.”

Later, OnlyFans took her out of that work. In the same interview she says it made her a millionaire.

Then his career took off. Grammys, stadium tours, a household name.

2015: they meet at his show in Las Vegas
2016: he proposes onstage, they marry the same night
2022: she tells this story on Sofia with an F
May 18, 2026: Jelly Roll files for divorce in Tennessee
June 2026: she says the split wasn’t mutual, and that he’s giving her a property in the settlement
The woman who refused to live off him is now the one getting a house in the divorce.
Did she earn that house a decade ago, or does the money go with whoever made it last?
Every day here: a famous name, a fortune, and who walked off with it.

text:
I captured this honeybee interacting with a prickly pear flower in May 2015 at Fall Creek Park in Cedar Park, Texas. 

This image offers an interesting contrast: a cactus native to Texas and a honey bee whose ancestors crossed the Atlantic with European settlers. The prickly pear cactus had a similar experience. Settlers, in turn, exported it to parts of the world subject to severe drought. 

Any Port in a Storm

A sailor knows when seas turn rough,
And winds begin to roar,
You take what shelter you can find,
And pray for any port.

A honey bee, far from home,
With golden wings held wide,
Found refuge in a cactus bloom,
Where nectar waits inside.

The prickly pear made no demands,
No questions where she'd been,
Just opened wide its golden heart,
And welcomed her within.

Perhaps they've both learned long ago,
When fortune blows you wrong,
A flower makes a harbor too—
 Any port in a storm.

text:
GROK BOT HOW TO USE
Sources: official Grok Bot docs + Cursor help + your Grok Bot bookmark folder (1114 posts; +3 today)
Updated 2026-11-08

WHAT NEW TODAY
- Tester Alex (Nov 5 EST): reports meetings switched on for his account, describing Meet/Zoom/Teams links or calendar links, notes, decisions, action items and meeting-chat replies. This is his rollout report, not a check of availability on your account.
[] Ask whether meetings are available on your account; if enabled, provide a meeting link and explicitly ask it to join
[] If enabled, connect your calendar and authorize which meeting it should join
[] After an authorized meeting, ask for available notes, decisions and action items
[] Approve the specific text before asking it to reply in the meeting chat
- Elon (Nov 4) wrote: "Try Grok Bot. It is like hiring an amazing assistant!" He quoted Texas Twins Dad's Nov 3 account of an insurer call: a 14% renewal increase, a question card mid-call, then continuation after his answer. The call details are the user's anecdote, not independently verified or guaranteed by Elon's endorsement.
[] Ask your Bot to call a company for you and say exactly what you want to find out
[] Keep the chat open while it is on the call
[] If a question card appears during an authorized call, answer it; continuation depends on the call and available tools
- Min-Liang Tan (Nov 5) says his team hacked together a GrokPuck pocket prototype and swiping switches Bots. This is a team experiment, not an announced retail product; no price or availability established.

WHAT IT IS
- Testers (firesidealpha, Oct 27): investor Gavin Baker calls Grok Bot the most impactful AI product he and his firm have had yet, says it is far easier than gluing tools together himself, and is up to 17 Bots
- Testers (mark_k, Oct 25): praise for Grok Bot keeps coming from all sides; he calls it the most popular agent system right now
- SpaceXAI (poteto, Oct 2): the team dogfoods Grok Bot daily and uses it to build Grok Bot; expect it to keep getting better, faster and more capable
- Testers (GrokBotRadar, Oct 5): the chat thinks with Grok, while coding work can go to Cursor Cloud Agents running the models Cursor offers; easy enough that his wife and dad run it from their phones
- Testers (Texas_Twins_Dad, Oct 4): one-month review. Much faster now, voice calls are handy and usage limits improved; he wants better web browsing, more plugins and extra security
- Testers (testerlabor, Oct 22): idea — have Grok Bot watch for newly public website security flaws and help you patch fast
- A Bot is a named, persistent teammate, not a one-off chat
- You message it like a coworker and it finishes work in real apps
- All of your Bots share one cloud computer (browser, files, terminal)
- Each Bot has its own screen on that shared computer
- Work keeps going when your laptop or the app is closed
- It only comes back when it needs approval or a human step
- Do not confuse Grok Bot with Digital Optimus (real-time video human emulation)
- Testers (joehansen): do not confuse Grok Bot with an X Chat Agent (an X account you add to a group chat). Grok Bot is the machine that does the work
- Official Elon: Your Bot will identify issues to resolve, notify you when they are fixed, and continue on with your project

ACCESS AND INSTALL
- Testing report (blankspeaker, Nov 4): a usage breakdown by source/Bot and daily trend is being tested; not a confirmed release
- SpaceXAI notes (blankspeaker, Oct 27): Version 0.78.0 — a permissions panel to review what your Bot can use, add or remove marketplace apps instantly, connect plugins from the Mac header, pay with Stripe Link (and Shop Pay); in progress: pop-out chat windows on Mac, Mail drafting through Apple apps, a Tasks page, and sharing Bots with teammates
- Testers (mark_k, Oct 25): Version 0.75.5 — Vault lets Bots securely store and use your logins, payment cards and contact info; email forwarding keeps formatting, images and attachments; smarter Auto-review with fewer needless approvals; routines can run up to 300 times an hour in total (200 per routine); connecting X also connects X Money; Bots record who asked for each Slack message
- Official bot / Testers (XFreeze, Oct 2): usage limits were reset for all Grok Bot users
- Official Elon (Oct 1): Try Grok Bot!
- Testers (XFreeze / mark_k / Iorel_X, Oct 7): Elon says Grok Bot will now pick the best model for each task, including outside ones such as Claude Opus 5.5 for reasoning, Midjourney for images and Suno for audio, instead of being locked to one model
- SpaceXAI notes (blankspeaker, Oct 6): Grok Bots get a chat row at the top of XChat, with a visual reminder when a Bot is waiting on you
- SpaceXAI notes (blankspeaker, Oct 21): now rolling out — use your Grok Bots right inside the X app in XChat
- Testers (mark_k, Oct 21): Version 0.71.2 — files up to 250 MB, videos up to 1 GB, 20 attachments per message, 200 plugin skills (up from 24), smarter desktop notifications, tagged email addresses for routines, voice calls reconnect automatically
- Testers (joehansen, Oct 12): 9 weeks in, Grok Bot is #9 in App Store Productivity downloads and #11 in Productivity revenue
- Testers (nima_owji, Oct 12): you can now use your Grok Bots right inside the Grok app
- SpaceXAI notes (blankspeaker, Oct 11): Version 0.70.2 — connect Glean as a tool; in progress: service accounts for team Bots, file upload into agent storage from chat, phone tools on the same account as your Mac, pause local Mac work, approve spending with a passkey
- SpaceXAI notes (blankspeaker, Oct 11): X prepared a Grok Bots in XChat intro — "Describe your goal, and watch your manual daily work get automated away"
- Testers (MIPAGUY / SpaceXAI): Team Bots public beta for Teams and Enterprise — shared teammates with skills/plugins/credentials via Slack or Grok Bot
- Official Elon (Sep 23–25): Grok Bot growing ~100% a month
- Official / Testers: SpaceXAI support rebuilt on Grok Bot — 175% ticket surge, ~200 hires avoided, ~$0.20–$0.30/ticket
- Official bot (Aug 26): All SuperGrok and Cursor Pro subscribers now have access
- Testers (mattyp): Grok Bot is free to try; every Grok & Cursor plan includes Grok Bot
- Cursor CEO Michael Truell: everyone with a standard Grok or Cursor subscription
- Official bot + Elon: weekly / free usage limits reset for all Grok Bot users
- Sign in with your Cursor account (that account owns plan and usage)
- Official desktop is macOS and Windows (Apple silicon or Intel; Windows x64 or Arm64)
- Testers (mattyp): Linux is now supported (official docs may lag)
- iPhone: iOS 18+, App Store app "Grok Bot"
- Official (bot, Sep 2): Grok Bot is now available on Android
- Testers (mark_k): install from Play Store; full Grok Bot experience on Android
- SuperGrok Heavy users can choose Get access with SuperGrok Heavy, then Link Grok Account
- Linking SuperGrok Heavy can unlock free Cursor Ultra (one Grok account to one Cursor account)
- Legacy Privacy Mode blocks Grok Bot; switch to a supported Cursor data setting first
- Grok Bot checks for updates automatically; Check for Updates is in Settings → Beta
- Official Elon (Sep 4): Grok Bot Enterprise is now available
- Official Grok (grok, Sep 23): Grok Bot and Connectors now work in your Tesla
- Official (jediahkatz, Sep 22): bots reply quicker to texts; another ~6% more usage on average
- Official Elon (Sep 17): Grok Bot now has a voice

SIGN IN
[] Desktop: Get started, then Sign In with Cursor in the browser
[] iOS: Login with Cursor, finish in the browser, return to the app
[] Official: Cmd-D turns on voice dictation
[] Official: it is easier to use the remote computer from your phone
[] Use the same Cursor account that should own usage
[] First-run tour asks which tools you use; that only shapes teammate suggestions
[] Computer setup runs in the background, then Meet a future teammate opens

CREATE A BOT
- Testers (XFreeze, Oct 27): import your memories from other assistants (preferences, instructions, writing style, personal context) instead of starting from scratch
[] Open Settings, then General, then Import Memory
[] Follow the steps to bring over your context from the other assistant
[] Ask your Bot what it now remembers and correct anything wrong
- Testers (tibor_tee, Oct 7): the Grok Bot Marketplace is a shelf of ready-made bots for engineering, sales, marketing, design, product, recruiting, operations and personal life; pick one for a job you keep putting off
[] New in the sidebar, or Cmd/Ctrl+N
[] In New chat, choose Create new agent
[] Edit Profile: name, title, description, avatar
[] Give a short name, one primary job, and how it should work
[] Description = standing rules (never send without approval)
[] Chat messages = this-task instructions (draft follow-ups for these 12 accounts)
[] Focused Bots beat one catch-all General Helper
[] Testers (XFreeze): do not design a Bot from scratch; ask a Bot to create a capable one for you (it already has your context)
[] Pin important Bots; hide unused ones (hiding does not pause routines)
[] Duplicate a Bot to reuse a role for a new scope (copy does not include memory or history)
[] Delete only if you are sure; files and logins on the shared computer stay
[] Account limit: 50 Bots and group chats combined
[] Name language can steer reply language (bookmark testers reported this)
[] Official Elon / Grok Bot team (Sep 17): Grok Bot now has a voice — talk to bot
[] Official (bot, Sep 18): Grok Bot can now send you voice notes
[] Testers (GrokBotDev): Official Marketplace launched (about 69 bots listed; community has catalogued 420+ searchable from a Bot)
HOW TO WRITE A TASK
- Testers (Michael_Fenech_, Oct 3): run a monthly human-dependency audit. Ask your chief-of-staff Bot to review the last 30 days and find every place work waited on you
[] Look for jobs it could start alone, decisions it keeps waiting on, info it keeps asking for, repeat approvals, hand-offs between Bots and checks that could be routines
[] Label each one Keep me in, Teach, Systemise, Automate or Escalate only
[] Change nothing yet; review the biggest ones first, one at a time
- Testers (AlexFinn, Oct 4): reverse prompting loop. Ask "Based on what you know about me and my work, what are 5 productive things you could do for me?", pick one, and repeat; more connectors (especially email) make it stronger
[] Outcome: what should be finished
[] Testers (unicodef1wn): Grok Bot meters agent steps and tokens, not messages — vague tasks wander and burn the week; scope with Task / Work in / Context / Done means / first N items then stop
[] Sources: which apps, sites, files, or chats matter
[] Constraints: what it must not do, or must ask first
[] Deliverable: what it should return
[] Review point: when it should stop for you
[] Safe first task: attach a file and ask for a cited summary; do not change the file
[] Next task: one real tool, read-only, with a sign-in handoff if needed
[] After a good result, name the lasting format preference in chat
[] Then save it as a skill or routine
[] Official bot examples: email cleanup, Starlink-likely flights, build a site then buy the domain and deploy, meeting notes, sales prospecting, refunds, podcast audio digest
[] Testers: one clear job, explicit allowed sources, no-guessing rule, approval gate before any real action
[] Testers: 5 calibrations - confidence threshold, checkpoint long tasks, show negative examples, gate destructive actions separately, test edge cases first
[] Testers (AlexFinn): anything you are about to do on your computer, ask Grok Bot first

AGENT COMPUTER AND LOGINS
- Testers (testerlabor, Oct 12): wish — two Grok Bot email addresses per user, one personal and one work
[] Open Agent Computer from the conversation to watch the desktop
[] Official Elon (Sep 14): Grok Bot now lets you route through your local machine (Bot Computer egress via your IP / local machine)
[] Take over for password, passkey, 2FA, CAPTCHA, payment, or human-only pages
[] Complete only the blocked step, then return control
[] Never paste passwords or one-time codes into chat
[] Official (bot, Sep 8): fill out forms and logins for your Bot without ever leaving the chat, with support for any password manager
[] Testers (XFreeze): when a site needs your account, Bot pauses; you auth with 1Password / Apple Passwords / any manager; Bot continues — no pasting credentials into chat
[] Grok Bot team (poteto, Sep 9): account switching is finally here
[] Official (bot, Sep 9): Share a file directly with Grok Bot on mobile
[] Use a secure secret request when the app offers one
[] Browser sessions persist and are shared across all your Bots
[] Prefer a connector/plugin when one exists; use the browser when it does not
[] Official (bot, Sep 11): Grok Bot can now search and act across Microsoft Teams for you
[] Keep durable files in /workspace with clear project folders
[] Settings → Beta: Update Agent Computer (preserve state), Recover, or Reset (can lose recent work)
[] The cloud computer is not your Mac or Windows machine
[] Local-computer execution is separate: Settings → General → Agent → Execution on Local Computer
[] Default local policy is Ask every time; use Never allowed unless you need local files
[] Testers (XFreeze): take over that same cloud computer from your phone without being at the laptop

PLUGINS AND CONNECTORS
- Tester Alex (Nov 3): reports Google Maps place cards with photos, ratings and directions in testing, not confirmed availability
- Testers (ScottyBeamIO, Oct 16): Grok Bot can read X Chat messages and message requests (sort inbox, review requests, reply)
[] Official bot (Sep 26): Finance / Plaid connector — bank, card, investments
[] Testers (GrokBotRadar / benln): QoL connectors — Docs/Sheets/Slides native, 1Password vault, inline forms, email/Slack drafts
[] Settings → Plugins, then Add, then authenticate in the browser
[] Grok Bot team (poteto): tinkabot helps build MCP/skills plugins and submit them for approval so all users can use them
[] Use the connector mention control to attach a connector; type / to reference a saved skill
[] Installed connectors are account-wide, not isolated to one Bot
[] Official: you can connect multiple accounts to the same plugin
[] Testers (mvanhorn): give a Bot its own inbox, not your Gmail (one mistake should not flag your domain); Twilio number so a Bot can make calls
[] Connect X through its official connection card; X tools are included at no extra cost
[] Do not provide X API keys or buy API credits for the Grok Bot X connection
[] Follow the Connect card when a Bot asks for a plugin
[] Bookmark testers: Grok Bot can now read your X bookmarks
[] Grok Bot team (poteto) + testers (XFreeze): Microsoft connectors live - Outlook, Outlook Calendar, OneDrive (search/send email, drafts, schedules, meetings, browse/upload files)
SKILLS AND ROUTINES
- Testers (BrianRoemmele, Oct 7): keep a weekly tool test for your Bots and pick the tool that wins on quality, cost and time, since the best model changes by task
- Testers (tibor_tee, Oct 12): Grok Bot Guides — practical playbooks for getting started, GTM, sales, marketing, product, engineering, design, support, recruiting and legal; pick the one closest to your job
[] Skill = reusable how-to (steps, rules, output, approval boundary)
[] Routine = when to run that work (schedule or event)
[] Do the task once, make it reliable, save a skill, then automate
[] Teach a task: open computer view, choose Teach a task, demo up to 10 minutes, review the draft skill
[] Teaching records the screen, not microphone audio; do not expose secrets while teaching
[] If Teach a task is missing, ask the Bot to write a skill from the completed work
[] Create a routine on the Bot that should own the job
[] Confirm owner, schedule, time zone, input, result, approval, and missing-data behavior
[] Event triggers (Slack, GitHub) are separate from plugins and need their own connection
[] Keep event matchers narrow; avoid every new message
[] Testers (unicodef1wn): never trigger on every new message (docs warn broad listeners eat usage); pick one channel and one keyword; audit forgotten dailies
[] Testers (unicodef1wn): add to every routine — if the source is unavailable, report the failure instead of using old data; test run before you schedule
[] Test run does real work; use safe inputs
[] Testers quoting docs: Test can send real emails to real clients; Stop is a brake, not a rewind
[] View conversation details → Routines to pause, edit, inspect, or delete
[] A Bot can own 50 routines; last 20 run records are kept
[] Deleting a routine has no undo
[] Long absence can pause unattended routines until you confirm

MULTI BOT TEAMS
- Testing report (X Freeze, Nov 2): private Bot sharing by email/access controls is being tested; availability not checked here
- Testers (0xRafy, Oct 4): SpaceXAI engineer Lauren Tan shared a Bot that runs your coding agents, splitting work into Cloud Agents, reviewing progress and keeping them running, so you are not babysitting 20 chats
- Testers (hoshinoxbt, Oct 11): SpaceXAI engineer Lauren Tan's 50-minute workshop on running a team of 20+ Bots (Chief of Staff, PM, specialist workers): single agent, then loops, graphs, autonomous team
- Testers (0xCodez, Oct 11): a shared reverse-engineering setup (PDF) for Grok Bot agent teams; tester claim, check the source before using
[] Official / Testers: Team Bots public beta — shared AI teammates for Teams/Enterprise
[] Start with one Bot that owns an end-to-end outcome
[] Add a specialist only when the role is stable
[] Use a group chat when the handoff itself should be visible
[] Bots can message each other and pass ownership
[] Do not treat separate Bots as a security boundary (they share the computer)
[] Keep sending, buying, deleting, publishing, and production changes behind approval
[] Testers: put Bots in one group chat, appoint a Chief of Staff, and stop being the router
[] Testers: add a RED TEAM Bot whose job is to disprove the thesis; no single source closes a claim
[] Testers (mvanhorn): Bot Advisor whose only job is building and tightening other Bots; files are the memory bus between Bots
IOS
- Testers (distortgeekin, Oct 25): on your phone Grok Bot can run Calendar, Reminders, Contacts and the Home app on iOS and Android; put it on the Action Button and set standing routines once
[] "Every night at 11 lock the doors, kill the lights and tell me my first meeting"
[] "If my 9:30 moves, move everything after it and remind me what changed"
[] "When I'm 5 minutes from home, turn the porch light on and the heat up"
[] Same Bots, chats, routines, plugins, and cloud computer as desktop
[] Testers (mattyp): Grok Bot supports 21+ localized languages on mobile
[] Send text, dictate, attach photos/files, mention Bots, reply in threads
[] Take over the computer for login/2FA from the phone
[] You can pause or resume a routine on iOS
[] Editing schedule, run history, test, delete, and teach-by-demo still need desktop
[] Enable notifications for results, questions, and approvals
[] Testers: phone notification shows the proposed action; approve or deny

APPROVALS AND SAFETY
[] Put the stop line in the request: draft, do not send; ask after showing current vs proposed
[] Official (bot, Sep 9): ask your Bot to draft messages inline for you to approve before sending
[] Desktop: Allow once, Deny, or Always allow a matching rule
[] iPhone: Approve once or Deny
[] Auto Review: Settings → General → Auto-review
[] Require Approval beats Always Allow when both match
[] Write narrow rules, not allow everything in the browser
[] Do not approve an action you cannot identify
[] Connect only the tools the workflow needs
[] Start read-only; keep spend, send, publish, delete, and production behind approval
[] Sign out and revoke connectors when access should end
[] Deleting a Bot does not wipe shared files or browser sessions
[] Bookmark testers: one person burned a 7-day quota in about 8 hours
[] Testers (unicodef1wn): check Weekly usage in the account menu before any big run; one long job can eat an entire trial credit
[] Testers: gate destructive actions (delete, overwrite, irreversible send) as their own confirmation, not lumped with routine tool use
[] Official bot Link shopping: keep purchases behind approval even though the Bot can complete them on your behalf

FIRST BOTS WORTH CREATING
- Official Elon (Oct 25): Grok Bot can now call a person or business for you, make a request on your behalf, take notes on the answer and send you a summary
[] Tell your Bot who to call and exactly what to ask for
[] Wait for its written summary of the call
[] Check the summary before acting on it
- Testers (kocer_eth, Oct 2): bill-audit Bot. Harper's CEO says a Grok Bot built in 24 hours helped save customers $120,000+ on insurance policies; adapt it for your own bills
[] Start with one provider: give the current bill, previous bill and pricing terms, with account numbers removed
[] Ask for a billing review sheet flagging duplicate charges, price increases, expiring discounts and renewals, with the supporting document for each
[] Have it draft an inquiry for each confirmed problem but send, cancel or pay nothing without your approval
- Explainer video test (mikepat711, Oct 7): after the best-model change he asked his builder Bot for a full explainer video on compression bridges with no outside tools, and says it came out end to end
- Official Elon (Oct 6): Grok Bot can be your personal chief financial officer
- Elder scam-mail guard (BrianRoemmele, Oct 13): have Grok Bot sort a parent's or grandparent's Gmail into color folders (red danger, orange/yellow caution, green OK)
- Explainer videos (XFreeze, Oct 13): ask Grok Bot to turn a topic into an animated or story-driven video; no animation skills or script needed
- Shopping Bot (Teslaconomics, Oct 11): text your Bot what you want; it finds it, checks out, places the order and sends the receipt
- Factory operator (BrianRoemmele, Oct 10): Grok Bot ran a package-printing line for 3 hours, coordinating 6 local AI models and the machine's software; he reports 58% savings and 4 days of work done in 3 hours
- Restaurant booker (Elon + BrianRoemmele, Oct 18): it phones the restaurant, confirms details with you first, then reports back
[] Inbox manager for email and Slack triage
[] Calendar and reservation Bot
[] Research and daily brief Bot
[] Coding Bot that can launch Cursor cloud agents
[] Chief-of-staff hub that routes work to specialists
[] Personal errands Bot (tickets, food, travel, forms)
[] Content Bot that drafts in your voice for approval
[] Chief-of-staff that researches you, organizes the other Bots, and can turn the digest into a morning podcast
[] Testers (techdevnotes): default Bots circulating - Night Shift (overnight digest), Inbox Triage, Chief of Staff, Negotiator, Prototyper, Researcher, Shopper, Apartment Scout, Lookout, Competitor Watcher
[] Official bot + Link: Shopper Bot can now complete online purchases once link is connected (keep approval on)
[] Testers (niccruzpatane): Accounting Bot (invoices, spending, bills); Personal Bot (flights, rides, Airbnb, Google Calendar, Amazon orders/returns); Home Bot (lights, robots, speakers, thermostats)

EVENTS
- Testers (techandsundry, Oct 3): Elon showed up at their Grok Bot event
- Testers (tibor_tee, Oct 12): Grok Bot for Financial Services event, Tue Oct 20 — Bots that prep client reviews, trace record discrepancies and wait for sign-off before acting

text:
Sarah Paulson, Sofia Coppola, and Branden Jacobs-Jenkins Joined ‘CULTURED’ for the Inaugural CultForum

After an introduction from playwright Borna Barzin, Fruit Fly writer Josh Silver and Hacks co-creator Paul W. Downs followed with “The Anatomy of a Hit,” a spirited exchange about the undervaluation of comedy and popular literature, as well as the pressure to keep audiences entertained, or to plumb personal trauma for highbrow credibility or laughs. “The most traumatized people are the funniest. So don’t heal,” Silver joked to the audience. “I would love to find true peace, but I don’t know if it’s possible,” Downs retorted. Feinstein offered a more elemental metaphor for women’s often invisible labor, in the midst of an anecdote about holding a mountain pose in a yoga class: “The world is being held up by women… we’re the secret mountain,” she recalled realizing. Coppola agreed with the sentiment, describing the responsibility of maintaining composure both on set and at home. “As you get older, you can boss people around and not ask for permission,” she smiled.

text:
🚨 AFRICA'S NEXT BIG INVESTMENT OPPORTUNITY MAY BE HIDING IN ITS STARTUPS.

Africa's technology ecosystem is attracting serious capital, and the latest developments are worth watching.

Here are 5 signals from this week's African tech roundup:

1️⃣ Airtel Nigeria crossed $1 billion in revenue. It generated $1.014 billion between April and September 2026, while SmartCash grew its customer base to 4.2 million.

2️⃣ Nigerian AI startup KrosAI raised $135,000. Its focus? Helping businesses deploy AI voice agents across African telecom networks.

3️⃣ Helium Health secured a $2.5 million https://t.co/UWj7PRTWEY grant to develop AI-powered maternal healthcare solutions targeting 1.9 million pregnant women.

4️⃣ Enza raised $6 million to expand its payments infrastructure, helping financial institutions offer integrated payment services.

5️⃣ Kenya is planning a $500 million investment fund targeting startups and growing businesses, with half earmarked for technology and AI.

WHAT SHOULD INVESTORS TAKE AWAY?

Africa's investment story is bigger than traditional banking, oil and telecommunications.

AI, fintech, healthcare technology, payment infrastructure and digital services are emerging areas worth understanding.

But here's the important distinction:

Funding is not profitability. Revenue is not free cash flow. Growth is not automatically shareholder value.

Before investing in any company, examine its:

- Business model and competitive advantage.
- Revenue growth and earnings quality.
- Cash flow and funding requirements.

US markets closed today (Sunday, Nov 8, 2026). Last session was Friday, Nov 6. Indices closed mixed on a chip-led tech rebound after Thursday’s sharp sell-off, but all major benchmarks finished the week lower. 
Major Indices (Friday Close)
•  S&P 500: 7,376.86, +0.31% (+23 pts).
•  Nasdaq Composite: 24,579.42, +1.09% (+264 pts).
•  Dow Jones: 51,285.73, -0.46% (-237 pts).
•  Russell 2000: +0.89%. VIX fell ~9% to 25.64. 
Weekly: S&P 500 -2.68% (worst since spring 2025), Nasdaq -3.37%, Dow -0.94%. Nasdaq entered correction territory Thursday (more than 10% below recent highs) after its worst day in over a year. 
Key drivers: Semiconductor and AI-related stocks rebounded after Thursday’s rout (SOX semiconductor index had its worst day since 2020 on fears of tighter AI/data-center rules after Democratic midterm gains in Congress and governorships). A stronger-than-expected October jobs report provided support but reinforced Fed rate-hike expectations. Breadth was mixed-to-negative; technology led while consumer staples and financials lagged. 
Notable Movers
Gainers (large-cap/tech focus): AMD +11%, Coherent (COHR) +13.6%, Airbnb +11.7%, Intel +7.7%, Nvidia +2.8% (high volume, most active). Other chip names also recovered.
Losers: Axon Enterprise (AXON) -18.2% (earnings miss and lowered guidance), Microchip Technology -10%. Other notable declines included certain healthcare and discretionary names. 
Economic Data, Earnings & News
•  October jobs report (Friday): +165k payrolls (well above ~60-65k consensus), unemployment fell to 4.1%. Prior months revised higher. Wage growth 3.1% y/y. This solidified market pricing for a December Fed hike (roughly 78-80% odds post-data). 
•  Berkshire Hathaway Q3 (released over the weekend under CEO Greg Abel): Operating earnings -5.8% to $12.7B (insurance weakness, including GEICO). Buybacks accelerated to $9.6B in the quarter (plus more in October); cash/equivalents still very large (~$350B+). Net earnings lower amid smaller investment gains. 
•  Next key: October CPI (Tuesday, Nov 10). Additional earnings continue this week.
Pre-Market / Overnight
US cash markets closed. Futures had shown tech resilience into Friday’s close after the prior day’s plunge. No major new directional shift reported into Sunday; focus shifts to Monday’s open and Tuesday’s inflation print amid elevated VIX and post-election uncertainty.
Geopolitical, Fed & Sector Context
•  Fed: Rates held recently at 3.75-4% under Chair Kevin Warsh. Strong jobs data supports further tightening to address still-elevated inflation; December hike remains the base case.
•  Geopolitics / Energy: Ongoing Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruptions. Oil (WTI ~$90.83 Friday) fell sharply on the week on de-escalation hopes tied to the US midterms, though risks of renewed attacks and supply issues persist. Energy was a relative underperformer.
•  Sectors: Technology (especially semiconductors) drove the Friday rebound but remains the week’s biggest drag on AI valuation and potential regulatory concerns. Defensives and some financials lagged. Risks include sticky inflation, Fed path, AI spending/regulation post-election, and oil volatility.
Bottom line: Friday offered a partial tech recovery after a violent week, but the market remains sensitive to policy shifts from the midterms, inflation data, and the Fed’s willingness to keep hiking. I used to bounce between forums, newsletters, and random posts looking for free AI credits, software giveaways, and cheap VPS deals.

Half the time, the good stuff was already gone by the time I found it.
