⚡ HISTORY'S BRAINS TOOK THE DAY OFF

═══════════════ ❧ ════════════════

THE WEIRDEST EVENTS IN HISTORY 🤯

═══════════════ ❧ ════════════════

STRANGER THAN FICTION — NOVEMBER 8TH EDITION

─────────────── ◈ ────────────────

🕒 ESTIMATED READING TIME: 12 MINUTES

─────────────── ◈ ────────────────

🗺️ CONSPECTUS

📜 EPIGRAPH — A little truth to set the tone.

🎬 INTRO — Five stories. One very strange date.

❓ HISTORY QUIZ OF THE DAY — Test your instincts.

⭐️ MAIN EVENTS — Five moments when history got spectacularly weird.

🎙️ HARVEY'S CORNER — The rest of the story.

⚖️ CLOSING — The day, considered.

✅ QUIZ ANSWER — The answer revealed.

🍬 CANDY — One last sweet bite, with a look at tomorrow.

💋 SEND-OFF — Pass the madness along.

📚 SOURCES & FURTHER READING — Follow the evidence.

✒️ PUDD'NHEAD WILSON HAS THE LAST WORD — Mark Twain gets the final say.

─────────────── ◈ ────────────────

📜 EPIGRAPH

“Truth is stranger than fiction, but it is because Fiction is obliged to stick to possibilities; Truth isn't.” — Mark Twain, Following the Equator (1897).

─────────────── ◈ ────────────────

🎬 INTRO

November 8 has a peculiar talent for watching history’s most self-absorbed individuals stroll confidently into rooms only to discover, somewhat late, that they left their pants—and any remaining sense of control—back at the door.

Consider the emperor who welcomes a group of scruffy foreigners into his magnificent capital, apparently under the impression that “hospitality” and “strategic vulnerability” are interchangeable concepts. Or the captain who decides that diplomatic kidnapping is a fine idea, nearly arranging an unplanned war between two empires.

Elsewhere, a physicist notices an inexplicable glow, investigates, and discovers a form of radiation no one is entirely sure they want. Then there is the failed coup that becomes the opening chapter of a movement that will rearrange the century.

And finally, one determined individual whose carefully laid plans come remarkably close to changing history—if only events had cooperated.

Five moments. Grand ambitions, dangerous assumptions, scientific accidents, political miscalculations, and one spectacularly poorly timed appointment with history’s exit.

Different people. Different plans. One recurring problem: humanity possesses an extraordinary talent for mistaking confidence for competence, and then acting surprised when reality declines to play along.

Apparently, being absolutely certain you're right and actually knowing what you're doing are two entirely different things. History has been demonstrating that distinction for centuries. Humanity, unfortunately, remains a slow learner.

Cue the chaos. Let’s roll. 💥

─────────────── ◈ ────────────────

❓ HISTORY QUIZ OF THE DAY

In November 1939, a German carpenter's carefully timed bomb nearly killed Adolf Hitler. The device exploded after Hitler had unexpectedly left the building.

What happened to the man who built it?

[A] He escaped into Switzerland and was never found.

[B] He was arrested at the border before the explosion.

[C] He was captured inside the building.

[D] He was betrayed by another member of the resistance.

👇 (Answer at the end of the issue.)

─────────────── ◈ ────────────────

⭐️ MAIN EVENTS

🏛️ 1519 — THE WORLD’S MOST POLITE HOME INVASION 🌎

Tenochtitlan, Mexico | November 8, 1519

On November 8, 1519, Hernán Cortés and his Spanish expedition entered Tenochtitlan, the magnificent capital of the Mexica Empire.

Waiting to meet them was Moctezuma II, the ruler whose authority extended across a powerful network of cities and tributary territories.

The encounter was extraordinary. Cortés was leading an armed expedition into the heart of a wealthy, powerful empire.

According to Cortés's own account, the Spanish approached along a causeway. Moctezuma's welcoming party included leading inhabitants of the city, who greeted the newcomers in a carefully ordered ceremonial procession. The ruler himself then came forward to meet Cortés.

The meeting became one of the most famous encounters in the Americas, but the familiar story of two worlds colliding can obscure the political calculations on both sides.

Moctezuma was not simply a helpless ruler greeting his conqueror. Cortés was not entering an empty or defenseless landscape. The Spanish expedition depended heavily on Indigenous allies, including peoples who had their own reasons for opposing Mexica power.

The encounter did not end the conflict. The Spanish presence became coercive, Moctezuma was taken into their custody, and the struggle that followed helped bring down the Mexica capital.

A formal meeting. A ceremonial welcome. And an armed expedition whose arrival would have consequences neither side could fully control.

🧩 TRIVIA: Cortés reported that nearly a thousand of the city's principal inhabitants approached and greeted him individually, a ceremony that kept him waiting for about an hour.

🐶 SPOT: The meeting took place on a causeway connecting the island city to the surrounding mainland. Tenochtitlan was a sophisticated urban center connected by engineered routes across Lake Texcoco.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: History often remembers the conqueror's arrival as the beginning of a story. But the people already living there had their own history, political interests, and calculations. The encounter was not simply a meeting of two men. It was a collision of competing powers.

───────────────

⚓ 1861 — BUY ONE WAR, GET BRITAIN FREE 🇺🇸🇬🇧

Atlantic Ocean | November 8, 1861

The United States was fighting a civil war. It could scarcely afford another. Yet on November 8, 1861, a U.S. Navy captain nearly brought Great Britain into the conflict.

Captain Charles Wilkes, commanding the USS San Jacinto, intercepted the British mail steamer Trent, carrying Confederate commissioners James Mason and John Slidell to Europe to seek diplomatic support for the Confederacy.

Wilkes ordered his men aboard and seized the two commissioners and their secretaries. The Trent continued its voyage; the prisoners were taken into U.S. custody.

The North initially celebrated Wilkes. Britain saw an illegal violation of its neutrality and demanded the prisoners' release and an apology. It sent troops toward Canada and prepared for possible war.

President Abraham Lincoln and Secretary of State William Seward recognized the danger. Wilkes had acted without authorization, and the administration chose to release the prisoners rather than risk war with Britain.

On December 26, Seward formally announced the decision. Mason and Slidell were subsequently freed, and the crisis subsided.

The Trent Affair demonstrated how one naval interception could threaten to ignite a second war while the first was still raging.

🧩 TRIVIA: Captain Wilkes was court-martialed in 1864—but not for the Trent Affair itself. The charges arose from a later dispute with the Navy Department over his conduct and a letter criticizing the Secretary of the Navy. He was found guilty of disobedience and insubordination and received a public reprimand and suspension.

⚠️ IRONY: The Union had celebrated the capture as a diplomatic victory. It then had to release the very men whose capture had produced the crisis.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: A tactical success can become a strategic disaster when nobody considers what happens next. Wilkes captured two Confederate envoys. His government nearly inherited a war with Britain.

───────────────

🩻 1895 — RÖNTGEN BLOCKS LIGHT, ACCIDENTALLY INVENTS X-RAY VISION ⚡

Würzburg, Germany | November 8, 1895

Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen was experimenting with electrical discharges in a laboratory when something unexpected happened.

He had covered a Crookes tube with heavy black cardboard to block visible light. Yet a fluorescent screen nearby began to glow.
Something was passing through the cardboard and making the screen fluoresce. Röntgen knew that the familiar cathode rays could not explain what he was seeing.

He began investigating.

On November 8, 1895, Röntgen recognized that he had encountered a previously unknown form of radiation. He called it X-rays. The X stood for the unknown.

Further experiments showed that the rays passed through many materials that blocked ordinary light, penetrating soft tissue while being absorbed more readily by bone and metal.

For the first time, scientists had a way to produce images of structures inside the human body without cutting it open.

Physicians soon used the discovery to examine fractures, locate foreign objects, and investigate injuries that once required exploratory surgery.

Röntgen's discovery transformed physics and medicine. In 1901, he received the first Nobel Prize in Physics.

A strange glow in a darkened laboratory had opened a window into the human body.

🧩 TRIVIA: Röntgen deliberately called the new radiation X-rays because he did not yet know what the rays were. The name remained even after scientists learned much more about their nature.

💡 INSIGHT: The discovery began when Röntgen noticed an effect that his existing equipment was not supposed to produce. The breakthrough came from investigating an unexpected result rather than dismissing it as experimental noise.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: Some of the most important discoveries begin as inconvenient surprises. The difference between an accident and a breakthrough is often the willingness to investigate what does not fit.

───────────────

🍺 1923 — BEER HALL PUTSCH: HITLER FAILS TO SEIZE POWER, SUCCEEDS AT BECOMING FAMOUS ANYWAY  🇩🇪

Munich, Germany | November 8–9, 1923

Adolf Hitler and the Nazi Party wanted to overthrow the German government. Their first attempt began in a beer hall.

On the evening of November 8, 1923, Bavarian political leaders were addressing a large gathering at the Bürgerbräukeller in Munich. Hitler and his armed supporters arrived to force the meeting into becoming the launching point for a revolution.

Hitler entered the hall, fired a pistol into the ceiling, and announced that a national revolution had begun.
He then took three leading Bavarian officials into an adjoining room and attempted to compel them to support his plan.

The plan: seize Bavaria, march on Berlin, and overthrow the national government.

But the coup depended on the cooperation of men who were not nearly as committed to Hitler's ambitions as he believed.

The Bavarian leaders initially appeared to cooperate under pressure. Once they were free of the immediate threat, they repudiated their support and worked against the putsch.

The following day, Hitler and his supporters marched through Munich. Police confronted them, gunfire erupted, and the attempted revolution collapsed.

Hitler was arrested and later convicted of high treason.

The coup had failed. The Nazi Party was banned. Its leader had been sent to prison.

Yet the story did not end there.

The trial gave Hitler a national platform, and the failed putsch became a foundational myth for the Nazi movement. Hitler later shifted toward gaining power through the political system rather than attempting another immediate armed uprising.

The coup had not delivered the government Hitler wanted, but it made him far more visible.

🧩 TRIVIA: Hitler was sentenced to five years in prison for high treason. He was released on parole on December 20, 1924, after spending just over a year in custody overall, including his pretrial detention.

🏴‍☠️ HUBRIS: Hitler believed that a dramatic show of force and the pressure of the moment would bring Bavaria's leaders into line. Instead, he discovered that a revolution cannot be built on the assumption that everyone will keep a promise made at gunpoint.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: Failure does not always destroy an extremist movement. Sometimes it teaches the movement how to change tactics. The Beer Hall Putsch failed as a coup, but its aftermath helped Hitler refine his path to power.

───────────────

💣 1939 — HITLER SURVIVES CARPENTER’S DIY PROJECT BY THIRTEEN MINUTES  🕰️

Munich, Germany | November 8, 1939

Georg Elser was not a general, a politician, or a member of a powerful resistance organization.

He was a carpenter.

And he decided that Adolf Hitler had to be stopped.

Opposed to the Nazi regime and fearing another catastrophic European war, Elser planned an assassination with patience, precision, and a device of his own making.

For weeks, he worked secretly inside Munich's Bürgerbräukeller, where Hitler traditionally delivered a speech marking the anniversary of the 1923 Beer Hall Putsch.

Elser hollowed out a pillar behind the speaker's platform and installed a timed explosive device.

He returned repeatedly, working through the night and concealing his labor.

His plan was carefully timed. The bomb was intended to explode while Hitler was speaking.

But on November 8, 1939, Hitler's schedule changed.

His speech was shorter than expected. He left the building at approximately 9:07 p.m.

The bomb exploded at approximately 9:20 p.m.

The pillar and ceiling collapsed. Eight people were killed and 63 injured.

Hitler was already gone.

Elser had been arrested at the Swiss border in Constance at 8:45 p.m., before the explosion. He had been attempting to cross into Switzerland when customs officials detained him.

The Nazi regime tried to turn the attack into propaganda, suggesting foreign intelligence agencies were behind it, though investigators established that Elser acted alone.

Elser was imprisoned for years and ultimately murdered at Dachau concentration camp on April 9, 1945, shortly before the end of the war.

His attempt missed by minutes. His courage deserves to be remembered.

🧩 TRIVIA: Elser's arrest at 8:45 p.m. came just 35 minutes before the bomb exploded.

🐶 SPOT: The bomb used two clock mechanisms. They released a mechanical sled that drove three nails into modified cartridges, triggering the explosive charge. Elser had built a remarkably intricate timing system that allowed him to set the device days in advance.

🧬 HUMAN: Elser's family endured years of suspicion and false accusations that he could not have acted alone. A Gestapo interrogation record, rediscovered decades later, became crucial evidence confirming that he had independently planned and carried out the assassination attempt.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: Elser did not have an army, a title, or an organization behind him. He had a conviction, a set of tools, and the patience to work in secret. His bomb missed its target. His courage should not be forgotten.

─────────────── ◈ ────────────────

🎙️ HARVEY'S CORNER

THE MAN WHO LEFT THIRTEEN MINUTES TOO SOON

The room was full.

The speeches were underway. The anniversary crowd had gathered, and the man they had come to hear was standing at the front.

Behind the speaker's platform, hidden inside a wooden pillar, a clock was counting down.

It had taken a carpenter months to put it there.

Georg Elser had spent more than thirty nights inside the Bürgerbräukeller, quietly hollowing out the pillar and preparing the explosive device. He knew the room. He knew the schedule. He knew where Hitler would stand.

He had planned for the evening of November 8, 1939, when Hitler would address the Nazi faithful on the anniversary of the failed Beer Hall Putsch.

Elser expected the speech to last long enough for the bomb to do its work.

But Hitler had a train to catch.

His speech ended earlier than usual. At approximately 9:07 p.m., he left the building with other Nazi leaders.

Thirteen minutes later, the bomb exploded.

Timber and ceiling crashed down. Eight people were dead; dozens were wounded.

The man who had built the bomb was already in police custody.

At 8:45 p.m., customs officers had arrested Elser near the Swiss border. He had been carrying suspicious items, including components that would lead investigators back to the attack.

The timing was cruelly precise. Elser had planned for Hitler's usual schedule. Hitler had changed it.

But there was another story behind the clock.

Elser was not a professional assassin. He was a skilled craftsman who had come to believe that Hitler's rule would lead Germany and Europe into disaster. He had watched the regime grow more violent and had decided that waiting for someone else to act was no longer acceptable.

He worked alone. He built the device himself. He accepted that he might die in the attempt.

The Nazi regime tried to turn the bombing into a story about foreign conspirators. Elser was interrogated, imprisoned, and held for years. He was eventually executed at Dachau on April 9, 1945.

Propaganda and suspicion clouded his story for decades. His interrogation record became an important part of the historical evidence establishing that he had acted alone.

Think about that.

He wasn't a general. He commanded no army. He held no office and had no political machine behind him. He was a craftsman who saw what was coming, decided he could not simply stand aside, and acted.

His bomb missed its target by thirteen minutes. His warning, tragically, did not miss the mark.

—— ❦ ——

🧬 HUMAN

Sometimes history remembers the powerful because they changed the world. Sometimes it takes much longer to remember the ordinary person who tried to stop them.

—— ❦ ——

─────────────── ◈ ────────────────

⚖️ CLOSING

November 8, that quietly efficient little date when history clears its throat and reminds us that “control” is mostly a story people tell themselves just before the plot changes.

Cortés and Moctezuma met in a city whose political sophistication and engineering would have made much of Europe feel underdressed. Yet their encounter is still filed under “inevitable conquest,” a tidy way of overlooking the civilization already running there—and the visitors who underestimated it.

Charles Wilkes seized two Confederate envoys and nearly dragged his country into another war over the paperwork. The Trent Affair proved that one decision at sea can threaten peace across continents. Some people treat international incidents like others treat “reply all.”

Röntgen noticed a glow that had no business being there. Instead of blaming the equipment and going home, he investigated. His discovery transformed medicine and physics, though he probably never imagined how many future patients would associate it with paper gowns and “hold still.”

Hitler’s first attempt to seize power collapsed so spectacularly it should have been a cautionary tale. Instead, it gave him national attention, a trial he turned into propaganda, and a lesson: next time, try taking power through the system you tried to overthrow. Some people turn failure into an unpaid marketing campaign.

And Georg Elser came within thirteen minutes of making that learning curve irrelevant. He had accounted for the room, the pillar, and the schedule—but not a speech that ended early. History occasionally changes the runtime after the tickets have been sold.

Five events. Five reminders that history is less a carefully managed production than a procession of people certain they have everything handled.

Sometimes the turning point is a discovery others overlooked. Sometimes it is one reckless decision. And sometimes it is a clock that keeps ticking after its target has left the room.

The past is full of people who thought they had everything under control up until they didn't.

History has a way of checking their work. It is thorough, unsentimental, and rarely offers a revision period.

Humanity had a plan. What could possibly wrong? 🤷‍♀️

─────────────── ◈ ────────────────

✅ QUIZ ANSWER: [B] He was arrested at the border before the explosion.

Georg Elser was detained by German customs officials in Constance at approximately 8:45 p.m. on November 8, 1939. The bomb he had planted in the Bürgerbräukeller exploded at approximately 9:20 p.m.

Hitler had already left the building.

Elser's arrest came before the explosion, not after it. The man who had built the device was already in custody when it detonated.

─────────────── ◈ ────────────────

🍬 CANDY

Tomorrow, November 9, history serves up a date with an extraordinary appetite for upheaval.

A monarchy will tremble. A wall will come down. A political movement will turn a failed uprising into a legend. And one of the darkest nights in modern European history will leave broken glass scattered across the streets.

The calendar says November 9.

History says: brace yourself. 👀

text:
The 1950s as a horror setting  and why it might be perfect.

The 1980s nostalgia of Stranger Things was essential to the show’s identity  the synths, the BMX bikes, the walkie-talkies, the Dungeons & Dragons, the Stephen King and Spielberg references. The decade wasn’t decoration. It was DNA.

The 1950s offer a different but equally potent aesthetic for horror. The decade was defined by a specific tension: the surface of American life was ordered, optimistic, and conformist  picket fences, nuclear families, suburban expansion, the American Dream in full bloom. But underneath the surface, the anxiety was immense  the Cold War, nuclear testing in the Nevada desert, the McCarthy era’s paranoia about infiltration, the space race’s existential questions about what else was out there.

The contrast between surface and depth  between the clean, bright world America presented and the dark, fearful world America felt  is the perfect foundation for supernatural horror. Something terrible hiding beneath something beautiful. A monster in the desert that nobody talks about because the decade’s defining trait was not talking about things.

Marion, Nevada, in 1955 sits in the geographic and psychological center of this tension. Nevada was where America tested nuclear weapons  the landscape of the atomic sublime, where mushroom clouds rose over the desert while tourists watched from Las Vegas hotel rooftops. The idea that something came through  that the tests opened something, or attracted something, or awoke something  is a horror premise that writes itself against the historical backdrop.

The Duffers told fans to “watch the skies.” In 1955 Nevada, the skies held nuclear fallout  and maybe something else.

Parker, 29, died on November 7. He joined the sheriff's office in 2020, served on the SWAT team and became a K9 deputy with his partner, Brego. He also served as a captain in the Washington Army National Guard. He leaves behind his wife, two children and a third child on the way. His family's decision to donate his organs carries his service to others forward.

Two husbands. 

Two fathers. 

Two men who served their country and their community, and gave everything trying to protect someone else.

Rest in peace, Mason and Parker.

You were the best America has to offer, and you always will be 🇺🇸

text:
The [UK Ministry of Defence’s February 2024 announcement](https://t.co/3E6NgR1xqh) documents British–Latvian drone assistance to Ukraine. It does not establish that Britain—or King Charles personally—engineered Operation Spiderweb to sabotage Trump. That is the central gap in this clip: documented events are connected by assertions about motives, rather than evidence of operational control.

First, the context matters. The video discusses the June 1, 2025 attacks and displays a June 3, 2025 news article. It concerns events from that period, not a newly documented November 2026 operation. Its exact recording date is not established here.

The drone coalition is real. But providing military assistance does not, by itself, establish who planned a particular operation, supplied its specific equipment or selected its targets. Nor does announcing that assistance during an American election establish an anti-Trump motive.

The parliamentary quotation is especially revealing. [Paragraph 39 of the House of Lords report](https://t.co/8qK296eWW6) says another Trump administration could make damage to UK–US relations “longer lasting,” requiring Britain to rely less on agreement with Washington. That is an assessment of diplomatic divergence—not a declaration that Britain could not survive another Trump presidency, let alone evidence of a plan to provoke world war.

George Beebe’s quotation is genuine. In his [June 2 interview with Foreign Policy](https://t.co/vBFXusONH4), he argued that Washington was Ukraine’s intended political audience and warned about escalation. Those are analytical judgments worth examining, not intelligence findings proving British direction. He also said he did not consider the attack a significant blow to Russia’s nuclear triad and distinguished possible Russian perceptions from established facts.

Nuclear-capable aircraft can also carry out conventional missions. [Zelensky’s contemporaneous statement](https://t.co/EGfistBzeA) described the targets as aircraft used against Ukraine and attributed the operation to Ukraine’s Security Service. That is Ukraine’s account, not independent verification of every operational detail. But the clip needs evidence before replacing it with a British-command theory.

The railway deaths also require separate treatment. [Reuters reported distinct bridge and train incidents](https://t.co/cW4oq5ujOQ), with nobody claiming responsibility at that point. Events occurring around the same time do not automatically constitute one operation with one sponsor.

Likewise, accusing Charles requires evidence of his involvement. The [Royal Household’s constitutional explanation](https://t.co/rnwouTU4oL) describes a politically impartial monarch. That alone cannot settle every allegation, but a dramatic video title supplies no missing proof.

Escalation risks deserve serious scrutiny. So does Russia’s responsibility for invading Ukraine: the [UN General Assembly demanded Russian withdrawal](https://t.co/jVCcWSX48F). Seeking peace does not require denying Ukrainians agency or assuming their resistance is secretly directed against America.

Experience, confidence and a compelling presentation are not substitutes for a verifiable chain of evidence. Ask hard questions about military strategy and negotiations—but apply that same scrutiny to the sweeping conspiracy offered here.

Trump offered Dana White the job of White House Press Secretary. White said he has a meeting with him on Monday and is flying to Washington right now.

In the video below White is asked how he would balance the role with running the UFC. He answers that he already has a lot of jobs.

White and the Fertitta brothers bought the UFC in 2001 for $2 million. The company was later $40 million in debt. They put up the last $10 million themselves for the first season of The Ultimate Fighter after Spike TV passed. That season led to a $35 million Spike deal, then a $100 million Fox deal, then a multi-billion ESPN deal. The UFC is now valued in the tens of billions.

One side says taking the press secretary job would pull him away from the company he spent 25 years building from a $2 million buy into a multi-billion business. The other side says the offer itself shows how far the company he still runs has come.

Would taking the job be worth stepping back from the company that went from $2 million and $40 million in debt to tens of billions, or does he already have enough on his plate?

《Joyful Hiking, Kindred Spirits in Motion | Happy Planet's Hong Kong Coastal Offline Event Concludes Successfully》
This hiking event followed a classic coastal route in Hong Kong's Southern District — from Deep Water Bay to Repulse Bay, along the waterfront promenade. The entire route is nearly flat with minimal elevation gain, gentle terrain, expansive ocean views, and a soothing, healing landscape. It requires no intense physical exertion, making it ideal for community members to relax, connect, and enjoy ample time together in unhurried conversation.
A total of 13 friends joined this hike. To ensure everyone could set off together as a complete group, several participants who had arrived early at Repulse Bay特意 returned to Deep Water Bay for the meetup. Once the full team assembled, we departed together, side by side, embarking on our coastal hiking journey. The pace was leisurely, the atmosphere relaxed — everyone walked and talked freely, getting to know one another naturally. Amidst the mountains and the sea, distances closed and friendships deepened.
After everyone arrived smoothly at Repulse Bay beach, we stumbled upon an unoccupied semicircular bench just behind the sand. The group naturally settled in for a rest, and what followed was a relaxed yet deeply meaningful community exchange. Guards were dropped, conversations flowed with sincerity — in a laid-back atmosphere, participants truly got to know one another, resonating on the same wavelength. This hike was never just about walking; it was about human connection.
Following a brief rest and exchange, the group strolled along the beach toward the Pavilion of Universal Peace at the far end, taking in the unique blend of mountain, sea, and cultural heritage that defines Repulse Bay. The original plan had been to linger by the shore and await the sunset glow — but everyone was so immersed in the joy of each other's company, so absorbed in conversation, that we missed the sunset entirely. It was a gentle, fond little regret to carry home from an otherwise delightful hike.
As evening fell, the gathering moved to Chuen Seafood Restaurant for a dinner exchange. New friends joined the dinner portion — having missed the hike due to busy workdays, they made the trip specifically for the evening gathering. Meanwhile, a few hiking participants needed to leave early for personal matters. New and old friends sat together around the table, the atmosphere warm and lively.
Over dinner, the conversation ranged freely — from historical perspectives and career development to industry trends and life experiences. Topics spanned history, industrial enterprise, financial markets, personal growth, and more. The exchange was engaging and mutually stimulating, and within the easy rhythm of conversation, participants achieved genuine intellectual exchange, resource sharing, and a deepened sense of trust and understanding within the community.
The participants represented a high-quality, diverse circle, centered around Hong Kong's new immigrant community. The group included both long-time residents who have called Hong Kong home for over twenty years and newer arrivals — top talent pass holders, quality migrant admission scheme members, and investment immigrants. Professional backgrounds were equally varied, spanning finance, chemical industry entrepreneurship, scientific research, and university academia. This diversity of circles meant every conversation was rich with fresh insights, new opportunities, and unexpected sparks.
The Deep Water Bay to Repulse Bay coastal hike offered moderate exercise, was effortless and fatigue-free throughout, and allowed everyone to step away from the city's noise, get close to nature's mountains and sea, and decompress. More importantly, it embodied Happy Planet's offline event philosophy: "Light hiking, deep connection, shared growth." The distance may have been short, but the exchange was deep and the takeaways abundant — truly achieving the goal of gathering people through hiking, building momentum through conversation, and growing together through shared resonance.
This event also marked the official launch of Happy Planet's exclusive offline activity benefit: all participants who joined the hike and dinner received complimentary official Planet Tokens.
Planet Token is the core credential of the Happy Planet ecosystem, bridging both physical and digital virtual product scenarios. Holders can use it to redeem and purchase physical goods within the ecosystem, as well as participate in NFT digital collectible trading — collecting premium digital pieces, or creating and listing their own NFT digital products for circulation, achieving co-creation of value.
With this, Happy Planet has officially established a常态化 benefit mechanism for offline events: participate in a branded offline activity, earn Planet Token rewards, and engage deeply in ecosystem co-building while sharing in its value. Going forward, all our hiking events, salons, and offline meetups will continue to issue Token benefits to participants — giving back to every fellow builder who walks alongside us.

text:
🇺🇸 In December 1863, a young widow in full mourning walked into the White House. She was Emilie Todd Helm, Mary Lincoln’s half-sister. 

Her husband, Confederate Brigadier General Ben Hardin Helm, had been killed at Chickamauga three months earlier.

Lincoln had once offered Helm a commission in the Union army. Helm turned it down. “It almost killed me to decline,” he later told a friend. 

Emilie was 26. She would never remarry.

Lincoln called her “little sister.” He gave her a pass so she could travel freely. He also told aides he did not want it widely known she was staying in the White House.

The following year the relationship frayed. Emilie refused to take the Union oath of allegiance and was back in Kentucky. In August 1864 Lincoln wired the Union commander there that he would no longer shield her. “Deal with her for current conduct just as you would with any other,” he wrote.

In October she wrote him again. She was broke. “The last money I have in the world I used to make the unfruitful Appeal to you,” she said. “Your Minnie bullets have made us what we are.”

Lincoln still tried to help where he could. The war had put them on opposite sides, but the family tie was never fully cut.

In 1909, at the dedication of a Lincoln statue in Hodgenville, Kentucky, it was Emilie who pulled the cord that unveiled the bronze.

text:
Biography of Zion

One step beyond Jerusalem there will be no sea. But many fish now swim down stream in the bagoong of nations. We juxtapose the lighted cigar ends of fish tails Ben-Gurion saw in the upper Galilee sky that day in 1955 with every other trivia of fish and krill. These ferment with JFK telling Ben-Gurion at the Waldorf Astoria in 1961, “You know, I was elected by the Jews of New York. I will do something for you” (Tom Segev, A State at Any Cost. 2019. 556, 673).

Ben-Gurion’s esteemed biographer Tom Segev plumbs the depths where “several biographers have taken up the task of diving into the sea of written material that David Ben-Gurion produced (771). These Gadarene newsmen of the think tanks think Ben-Gurion speculated that the coasts of the Sea of Galilee were not deep enough to hold their herd, only 150 feet at its greatest. But now as the Euphrates River dries up, the Dead Sea yet offers 1000 feet deep, so there a series of Dead Sea immersions can be planned for the future coming, or would have been if they had not gone astray like Ben-Gurion’s approval of Shimon Peres’ proposal for Germany to establish military bases in Israel (642). Such matters as this produced 16 pages of correspondence to JFK (12 April 1963f) before his taking off, along with correspondence on the UAR alliance of Egypt, Syria and Iraq to liberate Palestine. Worried that even the Dead Sea depth were not enough to hold the queries, that region from which the beast with seven heads of blasphemy and ten horns would arise would be a last resort, the Aegean Sea colony prison of Rome at Patmos where St John was sentenced, an acceptable ten thousand feet.
If we say the internal is hidden like the future, like the sea while we are standing on the land looking out, then we must go into the water. We go down to the sea while the waves wash up on our ankles. Does a turtle think, whooshing in and out in a seaweed voice, the unutterable thoughts Wittgenstein contained? Thoughts roll up like the sea and fall back. We never know we stand on a beach and hear the thought within the waves until the wet. If I am the land and my thought is of the sea from which the land is made in the permanence of mind, it grows with the purpose of life, and the longer the land exists the more the wonder. The feet of history stand on the shore of memory as we watch the waves roll in.
They regard Ben-Gurion as one of the biggest bony fish in that sea, a selfish Sunfish, Mola mola, those conversation starters that hang on, seeking repute. Blaming him for sharing his inner thoughts he was blamed for not sharing. They said he was lonely and unfeeling and without the supernatural which he did not entirely disbelieve, but still upheld the soul of a nation. The crux of it all for us is that a defense of Ben-Gurion is a defense of the earth and meaning a defense of the human.
The fallen bodies of newsmen and their conspiracy theories on Ben-Gurion, of his Saturday night bible studies, conversing on the increase of human brain size, how to demolish the Old City Wall, start a new party called Rafi four months after his retirement, makes them also lose their minds.
The great tragedy that “no soul is close to him” (A State at Any Cost, 653) needed convincing in the twilight years. Six months after he resigned, June 16, 1963, conspiracy theory had already explained away the JFK assassination replete with CIA contract psychologists, MKUltra, and long letters between Ben-Gurion and President Kennedy, who had less time than any. As if that were not enough bagoong forced upon the unwilling, now his nephew, Robert Kennedy, and even newsman Tucker Carlson (Dec 2022), reveal how these agencies cannot feel safe as long as witnesses of that time remain alive. What is surrealism, if not the hammer that breaks the bars of the iron cage that imprisons where commodity fetish leads many individuals to confuse freedom with the free choice of a product on the shelves.
2. In these circumstances we approve Ben-Gurion’s sense of himself if he thinks he is Balaam’s Ass, made to speak so that Balaam-Israel will not err even more than it has. It is worth remembering that Balaam beat the ass three times, with his fist, his foot and his stick, simply because it would not do as he said and ride the angel down. It is always a predicament when the invisible confronts the seen. Is Ben-Gurion given the benefit of doubt for seeing? When Ben-Gurion calls himself the ass it implies he does believe in the supernatural, just not in men, no happen-stance agreeing. That Israel-Balaam would go astray, yet be protected against itself, even in its untoward alliances bringing harm to the people with devious advice is not entirely a story with an ending.
In this context we can hardly call Ben-Gurion extremist even if he was ready to aright the classical “Hitlerist type,’ meaning he thought Begin ready to exterminate the Arabs and install absolute rule (Segev. A State at Any Cost. 648-9). Compulsive behavior blurred with vehemence and conviction enabled Ben-Gurion to argue Jewish religious law did not prohibit pork at all! That he ate pork had to be excised from his letters to his wife, the principle being that “a Jew can be an unbeliever but still be a Jew” (Segev, 665). Ben-Gurion, rarely seen in synagogue, was least observant. Whether a Jew can be registered among children of mixed parentage, could have Kaddish said, or even be buried within the bounds, this memoir must consider Ben-Gurion as an unbelieving Moses at founding new Israel. When the curtain rises on those Tartary kingdoms of the literature of the erev rev, the ORCapoi gone into the Malebolge right out of Dante, mixed multitudes that resemble the true wheat, it is almost a new Israel. After Ben Gurion’s lifetime resume in artificial intelligence he kept informed of the wheat and tares, the changeling database faiths, CRISPR implants, aliens, mutants until finally America got its way into the Bible too, which Rhinoplasty provoked by the joint resolution of the U.S. House and Senate doubled down, as speaker Daschle says, a strike at"the heart of the American community and the symbols and structures."The corresponding elders of infamy of church, military, corporate backgrounds would need that further depth off the Aegean where that beast of seven heads resides.
Asked in 1957 whether thinking machines would exchange letters of philosophical, ethical or scientific questions with each other Ben-Gurion differed with physicist Amos de-Shalit's notion that a machine “would resemble man in everything, with no difference between a living human and a sophisticated machine, a machine to replace a single human intellectual function, that by linking together several coordinated machines through another machine, it would be possible to replace humans by creating an artificial form of intelligence.” Singularity of course has nigh done. The argument proceeds with the analogy that temperature does not exist for a single atom and is only relevant when a group of atoms operate, thus the coordinated activation of a large number of machines could evoke a new type of phenomena, one which could not arise from or be attributed to one machine or another.
Ben-Gurion’s relation with the intellects of his time, might be considered a relief from the statecraft he practiced with the American presidents even if he, as Abba Hillel, did not pound Truman’s desk, he had more freedom of speech than Eisenhower and was maybe better informed about their fears to “guard against the acquisition of unwarranted influence, whether sought or unsought, by the military-industrial complex. Likewise JFK’s fear of CIA, for Ben-Gurion was ultimately conversant on the progress of AI, especially in his awareness of de-Shalit’s notions that a machine would replace a single human intellectual function, and Singularity linking together several coordinated machines through another machines, replace humans with an artificial form of intelligence. The argument went that just as temperature does not exist for a single atom and is only relevant when a group of atoms operate the coordinated activation of a large number of machines could evoke a new type of phenomena, one which could not arise from or be attributed to one machine or another. These concerns together Ben-Gurion here calls leviathan, which he takes as the angel of death, viz. Klee’s angel, and the angel of destruction, the Little Boy bomb, but further, esp. in ORCapoi attributes third strand implants, shoggoths, hybridized decayed, debased angel AI of a cyclopean science run by centaurs in a secret space pogrom.

Biographers are politicians too, need to please their own alters and faculties of themselves right and wrong, good and bad. That Ben-Gurion should be and remain an enigma to the most recent best of them, Tom Segev in A State at Any Cost (2018 tr. 2019), blurs the lines, full of contradictions, but Ben-Gurion is not in the company of Lenin or Churchill as the blurb would have. To wish he had not done so much, said so much, behaved better according to their standards is what that school of Israel's new historians challenge in the country's traditional and biblical narratives, doubts seen everywhere now in all the founding intelligences of all Western countries that pull themselves down.

There is no mention of Baal or Trials in the Wilderness in the revised history, a forgetfulness of the peeled watering trough where Ben Gurion University closed its Bible department in 2021. Mount Hermon, ritual home of Baal sacrifices, does get mention by Ben-Gurion, “its white locks gazing down on all the land of Galilee” (86), the very place where Yeshua Messiah stood when he declared the gates of hell shall not stand (Heiser. Reversing Hermon. 2017. 95f.). Of course Ben-Gurion is surrounded by supernatural events in and out of time that his biographers don’t believe in either, overwritten by emotions of extreme statements that get promoted, that so and so never forgave him, or his own view of Plato in old age turned against him, “heart grown hard, soul ruthless and mind angry,” which Segev says, “the same thing would happen to Ben-Gurion.” That’s what comes of trying to make the rough places plain. We infer that Segev reached the age of his writing in the mid seventies in such good health that he has not known the thing that made Plato old. Bless him if he gets away. We have not.

How to deal with the pettifogging small town prejudices of villagers as different as Yemen from Ukraine, Iraq from Poland all over the world and bring them into unity was a gift of Ben-Gurion. But he had the history of the character of Abraham denied him and likewise was if David denied authorship of Psalms. It is absorbing to confront the critic-editor in Gunkel's Transmission of the Legends of Oral Tradition where at least five times Gunkel calls Abraham's hiding Sarah as his wife while in Egypt "the lie of Abraham...seems to us Jesuitical." Oh dear, it’s devious! Later editors turn "Abraham's lie into a mental reservation." In the "shrewd deceit of Abraham in Egypt," the "patriarch's deception" the problem is that using the same evidence over and over suggests reaching for something not there. Gunkel wants to pose an ethical divide between the bald account of Abraham's lie and later “cover ups” that embarrassed the so-called editors of Abraham. This is all according to the Gunkel premise that legends incur alterations over time as if the writers were deluded fictionalists, not sincerely scribal, who needed editors to alter text from ignorance, whimsy, and worse, from ethical betrayal. They will set things right but are as dishonest as a government Ph.D. All this extrapolates from the confusion of Mizraim and Muzrim, from which he derives a whole principle. Gunkel is most vexed with the beauty of Abraham’s wife and their virility.

But Ben-Gurion had to pay for the inclusion in return with pettiness visited back. So Anita Shipira says there is some doubt whether he did not know Polish in Plonsk (Ben-Gurion, 6) so that to “escape the stifling atmosphere of a small remote town,” as if that were anything but a clique, or that “the boy lacked love and affection” (9), simple gossip. How would she know? Freud? It’s part of the usual damned with faint praise the blind Fury brings with abhorred shears to slit the thin-spun life (Milton, Lycidas). Is it actors or biographers who couch asides that it was “not exactly music to David’s ears” (14), when Schlomo Zemach got to Palestine first? Similar extremities are noted in the life of Golda Meir where she is touted on one hand and made inscrutable on the other. It’s an Israeli habit to treat its leaders like asses and beat them with books. But who lives up to the life of Adam, Samuel, David, Amos, Jeremiah, Elijah, Jonathan, Deborah, Ruth, so realized that the only possibility is to live yourself truly the existential moment of fertile inspiration with contradiction, so much that when the European nationalities from protestant countries came to the new world to seek and live in their own Aliyah, they came with wooden trunks on ships.

It’s a tossup whether Zion knows the life of Ezra any better than the kid with the device in his hand. As Ben-Gurion says somewhere within, the diffusion was planned. It’s Star-Linked, which is not to say that such attention to detail even with a tin ear could not attach discrimination, but the content neutral standard went awry. Excesses of  Bagoong in all the historiographers, Segev, Shapira, Peres think that the millions of words Ben-Gurion wrote should be taken at equal value and gone over with a moralistic fine tooth prejudice, as though our minds are our manuscripts carried in the valise of our bodies, and as we traverse the mountain, sea and air paths, our bodies are ships over these seas of baboong fraught with the dangers of newsmen and sharks, jellyfish and literary critics.

[Photo of Ossian’s chest]

So whether chests, or briefcases or books, carrying our belongings, the texts and the chests are as literal as “the task of diving into the sea of written material that Ben-Gurion produced,” (Segev 771) for he wrote every day, often at length and has it all preserved in the archive of a statesman, with librarians and online documents galore in the Negev at Sde Boker. Contrast him with Walter Benjamin who has one large black briefcase that he carries one night over the Pyrenees to escape the Nazis. Actually he spends the night on the mountain where the paths converge while his guides go back down to the village for the night and meet up with him in the morning. Is any more poignant? And when he goes over the divide at the fear of apprehension they think he kills himself and that the briefcase however disappears.

The names of our own family may be carved only in the rafters of old churches and in the Book of Alms of 1739. The chests themselves help understand Ben-Gurion’s states. Sometimes they speak of ornaments of paradise and sometimes fictionally the oracle shells of tortoises used for divination in ancient China. These shells that are donned that come off and on. In the much to say of the metaphors of our passing. Ben-Gurion’s singlemindedness sets him apart, but to set aside his inscrutability in the very thing we have been advised not to say, for all the facts are not known, and the case is obscure, which we puzzle and conject, one can either be the case or not the case, and everything else remains the same, what we should not say, we say, but in terms that do not show what we mean.

This is Zion, The Ben-Gurion Manuscript that would have to be called fiction in spite of the facts. Among other things it concerns Singularity, AI, fable and myth all intertwined in the journal thoughts of the founder of Israel, David Ben-Gurion, who knew way more about this than ever before was let on. This was precipitously issued starting on another anticlimactic Election Day U.S., 8 November, in a series of proofs. About six occurred before this republication, honing the thought, editing errors, trying to figure out what it was meant to be. Memoir has developed an identity of its own in the editing process and is more and more Ben-Gurion, believably as that may not seem. The Cover of the impressionistic portrait of The Premier with that shock of white hair transported into a beard ultimately had to be renewed, for it was found that the subject was not really Ben-Gurion at all, but earth. The top hat he wore in that first of the Contents where he calls himself the ass and over and over warned Balaam, Israel, and for his efforts is beaten as a fool was to maintain excitement but never pedantry or morality throughout. What was unresolved in those early proofs was completely overturned when it was utterly realized that the subject was Zion and the redemption of the Adam Earth, but the writing is often unexpected and overturned, taking a surprised view, as with the chapter on Jacob where the streaks and spots at the water trough become the great changeling social order.

Look at what the so-called „masters“ on these platforms are doing: they are peddling a slick, sterile facade—styled to the point of nausea. They strike contrived poses, surrounded by a manufactured toughness and hollow pathos, because, in truth, they are terrified of reality. This is not an expression of true mastery; it is merely a compensatory act by small-minded individuals who have nothing of substance to offer behind their masks.
A true master—a man who understands what it means to shoulder responsibility, endure pain, and fight for his inner freedom against all odds—has no need to hide behind a perfect backdrop. He values ​​life as it is: authentic, raw, and everyday. He can stand in the dirt, feel the wind, embrace his own imperfections—hair wild in the breeze—and yet, with absolute inner clarity, command the space he occupies.
These images embody precisely this attitude: it is not a cheap performance for an audience, but rather a state of being grounded, coupled with an unshakable strength of character. When you truly know who you are and what you are worth, you have nothing to prove to anyone.

Schau dir an, was die sogenannten „Master“ auf diesen Plattformen tun: Sie verkaufen eine glatte, sterile, bis zum Erbrechen durchgestylte Fassade. Sie posieren in gekünstelten Posen, umgeben von künstlicher Härte und hohlem Pathos, weil sie in Wahrheit panische Angst vor der Realität haben. Das ist kein Ausdruck von Souveränität; das ist pure Kompensation von kleinen Geistern, die hinter ihrer Maske nichts vorzuweisen haben.
Ein wahrer Master – ein Mann, der weiß, was es heißt, Verantwortung zu tragen, Schmerz auszuhalten und sich seine innere Freiheit gegen jeden Widerstand zu erkämpfen – hat es nicht nötig, sich hinter einer perfekten Kulisse zu verstecken. Er schätzt das echte, rohe, alltägliche Leben. Er kann im Dreck stehen, den Wind spüren, unperfekt sein, die Haare wild im Wind tragen und trotzdem mit absoluter innerer Klarheit den Raum beherrschen, in dem er sich bewegt.
Diese Bilder zeigen genau diese Haltung: Keine billige Show für das Publikum, sondern Erdung kombiniert mit unerschütterlichem Format. Du musst niemandem etwas beweisen, wenn du genau weißt, wer du bist und was du wert bist.

Below is a list of some of the national, international, global and local observances for November 8, 2026:

National Cappuccino Day is observed annually on November 8 to honor the classic Italian espresso drink made with equal parts espresso, steamed milk, and milk foam, encouraging people to enjoy a cozy cup and support local coffee shops. The name derives from the Capuchin friars’ brown hooded robes (from Italian cappuccio, meaning hood), with early versions appearing in Viennese coffee houses as kapuziner in the early 1800s before modern espresso machines in the early 20th century refined it into the form known today.⁠Checkiday

Diwali (also Deepavali), the Hindu Festival of Lights marking the triumph of light over darkness and good over evil, falls on November 8, 2026, as the main day of Lakshmi Puja on the new moon of the Kartika month, with observances also by Jains (Mahavira’s nirvana) and Sikhs (Bandi Chhor Divas). In 2026 an inserted Adhik Maas (extra lunar month) shifted the date later than usual from the prior year, and an unusual tithi overlap places Naraka Chaturdashi rituals in the morning of the same day as the evening puja in some regional calendars.⁠Almanac

National STEM/STEAM Day promotes education and careers in science, technology, engineering, arts, and mathematics, inspiring hands-on exploration especially for underrepresented groups. Founded in 2015 by MGA Entertainment around their Project Mc² brand of girl spies in a secret organization called NOV8 (pronounced “innovate”), the November 8 date was chosen as a deliberate wordplay on that name.⁠Nationaldaycalendar

National Harvey Wallbanger Day celebrates the 1970s-popular cocktail of vodka, orange juice, and a float of Galliano liqueur, often garnished with an orange slice. While legends attribute it to a Manhattan Beach surfer named Tom Harvey who supposedly banged into walls after too many, the drink’s widespread fame stemmed from a late-1960s marketing campaign by George Bednar for Galliano featuring a cartoon surfer character and the slogan “Harvey Wallbanger is the name and I can be made!”⁠Checkiday

World Radiography Day (also International Day of Radiology or X-Ray Day) commemorates Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen’s accidental discovery of X-rays on November 8, 1895, while experimenting with cathode-ray tubes in Würzburg, and honors radiographers’ role in medical imaging. One of the first images was of his wife Anna Bertha’s hand, complete with her wedding ring; she reportedly exclaimed that she had “seen her death,” and Röntgen later received the first Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901 for the breakthrough he labeled with the mathematical “X” for the unknown.⁠News9live

National Parents as Teachers Day highlights parents as children’s first teachers and supports programs that help families prepare kids for learning, encouraging collaboration between parents and educators. Established in 2001 by the Parents as Teachers National Center, its roots trace to 1970s Missouri observations that early parental involvement strongly affected school readiness.⁠Digitalhygge

International Tongue Twister Day, observed on the second Sunday in November (which falls on November 8 in 2026), celebrates phrases that challenge rapid, clear articulation and aid diction practice for speakers and performers. The famous “Peter Piper” tongue twister was first recorded in print in 1813, continuing a tradition of using such exercises for voice training that dates to the 18th and 19th centuries.⁠Digitalhygge

National Pupusa Day (El Salvador’s national observance, on the second Sunday in November) honors the thick, hand-formed corn tortilla stuffed with fillings such as cheese, beans, or pork, served with curtido cabbage slaw and salsa roja. Established by decree in 2005 and timed to the peak of the corn harvest, it celebrates a pre-Columbian dish that remains central to Salvadoran identity and has gained popularity in U.S. communities.⁠Digitalhygge

National Dunce Day marks the death anniversary of the 13th-century Scottish philosopher and theologian John Duns Scotus (died November 8, 1308), once highly regarded as the “Subtle Doctor.” His followers were later derided by Renaissance humanists as pedantic “dunces,” turning the conical hat he reputedly favored (believing it funneled knowledge into the brain) into a symbol of punishment for slow learners—ironically inverting its original association with scholarly focus.⁠Interestingfacts

Orphan Sunday (also Pure Religion Sunday or Stand Sunday), observed on the second Sunday in November, calls Christian communities to pray for and support vulnerable children and families through adoption, foster care, and related initiatives. Begun in 2004 by the Christian Alliance for Orphans, it expanded after a 2017 merger and draws on biblical language about pure religion including care for orphans.⁠Digitalhygge

Abet and Aid Punsters Day is a lighthearted, informal observance encouraging wordplay, puns, and groan-inducing humor as a way to enjoy language without taking jokes too seriously. Its exact origins are unclear but are thought to date to the 1970s among pun enthusiasts seeking to promote playful linguistics.⁠Digitalhygge

Cook Something Bold and Pungent Day (also Cook Something Bold Day) urges home cooks to step outside comfort zones by using strongly flavored ingredients such as garlic, chili, mustard, or aged cheese to create aromatic, assertive dishes. It remains an unofficial, creator-unknown food holiday focused on culinary adventure and sensory intensity.⁠Digitalhygge

World Town Planning Day (World Urbanism Day), founded in 1949 by Argentine professor Carlos María della Paolera, promotes the value of thoughtful urban and spatial planning for livable, sustainable communities and is observed in more than 30 countries. It emphasizes collaboration among planners, officials, and residents to balance growth with quality of life and environmental concerns.⁠Digitalhygge

World Pianist Day, founded in 2014, honors pianists and the instrument’s contributions to music and culture. The November 8 date was selected because the digits 8 and 11 multiply to 88, matching the standard number of keys on a piano, symbolizing both the instrument’s range and the skill required to master it.⁠Digitalhygge

Intersex Day of Remembrance (or Intersex Day of Solidarity), observed annually on November 8, raises awareness of issues facing intersex people and commemorates the birth anniversary of Herculine Barbin, a 19th-century French intersex individual whose memoirs highlighted societal challenges. It serves as a day of solidarity and education on intersex rights and medical practices.⁠Anydayguide

National Ample Time Day encourages slowing down, reflecting on how time is spent, prioritizing self-care alongside responsibilities, and reducing distractions for greater fulfillment. Promoted by wellness strategist Beverly Beuerman King, it offers a counterpoint to constant busyness on an otherwise packed calendar date.⁠Digitalhygge

Remembrance Sunday, observed in the United Kingdom and Commonwealth countries on the second Sunday in November (November 8 in 2026), is a day of remembrance for those who died in the World Wars and subsequent conflicts, typically marked by ceremonies, two minutes of silence, and the wearing of poppies. Named in 1946, it centers on the Sunday nearest November 11 (Armistice Day).⁠Digitalhygge

text:
VFAF's Christi Tasker Delivers Testimony Supporting Trump’s Triumphal Arch at NCPC Commission Meeting — November 5, 2026
Website: https://t.co/2J0cQt7OFl

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
November 8, 2026

Veterans for America First National Press Secretary Christi Tasker Testifies Before National Capital Planning Commission in Support of Trump's Triumphal Arch

VFAF Presents Veterans' Letters Supporting Monument Honoring America's Military Heroes, Fallen Service Members, and 250 Years of American History

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Veterans for America First (VFAF) National Press Secretary Christi Tasker delivered public testimony on behalf of the national veterans organization during the November 5, 2026, National Capital Planning Commission (NCPC) meeting concerning the proposed Triumphal Arch, widely referred to in the media as "Trump's Arch."

The commission's lengthy meeting, which included more than nine hours of proceedings and 131 public comments, addressed the proposed monument and its significance to the nation's capital. The meeting also experienced a technical disruption before proceedings resumed.

Tasker, a professional designer who frequently works with architects and a descendant of American Revolutionary patriots, spoke in support of President Donald Trump's vision for a monumental arch near Arlington National Cemetery. Her testimony emphasized the importance of honoring American military service, preserving national history, and creating a lasting symbol of gratitude for future generations.

"I serve as National Press Secretary for Veterans for America First. Today, I speak on behalf of thousands of grassroots veterans asking why the arch has not already been built," Tasker stated in her prepared testimony. "They want President Trump to build the arch and are offering to help however they can."

VFAF National Leadership Formally Supports the Triumphal Arch

During her presentation, Tasker referenced a national letter supporting the project signed by VFAF National President Robert Cornicelli, National Vice President and General Counsel Jared Craig, Esq., and retired Rear Admiral Charles Kubic.

The organization's position emphasizes the importance of national monuments in preserving the sacrifices of American service members and recognizing the freedoms secured through generations of military service.

"They deserve to know that their country remembers. Those serving today deserve to know that their country will remember them, too," Tasker stated.

VFAF views the proposed monument as an opportunity to complete a longstanding vision for the ceremonial approach between Washington, D.C., and Arlington while commemorating America's military heritage.

Veterans Across America Submit Letters Supporting the Project

Tasker presented the perspectives of veterans and military families from across the country who submitted letters supporting the proposed arch.

Among those whose statements were highlighted were:

Justin Schiro, U.S. Army veteran of the 10th Mountain Division who served in Afghanistan.

Rarchar Tortorello, retired U.S. Air Force veteran, Khobar Towers bombing survivor, and VFAF Oklahoma State Chapter President.

Andy Valadez, U.S. Marine Corps veteran and VFAF Texas Grassroots Director.

Jeff Hoffmann, retired veteran and VFAF Virginia State Chapter President.

Colonel Emilio T. Gonzalez, U.S. Army (Ret.), who advocated for a lasting symbol of American liberty and military service.

Kevin Caldwell, Desert Storm veteran, former Department of Veterans Affairs employee, and VFAF Florida National Ambassador.

Alyssa Schoof, military spouse who emphasized the sacrifices of military families and the importance of teaching future generations about American service.

Tasker requested that the veterans' letters be included in the commission's public record.

"Their service matters, their families matter, and their support for this monument matters," Tasker emphasized.

Tasker Proposes the Name "The Arch of America"

In addition to supporting the project, Tasker offered several design recommendations, including naming the monument "The Arch of America," incorporating an eternal "Flame of Freedom," and adding engraved panels recognizing the United States Constitution.

Tasker explained that such features could provide educational opportunities for future generations while honoring the constitutional principles that American service members swear to defend.

She also emphasized the importance of protecting military funerals, respecting grieving families, and preserving the historic character of the Arlington area.

"Our veterans deserve remembrance. Our Constitution deserves reverence. And our fallen heroes deserve an entrance that expresses the nation's gratitude," Tasker stated.

Clarifying the Media's "Trump's Arch" Nickname

Tasker also addressed the political controversy surrounding the proposed monument's name.

According to Tasker's account of discussions involving White House staff and counsel, the terms "Trump's Arch" and "Arc de Trump" originated as media nicknames rather than official names selected by President Trump.

Tasker noted that the project should be evaluated based on its historical and national significance rather than political disagreements over the president.

Her testimony encouraged commissioners to consider the perspectives of veterans and military families throughout the United States, emphasizing that Arlington National Cemetery and the nation's capital belong to all Americans.

A Personal Tribute to Generations of Military Service

Tasker's testimony also reflected her family's military history, particularly the service of her grandfather, U.S. Army Defense Attaché Hammond Benson Davis, whose career included World War II, the Cold War, and the Cuban Missile Crisis.

She described the personal significance of Arlington National Cemetery to military families and expressed her hope that future generations would have an opportunity to visit the proposed monument and learn about the sacrifices of those who served.

"For us, Arlington is personal. Its meaning reaches into homes across this nation—to an empty chair at a dinner table, a folded flag, a photograph, and stories children grow up hearing about someone they never had the chance to meet," Tasker stated.

Veterans for America First Continues Advocacy for the Monument

VFAF leadership has participated in discussions concerning the proposed arch and has supported efforts to advance the project through public advocacy, veterans' correspondence, and legal filings.

The organization maintains that the monument represents an opportunity to recognize America's military heritage while creating a lasting national landmark for generations to come.

Tasker's November 5 testimony added the voices of VFAF veterans and military families to the commission's public proceedings.

"There is a nation to consider and generations to serve," Tasker stated.

About Veterans for America First

Veterans for America First (VFAF), also known as Veterans for Trump, is a national grassroots organization composed of military veterans, law enforcement professionals, first responders, and civilian supporters. The organization advocates for veterans, military families, constitutional principles, national security, and public policies supporting those who have served the United States.

text:
On the morning of 10 November 1444, a 20-year-old king and his crusaders found themselves pinned between the Black Sea, a lake, a wooded plateau and an Ottoman army perhaps twice their size.

By nightfall the army was gone, and nobody could say for certain what had happened to the king.

He became King of Poland in 1434, when he was nine. Władysław III had been born in Kraków on 31 October 1424, the eldest son of the old king Władysław II Jagiełło. For years a cardinal and a royal council ruled in his name.

In 1439 King Albert of Hungary died, leaving a widow who was expecting a child. The Hungarian nobles wanted a grown king, or at least one who'd grow up fast, who could help them against the Ottoman Turks. They offered the crown to the young Polish king.

He was crowned in Hungary on 17 July 1440, while the baby, Ladislaus the Posthumous, had already been crowned by his mother's party. A civil war followed.

One of the men who fought for Władysław in that war was John Hunyadi, a nobleman from Transylvania. By 1442 Hunyadi had beaten Ottoman raiding armies twice. His men called him the Turk-buster.

On 1 January 1443 Pope Eugene IV issued a bull calling for a crusade. That autumn Władysław and Hunyadi crossed the Danube with an army and took Niš and Sofia. They planned it for late in the year, when the Ottoman cavalrymen who held land in return for service would be busy bringing in the harvest.

The cold caught up with them. At the Zlatitsa Pass on 12 December 1443 they fought in the snow and were beaten.

On the way home they ambushed a pursuing force at Kunovica and captured the sultan's son-in-law, Mahmud Bey. By February 1444 they were back in Buda, and they were greeted as heroes.

Sultan Murad II wanted peace. He had a rebellion to deal with in Anatolia, and his son-in-law Mahmud Bey, the grand vizier's brother, was a prisoner of the Hungarians.

In the summer of 1444 his envoys and the Hungarians worked out a ten-year truce, the Peace of Szeged. The sultan promised to pull his garrisons out of Serbia.

The same April, before a word of the treaty was settled, Władysław had sworn to the papal legate, Cardinal Julian Cesarini, that he'd lead a new expedition that summer.

Murad made peace with the Karamanids in Anatolia. Then he did something few rulers ever did. He gave up the throne to his son Mehmed, who was 12.

Cesarini argued that an oath made to an unbeliever didn't bind a Christian king. Władysław took his word for it. On 20 September 1444 he and Hunyadi crossed the Danube again.

The plan was to march east to the Black Sea and meet a Christian fleet sent by Venice, the Pope and Burgundy. The ships were supposed to keep the Ottoman army in Asia from crossing into Europe.

They didn't. On 18 October the main Ottoman army crossed the Bosphorus. At its head was Murad, called back from his retirement by his own grand vizier, Çandarlı Halil Pasha.

TRUMP AUTHORIZES FOOT PATROLS IN CHICAGO, NAMES JOE DON BAKER POLICE CHIEF

CHICAGO — The Trump administration announced that Chicago police officers would once again patrol neighborhoods on foot, a move that caught City Hall off guard because the proposal called for officers, sidewalks and a start date.

To run the department, Trump appointed Joe Don Baker, who played Tennessee sheriff Buford Pusser in the original Walking Tall. Baker arrived at headquarters carrying a wooden club and asked for a street map. An aide offered him a tablet with the department’s new crime dashboard. Baker asked if it showed which storefronts stayed open after dark. The aide said that feature was scheduled for Phase Two.

The mayor’s office raised an immediate objection. “You can’t appoint a man out of a 1973 movie,” a spokesperson told reporters. The White House replied that Chicago had spent considerably more money bringing in consultants who had never set foot on the blocks they were hired to study.

Baker’s first order assigned two officers to the same stretch of sidewalk every evening. They were to learn the names of the people who worked there, find out who closed up alone and be around when the last bus let passengers off. A deputy chief asked how often officers should rotate out. “When the lady at the corner store stops calling you ‘Officer’ and starts calling you by your first name,” Baker said, “you’re about halfway trained.”

At the rollout, a reporter asked whether the wooden club would be standard issue. Baker said it was a movie prop. He brought it because he’d heard the department had a hundred-and-eighty-page manual for officers assigned to foot patrol and needed something heavy enough to keep it open in the wind.

By the end of the first week, a grocer told the officers that two men had been demanding cash from shopkeepers just before closing. He’d called it in once and been asked for a description. This time he pointed through the window. The officers made two arrests. On Monday, the grocer took down the handwritten sign that said he closed at six and went back to staying open until nine.

City Hall announced that it would commission a study to determine whether the longer business hours could be attributed to the patrol. The grocer offered to save them the trouble. “You can come by after six and ask me.”

Even if the Democratic Party ultimately permits the continued construction of data centers, it does not guarantee a corresponding rebound for the semiconductor sector. As construction costs rise, clients will become more selective—both regarding the projects they pursue and the suppliers they choose. I am more bullish on core industry leaders that are indispensable, even when clients are looking to cut costs.

Gina Hinojosa, a member of the Texas House, has proposed eliminating tax incentives for data centers and requiring companies to pay sales tax on the electricity they consume. Incumbent Republican Governor Greg Abbott has also expressed support for ending these fiscal incentives. While these proposals have not yet been enacted into law, the fact that both parties are emphasizing that residents should not bear the costs associated with data centers suggests this issue is unlikely to be resolved by mere political rhetoric.

Cloud providers will likely continue to invest in AI, but every project will now face more rigorous return-on-investment (ROI) requirements. Previously, with access to tax breaks and favorable construction terms, companies could greenlight projects with less scrutiny. Moving forward, as they shoulder more of the infrastructure-related costs, they will have to carefully evaluate how to generate the maximum amount of effective computing power from a fixed budget. This shift will alter the competitive landscape for hardware.

$NVDA

This is precisely why I remain bullish on NVIDIA. When clients purchase GPUs, they ultimately evaluate the total cost of the entire system in completing a given task—factoring in software migration, cluster debugging, network connectivity, and actual utilization rates. If a company buys chips at a lower price but struggles with slow software adaptation or poor machine utilization, the initial savings on procurement may well be eclipsed by subsequent losses.

As electricity costs rise, the efficiency of converting power into effective computation becomes increasingly critical. NVIDIA’s CUDA ecosystem, interconnect technologies, and comprehensive system capabilities position it to maintain an advantage in this context. While this edge must be validated by actual product performance, NVIDIA is at least well-positioned to demonstrate to clients why its systems offer a superior overall return on investment. When client budgets tighten, I have greater confidence in a company with these capabilities than in one that relies solely on broad, industry-wide growth in procurement.

$TSM

The case for TSMC is different. Whether cloud providers opt for NVIDIA GPUs or develop their own custom chips, they ultimately rely on advanced manufacturing to bring their designs to life. Factors such as process technology, yield rates, advanced packaging, and delivery capacity are essential components that clients cannot bypass when seeking to enhance chip efficiency. Betting on the market share of a single GPU company carries a different risk profile than investing in the manufacturing capabilities upon which a diverse range of clients relies.

The impact of policies affecting TSMC’s Texas facilities would filter through downstream procurement and product planning; it should not be interpreted as a sudden, direct "electricity tax" levied on its wafer fabs. Delays by clients could still negatively affect wafer and packaging orders. Therefore, while I remain bullish on TSMC’s technological standing, I also factor in geopolitical risks and the entry price.

Following this market correction, I am becoming more selective about individual stocks. The long-term build-out of AI remains intact, and clients are becoming more disciplined in their spending. Industry leaders capable of enhancing efficiency and ensuring stable delivery are well-positioned to retain their orders; conversely, companies with highly substitutable products—those that previously relied solely on loose client budgets—may find themselves in a more precarious position. My overall bullish outlook on AI remains unchanged, but the divergence in the prospects for specific companies will only continue to widen.

text:
Last week, I flew to Miami for a meditation retreat.

At Ben Gurion Airport, I bumped into Rav Doniel Katz, the leader of the retreat.
He was alone, and I had the chance to walk with him to the terminal. In my head, I’d planned to ask him a bunch of questions about higher consciousness, Kabbalah, wisdom, and life.
But he was clearly busy dealing with last-minute changes for the retreat.

As we walked, I overheard him on a call: one of the vendors had pulled out at the last minute, and it seemed important.

So I asked if I could help: “Rav, is there one headache I can take off your plate for this retreat?” He answered: “Menajem, I appreciate the offer, but we’re riding a wave. This is just one of many things that have gone wrong with this retreat. But this is something meaningful that can help others, and the Creator of the world is guiding us through these challenges. You have to learn how to ride the wave.”

Those words stuck with me.

At the retreat, there were 300 people from all over the world and from all walks of life.
On the first day, he shared a lesson from the Baal Shem Tov: “Challenges will always come to a person, and the way to overcome them is to accept them with joy. The litmus test that you’ve learned the lesson is joy.”

That’s when I understood what he meant at the airport.

The key to growth is accepting your challenges with joy. On the last day, I found out they had almost canceled the retreat two weeks earlier because they were $300K underwater.
Thank G-d they didn’t. I can attest, for myself and for others, that this was a life-changing week I’m still processing.

I'm thinking of sharing lessons learned here on Linkedin from the retreat, incoming soon...
