text:
Remember when, in 2012, Rush Limbaugh's comments on his show got him dropped by multiple advertisers?

The whole thing started when Sandra Fluke, a law student at Georgetown, was invited to speak to Congressional Democrats about why Georgetown (a Catholic university) should be mandated to pay for birth control drugs for any student getting health insurance through the university. Fluke argued that contraceptives could cost up to $3,000 for law students, and that not paying for them created financial hardship for the school's female students.

Rush jumped on that point, and argued that Fluke essentially wanted to be "paid to have sex," and called her a "slut" and a "prostitute." He continued to say that she was "having so much sex, she cannot afford her own birth control pills and she agrees Obama should provide them, or the Pope."

The backlash was swift. Over 100 members of Georgetown's faculty signed a letter in support of Fluke. 75 Democrats signed a letter condemning Limbaugh, saying his comments were "an abuse of public airwaves." Even Republicans came out against Rush—Mitt Romney, Rick Santorum, Ron Paul, John McCain, and then-Speaker John Boehner all condemned Rush's comments. Several artists even requested their songs not be used as bumper music on the show anymore.

The real heat came when several social media campaigns were formed to boycott advertisers for The Rush Limbaugh Show, pushing them to drop their sponsorships. And it worked. Over a dozen advertisers dropped within a few days. By the following week, the number had grown to 45 advertisers pulling out. Media Matters For America continued a sustained campaign to try and get local stations to drop their broadcasts of The Rush Limbaugh Show. That one didn't really work.

A few days after the comments and after the first sponsors started to pull ads, Rush offered an apology, saying that he didn't intend for his remarks to come off as a personal attack, and that he "acted too much like the leftists who despise [him]." This apology was roundly rejected as insufficient and insincere, including by Fluke.

Rush's show would eventually recover the advertising revenue, and he would keep hosting it until his death in 2021. Fluke attempted to run for California State Senate in 2014, but was defeated, and has kept a low profile since.

So why remember this at all? Three reasons. 

First boycotting advertisers for reasons related to politics has been a thing for a long time, so this is nothing new. Boycotts and buycotts are just how things work.

Second, there's a marked difference between defending a host calling someone a "slut" on their show, and defending one who laughs at the idea of digging up a victim of violence and subjecting them to it again. Insulting words and violent behavior are not on the same level, even if both can get you dropped by your sponsors.

And third, it's true what they say—freedom of speech doesn't make you free from consequences.

text: 19. A further miracle of the same kind was wrought by Christ our God through Willibrord’s blessing. On one occasion the servant of God came with his companions to the house of a friend of his and wished to break the tedium of the long journey by taking a meal at his friend’s house. But it came to his ears that the head of the house had no wine. He gave orders that four small flasks, which were all that his companions carried with them for their needs on the journey, should be brought to him. Then he blessed them in the name of Him who at the marriage feast of Cana changed water into wine-and, remarkable to relate, after this gracious blessing about forty people drank their fill from these small bottles, and with great thanksgiving and joyful hearts said one to another: “The Lord Jesus has in truth fulfilled His promise in the Gospel: ‘He that believeth in me will do the deeds I do, and greater than these shall he do.'” . 20. Once, when this holy preacher was going in haste towards Frisia in order, as usual, to preach the Gospel, he wanted to pasture his horses, worn out by the fatigue of the journey, in the meadows of a certain wealthy landowner. The man, seeing horses feeding in his meadows, began to beat them and drive them out of his pastures with great arrogance. The man of God accosted him with peaceable words and said: “Brother, do us no harm. Our purpose in wishing to rest in these meadows is not to do you harm but to meet our own needs. We are under obligation to pursue the work of God, and you also might share in its rewards if, as far as lies in your power, you help us in a friendly spirit, mindful of the sweet promise of Christ: ‘ He that receiveth you, receiveth me, and he that receiveth me, receiveth him that sent me.’ Be at peace, and rather as a friend take a drink with us by way of refreshment. Then when we have gone on our way, return to your house with the blessing of God.” The man, however, persisted in his ill-­will and would not listen to the reasonable words of the man of God, but, on the contrary, repeated his abuse and continued to insult him. “You ask me to drink with you,” he said, “and make peace: be assured that I set no store whatever upon drinking with you.” The man of God took the words out of his mouth and said: “If you will not drink with me, then do not drink at all.”Thereupon, as soon as his companions were ready, he went on his way. The obstinate man also hurriedly went home, but was seized almost at once with a burning thirst which he tried in vain to assuage with wine, for the mouth that had cast reproaches upon the man of God was unable to swallow a single draught. Thus the man who would not of his own accord make peace with the servant of God was now compelled to bear within himself the penalty of his fault. Doctors were called to relieve his thirst and to restore to the sufferer his power of drinking. His whole being cried out for relief, but no one could get a drop of wine to reach his parched throat. At last, struck with remorse, he came to his senses, and, discovering that the saintly man he had reviled was Willibrord, he began to yearn intensely for his return. In the following year, Willibrord came back by the same way, and on hearing of his approach the sick man hurried out to meet him. Confessing his sin and telling him of the suffering he had endured, he besought him for the love of Christ to release him from it. The man of God was moved with pity, released him from his punishment and allowed him to drink from his own cup. Thereupon the man who was released drank and returned to his own house cured. . 21. In the town of Treves there is a convent of nuns,[l9. Probably Saint Marien­ad ­Martyres, where the portable altar of Saint Willibrord is still preserved.] which in the days of Willibrord was visited with a terrible plague. Many of the nuns died of the infection, others were confined to bed by severe sickness, whilst the rest were in a state of extreme terror, expecting death at any moment. At a short distance from this town stands the monastery of the holy man, called Echternach, in which his body reposes to this day and which his successors are known to have held by lawful bequest of the said father and through the goodwill of pious kings. Learning that the holy man was coming thither, the women of the above-­mentioned convent sent a deputation beseeching him to come to them without delay. When he heard their request, the man of God, instructed by the gracious example of Saint Peter, Prince of the Apostles, who went from Joppa to Lydda at the request of the widows of Christ in order to raise holy Tabitha to life, went to their assistance without delay. On arriving at the convent, he immediately celebrated Mass for the sick and then blessed water and ordered it to be sprinkled about the buildings and given to the nuns to drink. Through the mercy of God they speedily recovered and there were no more deaths in that convent from the plague. . 22. It happened that a head of a family and his household were afflicted by a terrible visitation of devilish sorcery, and it became quite obvious from the horrors and evil tricks that occurred there that the house was haunted by a wicked spirit. For it would suddenly seize food and clothing and other household goods and throw them into the fire. Once, indeed, whilst the parents were asleep, it snatched their little boy as he rested in their arms and hurled him into the fire, and it was only with great difficulty that the parents, roused by the child’s screams, rescued him from the flames. Many were the ill turns that the family had to endure at the hands of this execrable spirit and no priest was able to exorcize it. Eventually the holy man Willibrord, at the father’s urgent request, sent them some holy water and directed them to sprinkle it over all the furniture after it had been taken out of doors, for the man of God foresaw that the whole house would be consumed by fire. When they had done this, a conflagration broke out in the very place where the bed had stood, and, quickly enveloping the house, reduced it to ashes. After another house had been built on the site of the old one and blessed with holy water the family suffered no more from their former trial and thenceforth lived in peace, giving thanks to the Lord who had deigned to deliver them through the hands of His servant. . 23. The same holy man, who was pleasing to God, also prophesied certain things that were subsequently verified by the course of events. He baptized Pippin the Short, son of the valiant Charles Martel, King of the Franks and father of the present illustrious Charles, who governs the Franks at the present day in triumph, dignity and glory. Of Pippin, father of the last named, Willibrord uttered the following prediction in the presence of his disciples: “Know that this child will be highly exalted and renowned. He will be greater than all the kings of the Franks who have gone before him.” The truth of this prophecy has been fulfilled in our times and there is no need to prove what is universally acknowledged throughout the whole kingdom. For all the people know what wonderful victories this illustrious conqueror has gained, how widely he has extended the bounds of his empire, how devotedly he has promoted the Christian religion and how he has defended the Holy Church of God abroad. All these things can be more clearly seen with the eye than set forth in words. . 24. Now this holy man was distinguished by every kind of natural quality: he was of middle height, dignified mien, comely of face, cheerful in spirit, wise in counsel, pleasing in speech, grave in character and energetic in everything he undertook for God. His forbearance is shown by the actions we have recorded above. How great was his zeal in preaching the Gospel of Christ and how he was sustained in the labour of preaching by the grace of God we need not set forth in writing, since it is vouched for by the testimony of all. His personal life can be inferred from his vigils and prayers, his fasting and singing of psalms, the holiness of his conduct and his many miracles. His charity is made manifest in the unremitting labours which he bore daily for the name of Christ. This holy man, who progressed every day of his life in the work of God, who was pleasing to God and friendly to all the people, was laid to his fathers in the time of the elder Charles, the valiant ruler of the Franks. He was then an old man coming to the end of his days and was about to receive from God a generous reward for his labours. He forsook this world to take possession of heaven and to behold Christ for ever in eternal glory, in whose love he had never ceased to labour as long as he lived in our midst. On the sixth of November, that is, the eighth day before the Ides, he passed from this place of pilgrimage to the eternal country and was buried in the monastery of Echternach, which, as we have said before, he had built to the glory of God. There to this day, through the mercy of God, miracles of healing are constantly performed beside the relics of the holy priest of God. That some of these should be appended to our account of his life we regard as redounding to the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ, who so often deigned to perform them at the request of His servant. . 25. His venerable body was laid to rest in a marble sarcophagus, which at first was found to be six inches too short to hold the entire body of God’s servant. The brethren were greatly concerned at this, and, being at a loss to know what to do, they discussed the matter again and again, wondering where they could find a suitable resting-­place for his sacred remains. Wonderful to relate, however, through the loving-­kindness of God the sarcophagus was suddenly discovered to be as much longer than the holy man’s body as previously it had been shorter. Therein they laid the remains of the man of God, and to the accompaniment of hymns and psalms and every token of respect it was interred in the church of the monastery which he had built and dedicated in honour of the Blessed Trinity. A sweet and marvellous fragrance filled the air, so that all were conscious that the ministry of angels had been present at the last rites of the holy man. . 26. The death of the holy man was revealed to one of his religious disciples who was stationed at some distance from the monastery as he was keeping watch in prayer. He testifies that he saw the soul of his saintly father surrounded by a bright radiance as it was being carried by a host of angels towards the realms above, all singing his praises. Likewise many of the brothers have testified that they have frequently seen a wonderful light over the bed on which he gave back his blessed soul to his Creator, and perceived there a ravishing fragrance and most sweet odour. From these signs one can only surmise that the denizens of heaven used to visit the spot from which his saintly soul had passed to the Lord. . 27. Many sick persons, through the grace of God and assisted by their own faith, have been cured after being anointed with the oil from the lamp which burns over the relics of the holy man. Penitents also frequently came to the church wearing rings on their arms, as the custom then was, and the links were broken and they were loosed from their bonds. Evidence of this are the rings which hang in the church to this day. . 28. There was a certain woman suffering from paralysis and who had been tormented for seven years with severe pain, whose infirmity had increased so much from day to day that she had completely lost the use of her limbs and had to rely upon the help of others. So frail was she that she could scarcely breathe. This woman was carried by her relatives to the church in which the saint of God lay at rest and placed near the casket of his relics. There, with many tears, she prayed that God in His mercy might have pity on her through the intercession of His holy servant. Her prayer was heard by the Lord our God, and suddenly she was delivered from all her infirmities and restored to health. And she, who had previously been carried into the church by others, ran home upon her own feet, joyfully giving thanks to God. . 29. In like manner a young man afflicted with sickness was brought by his friends to the body of the blessed prelate. He trembled in every limb and was totally unable to raise his head, which lolled and twisted this way and that as if it had not been fixed on his neck. Sometimes, too, he became so inert as to appear completely lifeless. This young man, as we have said, was placed near the body of the saint by his friends, and through the mercy of God was so quickly cured, in the presence of all the onlookers, that no trace remained of his former infirmity and long-­standing affliction. A certain man who held the office of deacon in the church of the saint though he was quite unworthy of it) did not scruple to steal, among other things that had been offered to the church, a golden cross which the holy man used to carry with him on his travels. The brethren were distressed at this, and, though ignorant of the perpetrator of this sacrilege, they felt confident that through the prayers of the saint of God so heinous a crime could not long be concealed. They tried, nevertheless, in their brotherly kindness to bring the culprit to repentance, not wishing to encompass his downfall. But the man who had committed the crime hardened his heart and despised his own salvation, even as, according to Solomon, “the wicked man continues when he comes to the depths of his evil deeds”. The unhappy wretch thought that the deed, which had been committed in secret and unseen by others, would remain undetected, but it could not be hidden from the eye of God, to whom all things lie open and who is often not slow to avenge the wrongs done to His servants. For the miserable wretch who had not scrupled to commit the offence was suddenly seized with sickness and died a miserable death, and in his dying moments confessed his guilt to some of the brethren and divulged the place where he had hidden the stolen objects. You see, brethren, what a fearful judgment was visited upon the man who presumed to desecrate the church of God’s saint by stealing. I beseech you, therefore, to keep your manner of life pure in this house, so that in His mercy and through the intercession of the apostolic man Saint Clement He may deign to hear your prayers when you make your petitions, just as we have already told you how he heard the prayers of the sick in this same church, enabling them to return home with the good health they had long yearned for. Nor need we doubt that just as he deigned visibly to heal their bodily diseases, so also through the intercession of the saint on our behalf, whose body rests here and whom we believe to be present in the spirit, listening to our prayers, he will continue daily to cure the hidden disorders of our souls, if with flrm faith and sincere confession we pour out our hearts with tears in that place before the merciful face of Him who in His mercy is quick to pardon if we are not slow to ask. Praise and glory be His for ever and ever. It only remains now to speak of blessed Wilgils, who, as we have said, was the father of this holy man, for as the first chapter of this story began with him, so the last must close with a reference to him. It was on the anniversary of the sacred death of Wilgils that the good abbot Aldberct, successor to the venerable archbishop, proposed to eat and rejoice with the brethren after the solemnities of the Mass and the thanksgiving due to God. In the monastery, unfortunately, there were left only two flagons of wine; and since one of them had been drunk at the midday meal, the other was put by for supper. Accordingly, after Vespers had been sung in honour of that day the brethren returned to the refectory; and when they came to the end of the reading the abbot addressed the brethren with these words: “It is fitting, reverend Fathers, that we should celebrate the feast days of our venerable predecessors with spiritual rejoicing and should allow our bodies somewhat more indulgence than our usual strictness permits, not from motives of gluttony but of love. Now if there were anything in the monastery that I could offer you beyond this single flagon of wine which is left over from the midday meal I should certainly not withhold it from you. But God is able through the prayer of His saints to make even this prove more than sufficient for our needs, alike to honour them as to gladden us, and to demonstrate to us, unworthy as we are, the kindly power of Him who once through the blessing of our former father, the holy Willibrord, condescended to satisfy forty men from four flagons. Let us drink what we have with rejoicing and with hope.” . After all the brethren had drunk from the boule a first and a second time the server found it as full as before. When the abbot was acquainted with this he joined the brethren in giving thanks to God; and, doing honour to the divine mercy, they drank soberly but gladly that night as much as they desired. . O happy father to beget such a son and to be deemed worthy by God of having such an heir! In thee is fulfilled the blessing which is read in Deuteronomy: “Blessed shalt thou be, and blessed shall be the fruit of thy body.”

text:
You're actually proving my point. You speak English here because it allows you to communicate with people from different countries. Now apply that same logic to a Polish hotel, restaurant, or business dealing with international tourists. How is that any different? They're adapting to tourists, who in return bring in revenue. That's literally how business works. You offer a service in exchange for money. So why would you deliberately limit your own opportunities for success?

And this idea that people should only speak the language of the country they're in is ridiculous. Poland itself was once part of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth (for over hundreds of years), a state where people from different ethnic and linguistic backgrounds lived alongside each other. Polish is a Slavic language, Lithuanian is Baltic, yet people still found ways to communicate.

Not everyone wants to live in a bubble, interacting only with their own countrymen. Some people actually enjoy meeting foreigners, learning about other cultures, expanding their knowledge, and making money while doing so.

Nobody is asking Poles to abandon their language or demanding that everyone speak English. You're arguing against something nobody said, while completely ignoring the arguments I've brought up.

Learning another language isn't surrendering your identity. It's expanding your opportunities. Why is that so difficult to understand?

text:
The book of Genesis is well known, and is the creationist story Judaism, Islam and Christianity view as the beginning of life on Earth. There is no point in questioning this story as there are so many interpretations and so much evidence in favor of and against the story that it just goes on and on without a conclusion. 

So Moses gave us the history of the beginning of the world. I don't know how he figured woman was made from the rib of man, but what do I know? I wasn't there and I'm not privy to the technology of a creative God.

As the story unfolds and we pass the Great Flood, we meet Abram.

Gen 12, 6. And Abram passed through the land unto the place of Sichem, unto the plain of Moreh. And the Canaanite was then in the land. 7. And the LORD appeared unto Abram, and said, Unto thy seed will I give this land: and there builded he an altar unto the LORD, who appeared unto him.

Here is where my suspicions begin. I'm looking to the Bible as a source of wisdom and a path to peace and tranquility. Here, the God of the Bible, is promising Abram and all his children the land the Canaanites lived in. I don't yet see the connection between being a good person and acquiring land that belongs to someone else. Who is this Abram that God would favor him with such wealth at the expense of others? What did he do to deserve this?

In the rest of this chapter Abram lies to the Pharaoh of Egypt, telling him that his beautiful wife is merely his sister. The alleged reason for lying is that Abram is afraid he will be killed so the Pharaoh could take his wife. But as soon as the Pharaoh discovers Abram is married to this beautiful woman, he simply tells them to go on their way, along with...

Gen 12 16. And he entreated Abram well for her sake: and he had sheep, and oxen, and he asses, and menservants, and maidservants, and she asses, and camels.

The Pharaoh gave them the wealth of animals and servants while thinking he was going to marry Abram's "sister". It doesn't take much to see this was a scam. Abram purposely duped the Pharaoh with a plan to steal some wealth for himself. The Pharaoh didn't kill Abram when he found out he was married to her. He actually seemed hurt. How can we believe the Pharaoh would have killed Abram for having a beautiful wife when he didn't kill him after pulling his scam?

Gen 13 1. And Abram went up out of Egypt, he, and his wife, and all that he had, and Lot with him, into the south. 2. And Abram was very rich in cattle, in silver, and in gold.

As I'm reading Genesis, I'm in a state of disbelief. But I read on, ever hopeful the story will change to the path leading to inner peace.

In Genesis 13 Abram and Lot have more cattle than the land can handle, so Lot goes to Jordan and Abram went to Canaan. And supposedly God speaks to Abram at that place and tells him he can own all the land he sees in all directions and that his progeny will increase vastly.

It's becoming clear that this story is about a man, made wealthy through a scam, becoming even greedier and taking the land of others, all in the name of God. This is the whole plot of all the books written by Moses. There is no story of becoming a good person, this is a story of how to destroy a nation so that one's personal fortunes can grow. It is the story repeated throughout history even to Pilgrims' invasion of North America and Hitler's attempt at taking Europe. It is the story continually played and replayed ad nauseum in the Middle East even today.

The story continues in Genesis 17 and God declares that all males should be circumcised. This practice started when Abram, whose name is now Abraham, and is 100 years old. At 100 Abraham would be suffering from infections of the fore skin so circumcision would make sense. But he declares that it was God's will that ALL men be circumcised.

So far we haven't heard one word concerning inner peace, spiritual growth, or goodness of behavior. It is becoming clearer that this God of Abraham's is just an alter ego. 300 years after the Roman destruction of the New Jerusalem Church (which Jesus was a member,) Constantine realized the same thing... That "God" is a means for controlling the masses. God is an unseen overseer much like Big Brother in George Orwell's 1984. In repeating the story of the Pentateuch, the Catholic Church was invented by Constantine for the very same purpose, and history once again repeated this cycle of mass control through fear of an unseen God.

In Genesis 19 we are given the story of justified incest. Whereas God would help Abraham have a son at age 100, he leaves it to Lot's daughters to get him drunk and to have sex with them. My spiritual path is on hold now as I force myself to read the rest of the Bible. I have to see where this is leading. I suspect that I may have found the source of today's worldly troubles.

In Genesis 20 Abraham tells another bold lie to Abimelech king of Gerar. He tells the king Sarah is his sister, pulling the same scam he pulled on the Pharaoh with his previous wife. And God, He doesn't think anything wrong with this. In fact, He has it out with Abimelech king of Gerar, the man Abraham and Sarah lied to. Does this sound familiar...

Gen 20 14. And Abimelech took sheep, and oxen, and menservants, and womenservants, and gave them unto Abraham, and restored him Sarah his wife.

In the story between Genesis 20 and 21 we are told the king didn't have sex with Sarah, but because he did have sex with her he had committed sin. So to appease God, the king gave Abraham sheep, oxen, menservants, maidservants, and gave back his wife, Sarah. Of course this is contradictory and we are to believe that Sarah came back, not having sex, but pregnant nonetheless. So Isaac was born, but was he really Abraham's son or was he King Abimelech's son?

God tells Abraham to offer his son, Isaac, up as a burnt offering in Genesis 22. This is supposedly to test Abraham's faith. Where were social services then? Is this the means a loving God uses to test the faith of his chosen ones? Aside from the fact that such a practice would be illegal today (along with incest and taking other people's lands and property through scams,) could any true Christian, Jew or Muslim honestly believe God would ask the same of them? Is this the level of human character we should aspire to? To be willing to offer our only child, which God helped us bear by having our wife impregnated by a deceived king, who didn't really have sex with her?

The Bible records a financial transaction between Abraham and Ephron for a cemetery plot for the deceased Sarah in Genesis 23. This land God was going to give to Abraham, Abraham had to purchase instead from the children of Heth.

Abraham then sends a servant to find Isaac a wife under auspicious pretenses. The servant meets Rebekah at a well and all goes according to plan. While reciting the story of these auspicious occurrences to Rebekah's father the servant states...

Gen 24 34.And he said, I am Abraham's servant. 35.And the LORD hath blessed my master greatly; and he is become great: and he hath given him flocks, and herds, and silver, and gold, and menservants, and maidservants, and camels, and asses.

If her father had only known the truth as to how Abraham gained his wealth...

As Rebekah's family is saying goodbye to her they are reported to have said...

Gen 24 60.And they blessed Rebekah, and said unto her, Thou art our sister, be thou the mother of thousands of millions, and let thy seed possess the gate of those which hate them.

This sounds suspicious. Someone already knew how her children would take the lands of those who hated them. Either that, or the author of the story embellished the tale a bit to justify the carnage yet to come.

Abraham then married one last time and had six more boys before dying at the age of 175, 75 years after the birth of Isaac.

text:
🇨🇳 五国：明明已经涨价很多年，脑海里却还停在旧价格的东西 TOP10
🇯🇵 5か国：値上がりして何年もたつのに、頭の中では昔の値段のままのもの TOP10
🇰🇷 5개국: 오른 지 오래됐는데, 머릿속 가격표는 아직 옛날에 멈춘 것들 TOP10
🇻🇳 5 quốc gia: Giá đã tăng từ lâu, trong đầu vẫn nhớ mức giá ngày trước TOP10
🇺🇸 Five Countries: Things That Cost More Now but Still Carry an Old Price Tag in Your Head TOP10
🇨🇳 中国
按童年、求学和初入社会的价格记忆，选取十个虚构场景。属于编辑选题，不是物价统计；个人记住的旧价，也不代表当年的统一市价。
1）早餐豆浆油条 | 豆乳と揚げパンの朝食 | 두유와 유탸오 아침식사 | Bữa sáng sữa đậu nành và quẩy | Soy milk and fried dough breakfast
点单时还是学生时代那套习惯，付款时才发现，脑子里的早餐预算还没毕业。
2）公交车票 | バス運賃 | 버스 요금 | Vé xe buýt | Bus fares
记得很牢的是第一次自己坐车时带的零钱。后来路线换了，支付方式换了，那枚记忆里的硬币还没换。
3）理发 | 散髪 | 이발 | Cắt tóc | Haircuts
头发已经从学生头剪到上班族的样子，心里对“一次理发多少钱”的答案，却还在以前那家小店里。

4）电影票 | 映画のチケット | 영화표 | Vé xem phim | Movie tickets
总拿当年那次优惠活动作比较。忘了自己记住的，可能是某个下午、某种渠道和一张特别便宜的票。
5）瓶装水 | ペットボトルの水 | 생수 | Nước đóng chai | Bottled water
拿水时动作很熟练，结账时会短暂停一下。然后才看见品牌、容量和购买地点，早已不是记忆里的组合。

6）方便面 | インスタント麺 | 인스턴트 라면 | Mì ăn liền | Instant noodles
脑海里的价格，连着宿舍热水和月底余额。现在买的是不同口味，比较的却还是那一碗旧日生活。
7）学校食堂的一餐 | 学食の一食 | 학교 식당 한 끼 | Một bữa ở căng tin trường | A school cafeteria meal
毕业很多年，还会用食堂那顿饭衡量外面的套餐。那个价格里可能有特定的供餐安排，记忆却只留下了实付金额。
8）第一次租房的房租 | 初めて借りた部屋の家賃 | 처음 구한 방의 월세 | Tiền thuê căn phòng đầu tiên | Rent on your first room
后来比较住处，总忍不住提起第一次租的房间。面积、位置、合租人数都变了，心里的参照物还没搬家。
9）打印复印 | 印刷・コピー | 인쇄·복사 | In và photocopy | Printing and photocopying
还记得学校门口按页算的那张价目表。换到别的店，才想起纸张、彩色和装订也都要分别计算。
10）生日蛋糕 | 誕生日ケーキ | 생일 케이크 | Bánh sinh nhật | Birthday cakes
记住的是小时候全家围着分的那一个。现在看见标价，会先惊讶，再发现自己想买回来的还包括那张饭桌。
你脑海里最顽固的旧价格是哪一个？它对应的是哪一年、哪家店，还是哪一段生活？

🇯🇵 日本
子どもの頃、学生時代、働き始めた頃の価格記憶から十の架空の場面を選びました。物価統計ではなく、個人が覚えている値段も当時の全国共通価格ではありません。

1）コンビニのおにぎり | 便利店饭团 | 편의점 삼각김밥 | Cơm nắm cửa hàng tiện lợi | Convenience store rice balls
手に取る動作は昔のままなのに、会計で少し立ち止まる。頭の中には、学生の頃によく買った商品の値段が残っている。
2）自動販売機の飲み物 | 自动售货机饮料 | 자판기 음료 | Đồ uống từ máy bán hàng tự động | Vending machine drinks
昔持ち歩いていた小銭の組み合わせを覚えている。商品も容器も変わったのに、予算だけがその頃のままだ。
3）ラーメン | 拉面 | 라멘 | Mì ramen | Ramen
最初に一人で通った店が基準になっている。別の街で別の一杯を食べても、心の中ではあの券売機と比べてしまう。
4）学食の一食 | 学校食堂的一餐 | 학교 식당 한 끼 | Một bữa ở căng tin trường | A school cafeteria meal
卒業してからも、外食の値段を学食で換算する。場所も提供の仕組みも違うのに、支払った金額だけは鮮明だ。
5）パン屋のいつものパン | 面包店常买的面包 | 빵집에서 늘 사던 빵 | Món bánh mì vẫn hay mua | Your usual bakery bread
名前を見ただけで、昔の値札まで思い出す。今の大きさや材料を確認する前に、記憶が先に計算を始める。
6）散髪 | 理发 | 이발 | Cắt tóc | Haircuts
子どもの頃に通った店が、今も頭の中の相場になっている。自分の年齢だけが先に進んだような気がする。

7）映画のチケット | 电影票 | 영화표 | Vé xem phim | Movie tickets
覚えているのは、学生料金や割引の日だったかもしれない。思い出の一枚を、いつの間にか普通の料金として扱っている。
8）バス運賃 | 公交车票 | 버스 요금 | Vé xe buýt | Bus fares
初めて一人で乗った日の小銭を思い出す。路線も距離も違うのに、そのときの金額がなかなか離れない。
9）荷物の配送料 | 包裹运费 | 택배 배송비 | Phí gửi bưu kiện | Parcel delivery fees
昔送った箱の値段を覚えている。今の箱の大きさと行き先を見て、同じ条件で比べていなかったと気づく。
10）初めて借りた部屋の家賃 | 第一间出租房的租金 | 처음 구한 방의 월세 | Tiền thuê căn phòng đầu tiên | Rent on your first room
最初の部屋は狭さも不便さも含めて思い出になっている。新しい物件の条件より先に、あの家賃を口にしてしまう。
今でも頭の中に残っている昔の値段は、どこの何の値段ですか？

🇰🇷 대한민국
어린 시절, 학생 시절, 사회생활 초반의 가격 기억에서 열 가지 가상 장면을 골랐습니다. 물가 통계가 아니며, 개인이 기억하는 금액이 당시의 전국 공통 가격을 뜻하지는 않습니다.
1）김밥 한 줄 | 一卷紫菜包饭 | キンパ一本 | Một cuộn kimbap | A roll of kimbap
학생 때 자주 가던 가게가 마음속 기준이다. 지금 메뉴판을 보면서도 당시 주머니 사정으로 먼저 계산한다.

2）편의점 라면 | 便利店方便面 | コンビニのインスタント麺 | Mì ăn liền ở cửa hàng tiện lợi | Convenience store instant noodles
밤늦게 간단히 먹던 기억과 가격이 함께 남아 있다. 다른 제품을 골라 놓고도 예전의 익숙한 금액을 기대한다.
3）테이크아웃 커피 | 外带咖啡 | 持ち帰りコーヒー | Cà phê mang đi | Takeaway coffee
처음 출근길에 사 마시던 한 잔을 떠올린다. 매장과 크기는 달라졌는데 머릿속 커피값은 그때에 머문다.
4）학교 식당 한 끼 | 学校食堂的一餐 | 学食の一食 | Một bữa ở căng tin trường | A school cafeteria meal
졸업한 뒤에도 바깥 식사를 학식 몇 끼인지로 바꿔 본다. 공급 방식은 달라도 직접 냈던 돈은 오래 기억난다.
5）동네 빵집의 빵 | 街坊面包店的面包 | 近所のパン屋のパン | Bánh ở tiệm bánh gần nhà | Bread from the neighborhood bakery
어릴 때 고르던 빵 이름을 보면 옛 가격표가 먼저 떠오른다. 지금의 재료와 크기는 그다음에 보게 된다.
6）이발 | 理发 | 散髪 | Cắt tóc | Haircuts
머리 모양은 학생 때와 달라졌는데 가격의 기준은 예전 가게다. 계산하는 순간 시간이 많이 흘렀다는 걸 느낀다.
7）영화표 | 电影票 | 映画のチケット | Vé xem phim | Movie tickets
가장 선명하게 기억하는 표가 할인받았던 한 장일 수 있다. 특별했던 조건을 잊고 평소 가격처럼 비교하게 된다.

8）치킨 한 마리 | 一份整鸡炸鸡 | フライドチキン一羽分 | Một phần gà rán nguyên con | A whole fried chicken order
친구들과 돈을 모아 주문하던 시절의 금액이 남아 있다. 구성과 추가 메뉴가 달라져도 기억은 먼저 반응한다.
9）버스 요금 | 公交车票 | バス運賃 | Vé xe buýt | Bus fares
처음 혼자 버스를 탈 때 준비했던 돈을 기억한다. 노선과 이용 조건이 바뀌어도 그 숫자는 쉽게 지워지지 않는다.
10）처음 구한 방의 월세 | 第一间出租房的租金 | 初めて借りた部屋の家賃 | Tiền thuê căn phòng đầu tiên | Rent on your first room
첫 방의 불편함은 추억이 되고 월세만 비교 기준으로 남는다. 지금 찾는 집과 조건이 얼마나 다른지는 뒤늦게 떠올린다.
당신의 머릿속에서 아직 바뀌지 않은 가격은 무엇인가요? 어느 시절의 기억과 붙어 있나요?

🇻🇳 Việt Nam
Mười tình huống giả định được chọn từ ký ức thời nhỏ, thời đi học và những năm đầu đi làm. Đây không phải thống kê giá; mức giá một người nhớ cũng không đại diện cho toàn thị trường lúc đó.
1）Một bát phở quen | 熟悉的一碗越南粉 | なじみの店のフォー | 단골집 쌀국수 한 그릇 | A familiar bowl of pho
Quán gần trường vẫn là mốc trong đầu. Ăn ở nơi khác rồi mà lúc nhìn hóa đơn, mình vẫn nhớ mức tiền của bát ngày trước.
2）Một ổ bánh mì | 一个越式三明治 | バインミー一本 | 반미 하나 | A banh mi sandwich
Nhớ rất rõ tờ tiền từng cầm đi mua bữa sáng. Phần nhân và kích cỡ đã khác, nhưng trí nhớ vẫn đưa ra tổng tiền cũ.

3）Một ly cà phê | 一杯咖啡 | コーヒー一杯 | 커피 한 잔 | A cup of coffee
Giá trong đầu gắn với chiếc ghế và buổi sáng ở quán quen. Đổi không gian rồi, mình vẫn vô thức mang quán ấy ra so.
4）Một suất cơm thời đi học | 学生时代的一份饭 | 学生時代の一食 | 학생 시절 한 끼 식사 | A student meal
Lâu lâu vẫn lấy bữa cơm ngày ấy làm đơn vị tính tiền ăn. Nhớ số tiền đã trả mà quên điều kiện bán và khẩu phần có thể khác.
5）Tiền đổ xăng một lần | 一次加油的钱 | 一回の給油代 | 한 번 주유하던 비용 | The cost of a fuel stop
Trong ký ức có một khoản tiền từng đủ cho lịch đi lại quen thuộc. Xe, quãng đường và lượng xăng mua đã đổi mà cảm giác ấy còn nguyên.
6）Một lần cắt tóc | 一次理发 | 散髪一回 | 이발 한 번 | A haircut
Tiệm cũ trở thành mức tham chiếu lâu dài. Tóc đã cắt theo nhiều kiểu, chỉ có giá trong đầu chưa cập nhật.
7）Một vé xem phim | 一张电影票 | 映画のチケット一枚 | 영화표 한 장 | A movie ticket
Có thể mình đang nhớ đúng một buổi có ưu đãi. Sau nhiều năm, điều kiện khuyến mãi mờ đi, con số lại ở lại.
8）Tiền gửi xe | 停车费 | 駐車料金 | 주차 요금 | Parking fees
Nhớ giá ở bãi xe từng gửi hằng ngày. Đến địa điểm khác vẫn chuẩn bị tiền theo thói quen cũ rồi mới nhìn bảng.

9）Tiền giặt đồ | 洗衣费用 | 洗濯サービスの料金 | 세탁 비용 | Laundry service costs
Lần đầu mang đồ đi giặt đã để lại một mức giá trong trí nhớ. Sau này khối lượng và loại dịch vụ khác đi, mình vẫn dễ lấy lần ấy làm chuẩn.
10）Tiền thuê căn phòng đầu tiên | 第一间出租房的租金 | 初めて借りた部屋の家賃 | 처음 구한 방의 월세 | Rent on your first room
Căn phòng nhỏ và những bất tiện dần trở nên dễ thương trong ký ức. Tiền thuê thì ở lại như một tiêu chuẩn khó thay đổi.
Món gì vẫn mang giá cũ trong đầu bạn? Bạn đang nhớ giá tiền, hay đang nhớ cuộc sống lúc ấy?

🇺🇸 United States
These ten fictional scenes were selected around childhood, student life and the first years of work. They are not price statistics; a remembered price is not necessarily what everyone paid at the time.
1）A cup of coffee | 一杯咖啡 | コーヒー一杯 | 커피 한 잔 | Một ly cà phê
The price in your head belongs to the shop on an old commute. The size and location have changed, but your mental coffee budget has not.
2）A slice of pizza | 一片披萨 | ピザ一切れ | 피자 한 조각 | Một miếng pizza
You remember the money you carried after school. That particular slice became a permanent reference point for slices everywhere else.
3）A student meal | 学生时代的一餐 | 学生時代の一食 | 학생 시절 한 끼 식사 | Một bữa ăn thời sinh viên
Years later, you still convert a restaurant bill into meals at the old cafeteria. The amount you paid is clearer than the arrangements behind that price.

4）A haircut | 一次理发 | 散髪一回 | 이발 한 번 | Một lần cắt tóc
Your style has changed several times since your first regular barbershop. Your idea of what a haircut should cost still sits in that chair.
5）A movie ticket | 一张电影票 | 映画のチケット一枚 | 영화표 한 장 | Một vé xem phim
The ticket you remember best may have been a matinee or a special offer. The discount conditions faded while the number became your idea of the normal price.
6）A loaf of bread | 一条面包 | パン一斤 | 식빵 한 봉지 | Một ổ bánh mì
An old family shopping trip supplies the price tag in your memory. Brand, weight and ingredients do not always get carried into the comparison.
7）A carton of eggs | 一盒鸡蛋 | 卵一パック | 달걀 한 팩 | Một hộp trứng
You have a firm remembered price and a less firm memory of the carton. Size, quantity and type become things to check only after the initial surprise.
8）A diner breakfast | 一份小餐馆早餐 | ダイナーの朝食 | 다이너 아침식사 | Một bữa sáng ở quán ăn |
The price belongs to a familiar table and a particular stage of life. Ordering breakfast somewhere new can bring back the whole scene before it brings a fair comparison.
9）A bus fare | 公交车票 | バス運賃 | 버스 요금 | Vé xe buýt
You remember the coins you once needed to get across town. The route and fare conditions may differ now, but the old handful of change remains vivid.

10）Rent on your first room | 第一间出租房的租金 | 初めて借りた部屋の家賃 | 처음 구한 방의 월세 | Tiền thuê căn phòng đầu tiên
The cramped space and inconvenient location have softened into nostalgia. The rent survives as a benchmark long after the rest of your housing expectations changed.
Which old price refuses to leave your head, and what time or place does it take you back to?

text:
🇨🇳 五国：家里没人炒股，却被一轮市场行情改变的生活 TOP10
🇯🇵 5か国：家族の誰も株を売買していないのに、相場で変わった暮らし TOP10
🇰🇷 5개국: 가족 중 주식 하는 사람은 없는데, 시장 흐름에 달라진 일상 TOP10
🇻🇳 5 quốc gia: Nhà không ai chơi chứng khoán, cuộc sống vẫn đổi theo thị trường TOP10
🇺🇸 Five Countries: Nobody at Home Trades Stocks, Yet Market Moves Still Change Daily Life TOP10
🇨🇳 中国
按行情传到家庭账单的路径选取十个虚构场景。这里包括商品、汇率、利率和住房市场，属于编辑选题；影响还取决于政策、合同和当地供需，不是同步涨跌公式。
1）加油时重新算通勤 | 給油時に見直す通勤費 | 주유하며 다시 계산하는 출퇴근비 | Tính lại tiền đi làm khi đổ xăng | Recalculating the commute at the pump
没买过石油公司的股票，也可能在加油时感受到原油行情。只是国际油价到国内油价，中间还隔着定价机制。
2）买菜时换一份清单 | 食料品の買い物リストを変える | 장을 보며 바꾸는 구매 목록 | Đổi danh sách thực phẩm khi đi chợ | Changing the grocery list
粮食、食用油原料和运输成本的变化，可能慢慢进入食品价格。家里感受到的，是同样的预算能装满几只袋子。
3）结婚首饰重新选款 | 結婚用の金製品を選び直す | 결혼 금제품을 다시 고르기 | Chọn lại vàng cưới | Rethinking wedding gold
原本按款式挑，后来开始认真看克重。金饰价格还包含工费等因素，不能只拿金价曲线直接对照。

4）交海外学费前看汇率 | 海外の学費を払う前の為替確認 | 해외 학비를 내기 전 환율 확인 | Xem tỷ giá trước khi đóng học phí ở nước ngoài | Checking exchange rates before tuition
学校没有改外币标价，家里需要准备的人民币仍可能变化。于是一个不看股市的人，也开始每天看汇率。
5）旅行目的地换了 | 旅行先の変更 | 여행 목적지 변경 | Đổi điểm đến du lịch | Changing the holiday destination
同一间酒店、同一份菜单，折回人民币的感觉可能不同。计划表上的国家，跟着预算重新排了一次。

6）装修报价又更新了 | リフォーム見積もりの更新 | 다시 바뀐 인테리어 견적 | Báo giá sửa nhà được cập nhật | Another renovation quote update
铜、铝、木材等原料的行情可能进入材料成本。最终报价还要看品牌、人工和库存，未必当天就跟着变。
7）买房计划提前或推后 | 住宅購入計画の前倒し・延期 | 앞당겨지거나 미뤄진 주택 구매 | Mua nhà sớm hơn hoặc muộn hơn | Moving a home purchase forward or back
附近房源价格和成交情况变化，首付目标也可能重算。家里没开股票账户，却天天研究同一个小区。
8）月供要等合同重定价 | 契約の見直し時期を待つ返済額 | 계약상 금리 재산정을 기다리는 상환액 | Tiền trả vay chờ kỳ điều chỉnh lãi suất | Mortgage payments awaiting a reset
听到利率变化，先去翻贷款合同。是否调整、什么时候调整，还得看自己的贷款类型与约定。
9）存款到期后重新问利息 | 預金満期後に確認する金利 | 예금 만기 뒤 다시 확인하는 금리 | Hỏi lại lãi suất khi tiền gửi đáo hạn | Asking about rates when a deposit matures
一直只存银行，也会遇到新一笔存款利率不同的时候。原本预计的利息收入，不能照着上一期直接抄。
10）工厂加班安排变了 | 工場の残業予定の変化 | 공장 잔업 일정 변화 | Lịch tăng ca nhà máy thay đổi | Changing factory overtime
汇率、原料和海外需求会影响企业接单与利润。传到家庭时，可能表现为排班变化，具体原因仍要看所在企业。
你家第一次觉得“市场行情跟我也有关”，是在加油、交学费、还贷款，还是收到工资的时候？

🇯🇵 日本
商品、為替、金利、住宅市場が家計につながる経路から、十の架空の場面を選びました。影響は契約、政策、企業の対応などで異なり、一律の値動きを示すものではありません。

1）輸入食品の買い物 | 购买进口食品 | 수입식품 장보기 | Mua thực phẩm nhập khẩu | Buying imported food
為替や国際原料価格の変化が、仕入れ費用に影響する。家庭では、いつもの商品を買うか別の商品にするかという話になる。
2）電気・ガスの請求書 | 电费与燃气账单 | 전기·가스 요금 고지서 | Hóa đơn điện và gas | Electricity and gas bills
燃料価格の変化が料金に反映される場合がある。ただし、反映時期や幅には料金制度や支援策も関わる。
3）海外旅行の予算 | 海外旅行预算 | 해외여행 예산 | Ngân sách du lịch nước ngoài | Overseas travel budgets
現地価格が同じでも、円で用意する金額は変わりうる。航空券だけでなく、到着後の食事まで計算し直す。
4）留学費用の送金 | 汇出留学费用 | 유학비 송금 | Chuyển tiền du học | Sending money for study abroad
外貨で決まった学費を払う日が近づくと、為替が生活の予定になる。株を見なくても、送金前の数字は気になる。
5）新しく借りる住宅ローン | 新申请的房贷 | 새로 받는 주택담보대출 | Khoản vay mua nhà mới | A new mortgage
物件価格だけでなく、借入条件によって毎月の返済額も違う。見学した家は同じでも、資金計画は変わる。
6）変動金利の返済計画 | 浮动利率还款计划 | 변동금리 상환 계획 | Kế hoạch trả vay lãi suất thả nổi | Variable rate repayment plans
金利のニュースを聞いて、自分の契約を確認する。返済への反映は契約ごとに異なり、全員が同じ日に変わるわけではない。

7）定期預金の満期 | 定期存款到期 | 정기예금 만기 | Tiền gửi có kỳ hạn đáo hạn | A term deposit maturing
更新するときの金利が以前と違えば、受け取る利息の見込みも変わる。預金だけの家庭にも金利の話は届く。
8）確定拠出年金の残高 | 缴费确定型养老金余额 | 확정기여형 퇴직연금 잔액 | Số dư hưu trí đóng góp xác định | Defined contribution retirement balances
個別株を売買していなくても、選んだ運用商品によっては相場の影響を受ける。残高を見ると、間接的な投資とのつながりが分かる。
9）観光の仕事の忙しさ | 旅游相关工作的忙闲 | 관광업 일의 바쁨 변화 | Mức độ bận rộn của công việc du lịch | How busy tourism work becomes
為替は海外から来る人の旅行費用にも関わる。予約や売上への影響は地域や店で異なるが、仕事を通じて家計につながることがある。
10）小さな店の仕入れ | 小店的进货成本 | 작은 가게의 매입 비용 | Chi phí nhập hàng của cửa hàng nhỏ | A small shop’s purchasing costs
家族の店で使う豆、油、包装資材の値段が変わる。値上げするか、そのまま受け止めるかが夕食の話題になる。
あなたの家では、相場の変化を最初に感じるのは、買い物、光熱費、仕事、それとも年金の残高ですか？

🇰🇷 대한민국
상품 가격, 환율, 금리, 주택시장이 가계에 전달되는 경로에서 열 가지 가상 장면을 골랐습니다. 실제 영향은 계약과 정책, 기업 상황에 따라 다르며 전국 가정의 경험을 조사한 순위는 아닙니다.
1）수입식품 장바구니 | 进口食品购物篮 | 輸入食品の買い物かご | Giỏ thực phẩm nhập khẩu | The imported food basket
환율과 해외 원재료 가격이 수입 비용에 영향을 줄 수 있다. 집에서는 늘 사던 식품을 계속 살지 고민하는 일이 된다.

2）난방비 고지서 | 取暖费账单 | 暖房費の請求書 | Hóa đơn sưởi ấm | Heating bills
에너지 가격과 환율 변화가 비용에 영향을 미친다. 실제 요금에는 제도와 조정 시점도 있어 곧바로 같은 폭으로 움직이지는 않는다.
3）해외 학비 송금 | 海外学费汇款 | 海外学費の送金 | Chuyển học phí ra nước ngoài | Overseas tuition transfers
외화로 정해진 학비는 그대로인데 필요한 원화가 달라질 수 있다. 주식 차트 대신 환율 화면을 열게 되는 이유다.
4）여행 예산 변경 | 旅行预算变化 | 旅行予算の変更 | Thay đổi ngân sách du lịch | Changing a travel budget
숙소와 식사에 쓸 돈을 환산하고 나니 일정이 달라진다. 환율은 여행지에서 머무는 하루의 가격에도 닿아 있다.
5）대출 이자 부담 | 贷款利息负担 | 借入利息の負担 | Gánh nặng lãi vay | Loan interest costs
금리가 바뀌면 대출 종류와 계약에 따라 부담이 달라질 수 있다. 뉴스 속 숫자가 우리 집에 언제 반영되는지가 중요해진다.
6）전세보증금 마련 | 筹措全租房押金 | チョンセ保証金の準備 | Chuẩn bị tiền đặt cọc jeonse | Funding a jeonse deposit
보증금과 대출 조건을 함께 맞춰야 한다. 같은 동네에 계속 살고 싶어도 필요한 자금 계획은 달라질 수 있다.
7）이사할 집의 가격 | 搬家目标房源价格 | 引っ越し先の住宅価格 | Giá căn nhà dự định chuyển đến | The price of the next home
집값과 임대 조건이 바뀌면 이동 가능한 지역도 달라진다. 투자 목적이 없어도 주택시장과 생활 계획은 연결된다.

8）결혼 금제품 예산 | 婚礼金饰预算 | 結婚用金製品の予算 | Ngân sách vàng cưới | Wedding gold budgets
금 시세를 본 뒤 무게와 디자인을 다시 고른다. 최종 구매 가격에는 가공비 등 다른 요소도 들어간다.
9）퇴직연금 운용 잔액 | 退休金投资余额 | 退職年金の運用残高 | Số dư đầu tư hưu trí | Invested retirement balances
개별 종목을 고르지 않아도 펀드 등으로 시장에 노출될 수 있다. 영향은 연금 유형과 선택한 상품에 따라 달라진다.
10）수출기업의 근무 일정 | 出口企业工作安排 | 輸出企業の勤務予定 | Lịch làm việc tại doanh nghiệp xuất khẩu | Schedules at an exporting employer
환율이 변해도 모든 수출기업에 같은 결과가 생기지는 않는다. 원재료, 계약, 수요가 함께 작용하고 그 결과가 일자리와 연결될 수 있다.
가족 중 아무도 주식을 하지 않는데도 시장을 신경 쓰게 된 계기는 무엇이었나요?

🇻🇳 Việt Nam
Mười tình huống giả định được chọn theo đường truyền từ giá hàng hóa, tỷ giá, lãi suất và nhà ở tới gia đình. Đây là lựa chọn biên tập; tác động còn phụ thuộc hợp đồng, chính sách và hoàn cảnh từng hộ.
1）Thu nhập của gia đình trồng cà phê | 咖啡种植家庭收入 | コーヒー栽培世帯の収入 | 커피 재배 가구의 소득 | Coffee growing household income
Không cần mua cổ phiếu để chịu tác động của giá cà phê. Tiền bán nông sản có thể ảnh hưởng tới việc chi tiêu và phân công lao động trong nhà.
2）Chi phí của quán cà phê gia đình | 家庭咖啡店成本 | 家族経営カフェの費用 | 가족 카페의 운영 비용 | Costs at a family coffee shop
Giá hạt cà phê thay đổi khiến người bán phải tính lại. Giá một ly còn gồm tiền thuê, nhân công và nhiều nguyên liệu khác, nên không đi theo giá hạt một cách máy móc.

3）Tiền mua gạo và tiền bán lúa | 买米支出与卖稻收入 | 米を買う費用と稲作の売上 | 쌀 구매비와 벼 판매 소득 | Buying rice and selling a harvest
Cùng một đợt biến động giá có thể được nhìn khác nhau từ phía người mua và người bán. Có gia đình đồng thời đứng ở cả hai phía.
4）Tiền nhiên liệu đi làm | 通勤燃料支出 | 通勤の燃料費 | 출퇴근 연료비 | Fuel for the commute
Đi làm bằng xe mỗi ngày khiến chi phí nhiên liệu trở thành khoản khó bỏ qua. Giá bán lẻ còn chịu tác động của thuế, điều hành và phân phối.
5）Ngân sách mua vàng cưới | 婚礼购金预算 | 結婚用の金の予算 | 결혼 금제품 구매 예산 | Wedding gold budgets
Gia đình có thể đổi trọng lượng hoặc kiểu trang sức sau khi xem giá. Giá quốc tế và giá bán trong nước cũng không nhất thiết trùng nhau.
6）Báo giá xây và sửa nhà | 建房与修缮报价 | 建築・修繕の見積もり | 주택 건축·수리 견적 | Building and repair quotes
Thép, vật liệu và vận chuyển thay đổi có thể đi vào dự toán. Thời điểm mua và điều khoản đã chốt quyết định phần nào được điều chỉnh.
7）Khoản trả lãi vay | 贷款利息支出 | 借入利息の支払い | 대출 이자 지출 | Loan interest payments
Lãi suất thay đổi có thể tác động tới khoản vay theo điều kiện hợp đồng. Câu hỏi của gia đình là khi nào tới kỳ điều chỉnh của mình.
8）Tiền lãi từ khoản tiết kiệm mới | 新存款的利息收入 | 新しく預ける預金の利息 | 새 예금의 이자 소득 | Interest on a new deposit
Không đầu tư chứng khoán vẫn phải tính lại khi gửi khoản tiền mới với mức lãi khác. Khoản chi dự định dùng tiền lãi có thể cần sắp xếp lại.

9）Tiền người thân gửi về | 亲属汇回的款项 | 家族からの海外送金 | 해외 가족이 보내는 송금 | Money sent home by relatives
Người gửi chuyển cùng một số ngoại tệ nhưng số tiền đồng nhận được có thể khác. Tỷ giá và phí chuyển tiền đều góp phần vào kết quả.
10）Việc làm gắn với đơn hàng xuất khẩu | 与出口订单相关的工作 | 輸出受注につながる仕事 | 수출 주문과 연결된 일자리 | Work linked to export orders
Nhu cầu ở nước ngoài và chi phí sản xuất có thể ảnh hưởng tới đơn hàng. Với gia đình, thị trường xuất hiện qua lịch làm việc, thu nhập và kế hoạch chi tiêu.
Nhà bạn từng thay đổi kế hoạch vì giá nông sản, giá vàng, tỷ giá hay lãi vay chưa? Đó là kế hoạch gì?

🇺🇸 United States
These ten fictional scenes follow links from commodity, currency, interest rate and housing markets into household life. This is an editorial selection; contracts, policy and local conditions shape the outcome.
1）Retirement account balances | 退休账户余额 | 退職口座の残高 | 퇴직계좌 잔액 | Số dư tài khoản hưu trí
Nobody picks individual stocks, but the household’s retirement funds may still hold them. Market exposure depends on the investments selected inside the account.
2）The first mortgage quote | 首次房贷报价 | 初めての住宅ローン見積もり | 첫 주택담보대출 견적 | Báo giá vay mua nhà lần đầu |
The house price has not changed, yet a different borrowing rate can change the payment. The family starts following financial news because it affects which homes fit the budget.
3）The decision to move | 是否搬家的决定 | 引っ越すかどうかの判断 | 이사 여부 결정 | Quyết định có chuyển nhà hay không
An existing fixed rate mortgage does not automatically reset when market rates rise. But replacing it with a new loan can make moving feel much more expensive.

4）The next lease renewal | 下一次租约续签 | 次回の賃貸契約更新 | 다음 임대계약 갱신 | Lần gia hạn hợp đồng thuê tiếp theo
Local rents reflect housing supply, demand and other costs. A household can avoid property investing entirely and still have to rearrange its budget at renewal.
5）The gasoline receipt | 汽油收据 | ガソリンのレシート | 주유 영수증 | Hóa đơn xăng |
Crude oil is one component of gasoline prices. Refining, distribution and taxes also matter, so a market headline and the price at a particular station need not move together immediately.
6）The grocery basket | 食品购物篮 | 食料品の買い物かご | 식료품 장바구니 | Giỏ thực phẩm |
Changes in crop, energy and transport costs can reach food prices. What a family notices is often the substitution: a different brand, a smaller package, or one item left behind.
7）The car payment quote | 汽车贷款月供报价 | 自動車ローンの返済見積もり | 자동차 할부금 견적 | Báo giá trả góp ô tô |
A financing offer helps determine whether replacing the car is manageable. The effect depends on the rate, loan term and amount borrowed, alongside the vehicle price.
8）Interest on savings | 储蓄利息 | 貯蓄の利息 | 저축 이자 | Lãi tiền tiết kiệm |
A household that keeps money in the bank can still feel a rate cycle. What it earns depends on the account’s terms and the rate the bank actually offers.
9）An employer’s spending plans | 雇主的支出计划 | 勤務先の支出計画 | 직장의 지출 계획 | Kế hoạch chi tiêu của doanh nghiệp |
Financing conditions and customer demand can affect investment and hiring. At home, that connection may arrive as a delayed opening, a changed schedule or a postponed expansion.

10）The overseas holiday budget | 海外度假预算 | 海外旅行の予算 | 해외여행 예산 | Ngân sách du lịch nước ngoài |
Exchange rates change what foreign prices mean in dollars. The same hotel room may feel more or less affordable even before the family changes its itinerary.
Which market move first changed a decision in your household, even though nobody was trading stocks?

Haawm, Bangkok. Deeply spiced curries, punchy aromatics, sharp acidity and a generous use of fresh herbs. The sort of meal where ordering more rice becomes inevitable.

On the wine front, François Carillon’s 2023 Puligny-Montrachet Champ Gain brought freshness and mineral tension, while Trinoro’s 2020 Palazzi offered a richer, more generous counterpoint to the spice. Two very different wines, both making a compelling case at the table.

text:
Margaret Brennan: “we turn now to republican congressman french hill. he is currently the chairman of the financial services committee, and he joins us from little rock, arkansas. good morning to you, congressman. you survived a tough race down in arkansas, usually ruby red. you finished just over 4,000 votes ahead of your democratic rival. what went wrong for so many other of your republican colleagues here?”

French Hill: “well, margaret, it's good to be with you. it was a very complicated, tough election cycle this year. look, we told the american people in 2024 that we'd secure the border, we'd make our communities safer, we would lead in the world. but we also told the american people that we would continue to fight to lower costs. and i think what we saw, no matter how many efforts that we made in the republican house, that americans are still concerned about the impact of 20% inflation that they experienced during the biden administration, and that while it's down from 9% to 3%, it has not gone lower. and that, i think, was a principal issue, the cost that the american people are having and experiencing in all of our families. so we have more work to do there.”

Margaret Brennan: “yeah, costs eating into wage gains, particularly over the past six months. but let's talk about what's possible now. president trump has changed his chief of staff, as you know, stephen miller, now in that role. your republican colleague don bacon of nebraska said, miller is not a good choice because he's antagonistic. he hurt republicans during the election, saying he, quote, took the immigration issue for president trump from a two-to-one favorable to a two-to-one unfavorable. do you agree with him? i mean, what does putting miller in the chief's role signal?”

French Hill: “well, first, i think susie wiles is leaving. president trump has the right to promote stephen miller to be the chief. that responsibility means that during this 120th congress, he'll be the point person for the president in discussing policy matters with congress. i'll tell you, though, on the immigration issue, i think we should focus on immigration reform, which i voted for twice back in 2018, to resolve the issues about how to seek asylum in this country, how we handle temporary protective services, and how we deal with children in this country that are here with legal green card holders, like our engineering community that's across the country, as well as those who've come in the country legally, but their kids are legal. we do need to resolve it. i think it's a place where president trump can leave. and this is an area that stephen miller is keen on, which is secure the border, yes, but can we now reform the immigration system and make it better for our country? and that will, i believe, answer the questions about the deportation issue.”

Margaret Brennan: “well, i understand the aspiration, but credibly, you believe stephen miller can persuade democrats and be persuaded himself to go for the kind of asylum you just spoke about?”

French Hill: “well, look, this is what president trump has said for years, that if the border was secure, he wanted to try to reform our broken immigration system. and that was an issue that came up in his first term. this is an opportunity that perhaps we could, on a bipartisan basis, find that solution in the next congress.”

Margaret Brennan: “there's a lot of business for you all to get done. your republican colleague, thomas massie, is spearheading an effort to impeach pete hegseth, the secretary. there is action expected this week. some of your colleagues, like james comer, has said, with a high level of confidence, there's a lot of questions about hegseth, and republican voters are upset. should hegseth be impeached?”

French Hill: “well, the question is for the president, should he continue to serve as the secretary of war?”

Margaret Brennan: “you're going to be asked to answer this, though, by representative massie.”

French Hill: “yeah, that's right. well, you know, i want to hear the debate on it to see if it merits impeachment versus some other disciplinary action or action by the president if he's not getting the job done in leading the department of war. that's the issue.”

Margaret Brennan: “are you satisfied with how the war has been handled?”

French Hill: “no, but i mean, i think the commander in chief has to take the responsibility for the strategy of conducting the war and how it's been conducted. but i'll tell you one thing. there's nobody in america that wants iran to have a nuclear weapon. this has been a goal of the united states for five decades. well, look at the 1990s, margaret. president clinton had the opportunity to prevent north korea from having a nuclear weapon, and it didn't happen. that's a big issue for north asia and for the u.s.”

Margaret Brennan: “and centcom just put out a $20 million reward offer for information about iran's nuclear program. so it's clear the u.s. government doesn't have clarity, nor has it completely obliterated the program. but just to go back to hegseth, do i hear you right? you don't necessarily approve of how the war is going, but you're undecided about whether he has committed an impeachable offense. are you open to considering impeachment?”

French Hill: “right, right here. look, look, this is no, this is the issue. if you don't think he's done a good job conducting his job, that doesn't mean per se that he's committed an impeachable offense. he's an executive officer of the executive branch. and if he's not conducting his mission in the right way, then the president ought to make a change there. the question is, are we leading at the pentagon in the right way or not the right way? that's very separate from whether or not somebody's committed an impeachable offense.”

Margaret Brennan: “and you don't want to commit on how you'll vote today. have you reached a conclusion on whether you'll vote for steve scalise or jim jordan for republican leader?”

@RepFrenchHill: “these are two excellent leaders. they both could lead the conference successfully. we have, as you know, new members. we have about 60, 65 members of our 170 majority that have only been in congress two years or less. and i think we need to have our family meeting and discuss it, but both steve scalise and jim jordan are fully capable of leading in the minority. and i look forward to our discussion in conference this week.”

@margbrennan: “all right. well, we will see who ends up. and we look forward to seeing how you end up voting on secretary hegseth as well.”

text:
Why Doesn't God Always Heal? | Who Heals All Your Diseases, by Kelly Irvin https://t.co/di4PgB0eag via @YouTube - #Healing #Psalm103 #SpiritualRenewal You prayed. You believed. You were anointed, just as the New Testament instructs. Yet the healing you hoped for came slowly, or not at all. Or it came, and then the illness returned. If God “heals all your diseases,” as Psalm 103 : 3 declares, what are we to make of that?

This message takes the question head-on. God cannot lie (Titus 1 : 2), and the Bible records instant, unexplainable healings: lepers cleansed, the lame walking, the dead raised, and Naaman made whole after dipping seven times in the Jordan. So why don’t we see those miracles as often today?

The answer begins with a closer look at the words of Psalm 103, where forgiving all our iniquities stands side by side with healing all our diseases. Two respected commentaries see a deeper meaning in that pairing, and James 5 : 14-15 joins the same two ideas in the anointing of the sick. Then comes the diagnosis of a disease we all share. Jeremiah 17 : 9 describes the human heart as desperately wicked, and the Hebrew word behind it can also be read as incurable or desperately sick.

Under the Old Covenant, God promised Israel physical health, wealth and prosperity for obedience. But Hebrews 8 : 6 speaks of a better covenant established on better promises. What could be better than health and prosperity? The message makes a bold claim: from baptism forward, we are offered miraculous, daily healing.

Through John 12, 2 Corinthians 4, Psalm 51, Lamentations 3, Ephesians 4 and Titus 3, we see how the inward man is renewed day by day, even while the outward man is perishing. David prayed, “Create in me a clean heart, O God.” God’s compassions are new every morning. And the renewing of the Holy Spirit is poured out on us abundantly.

Even faithful Elisha died of an illness (2 Kings 13 : 14). Every physical healing is temporary, but a healed heart and mind can enter eternity. That is why our sick hearts are the singular focus of God’s love and concern, and why every trial, whether health, finances or persecution, can become an avenue for spiritual healing.

A blind man longs to see, a mute man to speak, a lame man to leap. God’s desire for us is greater still: that we see all things, communicate all righteousness and leap into His eternal Kingdom. When we look in the rearview mirror, nothing else will matter.

If you have ever wondered why God doesn’t always heal, this message may change what you look for, and help you see how much healing you are already receiving.

Presented by Kelly Irvin, November 7, 2026, at United Church of God in Northwest Arkansas.

text:
J.G. Bennett and Owen Barfield: a unified comparison (Part 2 of 2)

—

3. METAPHYSICS AND POLAR LOGIC: SIX DIMENSIONS, SYSTEMATICS, SYNCHRONICITY, AND NATURA NATURANS VS. NATURA NATURATA
(Vols. I–III vs. What Coleridge Thought)

A. Bennett's six-dimensional framework and the six Laws of Synchronicity (Vols. I and II)

In Vol. I (Chs. 8 and 13–16, pp. 153–304) and Vol. II (Chs. 25–26, pp. 15–68), Bennett replaces four-dimensional spacetime with a six-dimensional geometry (s1, s2, s3; t1, t2, t3), plus a non-metrical seventh degree of freedom for value (Vol. II, §10.25.5, p. 30).

(1) Time (t1): the dimension of successive actualization (motion, thermodynamic entropy).
(2) Eternity (t2): a fifth dimension perpendicular to time. It is the timeless storehouse of potentiality, the inner level of coherence, and negative entropy, which Bennett calls "virtue."
(3) Hyparxis (t3): a sixth dimension perpendicular to both. It is "ableness-to-be," cyclical recurrence, and quantized action. Through it, potential patterns in eternity are regulated into actualization in time, within the present moment.

In Vol. II (Ch. 26, "Synchronicity," §10.26.1–10.26.5, pp. 41–68), Bennett shows that if you remove t1 (time) and combine space (S), eternity (E) and hyparxis (H) in their six possible orders (S-E-H, S-H-E, E-S-H, E-H-S, H-S-E, H-E-S), you get six Laws of Synchronicity: (1) common presence, (2) mutual adjustment, (3) organization and disorganization, (4) multiple existence, (5) connectedness, and (6) independence.

These non-causal, timeless structural laws explain how mind and body couple across different levels of eternity, how Jungian synchronicities and divination (such as the I Ching) work, and how the pattern of a newborn's life is stamped by the configuration of the solar system at birth. Bennett calls this last "Fate" (cf. Vol. III, Ch. 40, p. 171).

B. Bennett's multi-term Systematics vs. Barfield's Coleridgean polar logic

Both insist that ordinary binary logic (A vs. not-A) can only handle static things, never living wholes or transformation.

Bennett's Systematics (Vol. II, introduction and Chs. 25–36; Vol. III, Chs. 37–38, pp. 3–115):
• Monad (1): undivided totality, universality.
• Dyad (2): complementarity, polarity, force (fact and value; existence and essence).
• Triad (3): dynamism, relatedness, Will. The three cosmic impulses are (1) affirmation, (2) receptivity and (3) reconciliation. Their six orderings generate six fundamental laws: Expansion (1-2-3), Interaction (1-3-2), Concentration (2-1-3), Identity (2-3-1), Freedom (3-1-2) and Order (3-2-1) (Vol. II, Chs. 27–28).
• Tetrad (4): ordered activity, Being (ground/actual, goal/ideal, direction/theoretical, instrument/practical), and the twelve qualities of energy. E12–E9 are mechanical, E8–E5 vital, and E4–E1 cosmic: conscious (E4), creative (E3), unitive (E2) and transcendent (E1) (Vol. II, Ch. 32).
• Pentad (5): significance, potentiality, Essence, and the "reflux of the spirit" across twelve classes of essence. This draws on Gurdjieff's "reciprocal maintenance," and each class is defined by an inner limit, outer limit, nourishment, master and central Ipseity (Vol. II, Ch. 35; Vol. III, Ch. 39).
• Hexad (6): the Event and the human totality; triads coalescing in a present moment (Vol. III, Chs. 37, 40).
• Heptad (7): transformation, seven stages of evolutionary or historical realization (Vol. III, Ch. 37; Vol. IV, Ch. 43).
• Octad (8): the completed arena, two squares bridging fact and value (Vol. III, Chs. 37, 41).
• Ennead (9), the Enneagram: harmonization. It integrates a seven-stage lawful process (1-4-2-8-5-7) with a triangle (3-6-9) to overcome "universal hazard" at two critical shock-points. Bennett illustrates it with a working kitchen and the training of a singer (Vol. III, Chs. 37–38, pp. 63–71, 108–115; cf. Gurdjieff: Making a New World, appendix II, p. 296).
• Decad (10), Undecad (11) and Dodecad (12): integrative complementarity, synergism, and perfection, the ideal human society. The Dodecad is three tetrads: the stable (Psychostatic), the transforming (Psychokinetic) and the guiding (Psychoteleios) (Vol. III, Chs. 37, 41).

Remarkably, in What Coleridge Thought (Chs. 2–3, pp. 22–37, and the appendix, "Polar Logic," pp. 179–193), Barfield develops the same structural transitions, using the same Latin terms.

(1) Natura naturans vs. natura naturata.
– Barfield (Chs. 2–3, pp. 22–35) defines natura naturans as supersensible, productive spirit working through dynamic polarity ("two forces of one power"), and natura naturata as outward, passive phenomena, in which the productive power is "suspended and, as it were, quenched in the product" (coagulum spiritus).
– Bennett (Vol. II, Chs. 27–28, pp. 87, 116–118) uses the identical terms. Natura naturans, "Nature the Mother of all Birth" (essence, becoming), is the Law of Expansion: affirmation → receptivity → reconciliation (1-2-3). Natura naturata, "Nature the Mother of all Process" (existence), is the Law of Interaction (1-3-2): affirmation reconciled with receptivity, issuing in manifestation. It is a "pseudo-dynamic triad," in which cosmic dynamism is quenched into repeating physical processes with no change of level.

(2) From Triad to Tetrad: the Pythagorean Tetractys.
– Barfield (pp. 183–190) explains Coleridge's trichotomy and the Pythagorean Tetractys (prothesis or identity → thesis and antithesis → mesothesis or synthesis): "the Tetrad indeed in the intellectual and intuitive contemplation, but a Triad in discursive arrangement."
– Bennett (Vol. II, Ch. 32, pp. 173, 215) makes the same move from the Triad of Will to the Tetrad of Being, explicitly invoking the Pythagorean tetrad and Robert Fludd's Monochordum Mundi.

—

4. NATURE AND EVOLUTION: GOETHE, COLERIDGE'S THEORY OF LIFE, DARWIN, AND TEILHARD
(Vols. I and IV vs. Saving the Appearances, What Coleridge Thought, Unancestral Voice)

A. Shared sources: Goethe's morphology and Coleridge's Theory of Life (Vol. I, Chs. 9, 20–21)

One of the most striking discoveries in Vol. I is that Bennett explicitly cites Goethe and Coleridge's Theory of Life (1848), the two main pillars of Barfield's philosophy of nature.

• Goethe's morphology. In Ch. 9 ("The Scale of Being," §4.9.3, p. 179), Bennett writes:

"The transcendental morphologists, from Buffon and Goethe onwards, came near to understanding the principle of structure... Nevertheless, the insight of Goethe might well have led his followers to a new understanding of the principle of structure had the attention of the biologists not been diverted from morphology by the publication of Darwin's Origin of Species. The ubiquity of structure was lost to view and the conception of a 'form of all forms' gradually disappeared from biological thinking." (cf. Gurdjieff: Making a New World, p. 239)

This echoes Barfield's celebration of Goethe's Urpflanze and Urphänomen as "potential phenomena perceived and studied as such" through systematic imagination, in Saving the Appearances (Ch. XX, pp. 137–141), Worlds Apart (pp. 145–150) and What Coleridge Thought (p. 242 n.).

• Coleridge's Theory of Life and individuation. In Ch. 9 (§4.9.4, pp. 180–183), Bennett ranks a being on his "scale of potency" by its maximum capacity for individuation: "How far is this whole itself?" In Chs. 20–21 ("Life" and "Animal Magnetism," §8.20.4–8.21.5, pp. 381–410), he argues that the biological species is a genuine individual governed by an eternal pattern (t2), an epigenetic factor and a hyparchic regulator (t3), and he explicitly footnotes S.T. Coleridge, Theory of Life (London, 1848). That book, which defines life as the "principle of individuation" rising through physical, vital and conscious powers, is the centerpiece of What Coleridge Thought (Chs. 4–5, pp. 41–68) and of Worlds Apart (pp. 190–196).

• The living Earth and the cosmic hierarchy. In Vol. I (Ch. 12, §4.12.1–4.12.5, pp. 214–221, and Chs. 22–24), drawing on D.E. Harding's The Hierarchy of Heaven and Earth (1952), Bennett classifies the biosphere, the planet Earth ("Mother Earth," a sub-creative whole), the Sun (free creativity) and the galaxy as conscious beings above the level of organic life, each at an ascending level of potency. This complements Barfield's dictum in Unancestral Voice (p. 45) that "the interior is anterior" to outer space.

B. Shared critiques of neo-Darwinism and Teilhard de Chardin (Vol. IV vs. Saving the Appearances and Unancestral Voice)

In Vol. IV (Chs. 44–45, pp. 106–164, 195–196), Bennett uses thermodynamics and information theory to argue that large evolutionary leaps cannot arise from random mutation, given the astronomical improbabilities involved. He criticizes Teilhard de Chardin for relying on vague evolutionary "tendencies" (complexification) while refusing to admit non-human creative intelligences (E4/E3) working from what Bennett calls the hyparchic future.

Barfield makes the same double critique. In Saving the Appearances (Ch. IX, pp. 60–65), he exposes textbook evolutionism as an "evolution of idols," projecting modern, non-participating representations back into a pre-human past. In Unancestral Voice (Chs. 6 and 9, pp. 68, 105–107), he shows that Darwinism reduces transformation, which needs an immaterial persisting vehicle, to mechanical substitution, by blacking out the spiritual agent. He explicitly criticizes Teilhard de Chardin (Unancestral Voice, p. 68; Worlds Apart, p. 34) for missing the interior evolution of consciousness, the Logos, and reincarnation.

—

5. THE MODERN CRISIS AND THE HUMAN BEING: ETERNITY-BLINDNESS, IDOLATRY, HABIT, EGOISM VS. "I AM," AND THE "IMAGINATION" INVERSION
(Vols. II and III vs. History, Guilt, and Habit and What Coleridge Thought)

A. Eternity-blindness and the Nullity vs. idolatry and the force of habit

• Barfield diagnoses modernity as idolatry, "the sin of literalness": experiencing collective representations as wholly external, self-existent things, "outsides with no insides" (History, Guilt, and Habit, pp. 70–71). It is held in place by "the force of habit," a "frozen, unconscious will" (p. 76).

• Bennett diagnoses the same condition as "eternity-blindness" (Vol. I, p. 257; Vol. II, p. 203) and the "fallacy of misplaced existentiality" (Vol. II, p. 135). Psychologically, our conscious energy (E4) is absorbed into biological sensitivity (E5) and mechanical automatism (E6) (Vol. III, §15.39.5.2, p. 140; Vol. IV, p. 200). That traps us in the material self and the reactional self, the "Nullity" (Vol. II, Ch. 31, pp. 187–194).

B. Existential egoism ("me") vs. essential selfhood ("I AM"), and practical awakening (Vol. III, Ch. 39)

In Vol. III (Ch. 39, "Human Types and Portraits," §15.39.6.4, p. 151), Bennett contrasts the pentad of Existential Man, whose center has been usurped by egoism, with the pentad of Essential Man, whose master is the Cosmic Individuality and whose true center, or Ipseity, is "I AM":

"The Ipseity of essential man is Individuality—the achievement of essential independence—the Ipseity as I AM—the Ipseity of existential man is the egoism of the untransformed self-hood."

This is the same distinction Coleridge and Barfield draw in What Coleridge Thought (Ch. 11, pp. 144–160, and p. 226 n. 18): "separate I from Me... none but one—God—can say 'I am I,' or 'That I am'"; and in Saving the Appearances (Ch. XXIV, pp. 169–174).

• Practical awakening. For Bennett (Vol. III, §15.39.5.2, p. 140), the key to liberation is separating consciousness (E4) from sensitivity (E5). He explicitly equates this with Gurdjieff's self-remembering, the Greek Fathers' nepsis (sobriety, in the Philokalia), and Buddhist satipatthana (mindfulness). For Barfield (History, Guilt, and Habit, pp. 73–92; Worlds Apart, p. 187), the equivalent is "getting our will into our thinking": waking from habitual association into active, self-conscious Imagination.

C. A crucial inversion of terms: "imagination"

Reading Bennett alongside Barfield calls for one important caution. In moral psychology, they use the word "imagination" in opposite ways.

• Bennett, in Vol. II (Ch. 31, §11.31.4, "Imagination as the negative triad -(1-2-3)," pp. 192–194; cf. Vol. III, p. 139 n.), follows Gurdjieff's pejorative Russian usage (voobrazhenie). "Imagination" is the negative inversion of the Law of Expansion: the passive, compensatory daydreaming of the Nullity, "building castles in Spain," where "the ideal becomes the actual in 'imagination.'"

• For Barfield, following Coleridge's Biographia Literaria, passive daydreaming is Fancy. Imagination, the "esemplastic power," is the supreme active organ of final participation. In Bennett's system that corresponds to creative energy (E3), Understanding, and the positive Law of Expansion, +(1-2-3). (In Vol. IV, pp. 155–156, Bennett himself uses "imagination" positively, for multi-dimensional historical perception.)

—

6. REINCARNATION VS. THE SOUL-STUFF POOL, ADVERSARIAL POWERS, CHRIST, AND HUMAN DESTINY
(Vols. III and IV vs. Saving the Appearances and Unancestral Voice)

A. The major divergence: the Soul-Stuff Pool (Vol. III, Ch. 40) vs. individual reincarnation (Unancestral Voice, Ch. 6)

• Bennett (Vol. III, Ch. 40, "Constructive Anthropology," §15.40.3 and §15.40.8, pp. 169–175, 216–225) posits a planetary Soul-Stuff Pool made of vital/sensitive (E5) and conscious (E4) energies. At conception, a quantum of soul-stuff is drawn into the embryo under the joint action of Fate (the astrological or world pattern, via the Laws of Synchronicity) and Destiny (creative energy, E3). At death, ordinary people, "half-souls" who have not crystallized an imperishable individualized soul, pass through a timeless review (Sheol) and dissolve back into the Pool. They return their unredeemed egoic deformations and memory-complexes to the common human reservoir, which explains both original sin and Jung's collective unconscious. Bennett therefore rejects Western "determinate reincarnation," in which an intact personal ego passes through successive lives. He favors "indeterminate reincarnation," in which coherent psychic fragments in the Pool are absorbed into several later births. He allows only rare prophetic exceptions, such as Elijah and John the Baptist.

• Barfield (Unancestral Voice, Ch. 6, pp. 68–76; Worlds Apart, pp. 203–207), following Steiner, argues the reverse. All genuine transformation requires a persisting vehicle, and the evolution of consciousness, from original participation through idolatry to final participation, is a single continuous spiritual biography. So the individual human spirit, the "I," must reincarnate from epoch to epoch.

B. The Fall and the adversarial powers: corruption of the creative powers vs. Lucifer and Ahriman

• Bennett (Vol. IV, Chs. 46–48, pp. 253–259, 323–325): around 35,000 years ago, when higher creative intelligences gave creative energy (E3) to Cro-Magnon humanity, rebel powers among them tempted humanity into egoism, badly polluting the shared Soul-Stuff Pool.

• Barfield (Unancestral Voice, pp. 68, 113, 158–159) adopts Steiner's picture of two adversaries. Lucifer is prideful spiritual continuity that refuses earthly contraction, "the false Preserver." Ahriman is materialistic reduction and mechanical substitution, "monkeying from without." Standing in the tension between them gives humanity freedom, so that transformation becomes self-transformation. This parallels Bennett's doctrine of universal hazard (Vol. II, Ch. 36, pp. 329–337).

C. Christ as the pivot of history (Vol. IV, Ch. 48 vs. Saving the Appearances, Ch. XXIV and Unancestral Voice)

Despite their different esoteric vocabularies, both culminate in a cosmic Christology.

• Bennett (Vol. IV, Ch. 48, "Mind and Love" / "The Time of Christ," pp. 327–351; Vol. III, Ch. 41, p. 272): after the "Megalanthropic Epoch" opened around 600 B.C., it became clear that neither the human mind (E5/E4) nor the creative powers (E3) could cleanse the egoism-polluted Soul-Stuff Pool. Redemption required the historical Incarnation of the Cosmic Individuality, the Logos, in Jesus Christ. He concentrated unitive energy (E2, objective divine love) in a perfected human organism and, through the Passion, Resurrection and Pentecost, infused it into the Earth's "hyparchic present."

• Barfield (Saving the Appearances, Chs. XXIV–XXV, pp. 169–183; Unancestral Voice, pp. 100, 111–115) sees the Incarnation as the turning point of time. The historical contraction of original participation reached its zero-point in one man, Jesus Christ, who spoke the cosmic "I AM" from within fully contracted human self-consciousness. That planted the creative Word in the interior of humanity and the Earth, and began final participation.

D. Esoteric guidance, and the present threshold

Esoteric guidance:
• Bennett (Vol. III, Ch. 41, "Human Societies," pp. 242–273; Vol. IV, pp. 325–326, 367–372, 412–419) structures humanity as a Dodecad of three tetrads. The Psychostatic is sleeping society. The Psychokinetic is people in the process of transformation: candidates, specialists, counsellors, initiates. The Psychoteleios is guides, saints and prophets united in "Sophia Wahi," and messengers united with Christ. They operate through physical sanctuaries as the Hidden Directorate, such as the Central Asian Khwajagan. In Gurdjieff: Making a New World (pp. 26, 59–60) and Vol. IV (p. 166), Bennett explicitly compares his sanctuary hypothesis with Steiner's The Spiritual Guidance of Mankind, noting that Steiner relied on inner, clairvoyant verification rather than on geographical brotherhoods.
• Barfield (Saving the Appearances, pp. 139–141; Unancestral Voice, pp. 27–30, 44–46) follows Steiner's inward path. In Unancestral Voice, spiritual guidance is dramatized as an inner dialogue with the Meggid, "one of the least of Michael's servants," who speaks in "thinking that has been set free from the flesh."

The post-1848 threshold:
• Bennett's Synergic Epoch (Vol. IV, Chs. 49–50, pp. 385–437; Vol. III, Ch. 41, pp. 276–289). Around 1848, the very year Coleridge's Theory of Life was published posthumously, humanity entered the Synergic Epoch. Top-down, patriarchal guidance withdraws. Free individuals and transforming (Psychokinetic) groups must consciously cooperate with higher intelligences, heal our predatory rupture with the biosphere, and come together into a "greater present moment" and a universal individuality.
• Barfield's final participation (Saving the Appearances, Ch. XXV, pp. 180–186; Unancestral Voice, p. 115; History, Guilt, and Habit, p. 92). Barfield identifies the mid-19th century as the low point of idolatry. He warns against Ahrimanic "monkeying from without," meaning ecological and technocratic manipulation, and calls for final participation, in which awakened human beings accept inner responsibility for the appearances and become conscious co-creators with the Logos.

—

HOW BENNETT AND BARFIELD COMPLETE ONE ANOTHER

Read together, each supplies what the other leaves implicit.

1. Barfield gives Bennett's architecture its phenomenological and philological ground. Bennett's six-dimensional geometry, twelve energies and multi-term Systematics can look like what Barfield calls a neo-Cartesian "thought-model." Barfield's historical semantics and his phenomenology of figuration show, from inside everyday language and perception, why phenomena come before facts, why meaning is undivided before analysis splits it, and how eternity-blindness, or idolatry, arose historically.

2. Bennett gives Barfield's final participation structural, energetic and social precision. Barfield points toward final participation through poetic imagination and anthroposophical meditation. Bennett offers a concrete blueprint for how awakened individuals and communities can actually work together in the world: his Systematics from Monad to Dodecad and the Enneagram, his six Laws of Synchronicity, his practice of separating consciousness (E4) from sensitivity (E5), and his sociology of transforming groups in the Synergic Epoch.

Unlike civilian judges sworn to political donors, the JAG Corps is sworn directly and exclusively to the United States Constitution. Under JAG jurisdiction, compromised civilian judges and fraudulent officials can be swiftly arrested, tried, and removed.

💻 5. Voting Machine Hacks & 2020 vs. 2026

Let’s address the elephant in the room: electronic voting machines.
